outlooksByWeek.2: Saquon Barkley averaged 5.5 yards per tote in Week 1 for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 15 times for 83 yards, though was held out of the end zone in the 24-22 win over Washington. Barkley should have even greater success in Week 2 versus a dismal Titans squad. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Saquon Barkley missed portions of Philadelphia's last game due to a stinger, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Saquon had five carries for just 20 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown, while Will Shipley saw nine touches and managed 29 yards overall. Bigsby and Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 yards last game for the Eagles. Philadelphia fell behind in the second half, though, which forced the Eagles to all but abandon the run. Barkley has yet to rush for 100 yards in a game this season. In Week 4, Barkley will face a stout defensive line with Aaron Donald when the Eagles clash with the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Saquon Barkley left Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring ailment. While the injury is not considered serious, it remains to be seen whether Barkley will be able to suit up in London in Week 5 versus the Jags. If Barkley can play, he will face a stiff test, as Jacksonville is allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is second in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have given up just two rushing touchdowns through the first four games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Saquon Barkley missed Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina remains up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve and Will Shipley started last game but suffered a foot injury of his own and did not return. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Saquon Barkley has missed the last two games for the Eagles due to a hamstring ailment, leaving his status for Week 7 versus the Cowboys in jeopardy. Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Barkley's place, while also catching four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley can somehow suit up, he will be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.8: Saquon Barkley returned from injury for the Eagles, only to tweak his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown, though played sparingly in the second half of the game, and ultimately could be sidelined again in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If Barkley is able to suit up, he will face a Washington defense that has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026.  The Commanders are allowing 100.5 rushing yards per clash, which is 14th in the league. In addition, Washington has allowed just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the league. If neither Barkley nor backup Dameon Pierce can play, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back.
outlooksByWeek.9: Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, Saquon was otherwise held in check with 54 scrimmage yards in a dismal 27-10 loss to Washington. Philadelphia does not appear likely to trade Barkley to a contender, leaving him primed for a revenge game against his former squad, the New York Giants, in Week 9. New York is allowing 128.1 rushing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles, but was otherwise bottled up. Barkley managed just 22 yards on the ground along with the score in the 19-11 loss to the Giants before the bye. With third-string quarterback Joe Milton under center, Saquon will likely see a stacked box in Week 11 versus the Steelers. Pittsburgh has been stellar in defending the run in 2026 as well, allowing just 83.2 yards per tilt on the ground, which is third in the league. Likewise, Pittsburgh has yielded just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Saquon Barkley carried the offensive load for the Eagles last game, though exited the contest due to a left arm issue. Barkley rushed 17 times for 75 yards and a touchdown, though did not log a carry during the final eight minutes of the narrow 19-16 win over the Steelers. Barkley should be healthy enough to suit up on Thanksgiving versus the Cowboys, though. Dallas has been abysmal against the run in 2026, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is the worst mark in the NFL. In addition, the Cowboys have given up 15 rushing scores, which is 29th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dak Prescott was held to just 175 passing yards in the season opener for the Cowboys.  Dak did toss two touchdowns, but he also threw a costly interception before the end of the first half, which led to a Giants touchdown. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Dak with an uninspiring output. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns last game in a virtuoso performance for the Cowboys. Prescott completed 26-of-31 throws for 279 yards and the four scores in the dominant 37-20 win over the Commanders. Prescott has six touchdowns and just one pick through the first two games of the young season. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dak Prescott threw for 276 yards and a touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens last game. Dak has passed for at least 275 yards through the air in each of the last two contests for the Cowboys, while also failing to toss a single interception over that span. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dak Prescott crossed the 300-yard passing mark last game for the Cowboys for the first time in 2026. Prescott actually threw for 335 yards in the thrilling comeback win over the Texans. More than half of the yards came via CeeDee Lamb, as the duo combined for a staggering 17 of Dak's 32 completions. Dak has eight passing scores and just one interception through four games. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dak Prescott went over the 300-yard passing mark for the second-straight game for Dallas. Unfortunately, Dak threw just one touchdown pass for the second-consecutive contest, while also tossing two picks in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Nevertheless, Dak is currently fourth in the NFL in passing yards, and tied for eighth in the league in passing touchdowns. However, in Week 6, Dallas will face a Green Bay defense allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered just six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dak Prescott has thrown four interceptions in his last two games for the Cowboys. While Dak has also thrown for over 250 yards in five-straight outings, he has passed for one touchdown apiece in four consecutive contests. Dallas has lost three of those four games. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus division foe Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dak Prescott tossed multiple touchdowns last game for Dallas for the first time since the middle of September. Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Prescott now has 13 touchdowns in seven starts in 2026. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals have also given up the most points per game in the NFL overall to date.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dak Prescott scored two total touchdowns last game for Dallas. However, Prescott passed for one touchdown or fewer for the fifth time in six contests. Dak was also held under 200 yards passing for just the second time in 2026. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dak Prescott posted his third 300-yard passing outing of the season for Dallas in Week 9, throwing for 335 yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Colts. He's thrown for multiple touchdowns in two of the last three contests. However, in Week 10, Prescott will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The 49ers are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Francisco has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Dak Prescott tied a career high with five touchdown passes last game for Dallas. Unfortunately, the Cowboys defense could not stop a nosebleed, as they fell by a staggering score of 46-40 to the 49ers. Dak also threw for a season-high 343 yards, notching his second-straight 300-yard output overall. Dak has tossed multiple touchdowns in three of the last four contests. In Week 11, Dak will look to keep rolling against a suspect Tennessee pass defense. The Titans are allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Dak Prescott scored five touchdowns for the second-straight game for the Cowboys. Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns, while rushing for another score in the 51-30 thrashing of the Titans. Prescott has thrown for over 300 yards in three-straight contests, and now has 25 passing touchdowns on the season. That places him second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Prescott is entering his 11th NFL season following a successful 2025 campaign in which he led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, pass attempts, passing yards and passing TDs. Prescott appeared in all 17 games and has now finished no worse than 11th in fantasy points during all seven seasons in which he has played at least 16 games. Last season, his nine top-10 fantasy weeks were tied for third most at the position. Prescott is no longer much of a threat with his legs, but he should continue to put up big passing numbers with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at his disposal. The 33-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Golden will remain a top option for Jordan Love as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards against the Jets in Week 2, catching four of six targets for 58 yards. The second-year wide receiver is also now set to take on a larger role, at least in the short term, with Jayden Reed looking to miss some time with a neck injury.  Golden will look to expand on his 10-153-0 receiving line against an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Golden will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards and targets in Week 3 against the Falcons, catching five of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver is in the middle of a breakout season, outpacing more than half of his 2025 output in just the first three games of this year. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Golden will look to do more as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Golden finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a season-low three catches for 21 yards, but he was able to salvage his performance with a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher remains a top option for quarterback Jordan Love, and he has an 18-274-2 receiving line through four games. Golden will be a major factor in Green Bay's success against their big rival, but he will face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Golden will aim to stay hot as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Golden finished Week 5 versus the Bears with the highest yardage total of his career, reeling in six catches for 123 yards. The second-year pass catcher has continued to squash bust projections every week this season, with 24 catches for 297 yards and two touchdowns across five outings. He'll face a Dallas defense that's fared even worse against wide receivers, ranking 21st in fantasy points allowed to the position so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Golden will look to build off another statement performance as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Golden brought in six of 13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, which could have been more if not for a pair of dropped touchdowns. The second-year wideout has now recorded a 30-501-3 receiving line off a team-high 57 targets, and he's already outpaced all of his 2025 output in just six games this season. He'll take on a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Golden will look to bounce back as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Golden wasn't abysmal in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, but he logged a season-low 39 yards on six catches. The second-year pass catcher has still totaled 36 grabs for 540 yards and three touchdowns across the seven games of the season, completely obliterating his 39-361-0 receiving line from the 2025 season across 14 games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Matthew Golden remains a high-volume option ahead of Green Bay's Week 9 matchup at New England. Golden surpassed 10 targets for the fifth time this season in a Week 8 win over Carolina, and he finished the night with seven catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher has now posted a 43-619-4 receiving line on 82 targets this season. He should have plenty of opportunities to stay hot against a Patriots defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers in the last three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Matthew Golden will look to keep his tear rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Golden logged a career-best 164 yards on 10 catches and found the end zone in a Week 9 win over the Patriots. The second-year breakout receiver also caught every one of his targets in the win, which was a huge improvement from some drop-heavy games this season. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he caught six passes for 95 yards against in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.12: Matthew Golden will look to shine against a tough Rams defense in Green Bay's Week 12 matchup out of the bye. Golden was the Packers' leading pass catcher in a Week 10 loss to Minnesota, hauling in five of nine targets for 70 yards. The second-year pass catcher has now recorded a 58-853-5 receiving line across 10 games, impressing after a subpar rookie season. He'll face a Los Angeles squad that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Washington hopes for more efficiency when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Washington recorded a healthy eight targets in the team's opener, and while 17.7 yards per catch is encouraging, he caught only three balls. Washington has value as a returner in some leagues, and passing volume will likely remain high with Miami forced to throw from behind in the second half. Even so, Week 2's matchup against a defense that held more talented receivers to just 6.4 yards per target in their opener is a risky endeavor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Washington brings steady volume ahead of the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. With Malik Willis under center, Miami has completed just 29 passes through two games, but seven have gone to Washington, who's averaging 6.5 targets. Kansas City's rebuilt secondary has been terrific through two games, allowing just 204 yards to opposing wideouts. Washington seems unlikely to produce any massive numbers, but he also appears to be a steady cog in this limited offense, keeping him on WR3/Flex radars.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Washington remains heavily involved in the Dolphins' low-profile passing game heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. Washington is coming off of a season-high 10 targets in Week 3, and has collected three rushing attempts over the last two weeks while also being involved in kickoff returns, but he's yet to top 61 rushing/receiving yards per game or score. Washington's workload creates a viable floor, and Minnesota is allowing a healthy 8.2 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Washington's volume continues to be steady for the Dolphins as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. He hauled in five of QB Malik WIllis' nine completions in Week 4, his fourth-straight week with at least five targets while increasing his yardage in each of the last three outings. Cincinnati's secondary hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 63 yards, and while Washington's workload shouldn't be questioned, his potential remains capped by Miami's low-scoring offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Washington brings a steady workload but limited yardage potential into the Dolphins' Week 7 matchup with the Jets. Washington has commanded at least five targets in all five games, three times reaching eight or more, but has topped out at 67 yards, operating mainly on short, slot routes while Miami struggles to find a vertical passing game. The Jets are allowing just 7.3 yards per target; Washington too is averaging 7.3 yards per target, setting him up for a rather predictable Week 7 outing where he'll need a heavy target share to offer anything more than bye-week replacement scoring.
outlooksByWeek.8: Malik Washington will hope for additional volume in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He collected a season-low three targets in Week 7, and volume has been the key to his fantasy relevance, having topped 56 yards once all season. It's a low-volume passing game that may be pressed into higher throw rates if Miami falls behind early, but Washington's role underneath doesn't create much upside despite facing a secondary that's surrendering a generous 8.8 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malik Washington's usage is on a slight decline as the Dolphins prepare to face the Lions in Week 9. Washington has just nine targets over the last two games, and while he scored his first touchdown of the year in Week 8, he's averaged under 10 yards per reception in three straight games. Detroit is allowing the ninth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers, but they have been far more vulnerable to tight ends. Washington will require higher volume if he's to return meaningful fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.10: Malik Washington's workload appears to be drying up ahead of the Dolphins' Week 10 matchup with the Colts. Washington averaged 7.2 targets in five games prior to Miami's Week 6 bye but has just 12 looks over the three games since, reaching 28 yards just once. Indianapolis is allowing a generous 8.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but with Miami's passing game struggling and Caleb Douglas emerging, Washington's decreasing role will make for a risky play with minimal upside.
outlooksByWeek.11: Malik Washington's opportunities continue to decline as the Dolphins get set to face the Bills in Week 11. Washington recorded three targets in Week 10, the third time in four weeks since Miami's Week 6 bye that he's failed to garner more looks. While Miami figures to throw from behind against Buffalo, Kyle McCord spread his 32 pass attempts in Week 10 across 11 different options, all while rookie Chris Bell was sidelined. With just one touchdown catch all season, Washington doesn't seem likely to pop against a defense that's allowed 11 touchdown catches to wide receivers, the fourth-highest total in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Malik Washington brings steady but middling production for the Dolphins into a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. For the fourth time in five games since Miami's Week 6 bye, Washington caught three passes in Week 11, finishing with just 30 yards. With Caleb Douglas emerging as Miami's top option, their low-success passing game hasn't proven capable of sustaining multiple receivers. The Jets are allowing 7.6 yard per target, ranking towards the bottom portion of the middle-tier, not suggesting Washington can break out on limited opportunities.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was a sixth-round flier back in 2024, but that didn't stop him from working his way into a substantial offensive role last season. Washington finished third on the Dolphins in targets, trailing only Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane. Of course, Miami's shaky group of offensive personnel was an obvious factor and Washington's efficiency wasn't very good (5.0 yards per target, 7.0 yards per reception, 0.9 yards per route run). The 25-year-old is fine as a short-range target and occasional rusher, but that's likely his ceiling with newcomers Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. expected to factor in at wide receiver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathan Taylor has scored multiple rushing TDs in both of the Colts' games heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Texans. The star RB led the NFL with 20 scrimmage TDs last season and looks poised to finish near the top of the leaderboard again this season. Taylor is a set-and-forget fantasy RB1, even against a stout Texans front seven that allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to RBs last season and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jonathan Taylor has four rushing TDs through three games and is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London. Washington has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL while struggling to defend the pass, but the Colts have proven they intend to feed their star RB a steady diet of carries regardless of opponent. A positive game script is certainly possible against a Commanders team that's starting backup QB Marcus Mariota, so Taylor has a clear path to another heavy workload and remains a must-start fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD performances through four games and is averaging 88 rushing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers rank among the 10 most generous defenses against RBs, allowing 138 scrimmage yards and one TD per game to the position. Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1 while working as the focal point of the Colts' offense, which lacked talent at wide receiver even before injuries further depleted that position. His 26 scrimmage touchdowns since the start of last season are the most in the NFL over that span.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD outings on the ground through five games, and he's likely to be the focal point of the Colts' offense in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who are surrendering 120 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Taylor averages 23 touches per game and should handle a heavy workload, with the Colts expected to play from ahead at home. Start the star RB, who is averaging 101 scrimmage yards per game, with confidence in this clash between AFC South rivals.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jonathan Taylor has topped 90 rushing yards four times this season and has seven TDs, while the rest of the Colts' offense has scored six touchdowns combined. The star RB remains a set-and-forget fantasy RB1 for Week 7, even in a difficult matchup with a stout Vikings defense that's allowing 86.6 rushing yards per game (fifth-fewest) and a league-low 12.8 points per game. Opponents have been stacking the box against Taylor with Daniel Jones struggling to make defenses pay through the air, but Taylor has overcome those difficult situations to rank among the league's most productive players at his position as usual, despite the lack of help from his teammates.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jonathan Taylor has at least 92 rushing yards and a TD in five of the Colts' seven games, keeping him firmly in set-and-forget fantasy RB1 territory for Week 8 despite a difficult matchup against Jacksonville's elite front. The Jaguars are allowing a league-low 72 rushing yards per game and boast the league's third-best scoring defense at 17.3 points per game. Taylor has handled 20-plus touches in all but one game this season and should remain busy in Week 8, as long as the 2-5 Colts stay within striking distance of the 4-2 Jaguars.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jonathan Taylor set season lows with 12 touches for 47 yards in the Colts' 42-7 Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. Indianapolis got down big early and had to abandon the run. The Cowboys have enough talent on offense to repeat the scenario, but it's more likely that the Colts keep things close enough for Taylor to capitalize on facing a Dallas defense that has been among the most generous in the league to RBs, allowing 11 total TDs to the position through eight games. Taylor has eight rushing TDs in eight games, accounting for more than half of the Colts' offensive touchdowns this season. He'll be a fantasy RB1 if he's in his usual role, though it's possible Indianapolis limits Taylor's usage as trade rumors swirl around the star RB.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jonathan Taylor was not traded prior to Tuesday's deadline. He has rushed for 656 yards and eight TDs through nine games with the Colts, putting the star RB on pace for a fifth campaign with at least 1,169 rushing yards and 11 TDs. Taylor has a juicy Week 10 matchup against the 1-7 Dolphins. Despite staying with the Colts, he remains a set-and-forget fantasy RB1.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jonathan Taylor exceeded 100 scrimmage yards for the fifth time in 10 tries during the Colts' Week 10 win over the Dolphins, but he was held without a touchdown for a third consecutive game. Seth McGowan has two rushing TDs during Taylor's three-game drought, both of which came from inside the 5-yard line. The rookie seventh-round pick could remain a thorn in Taylor's side if the Colts continue to give McGowan goal-line opportunities. McGowan's emergence, coupled with the Colts' offensive struggles as a team, knocks Taylor down to the fantasy RB1/RB2 borderline moving forward, and expectations should be tempered in Week 11 against a stout Texans front that limited Taylor to just 72 yards on 25 touches for a season-low 2.9 yards per touch in their first meeting this season. You're still starting Taylor if you have him in virtually every fantasy format, but he's likely to perform closer to his floor than his superstar ceiling in Week 11.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jonathan Taylor has averaged just 16.3 touches over the Colts' last four games after averaging 22.4 touches in the first seven. Part of that decline has to do with the 3-8 Colts failing to remain competitive. Taylor has also started to cede a larger portion of rushing opportunities, including goal-line carries, to Seth McGowan, who won't suit up in Week 12 against the Giants due to a hamstring injury. Taylor remains too good to bench in most leagues, and perhaps Indianapolis' entire ground game will pick up the pace now that mobile, big-armed QB Anthony Richardson is running the show rather than Daniel Jones, but Taylor's nowhere near the top-five fantasy RB conversation at the moment. Treat the star RB as a fantasy RB2 for Week 12 against the Giants, who have been elite at defending the pass but rank in the middle of the pack against the run.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: RJ Harvey returned from a one-game absence due to a hamstring strain in Week 2 to contribute to the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, gaining just six rushing yards on two carries but producing a 6-41-0 line on seven targets. The second-year back is secure in his role as Denver's top pass-catcher out of the backfield while J.K. Dobbins is the main option on early downs. Rookie Jonah Coleman could challenge both once he's back from IR. Harvey will look to make a bigger impact in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that's already given up 17 catches to RBs this season, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: RJ Harvey is coming off the best performance of his career as a pass catcher, posting a 10-68-0 line on 10 targets while adding 25 rushing yards on seven carries in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers. Denver trailed most of the game, which helped boost the second-year back's usage, but J.K. Dobbins' struggles in the early-down role are also opening the door for Harvey to log more touches in general, as his seven carries were also a season high. The eventual return of rookie Jonah Coleman from a high-ankle sprain could shake up the backfield further, but until then Harvey's arrow appears to be pointed up. He'll look to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs..
outlooksByWeek.6: RJ Harvey all but vanished from the Broncos' game plan in Week 5, gaining seven yards on three carries and failing to catch his only target as Sean Payton returned to play-calling duties. His usage as a pass-catcher was especially disappointing after the second-year back was fed 17 targets over the prior two weeks, turning that volume into a 16-109-0 line. J.K. Dobbins is the preferred early-down option in the backfield, and Harvey's value could become very dependent on game flow as a result. He might see more work in Week 6 if Denver falls behind early against a Seattle team that's in the bottom seven in the league in receptions per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: RJ Harvey found the end zone for the first time in 2026 during the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The second-year running back managed just 56 scrimmage yards on nine touches as he continues to work behind J.K. Dobbins in the backfield. Harvey's target volume has declined since Sean Payton took back play-calling duties, notching only five targets the last two weeks while producing a 3-31-0 line through the air. Harvey will try to reclaim a more consistent role in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: RJ Harvey logged just five touches in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, but he turned one of them into a 52-yard TD reception in the third quarter to salvage his day. The second-year back finished third in the backfield in workload behind rookie Jonah Coleman (11 touches) and veteran J.K. Dobbins (six touches), but Harvey seems to have a steady role as a passing-down option for Bo Nix. Even if Sean Payton continues to roll with a committee approach to his ground game, Harvey's floor should be relatively secure, even if his ceiling is limited to occasional big plays. He's unlikely to make a splash in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jonah Coleman didn't see the ball in his NFL debut during the Broncos' opener, but his role increased in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Coleman ended up getting more touches than J.K. Dobbins, with the 2026 fourth-round pick turning 10 carries into 39 yards and his first career touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 19 yards. It's not clear how much time Harvey might miss, but Coleman's solid showing in his first opportunity could begin the process of turning the backfield into a three-man committee, with the workload dependent on whoever happens to be healthy. Coleman could be a risky play in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jonah Coleman had the biggest share of the backfield workload in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, handling 11 touches to J.K. Dobbins' six and RJ Harvey's five. Coleman's 69 scrimmage yards led the trio, but the other two each made trips to the end zone while the rookie RB was held out. It was still an impressive effort in his return from an IR stint due to an ankle injury, and Coleman might be the most likely player from the group to emerge as the lead back. A messy committee is the more probable arrangement, however, heading into a Week 8 clash with a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jonah Coleman may be emerging as the Broncos' lead running back. The 2026 fourth-round pick topped 100 scrimmage yards for the first time in a comeback win over Kansas City in Week 8, and he scored the winning touchdown on a five-yard run after getting Denver into the red zone with a 51-yard catch-and-run. J.K. Dobbins logged seven carries, compared to Coleman's 15 total touches, and with RJ Harvey on injured reserve, the path is clear for the rookie to handle a significant workload. Coleman could be headed for a true breakout performance in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jonah Coleman captured the No. 1 job in the Broncos' backfield prior to the team's bye. Over the team's last two games, the rookie running back amassed 192 scrimmage yards and two rushing TDs, with his yardage split almost equally between the ground and the air. Coleman's usage as a pass catcher could decline once RJ Harvey gets healthy in a couple of weeks, but he's clearly surpassed J.K. Dobbins as the preferred ball carrier in all situations, including at the goal line. Coleman will take on a Raiders defense in Week 11 that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jonah Coleman cemented himself as the Broncos' No. 1 running back with a stunning performance in a Week 11 win over the Raiders. The fourth-round rookie romped for 129 scrimmage yards on 28 touches while scoring three rushing touchdowns, extending his streak of games with at least one score to three. Coleman appears capable of handling a bell-cow workload and a three-down role, but he could face competition for passing-down snaps once RJ Harvey is cleared to return from a knee injury. Coleman will face a Steelers defense in Week 12 that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of April's draft. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient during four collegiate seasons at Arizona and Washington. Coleman didn't get much pre-contact help (1.80 YBC), but he made up for it after contact (3.73 YAC ranks second in this rookie RB class) and his career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is best in this class. Also solid as a receiver and blocker, Coleman has three-down ability, but may not get that opportunity until 2027. The rookie will begin his career behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Coleman should be added only if Dobbins or Harvey goes down with an injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to face the Texans in Week 2. The 25-year-old rookie and former CFL receiver played nine snaps on offense and six on special teams during Cincinnati's Week 1 win. Meyers flashed with his limited opportunities, catching his lone target for 18 yards while rushing once for 10 yards. There's a chance he could leapfrog Colbie Young on the depth chart, but we'll have to see what he does against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals host the Jaguars in Week 4. The rookie receiver caught three of five targets for 29 yards during Cincinnati's Week 3 loss, stepping up with Colbie Young (knee) and Andrei Iosivas (thumb/IR) out due to injuries. Meyers tied Mike Gesicki for third on the team in receptions, though he garnered two more targets than the tight end. He's still firmly behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins in the passing game, but he's showing signs of being a reliable option in a banged-up WR room. Meyers will look to contribute against Jacksonville, whose defense ranks 26th in receiving yards allowed (527) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He caught seven of nine targets for 82 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 Week 4 loss, setting new career highs across his receiving line, while returning six kickoffs for 161 yards and two punts for nine yards. Meyers finished second on the team in receiving yards and third in receptions and targets, and there's a decent chance he could earn a similar workload versus Miami's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are both questionable to play, along with fellow rookie Colbie Young (knee), and Andre Iosivas (thumb, IR) remains out for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals visit the division-rival Ravens in Week 7. He caught both of his targets for 12 yards during Cincinnati's Week 5 victory. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both healthy, Meyers returned to a supporting role, supplying 91 yards on three kick returns and another 13 yards on two punt returns. Rookie Colbie Young (knee) could also return from a two-game absence, so both receivers could struggle to make much of a contribution against the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals are at home in Week 8 to square off against Tennessee. He failed to catch either of his two targets in Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Meyers was unable to take advantage of Joe Burrow's productive day, as he threw for 292 yards and four TDs. Meyers should remain on fantasy benches, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins occupying a massive target share despite a solid matchup versus the Titans.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals are in Spain to square off against the Falcons in Week 9. He caught all three of his targets for 34 yards during Cincinnati's thrilling overtime victory in Week 8. Meyers also accumulated 119 yards on five kick returns and 31 yards on two punt returns, as the Bengals clearly value his speed and versatility. However, with Ja'Marr Chase (11-141-1) and Tee Higgins (10-155-2) commanding most of Joe Burrow's attention in the passing game, Meyers' contributions will likely remain limited.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals host the division-rival Steelers in Week 10. He caught two of three targets for 47 yards and had a 16-yard carry during Cincinnati's 34-17 victory in Week 9. Meyers also returned four kicks for 100 yards and finished second on the team in receiving yardage. The Bengals like to get the ball in his hands, but with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins occupying the majority of Joe Burrow's attention, Meyers should remain on fantasy benches.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals pay Washington a visit on Monday Night Football. He caught both targets for 20 yards and his first career touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 10 win. Meyers was on the receiving end of one of Joe Burrow's four passing scores while finishing fifth in receptions and yardage. Meyers should remain on fantasy benches despite playing in a very pass-friendly offense, as his role is simply capped with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dominating the target share.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals welcome the Saints to town for an interconference tilt. He caught one of two targets for two yards, returned one punt for five yards, and returned six kicks for 150 yards during Cincinnati's loss in Week 11. The Bengals continue to deploy the versatile Meyers on offense and special teams, but he doesn't offer much fantasy value while playing behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Meyers should remain on fantasy benches outside of deep formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded 216 rushing yards to RBs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Monangai should remain the complementary option in Chicago's backfield in Week 4 against the Jets. Monangai logged his third straight showing with 10 carries in Week 3 versus the Eagles, but he converted them for a season-low 31 rushing yards. The second-year running back also garnered no targets in the passing game, which came as a letdown after he posted a 4-35-0 receiving line leading up to the Monday Night win. He'll look to improve on his consistent volume against a New York defense that's allowed an eighth-most 24.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Monangai will look to shed a questionable tag after a huge performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Monangai dominated the Jets on the ground in Week 4 with 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns, but he also injured his thumb and is currently day-to-day. The second-year ball carrier's practice availability should dictate whether he's able to play in Chicago's rivalry debut of the 2026 season. If he's active, he'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Monangai will aim to return to the field as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Monangai sat out in Week 5 with a toe injury, but he's week-to-week and not a candidate for IR. The second-year ball carrier put together a career-best 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets in Week 4, so he could be inching towards a featured role if he can get back to the field. If he plays, Monangai will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Monangai has missed back-to-back games with turf toe, and he'll need to get back to practice if he hopes to see the field in a TNF matchup. If he is active, he'll return to a favorable backfield role versus a Falcons defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyle Monangai will aim to make a return as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Monangai has missed the last three games with a turf toe injury, but Chicago is not planning to place him on IR. This makes it likely the second-year running back at least has a chance to return in the upcoming away tilt. With two 100-yard rushing games and three touchdowns across the first four games of the season, Monangai is an intriguing option if he returns, even against a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Monangai has sat out the last four weeks with thumb and toe issues. The second-year ball carrier recording a 30-146-2 rushing line before his inactive streak makes it even more frustrating, so he'll hopefully get back to practice sooner rather than later. If he is healthy against Tampa Bay, he'll face a defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Monangai has sat out five straight games as he works back from a turf-toe injury. The second-year ball carrier's status is very likely correlated with his ability to practice, so this week should reveal his expected return timeline. He accrued 324 rushing yards and three touchdowns off 60 carries in the first four games of the season. If he returns, Monangai will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kyle Monangai will look to get more opportunities as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Monangai was quiet in his return from a five-game absence due to turf toe, carrying the ball eight times for just 18 yards. The second-year ball carrier could be in line for a ramped up role in the upcoming away matchup, but D'Andre Swift currently looks to have the RB1 role in his grasp. Detroit's defense has ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry will look for more opportunities in Week 2 when New England hosts Pittsburgh. Henry caught all three of his targets to open 2026, and with the Patriots losing A.J. Brown (ankle) for the foreseeable future, additional targets could come Henry's way. Pittsburgh didn't allow a catch to tight ends last week, but that was a product of poor opponent quarterback play. Henry can be considered a back-end option at the position with the potential for far more against a defense he posted two touchdowns and 90 yards against a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hunter Henry will look to keep expanding his role for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Jaguars. In their first full game without A.J. Brown in Week 2, Henry logged a 92% snap share but drew only five targets, turning them into three catches for 40 yards. Drake Maye has struggled to open the season, posting a 1:4 TD:INT ratio, and while someone has to catch the limited passes, Henry faces a challenging matchup against a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing tight end to top 32 yards against them so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Hunter Henry is laboring for opportunity in a sputtering Patriots passing offense ahead of a Week 4 game against the Bills. Henry caught just one of two targets in Week 3, finishing with five yards, and has yet to score or top 40 yards. There are likely better Week 4 options with Henry facing a defense that's allowed one opposing tight end to top 35 yards.
outlooksByWeek.5: Hunter Henry could have an expanded role in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders with Eli Raridon (ankle) uncertain. Henry was already playing at least 70% of the snaps, and he posted a season-high five catches for 62 yards in Week 4, collecting five targets for the second time this season. Las Vegas has allowed five touchdown catches to opposing tight ends, but also just 6.1 yards per target through four games, suggesting Henry may need to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 to be a fantasy asset.
outlooksByWeek.6: Hunter Henry has been steady in the Patriots passing game ahead of a potentially difficult Week 6 matchup with the Jets. He has three catches in four of the Patriots' first five games, three times recording at least 40 yards, and he posted 45 and 49 yards in two matchups last season against this divisional opponent. However, the Jets have been stingy against tight ends, allowing just 191 yards (6.0 yards per target) and zero touchdowns through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Hunter Henry brings a two-game scoring streak into the Patriots' Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With Drake Maye clicking on all cylinders over the last three weeks (10 touchdown passes), Henry has posted at least three catches and 44 yards during that stretch. Chicago has defended tight ends well for most of the season, but over the last two weeks, an opposing tight end has gone for 60 or more yards, and they've surrendered their first two touchdowns of the year to the position. Henry's volume is steady, giving him a bit more of a reliable floor than high potential.
outlooksByWeek.8: Hunter Henry is poised to build on a season-high performance in Week 7 when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. While he failed to reach the end zone for the first time in three games, Henry hauled in all seven of his targets for 71 yards, all season bests. Miami has been exploited by opposing tight ends with six touchdown receptions in six games and 9.3 yards per target, the second highest mark in the league. New England continues to spread targets around, but it seems wise to scheme into this vulnerability, making Henry a preferred Week 8 option.
outlooksByWeek.9: Hunter Henry will need to overcome a foot injury if he's to help the Patriots loosen up a stingy Packers defense in Week 9. Henry hauled in all three of his first-half targets in Week 8 before exiting. Should he play, the challenge becomes finding holes against a Green Bay defense that's allowing just 5.8 yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends. Eli Raridon has shown promise and would benefit from a potential Henry absence, but the matchup concerns remain.
outlooksByWeek.10: Hunter Henry figures to be a popular option for the Patriots in Week 10 against a Lions defense that struggles against opposing tight ends. Henry has just three targets in each of his last two games and has topped 48 yards just twice all season, but Week 10 presents an inviting opportunity. Detroit has allowed 11 touchdown receptions to tight ends and 8.2 yards per target, the highest numbers across the league. With New England potentially missing its top two running backs, a pass-heavy script would set Henry up for top-end production.
outlooksByWeek.12: Hunter Henry is saddled with an unfavorable Week 12 matchup when the Patriots take on the Chargers. He has just three targets in each of New England's last three games. Tommy DeVito playing quarterback could lead to additional check-downs, but that wasn't the case in Week 10 against Detroit. The Chargers have allowed one touchdown to a tight end, though a league-high 9.4 yards per target. Still, Henry isn't set up for a productive effort.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Stefon Diggs had more than double the targets of teammate Terry McLaurin in Week 1 for Washington. Diggs was targeted a team-high nine times, though managed only four catches. However, he gained 55 yards and also found the end zone, though had a costly celebration penalty on the score that cost Washington a chance to go for two and tie the game late. Still, it was an extremely promising start for Diggs, who will have a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus Dallas. The Cowboys allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Stefon Diggs has scored three times in two games as a member of the Commanders. Diggs snagged five passes for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Washington's loss to Dallas last week. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Stefon Diggs finished second in targets for the Commanders last game. Diggs caught four balls on seven looks, though managed just 33 yards in the surprising win over Seattle. Diggs was also held out of the end zone for the first time this season. Diggs caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Stefon Diggs led the Commanders in targets and receptions last game. With Terry McLaurin sidelined due to a hamstring issue, Diggs managed five catches on nine targets. However, he could only muster 35 yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Diggs, regardless of whether McLaurin also suits up. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Stefon Diggs missed Washington's last game due to a hamstring issue. In his absence, Terry McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams would likely benefit if Diggs cannot suit up in Week 6 versus the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Stefon Diggs will serve as the No. 1 wideout for the Commanders for the remainder of the season, as Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign due to a knee injury. Diggs has scored four times in five games played for Washington, following a return from a hamstring injury of his own. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Stefon Diggs found the end zone again last game for Washington. Diggs snagged three balls for 38 yards and the score in the 27-10 win over the Commanders. Diggs has scored in back-to-back outings, and five times overall in 2026. However, in Week 9, Diggs will face a stellar Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Stefon Diggs had a two-game scoring streak snapped last game for Washington. Diggs caught three passes for 51 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams. Diggs will look for a return to the end zone in Week 10 versus the Giants. New York has given up 14 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 20th in the league. However, do not expect much in the way of yardage, as the G-Men are yielding just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Stefon Diggs has scored in three of his last four games played for Washington. Diggs scored the game-winning touchdown last Thursday versus the Giants to bring his season total for receiving touchdowns to six. Diggs also posted a season-high 83 receiving yards for the game. He was targeted 10 times for the game, and should continue to see increased looks in the absence if Terry McLaurin. However, in Week 11, he will be facing a Bengals defense allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. In addition, Cincy has yielded just 11 passing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Stefon Diggs finished second on the team in targets last game for Washington. Diggs saw six looks en route to four catches for 45 yards in the thrilling 22-20 win over Cincy. Diggs has at least three catches in every game played this season, though has gone over 50 yards receiving on just three occasions. In Week 12, Diggs will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Wright's role in the Dolphins' offense is limited entering a Week 2 matchup against the 49ers. Despite being their No. 2 back, Wright played just 6% of their offensive snaps to De'Von Achane's 88%. With Miami likely falling behind early and being forced to pass, Wright is far more insurance for Achane managers than a viable fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Wright's role is limited in the Dolphins' backfield entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. He has logged just seven snaps through two games and is now dealing with a stinger issue that makes him uncertain to play. With no clear immediate path to touches, Wright is an insurance policy in a matchup against a defense allowing 4.0 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out last Sunday. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins falling behind often in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the better pass-catching option of the two. Facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 ypc and 11 catches to running backs to date however doesn't inspire confidence.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Wright hasn't emerged from the Dolphins' backfield ahead of a Week 5 tilt against the Bengals. After missing Week 3, Wright was thought to have an ascending role following De'Von Achane's season-ending knee injury but received only five carries in Week 4 while Ollie Gordon shined with 100 yards and a touchdown on nine carries. It doesn't appear Wright was limited by the foot issue that cost him a game, as he remained the team's primary kick returner. Facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry should afford Wright additional running lanes, but the role uncertainty puts Wright in wait-and-see territory rather than as a viable flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Wright hopes to come out of the Dolphins' bye with a larger role in Week 7 against the Jets. Wright has only amassed 11 carries over his last two outings, finishing with 18 yards while not being targeted in the passing game. Ollie Gordon has dominated backfield work since De'Von Achane (knee) went down for the season, leaving managers in a wait-and-see mode with regards to Wright against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, ranking near the middle of the pack league-wide.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Wright has not played a meaningful role out of the Dolphins' backfield and is uncertain to play in Week 8 against the Patriots due to a quad issue. He had five or six carries in each of his last three games, failing to average better than 1.8 yards per carry, and has not caught a pass all season. Facing a middling New England run defense seems less important than considering Wright's continued lack of clean health and the potential that Miami falls behind early and abandons the run.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaylen Wright continues to play a minor role in the Dolphins' rushing game ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Lions. Wright has logged a 12% to 14% snap share over the last three weeks, not topping six offensive touches in any outing, with Ollie Gordon dominating carries. Detroit is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, which is in the middle of the pack, but they allow the third-fewest fantasy points to the position. Barring an injury to Gordon, Wright's usage is unlikely to change, keeping him off most fantasy radars.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jaylen Wright didn't factor into the Dolphins' backfield even before a quad injury cost him Week 9. He'll need to overcome that issue if he's to take aim at Indianapolis' vulnerable run defense in Week 10. Wright has just 19 total carries across his last four games, with Ollie Gordon dominating touches. The Colts are allowing 4.8 yards per carry and the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing rushers, but Wright hasn't been afforded enough chances to take advantage of those deficiencies.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jaylen Wright continues to be on the wrong side of rushing attempts as the Dolphins get set to face the Bills in Week 11. Wright hasn't logged more than six touches in any game this season and has reached 11 rushing yards just twice. With Buffalo allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, Ollie Gordon dominating carries and Miami's likely need to pass from behind as the game moves along, Wright doesn't offer much appeal.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jaylen Wright remains minimally used in the Dolphins' rushing game ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. He played just nine offensive snaps in Week 11 rushing just five times for the fourth time in six games. While the Jets are allowing the eighth most fantasy points per game to running backs, Ollie Gordon dominates Miami's backfield. Wright lacks much fantasy appeal.

player.seasonOutlook: Wright will once again compete with second-year Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind feature back De'Von Achane. Wright has barely cleared 70 touches during each of his first two NFL seasons, but he has shined at times, including a 24-107-1 rushing line in Week 14 last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick has been effective as a rusher, but hasn't been involved in the passing game (15 targets in 25 games). The 23-year-old would be worth adding only in the event of an Achane injury and even then, it's possible he would split (or be on the short end of a committee) with Gordon in a rebuilding offense that may not score very often.

outlooksByWeek.7: Myles Price will look to stay involved as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Price mostly contributed on special teams to start the season, but he's seen an uptick in usage, with five catches for 45 yards in his last two outings. While more targets will be needed to make him an attractive target beyond his return abilities, he's worth keeping an eye on, especially against an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Myles Price remains a depth option heading into Minnesota's Week 8 matchup at Detroit. Price didn't log a full game in Week 7 against the Colts as he was being evaluated for a concussion, and this translated to zero targets. The sophomore remains a return guru at this point in the season, but it remains to be seen if his five catches for 26 yards across Weeks 4 and 5 before Minnesota's bye were a fluke. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Myles Price will remain a depth option in the passing game in Minnesota's travel to Green Bay in Week 10. Price reeled in one of four targets for six yards in the Vikings' Week 9 loss to the Bills, which was his first grab since Week 5. The second-year wide receiver has now recorded six catches for 32 yards this campaign. The Packers have ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Myles Price could benefit from an uptick in usage again as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. With teammates Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) both out in Week 10, Price caught four targets for 49 yards and a touchdown and rushed the ball once for 12 yards, which were all season highs or tied season highs. With Addison set to be out for multiple weeks and Jennings not showing much when on the field, Price could be the flashy target opposite Justin Jefferson that Minnesota needs. Price look to keep his success going against a San Francisco defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to his position.
outlooksByWeek.12: Myles Price will aim to stay involved as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Price put together another solid game with Jordan Addison sidelined again in Week 11, catching both of his two targets for 26 yards. The sophomore has now logged six catches for 75 yards in his last two outings. He'll face an Atlanta squad that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chig Okonkwo had a rough debut Week 1 for the Commanders. On only three targets, the former Titan caught a mere two passes for 16 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. He subsequently injured his hamstring and did not return. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. John Bates and Ben Sinnott would step in at tight end if Chig misses Week 2 versus Dallas. If he suits up, Okonkwo would have a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that allowed two touchdowns to Giants tight end Isaiah Likely in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chig Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 for the Commanders. Washington's active tight ends did not fare well, catching a combined two passes for 20 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Okonkwo, even if he is able to suit up.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chig Okonkwo is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4. John Bates has handled the tight end slot amid limited fanfare without Okonkwo, as Bates caught a nine-yard pass last game in Okonkwo's absence. If Okonkwo can suit up in Week 4, he may have an intriguing matchup versus the Colts, even with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chig Okonkwo returned to the lineup for the Commanders following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment. Okonkwo was targeted four times, but managed two catches for a mere five yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, though, which would certainly be a boost for the passing game. However, New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chig Okonkwo made his presence felt for Washington in his return to the lineup. Following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment, Okonkwo led the team with six targets en route to four catches for 60 yards in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chig Okonkwo has posted back-to-back 60-plus yard outings for Washington, and could see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season.  No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Okonkwo has amassed 13 targets in the last two games alone. In Week 8, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season. Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chig Okonkwo made a dazzling one-handed catch last game for Washington. The highlight-reel grab is a candidate for one of the top receptions of the NFL season to date. Okonkwo finished with two catches for 32 yards in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. He was targeted four times. In Week 9, Okonkwo will face a stellar Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chig Okonkwo has been targeted at least six times in three of the last four contests for the Commanders. Okonkwo caught six passes for 57 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams last game. Okonkwo has at least 55 receiving yards in three of the last four games for Washington. However, he will face a difficult test in the form of the New York Giants in Week 10. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chig Okonkwo has been a frequent target of quarterback Jayden Daniels since returning from injury for the Commanders. Okonkwo has at least six targets in four of the last five contests for Washington.  In fact, Okonkwo has been targeted 15 times over the last two games alone. Okonkwo is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, though. In Week 11, he will face a fairly stingy Cincinnati pass defense. The Bengals are allowing only 216.2 passing yards per clash, which is 11th in the league. Likewise, Cincy has given up just 11 throwing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chig Okonkwo continues to serve as an excellent safety valve for the Commanders. Okonkwo reeled in four passes for 66 yards in the stunning 22-20 win over the Bengals. Okonkwo has at least four catches in five of his last six games played, though he is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. In Week 12, Chig will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

player.seasonOutlook: Okonkwo signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons in Tennessee. The 2022 fourth-round pick is one of only four tight ends who have appeared in all 68 games since he entered the league, and he's also one of only six tight ends who have registered 50-plus receptions each of the past three seasons. On the other hand, Okonkwo has yet to clear a 16% target share in a single season, and he has been a nonfactor near the goal line (eight TDs and 11 end zone targets in his career).
