As a result, he has finished exactly 21st in fantasy points each of the past three seasons. Perhaps he'll make a leap as one of Jayden Daniels' top targets, but the 27-year-old is no more than a back-end TE2 lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Omarion Hampton scored a touchdown for the third time in four games during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but his role in the backfield continues to slip. The second-year back's nine carries and 11 touches were season lows for a spark for his unit. Hampton has still been the most productive of the trio this season with 267 scrimmage yards and three rushing TDs, but his 4.0 yards per carry trails Mitchell's, while Keaton Mitchell handled 15 touches and Kimani Vidal got seven, indicating that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is moving toward a full-blown committee as he searches 4.6 mark. Hampton will try to re-establish himself as the clear No. 1 on the depth chart in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Omarion Hampton continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme while working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line. Hampton does have three rushing touchdowns in five games, but his 3.7 yards per carry is a significant downturn from his 4.4 mark as a rookie, and he's averaging just 61.2 scrimmage yards per contest. He's also lost snaps and touches to Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as the backfield devolves into a committee. Hampton will try to find a spark in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Omarion Hampton will look to turn his season around coming out of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. He failed to reach 50 scrimmage yards or get into the end zone in his last two games before the break, as Mike McDaniel turned his backfield into a committee. Hampton is the most talented back on the roster, but as long as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal are garnering significant shares of the workload, all of them will have limited ceilings. Hampton will try to reassert himself as the No. 1 option in Week 8 against a Rams defense that's tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Omarion Hampton remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Keaton Mitchell got seven touches and Kimani Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Hampton hasn't found the end zone since Week 4, and while he's nominally at the top of the depth chart, his current usage holds little appeal. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Omarion Hampton turned 13 carries into a team-high 60 rushing yards in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, his second-highest total of the season. Keaton Mitchell handled 10 touches, and Kimani Vidal got eight, as offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel continues to deploy a backfield committee that limits the ceiling of all three players. Hampton appears to be first among equals for now, but the struggles of the entire offense present an extra obstacle for him to overcome. He'll try to build on last week's modest numbers in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Omarion Hampton is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens, topping 100 rushing yards for the first time and scoring his first touchdown since Week 4. It was a big step toward Hampton regaining the clear No. 1 job in the backfield, as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combined for just seven touches and 18 scrimmage yards. Hampton will look to keep rolling in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the clear No. 1 option in the Chargers' backfield. Over the last three games, the second-year running back has turned 49 carries into 254 rushing yards and a touchdown, averaging a robust 5.2 yards per carry. Keaton Mitchell picked up a knee injury in a Week 11 loss to the Jets, which could leave Kimani Vidal as the primary backup. Hampton will look to keep surging in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Little made all three of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's Week 4 win over the Bengals. The big-legged kicker has yet to miss from inside 50 yards and has tremendous range, as Little made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season and narrowly missed a 70-yard attempt this season. Little remains a viable fantasy starter as usual in Week 5 against an Eagles team that's allowing 23.3 points per game but has given up only six successful field goals through four games. This game will be played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, where Spencer Shrader and Drew Stevens combined to make all five of their field-goal attempts in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Little made both of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's 19-17 Week 5 win over the Eagles in London, including the game-winning 57-yarder on the game's final play. He also missed a PAT, with a bad snap contributing after the Jaguars lost long snapper Ross Matiscik to a shoulder injury in the first quarter. Snaps could again be an issue on Jacksonville's kicking attempts in Week 6, but the big-legged Little has too much upside to bench as the Jaguars play their second consecutive game in London, this time taking on a Texans team that has allowed 12 made field goals (tied for third-most in the league), and 22.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Little has started 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts with a long of 60 across Jacksonville's first six games. The big-legged kicker could be in for a busy afternoon in Week 8 at home against the Colts, who are giving up 25.7 points per game and have allowed a league-high 21 field-goal attempts, 18 of which have been successful. Little is worth snagging off waivers if he was dropped during Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, as he profiles as a top-10 kicker for Week 8 and beyond.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cam Little has attempted 23 PATs compared to just 12 field goals this season, a testament to Jacksonville's high-octane offense. His ceiling remains immense given the frequent scoring opportunities and Little's elite range, making him a viable fantasy starter for Week 9. Little will face a reeling Ravens team in Week 9 that has dropped three consecutive games while allowing at least 35 points in each of the last two. Overall, Baltimore has given up 16 made field goals in eight games while allowing 25.4 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cam Little connected on a season-high four field goals in Jacksonville's Week 9 win over the Ravens, bringing him up to 14-for-16 through eight games this season. He has attempted 10 more PATs than FGs behind Jacksonville's efficient offense, but Little should enjoy plenty of kicking opportunities in Week 10, as the Titans are surrendering 24.9 points per game while the Jaguars are scoring 28.6 points per game. Tennessee has allowed 17 successful field goals, which is tied for 10th most in the NFL, so Little is a set-and-forget fantasy starter for Week 10.
outlooksByWeek.11: Cam Little has gone 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts in each of Jacksonville's last two games, with that two-game stretch accounting for nearly half of his 18 made field goals this season. The Jaguars are consistently moving the ball into scoring range, and while they have been adept at scoring TDs rather than settling for FGs, the team's offensive prowess coupled with Little's big leg keeps Jacksonville's kicker safely in the set-and-forget starter range. In Week 11, Little will face the Giants on the road. MetLife Stadium is one of the tougher kicking environments in the NFL, and the Giants' opponents have made just nine field goals in nine games, but the surging Little has the potential to make fantasy managers who over-index on the matchup look silly given his high ceiling.
outlooksByWeek.12: Cam Little has come up big for fantasy managers recently with three consecutive 4-for-4 performances on field-goal attempts. He's in great position to keep rolling in a Week 12 home game against the Titans, who have surrendered a whopping 44.7 points per game in their last three. That woeful stretch from Tennessee's defense includes Jacksonville's 40-23 win in Week 10, during which Little converted all four of his PAT tries to go with four field goals. Little's a set-and-forget Week 12 fantasy starter.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian McCaffrey heads into a Week 2 matchup against Miami with perhaps a bit less pressure to carry the 49ers' offense. Whereas McCaffrey led the NFL with 413 touches last season, he logged a modest 15 in last Thursday's Week 1 win over the Rams. Rookie Kaelon Black actually got more carries (14) than McCaffrey (10), though McCaffrey was still productive with 68 rushing yards along with 20 receiving yards on five catches. McCaffrey could feast upon a Dolphins defense that allowed Ashton Jeanty to accumulate 147 total yards and two touchdowns in a season-opening loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian McCaffrey will look to once again show off his dual-threat skill set when the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. McCaffrey is coming off a productive game against the Dolphins,  totaling 66 yards (23 rushing, 43 receiving) and getting into the end zone twice. The veteran RB has been ceding a fair amount of carries to rookie No. 2 RB Kaelon Black so far this season, but McCaffrey's work as a receiver (nine catches for 63 yards through two contests) has remained a key part of his game. Arizona has been middle-of-the-pack against running backs so far, yielding an average of 14.0 fantasy points per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian McCaffrey is coming off his best game of the campaign heading into San Francisco's Week 4 tilt versus the Broncos. McCaffrey compiled season-high marks with 75 rushing yards and 116 total yards in Sunday's win against Arizona while scoring his third TD of 2026. His 15 carries were also his most so far this season, as the 49ers appear to be pulling back on his workload a bit after he led the NFL with 413 touches last year. McCaffrey could find room to run on Denver, as the Broncos have so far given up the second-most rushing yards to RBs (129.7 per game) this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian McCaffrey will look to reach the end zone again for San Francisco in a Week 5 NFC West clash against the Seahawks. McCaffrey has scored at least one touchdown in three straight games and has four rushing TDs on the season. The scoring has helped keep his fantasy value high despite the fact that he's averaging a modest 16.5 touches per game so far after leading the NFL with 24.3 touches per game last season. Seattle has yielded just 3.35 yards per carry and one total rushing touchdown to running backs this season, but they've been more vulnerable through the air, allowing two receiving scores and an 88.5% catch rate to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Christian McCaffrey has had a nose for the end zone this season and will look to score again when the 49ers face the Commanders in Week 6. McCaffrey produced 83 total yards and a TD this past Sunday in a big win over Seattle, giving him at least one score four straight weeks. While his 16.0 touches per game this year are considerably lower than his 24.3 last season, he's been more efficient on the ground with 4.7 yards per carry (he averaged just 3.9 YPC during the regular season in 2025). With that said, Washington has been stingy against RBs through five weeks, yielding just 3.76 YPC and only two total touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Christian McCaffrey and the 49ers are on the road for a meeting against the Falcons in Week 7. He rushed 16 times for 64 yards and two TDs while losing a fumble, adding nine catches on 10 targets for 53 yards during San Francisco's Week 6 victory. McCaffrey set season highs in carries, receptions, receiving yards and targets while notching his seventh rushing TD in six games. He'll once again lead the 49ers backfield for their matchup against an Atlanta defense allowing 23.3 fantasy points per game (21st) to RBs and just surrendered three rushing TDs to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.9: Christian McCaffrey's hamstring issue will be worth keeping an eye on ahead of San Francisco's Week 9 matchup against the Raiders. McCaffrey suffered a mild hamstring strain Week 7 against Atlanta, but a well-timed Week 8 bye provided an opportunity for him to get abundant rest. Should McCaffrey be unable to suit up in Week 9, however, rookie Kealon Black is likely to take on lead RB duties for the 49ers. Whichever player leads the team's backfield has a juicy matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yielded a league-worst 5.31 yards per carry to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Christian McCaffrey will seek to add to his seven-game scoring streak when San Francisco faces Dallas in Week 10. With two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving) this past Sunday against Las Vegas, McCaffrey has gotten into the end zone at least once in each of his past seven games. While he has been logging fewer touches per game this season, McCaffrey continues to be a workhorse for the 49ers and has averaged 4.5 yards per rush, his highest mark since 2023. He could be in for a big game against the Cowboys, who are giving up 22.0 fantasy points per game to running backs, fourth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Christian McCaffrey enters San Francisco's Week 11 matchup against Minnesota on the heels of one of the biggest performances of his career. In this past Sunday's win over Dallas, McCaffrey recorded a career-best 161 receiving yards en route to 223 total yards and three touchdowns. The star RB has logged at least one TD in each of his past eight games and has multiple scores in three of his past four contests, making him an elite week-to-week fantasy asset. With that said, McCaffrey is slated for a tough matchup against the Vikings, who rank eighth in the NFL by allowing 15.3 fantasy points per game to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Christian McCaffrey will look to extend his touchdown streak to 10 games when San Francisco faces Seattle in Week 12. Though McCaffrey finished with a modest 62 total yards in this past Sunday's win over Minnesota, he got into the end zone for the ninth straight game with a six-yard touchdown run. McCaffrey is tied for second in the NFL with 11 rushing TDs this season, and he's added three scores as a receiver. He figures to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that leads the NFL with just 3.16 yards per carry allowed to wideouts on the season.

player.seasonOutlook: McCaffrey is back for his fifth season with the 49ers after a bounce-back 2025 campaign in which he led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points. McCaffrey's rushing efficiency wasn't great (3.86 yards per carry), and he's entering his age-30 season after handling 450 touches (including the playoffs) in 2025. The history of overworked backs suggests we should expect a step back in 2026, but CMC is a unicorn, and the combination of his skill set and hefty usage in Kyle Shanahan's offense suggests he can overcome history. There's obvious risk here, but McCaffrey will be an elite option whenever he's on the field.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride marches into a Week 2 matchup versus Seattle fresh off a strong season-opening performance in Arizona's victory against the Chargers. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers across the board with nine catches, 13 targets and 95 yards in that win, and he scored the team's lone passing touchdown. The All-Pro is essentially matchup-proof as possibly the league's premier tight end, though he'll draw a tough Seahawks defense in Week 2. However, it's worth noting that Seattle gave up the sixth-most receiving yards to tight ends during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey McBride remains one of the most matchup-proof pass catchers in the league heading into the Cardinals' Week 3 tilt versus San Francisco. Though QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards in a loss to Seattle on Sunday, McBride accounted for 41 of those yards and got into the end zone. Through two weeks, McBride leads NFL tight ends with 17 receptions and ranks fourth with 136 receiving yards. The 49ers have been tough on the position so far, though, giving up just seven catches for 52 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey McBride will look to continue a strong start to the campaign when the Cardinals face the Giants in Week 4. McBride posted a 9-75-0 receiving line in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. The All-Pro has now logged at least eight catches and at least 10 targets in every contest so far in 2026, giving him the highest floor of any TE in the NFL. The Giants rank in the bottom 10 leaguewide in catch rate and receiving yards allowed to tight ends, so they don't figure to be a threat to McBride's run of success.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trey McBride enters Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit coming off his quietest performance of the season. While the star tight end logged a healthy 12 targets and seven catches against the Giants in Week 4, he finished with just 31 receiving yards. It's a testament to McBride's excellence that such a stat line represents a downturn by his standards, and he'll have a good chance of bouncing back against the Lions. Detroit has allowed a whopping 19.2 fantasy points per game to tight ends so far this season, by far the most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trey McBride will look to remain productive for Arizona's offense in Week 6 against the Rams. McBride put up another big line against Detroit this past Sunday, catching nine of 10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end leads all NFL players with 42 receptions this season, and only Amon-Ra St. Brown (57) has more targets than McBride's 56. That should mean McBride gets plenty of opportunities against the Rams, but to find success he'll have to overcome a defense that is giving up the fewest fantasy points per game (3.2) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Trey McBride remains Arizona's most dependable receiving weapon, compiling 49 receptions for 361 yards and three touchdowns through six games. His 49 catches lead the Cardinals by a wide margin, and his consistent involvement provides a strong PPR foundation despite the team's struggles to generate explosive plays, as he has had at least seven catches in each of his six appearances to date. McBride also led Arizona's passing attack during its Week 6 victory over the Rams, reinforcing his importance to Jacoby Brissett. He faces a relatively neutral matchup against Denver in Week 7, with the Broncos allowing 8.2 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs in 2026, the 15th-best mark in the league. Given his involvement on offense, however, McBride should remain a reliable TE1 regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.8: Trey McBride has established himself as one of the NFL's top pass catchers ahead of Arizona's Week 8 matchup in Dallas. The star tight end posted season-best marks with 10 catches and 111 yards while scoring his fourth touchdown in Week 7 against Denver. McBride leads the NFL with 59 catches on the campaign, and he's tied for second with 78 targets. The Cowboys rank middle-of-the-pack against tight ends this season, but McBride is as matchup-proof as any player at his position in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Trey McBride doesn't seem likely to slow down despite a quarterback change in Arizona with a Week 9 tilt in Seattle on tap. McBride logged seven receptions for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in an overtime win over Dallas in Week 8, extending his streak of games with seven-plus catches to eight to begin the season. Five of his receptions (including his TD catch) and 52 of his yards came after Gardner Minshew took over at quarterback in the third quarter, so the Cardinals' switch to Minshew as the starter in Week 9 doesn't figure to slow down McBride's production. However, the Seahawks present a tough challenge, as they've given up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (5.4) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Trey McBride could be extremely busy for the Cardinals in Week 10 against the Rams. McBride has already been drawing constant attention in the Arizona passing game, recording at least seven catches and eight targets in all nine of the team's games this year. Now that top wideouts Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are likely done for the season, McBride may be even more heavily targeted. However, he'll be working with rookie QB Carson Beck for the first time due to Gardner Minshew's potentially season-ending elbow injury. McBride will also be going up against a Rams defense that is tied for second in the league in fewest fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends, though he notched a fine 7-53-0 line against them in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.11: Trey McBride is set to work with rookie quarterback Carson Beck for the second time when the Cardinals travel to Kansas City for a Week 11 clash. McBride had his season-opening streak of logging at least seven receptions snapped this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams, when he managed a quiet 5-37-0 receiving line on five targets. Nonetheless, every part of his line (catches, receiving yardage and targets) led the Cardinals in a game during which Beck struggled mightily to move the ball. There could be an opportunity for McBride to post better numbers against Kansas City, who have given up the fifth-most fantasy points per game (9.8) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Trey McBride stands as perhaps the Cardinals' last healthy reliable producer ahead of a battle against the Commanders in Week 12. With WR Michael Wilson (neck) done for the season and RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) still on IR, McBride has been counted on to carry the offense. The star tight end has mostly held up, including in a loss to Kansas City this past Sunday when he posted a 9-54-0 line on a team-high 14 targets. It remains to be seen if McBride will be catching passes from rookie Carson Beck (back) or veteran journeyman Josh Johnson this weekend, but either way he'll likely be the team's offensive focus in a matchup versus a Washington defense that has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game (13.5) to tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.

outlooksByWeek.2: Garrett Wilson should maintain steady volume for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. He garnered seven targets in a run-heavy situation to open the year, catching six for 79 yards. Green Bay's secondary is suspect and just allowed Vikings' top receiver Justin Jefferson to score twice, despite Carson Wentz being under center. The Jets will likely need to throw more in Week 2, potentially pushing Wilson into double-digit targets and setting him up for elevated numbers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Garrett Wilson's clear lead role in the Jets' passing game could pay dividends against a porous Lions secondary in Week 3. Wilson has registered seven targets in each of the Jets' first two outings, giving him ample opportunity to exploit a defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts through two weeks. The Lions' defense is vulnerable to all positions, but Wilson's spot as the top target is unchallenged.
outlooksByWeek.4: Garrett Wilson likely remains a heavily targeted option for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears. Wilson is coming off a terrific 10-catch, 107-yard Week 3 where he scored his first touchdown of the season and faces minimal competition for volume in the Jets' passing game. Chicago's secondary has rallied over the last two weeks, not allowing more than 153 yards through the air, but the pieces at corner leave plenty to be desired, setting Wilson up to take advantage of continued high looks in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Garrett Wilson seeks a rebound in Week 5 when the Jets face the Browns. After collecting seven or more targets in each of his first three games, Wilson bottomed out with only four looks in Week 4, finishing with a season-low 27 yards. Cleveland's secondary has allowed at least 291 passing yards in each of the last two weeks, and three opposing wideouts have topped 70 yards. With his usual volume, Wilson appears to be in a favorable Week 5 spot.
outlooksByWeek.6: Garrett Wilson commands a heavy volume of targets in the Jets' passing game heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Wilson collected 11 looks in Week 5, topping 100 yards for the second time this season, and has now garnered at least seven targets in four of five outings. New England's secondary is banged up, and the availability of star CB Christian Gonzalez remains uncertain. While the Jets don't want to pass heavily, when they do, targets should be funneled toward Wilson. He has a great chance to exploit a defense that has allowed two 100-yard receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Garrett Wilson plays a steady role in the Jets' middling passing game and enters a Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Wilson managed just 44 yards in Week 6, his second-lowest output of the year, but still enters Week 7 with seven or more targets in four of his first six games. Miami has been stingy against wideouts, allowing just two touchdown catches and only two receivers to record more than 55 yards, but Wilson's volume should allow him to flirt with the upper end of that production.
outlooksByWeek.8: Garrett Wilson's high-volume role has faded over the last two weeks as the Jets prepare to host the Raiders in Week 8. After recording 57 or more yards in four of his first five games, Wilson has just 70 total yards over the last two weeks, coinciding with Omar Cooper's emergence. While the Raiders are allowing 8.9 yards per target to opposing wideouts, smaller, shifty receivers have given them fits (DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Xavier Worthy), suggesting Wilson carries ample volatility into Week 8.
outlooksByWeek.9: Garrett Wilson's usage has been inconsistent ahead of the Jets' difficult Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs. After showing frustration following a three-target Week 7, Wilson was peppered with 12 looks in Week 8-the third time he's amassed double-digit targets. However, he's drawn only 27 total looks in the Jets' other five games. Kansas City has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers but was without corners Mansoor Delane and L'Jarius Sneed in Week 8. Week 9 absences would help Wilson's potential.
outlooksByWeek.10: Garrett Wilson needs to clear the concussion protocol to help the Jets against the Bills in Week 10. Wilson has seen sporadic usage when healthy, amassing double-digit targets three times while averaging 5.8 looks in five additional outings. Assuming he receives a clean bill of health, he'll face a secondary that's allowing the eighth-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts. With the Jets likely falling into an early hole, a pass-heavy game flow is probable, with Wilson being an active participant.
outlooksByWeek.11: Garrett Wilson continues to dominate targets in the Jets' passing game ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. He garnered a season-high 14 targets in Week 10, his fourth outing with double-digit looks, while topping 100 yards for the third time. Wilson has only three touchdowns on the year and faces a bit of quarterback uncertainty with Geno Smith dealing with an ankle injury, but the Chargers have allowed 11 receivers to score in nine games and have surrendered 340-plus passing yards in consecutive weeks. With steady volume, Wilson profiles as a safe lineup cog in Week 11.
outlooksByWeek.12: Garrett Wilson brings inconsistent volume into the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. Wilson drew only five targets in Week 11, with the Jets attempting only 21 passes, and quarterback Geno Smith has not completed 20 passes for three straight outings. Wilson has four games with double-digit targets and four games with 44 receiving yards or fewer through 10 games. With the Jets likely to remain run-first, Wilson's workload could be limited facing a secondary that's allowing a whopping 9.2 yards per target but the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game to receivers due to limited volume.

player.seasonOutlook: Wilson is eyeing a bounce-back following an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to seven games. It was the first time Wilson had missed time, having appeared in all 51 games during his first three seasons. The 2022 first-round pick ranked no lower than sixth among receivers in targets in each of those years, but he failed to produce a fantasy campaign better than 20th (PPG) due to New York's quarterback woes. Wilson was off to a hot start last season (four TDs, 14.2 fantasy PPG) thanks to a massive 33% target share (second highest). New York's signal-caller problems still aren't completely solved, but veteran Geno Smith should provide an upgrade over last year's Justin Fields/Tyrod Taylor duo. Wilson, 26, is one of the best raw talents at the position and should be valued as a good WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to take on the Buccaneers and their 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.8) to RBs in Week 2. The second-year back rushed 12 times for 33 yards and caught both targets for 17 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 Week 1 loss. Running lanes and beneficial game flow are two things to be concerned with for Judkins, as the Browns again appear to be one of the worst offenses in the league. If the QB play improves even slightly, he could see an uptick in opportunities in both the running and passing games, but he should be started with caution until that situation improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Steelers to town for an AFC North clash on Thursday night in Week 4. He rushed 18 times for 70 yards and caught both targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset win over the Panthers in Week 3. Judkins surpassed 35 yards on the ground for the first time this season, and there's a chance he could build upon that against their division rivals. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (22.1) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Jets in Week 5, looking for their fourth consecutive win. He had his best performance of 2026 in Week 4, rushing 17 times for 53 yards and his first TD of the season while catching six of seven targets for 43 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory. No other back recorded more than two carries, and Judkins led the team in receptions and tied for third in targets. Up next is a Jets defense that allows 28.3 fantasy points per game to RBs, which ranks 30th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the division rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He tallied 14 carries for 44 yards and caught three of four targets for six yards during Cleveland's Week 5 loss. Judkins played just 52.9% of snaps, likely due to a right ankle injury suffered in-game, and he was reportedly spotted wearing a walking boot afterward. Head coach Todd Monken called it a "tweak" on Monday and considers his starting running back day-to-day. Judkins' practice participation this week will be worth monitoring, as he'll be facing a Baltimore defense that allows 18.8 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.
outlooksByWeek.7: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns visit the Titans for an interconference clash in Week 7. He was inactive for Cleveland's 13-10 victory in Week 6 due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 5. Jaleel McLaughlin (9), Audric Estime (9), and Michael Burton (1) handled the backfield responsibilities, with Estime notching his first TD as a Brown. Judkins is averaging 3.0 yards per carry on 73 attempts, and if he's active for Week 7, he'll face a Tennessee defense allowing 20.3 fantasy points per game (13th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He rushed 17 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns and caught his only target for eight yards during Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Judkins returned from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury and posted his best performance of the year, setting season highs in rush yards and yards from scrimmage (104). He'll aim to stay hot against a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to face the Saints in Week 9. He rushed 11 times for 25 yards and caught both of his targets for 24 yards during Cleveland's 27-6 Week 8 loss. Judkins handled 11 of 12 carries out of the backfield but took a backseat to Dylan Sampson in the passing game. Judkins will aim to bounce back against a New Orleans defense that ranks last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.8) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Quinshon Judkins and the Browns return home for the first time in three weeks to host the Texans. He rushed 15 times for 43 yards and caught his only target for two yards during Cleveland's overtime loss in Week 9. Judkins and the entire Browns offense struggled to make much happen on the ground, registering 95 yards on 34 carries for a meager 2.8 yards per attempt. Judkins has been underwhelming in 2026, racking up 385 yards on 116 carries (3.3 YPC) with three TDs and a 22-136-0 receiving line on 25 targets. He'll try to turn things around versus a Houston defense allowing 22.4 fantasy points per game (20th) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Raiders to town on Sunday Night Football. He had 10 carries for 38 yards and a touchdown and caught three of five targets for 33 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 win. Judkins has struggled to find running room in 2026, rushing 126 times for 423 yards (3.4 YPC) and four scores, but there's hope that could change in Week 12. Las Vegas allows 26.9 fantasy points per game (28th) to RBs and just gave up 133 yards and three TDs on the ground in their latest outing.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colston Loveland will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Loveland disappointed in Week 1 against the Panthers, failing to bring in either of his two targets, even though it was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The second-year tight end's output was hopefully a fluke, especially as he was still on the field for 86 percent of Chicago's offensive snaps. Loveland will also face a Minnesota defense that allowed five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colston Loveland will look to turn things around as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Loveland disappointed again in Week 2, catching just one of three targets for three yards against the Vikings. The second-year tight end now has just one catch on the year, which is nowhere near the breakout season managers were projecting. He'll likely be thrown to by Tyson Bagent against Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).
outlooksByWeek.4: Colston Loveland will look to improve his role even more as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Loveland finally saw more than a chalked role against the Eagles in Week 3, reeling in all four of his targets for 31 yards. This output is far from what was expected of the second-year tight end heading into the season, but it's still optimistic for the future. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 8.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Colston Loveland will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Loveland commanded nine targets in Week 4 against the Jets, which allowed him to finish with six catches for 57 yards. The second-year tight end has now increased his yardage from zero to three to 31 to 57 in the first four games of the year. He'll aim to find the end zone for the first time of the campaign against a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Colston Loveland will look to do more as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Loveland wasn't able to build on a solid six catches for 57 yards in Week 4, reeling in just two of five targets for 19 yards versus the Packers in Week 5. The second-year pass catcher has been thrown to by three quarterbacks of varying skill so far this year, which could add to the struggles of his output. He'll take on an Atalnta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Colston Loveland will look to build off a season-best outing as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 6. Loveland caught six of seven targets for 65 yards and a touchdown in Caleb Williams' return to the field. The second-year tight has now caught six passes in two of his last three games, and he sits in a favorable spot after a rough start to the year. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to TEs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Colston Loveland will aim to continue producing as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Loveland stayed hot in a Week 7 win over New England, finishing with season highs in catches (7), targets (12), yards (69) and tacking on a touchdown. The second-year tight end has had a promising turnaround to the season, with 50 or more yards in three of his last four games and back-to-back outings with a score. He'll face a Seattle defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Colston Loveland will look to remain a high-volume option as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Loveland was solid again in a Week 8 win over the Bears, bringing in seven of nine targets for 65 yards but losing a fumble. The second-year tight end has now brought in six or more receptions in four of his last five games, and he's found the end zone in two of his last three. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 22nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Colston Loveland will remain a top option in Chicago's passing game against the Saints in Week 11. Loveland has seen success lately after a shaky start to the season, surpassing 50 yards in his last four games and finding the end zone twice in that stretch. The second-year tight end has now posted a 37-363-2 receiving line off 57 targets in the first nine outings of the season. He'll face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Colston Loveland will seek to keep it rolling in Week 12 as the Bears play the Lions. Loveland found the end zone again in Week 11 against the Saints, pairing his touchdown with three catches for 29 yards. The second-year tight end has now put together a 27-282-3 receiving line over the last five games after a shaky start to the season. Detroit has allowed the most fantasy points per game to the TE position.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy PPG during his first 14 NFL games, Loveland leaped to 12.0 targets (10-plus in each) and 20.0 fantasy PPG during his final four games of 2025 (including the playoffs). For perspective, there have been only 12 instances of a tight end seeing at least 10 targets in four consecutive regular-season games in NFL history (and only one was a rookie). Loveland's overall efficiency was terrific, as he ranked eighth or better among tight ends in YPR, YPT and YPRR. With DJ Moore gone, the 2025 first-round pick enters his age-22 season all but locked into a massive workload alongside Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Loveland's ceiling is lofty, and midrange fantasy TE1 should be his floor.

outlooksByWeek.2: Courtland Sutton was held in check along with the rest of the Broncos' offense in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching two of five targets for just 11 yards. Quarterback Bo Nix couldn't connect with either of his top two wideouts, as Jaylen Waddle also had a poor showing in his Denver debut, and new offensive coordinator Davis Webb may need to go back to the drawing board quickly to get his passing game going. Sutton should face a softer matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Courtland Sutton has had a slow start to the season as the focus of the Broncos' passing game has shifted to Jaylen Waddle. Through two games, Sutton has posted only nine targets, catching five for a meager 36 yards. He still has plenty of existing chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo could rekindle it once defenses begin shifting more attention to Waddle, but Sutton figures to be hard-pressed to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2026 for a third straight season. He'll take on a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, though three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Courtland Sutton continues to fade into a support role in the Broncos' passing game following the acquisition of Jaylen Waddle. His seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams were a season-high, and through three games, he's managed just an 8-82-0 line on 16 total looks from Bo Nix. Sutton should see more volume once new play-caller Davis Webb settles in, but he'll have an uphill battle to produce his fourth career 1,000-yard season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Courtland Sutton was nearly invisible in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, catching only one of six targets for a measly four yards. The veteran wideout remains firmly behind Jaylen Waddle on the depth chart, but the entire Denver offense is struggling under first-time play caller Davis Webb, and Sutton has produced a weak 9-86-0 line on 22 targets through four games. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming play-calling duties is an open question. Sutton will try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Courtland Sutton ended his touchdown drought in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, catching two of three targets for 18 yards and his first score of the season. The team's entire offense has been sluggish to begin the year, and having Sean Payton take over play-calling duties didn't pay immediate dividends, but it should bode well for Sutton in the long run. He'll face another tough challenge in Week 6 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Courtland Sutton's struggles continued in the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The veteran wideout has yet to catch more than three passes in a game this season or reach 50 receiving yards, leaving him with a paltry 13-123-1 line on 28 targets through six games. With quarterback Bo Nix unable to build any momentum, Sutton and the entire passing game offer little upside. He could at least get into the end zone again in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to WRs this season, 31st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Courtland Sutton had another quiet day in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, managing to catch three of five targets for 45 yards. The veteran wideout has been held under 50 receiving yards and three catches or fewer in all seven games so far this season, and he's scored just one TD after hauling in 25 over the prior three years. Sutton isn't likely to break out in Week 8 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Courtland Sutton set new season highs in catches and receiving yards during the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, but he still came away with just a 4-53-0 line on four targets. The struggles of quarterback Bo Nix, as well as the offseason addition of Jaylen Waddle, have reduced Sutton's target volume considerably from 2025, and he's on pace for only 79 targets this season after topping 120 in each of the prior two years. He'll try to make do with new role in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator, and which is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Courtland Sutton caught a season-high five passes in the Broncos' last game before their Week 10 bye, turning one of the receptions into his second touchdown of the season. The veteran wide receiver's target volume increased after Jaylen Waddle left the contest early due to a concussion. He has yet to reach 50 receiving yards or see double-digit targets in any game this year as the No. 2 option in a sluggish passing game. Sutton will attempt to contribute in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Courtland Sutton disappeared from the game plan in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders, failing to catch either of his two targets. It's the first time since Week 7 of the 2024 season he hasn't caught a pass, but with the offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, there hasn't been much need for Bo Nix to air it out. Sutton is on pace to fall short of 500 receiving yards over a full season for the first time in his career, and fail to reach 50 catches for the first time since he was a rookie in 2018. He'll be a risky play in Week 12 against a Steelers secondary that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Nix was held in check by the Kansas City defense in the Broncos' season opener, completing 17 of 28 passes for just 131 yards and a touchdown. He also threw an interception and committed three fumbles, losing one of them, while getting sacked four times. Nix also wasn't able to take advantage of his newest asset, as Jaylen Waddle logged only three targets and caught one of them for two yards. It was a hugely disappointing effort from Nix and the reigning AFC West champions, but they'll look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 18th last season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Nix rebounded from a sluggish opener to lead the Broncos to a comeback win over the Jaguars in Week 2. The third-year QB has a meager 2:2 TD:INT through two games and has yet to add any production on the ground, but his 288 passing yards In Week 2 were more than double the Week 1 total, and his completion rate jumped from 60.7% to 71.0%. Nix also began establishing some chemistry with new top wideout Jaylen Waddle, who erupted for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets. Nix will face a Rams defense in Week 3 that has held opposition QBs under a 60% completion rate to begin the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bo Nix engineered an impressive second-half comeback in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, producing two passing TDs and one rushing score despite completing just 50.0% of his passes. The third-year quarterback hasn't had a statistically impressive start to the season, posting a 4:3 TD:INT ratio and passing for barely over 200 yards a game, but Nix has led his team to a 2-1 record. He'll take on a 49ers defense in Week 4 that's been stingy to begin the year, ranking eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bo Nix wasn't able to pull off another comeback win for the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers. The third-year QB failed to complete 60% of his passes for a second straight game, and through four weeks, he's produced just six touchdowns (five passing, one rushing) while committing four turnovers. Denver's lack of a consistent running game isn't helping the offense find a rhythm, but Nix shoulders plenty of responsibility for the team's 2-2 start to the season. He'll try to bounce back in a Week 5 road game against a Chargers defense that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bo Nix didn't show any improvement in Week 5 as the Broncos switched back to Sean Payton as their play-caller, throwing for a season-low 123 yards and producing just one touchdown in a win over the Chargers. The third-year QB has a meager 6:3 TD:INT through five games and is completing fewer than 60.0% of his passes, averaging fewer than 200 passing yards per game. There's still reason to believe Nix's numbers will improve once Payton gets back in a rhythm, but the Denver offense's ceiling seems limited even if it's operating at peak efficiency. Nix isn't likely to break out in Week 6 against a Seahawks defense that ranks sixth this season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bo Nix continues to struggle, failing to throw a touchdown in Week 6 for the first time this season while compiling a season-low 107 passing yards. The third-year quarterback has produced fewer than 6.0 yards per attempt in four straight games, and the Broncos' switch back to Sean Payton as the play-caller hasn't yet sparked the offense. Nix has just seven total touchdowns (six passing and one rushing) against five turnovers through seven games, but he'll get a chance to build some momentum in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bo Nix contributed most with his legs in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, throwing one TD and running for another. The second score came in the second quarter on a 62-yard scamper, the longest rushing touchdown by a QB in an NFL regular-season game since 2022. Nix's 73 rushing yards on the day nearly doubled his total from the first six weeks combined. Despite that performance, Nix is still on pace for a career-worst campaign, and things won't get easier for him in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bo Nix put together another fourth-quarter comeback in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City. While the third-year QB's own numbers are nothing special this season, he's led his team to a 6-2 record and first place in the AFC West. Week 8 was only the second time in eight games he's thrown for multiple touchdowns, and his 59.6% completion rate and 6.0 yards per attempt are both career lows. Nix could be poised for his best game of the season in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and is tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Bo Nix comes out of the Broncos' bye having built up a bit of momentum, producing multiple touchdowns in three straight games prior to the break while turning the ball over only once during that stretch. The third-year quarterback didn't get any reinforcements at the trade deadline, but the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman in the backfield gives Denver a legitimate running option to help balance the offense, and second-year wideout Pat Bryant returned from IR right before the bye. In Week 11, Nix will take aim at a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Bo Nix didn't need to do much in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders, as rookie running back Jonah Coleman carried the offense. Nix has thrown for 240-plus yards just once all season, and he's produced more than two TDs only once, as the Denver offense has mostly been stuck in neutral. Coleman's emergence could provide Nix with the security he needs to try to throw downfield more often. The third-year quarterback will take on a Steelers defense in Week 12 that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nix enters his third NFL season after finishing exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points during each of his first two campaigns. Nix's passing efficiency has a ways to go (career 6.5 yards per attempt), but his dual-threat ability has kept him in the weekly QB1 mix. Nix has finished both seasons no lower than 11th in pass attempts, completions, passing TDs, carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs. Last season, he provided a solid floor (11 games with 15-plus fantasy points), but his ceiling was low (four top-10 weeks). In 2026, he'll have a new playcaller in Davis Webb and an upgraded group of pass catchers with Jaylen Waddle added to the mix. The 26-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian Watson will seek to build off a monster outing as the Packers travel to take on the Jets in Week 2. Watson ended a Week 1 loss to the Vikings with a dominant stat line, catching six of his eight targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout could be a breakout star this season, especially if Green Bay continues to deploy a pass-heavy offense. The Jets secondary, who gave up a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1, looks weaker than Minnesota's as well.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian Watson remains the top option in Green Bay's offense as they take on the Falcons in Week 3. Watson finished with a quieter four catches for 41 yards and a touchdown against the Jets in Week 2, but he did garner an impressive 11 targets. The fifth-year wideout has now scored three touchdowns on a team-high 19 targets across two games. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian Watson will look to keep his touchdown streak rolling as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 4. Watson finished Week 3 against the Falcons with seven catches for 96 yards and a touchdown, putting him at a 17-284-4 receiving line on the year. The fifth-year wideout remains quarterback Jordan Love's top option at this point in the year, with him and Matthew Golden making for a dangerous duo so far. Watson will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian Watson will remain a top option in Green Bay's passing game against the Bears in Week 5. Watson finished Week 4 at Tampa Bay with a quiet three catches for 47 yards, but Jordan Love threw for just 197 yards. The go-to wideout has now posted a 20-331-4 receiving line on 32 targets so far this campaign, and he's on pace for his first 1,000-yard season if he can stay healthy. Watson could have a tough task versus a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Christian Watson will look to continue his dominance as the Packers take on the Cowboys in Week 6. Watson recorded a stellar performance in Week 5 against the Bears, bringing in six of eight targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout has cemented himself as Jordan Love's top option in the passing game, with a 26-474-6 receiving line through five games. Watson will face a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Christian Watson will look to get back in the end zone as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Watson finished Week 6 against the Cowboys tying a season-low of three catches, but he was still able to convert them into 64 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now amassed 29 catches for 538 yards and six touchdowns this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Christian Watson will aim to return to dominance as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Watson brought in five of eight targets for a team-leading 57 yards in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, which was his lowest yardage total since Week 4. The wideout still has a 34-595-6 receiving line through the first seven games of the season, and he's not far off from outpacing his stat totals from the 2024 and 2025 season. Carolina has ranked a stern fifth in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.9: Christian Watson will look to heal from a broken rib ahead of Green Bay's Week 9 matchup at New England. Watson injured himself in the second quarter of Week 8 against the Panthers, but he returned to the game in the third quarter after a brief trip to the hospital. Even with these setbacks, the starting wideout finished the game with an impressive stat line, hauling in eight of 10 targets for 113 yards. He's now sitting at a receiving line of 42-708-6, which is career-high in both receptions and yards. He'll face a Patriots defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to WRs in the last three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Christian Watson will look to build off a career day as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Watson put together a prolific performance in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, bringing in seven of eight targets for 171 yards and a touchdown. The wideout now holds a career-high receiving line of 49-879-7 on 74 targets. He'll face a Minnesota secondary that he tore up with 6 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns against in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.12: Christian Watson will look to make a bang out of the bye week as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Watson struggled against a tough Minnesota defense in Week 10, catching three of five targets for a season-low 37 yards. The premier wideout has still impressed across the first 10 games of his fifth campaign, posting a 52-916-7 receiving line on 79 targets. His next challenge will be a Los Angeles defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson has had quite the boom/bust NFL career and that was on full display in 2025. After missing the first seven games due to injury, Watson returned and scored 18-plus fantasy points four times, but averaged 7.7 in his other six outings. The oft-injured 2022 second-round pick has still yet to play a full regular season, but has weirdly finished with between 611 and 620 receiving yards in three of his four campaigns. Though Watson has yet to deliver a top-40 fantasy season, he's been extremely efficient in his vertical role, ranking exactly second in average depth of target, YPR and YPT each of the last two seasons. Durability is an obvious concern, but the 27-year-old could very well lead Green Bay in targets following Romeo Doubs' departure. Watson should be valued as a volatile flex option with added value in non-PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
outlooksByWeek.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tony Pollard is averaging 61 scrimmage yards per game and scored his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Ravens, though that wasn't enough to keep the Titans from dropping to 0-4. In Week 5, Tennessee hosts the AFC South rival Texans, who are also 0-4. The Titans should manage to stay within striking distance and give Pollard his full workload on the ground, though Houston has held RBs to just 91 scrimmage yards per game. Pollard is a high-floor, low-ceiling flex play as usual for Week 5 given his role as the lead back in a struggling Titans offense that's averaging the fewest yards and second-fewest points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tony Pollard remains a viable flex option in Week 6 against the Colts thanks to his high touch floor as the starting RB in a putrid Titans offense. Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season but has been limited to one TD on a Titans offense that has found the end zone just six times through five games. Indianapolis is giving up 100 rushing yards per game to RBs as well as a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to the position, so Pollard has a higher ceiling than usual in this Week 6 matchup to go with his steady floor.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tony Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in each of the Titans' last five games. He's locked into a high touch floor in any game the 1-5 Titans can keep within striking distance, and Tennessee is unlikely to fall too far behind in Week 7 at home against the Browns, who are scoring just 17.7 points per game, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL. Cleveland has started 4-2 thanks to a stout defense that's allowing 20.3 points per game and has allowed just one TD to a running back all season, but Pollard's hefty usage keeps him locked in as a viable flex play for Week 7, even though he looks unlikely to add to his season total of one TD in a Titans offense that's tied for the worst in the league at 14.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tony Pollard is coming off his best game of the season, as he racked up 129 rushing yards and three TDs against the Browns in Tennessee's Week 7 loss. The veteran RB is the most consistent offensive player on the Titans, having racked up at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in six consecutive games. His solid touch floor makes Pollard a passable fantasy RB2 for Week 8, but don't expect a repeat of his Week 7 outburst against a Bengals defense that has limited RBs to three total TDs in six games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tony Pollard delivered consecutive elite performances prior to Tennessee's Week 9 bye, racking up 292 scrimmage yards and five TDs across losses to the Browns and Bengals. Prior to that two-game stretch, he had just one TD through seven games and no 100-yard performances. If he isn't traded prior to Tuesday's deadline, Pollard would maintain fantasy RB2 upside for Week 10 despite a difficult matchup against a Jaguars defense that's holding RBs to 68 yards per game. Even before his recent uptick in production, Pollard had a solid floor as the clear lead back for Tennessee.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tony Pollard has racked up 391 scrimmage yards and six touchdowns over Tennessee's last three games, putting him in the fantasy RB1 conversation for a Week 11 trip to Dallas. After a pair of dominant rushing performances, Pollard struggled to find running room against Jacksonville's elite front in Week 10 but racked up 66 receiving yards and a TD on a career-high eight catches. The former Cowboys RB is locked into a workhorse role for the Titans, and Pollard's old team has given up the most fantasy production in the league to RBs, allowing 155 scrimmage yards per game, as well as a league-high 16 total TDs to the position through 10 games.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tony Pollard rushed for 110 yards in the Titans' Week 11 loss to Dallas. His touchdown streak was halted at three games and six TDs, but he's up to 501 scrimmage yards over the past four games. Tennessee's entire offense has picked up the pace over that span, with QB Cam Ward stringing together his best three games of the season. Pollard faces a daunting Week 12 matchup against Jacksonville's elite run defense, but he navigated this matchup effectively in Week 10, setting season highs across the board with eight catches for 66 yards and a TD on nine targets to complement his modest 33 rushing yards on nine carries. You may as well keep rolling with the surging Pollard, though the tough opponent drops him to the low-end fantasy RB2 range for Week 12. With Tyjae Spears (knee) on IR, Pollard faces virtually zero competition for carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will look to bounce back from a quiet season-opening performance when Seattle visits Arizona in Week 2. Shaheed caught just one of three targets for four yards against New England in Week 1. Drew Lock played most of that game behind center for the Seahawks after Sam Darnold (glute) made an early injury exit, and Lock figures to again lead the offense against Arizona. The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 3 game against Washington on the heels of a quiet but versatile start to the season. Shaheed logged a modest three catches for 35 yards against Arizona in a Week 2 win, though he promisingly ranked second on the Seahawks with six targets, added a four-yard rush and combined for 76 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba appears set to dominate Seattle's targets for a second straight campaign, so both Shaheed and Cooper Kupp may have to settle for complementary roles on offense. Nonetheless, Seattle's WR corps as a whole could thrive in Week 3 against a Washington defense that has yielded a 73.0 percent catch rate to the position, tied for fifth-highest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashid Shaheed has yet to make a big impact in fantasy this season with Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers coming up. Though Shaheed has been valuable as a return man for the Seahawks, he's averaging just two catches for 17.7 yards through three weeks. Shaheed also fell below a 50% offensive snap share in Week 3 against Washington, as Cooper Kupp served as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Shaheed may need a big play or two to break out against the Chargers, who have allowed nine receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for 13th-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rashid Shaheed should continue to operate in a versatile role for Seattle in a big Week 5 battle against San Francisco. Though Shaheed had just one catch for 20 yards versus the Chargers in Week 4, he added two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown while also returning kickoffs and punts. The 49ers have a similarly versatile player in Deebo Samuel, and the pair of Swiss-army-knife wideouts could be keys in what figures to be a battle of tough defenses. San Francisco has allowed just 17.0 fantasy points per game to WRs this season, sixth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashid Shaheed has been a relatively quiet contributor to Seattle's passing game heading into a Week 6 tilt in Denver. Shaheed has caught three or fewer passes in all of the Seahawks' games so far this season and has yet to record a receiving touchdown, though he does have rushing score on his ledger. The speedy wideout has a big role as an electric kick returner, but Shaheed may struggle to produce as a pass catcher as long as Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to eat up targets. The Broncos are giving up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (16.3) to wideouts this season, but they could be without both starting cornerbacks -- Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) -- in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashid Shaheed and the Seahawks look to snap a two-game losing streak in Week 7 when the Chiefs pay a visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught five of eight targets for 66 yards while rushing once for two yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6. Shaheed also compiled 77 yards on three kickoff returns and another 39 yards on three punt returns, but he fumbled twice while only losing one. He finished second on the Seahawks in yardage, tied with Cooper Kupp for second in receptions, and was third in targets. Shaheed will look to build on that performance versus Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rashid Shaheed isn't certain to suit up for Seattle in Week 8 against the Bears. Shaheed injured his knee in Week 7 versus Kansas City, and though initial reports on the injury were promising, it's not clear if he'll need to miss time. The versatile wideout has been pretty quiet as a receiver throughout the campaign, surpassing three receptions just once through seven weeks. That makes him relatively dependent on big plays, and Chicago has given up nine receptions of 40-plus yards this season, most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rashid Shaheed will look to return from a knee injury in time to suit up for Seattle's Week 9 battle against Arizona. Shaheed missed the Week 8 loss to Chicago due to the injury, and it's unclear how close he is to returning to action. Should he be able to return to face the Cardinals, he'll have a good opportunity for success against a suspect Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals have given up 25 receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the league.
