outlooksByWeek.10: Rashid Shaheed (knee) has missed Seattle's past two games and isn't certain to return in Week 10 against the Raiders. Shaheed hasn't practiced since getting hurt in Week 7, and he'll likely need to return to at least a few limited sessions before being ready to play in games again. Should Shaheed sit out another contest, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton will likely continue to be the Seahawks' top wideouts behind superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If Shaheed can suit up, though, he'll face a Raiders defense that has allowed 27 passing plays of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 12 matchup against San Francisco looking for his first big game of the campaign. Shaheed returned from a two-game absence to suit up against the Raiders in Week 10 but managed just one catch for eight yards on two targets. The speedy wideout doesn't yet have a receiving touchdown this season, and he's topped out at five catches and 66 yards, though he's added value with occasional carries and especially with his work as a punt and kickoff returner. Shaheed may be dependent on big plays to put up useful fantasy production, and the 49ers have given up just 27 receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for ninth-fewest in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Butker was perfect in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, connecting on all four of his extra points and converting his only field-goal attempt from 28 yards. The offense looked more potent with a healthy Patrick Mahomes under center, Kenneth Walker as the new bell-cow back, and a returning Eric Bieniemy as offensive coordinator, and Butker should see his opportunities rise if that trend holds. He could be busy in Week 2 against a Colts team that just got routed by the Ravens and was tied for 20th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field-goal attempt in the second quarter of Week 2, but he made up for it by converting the rest of his opportunities, including a 40-yard FG that gave Kansas City the overtime win over the Colts. The veteran kicker has been busy in the early going with six FG attempts and seven PATs, and a resurgent offense led by a healthy Patrick Mahomes and new bell-cow back Kenneth Walker should continue to supply Butker with volume. He'll face a Dolphins team in Week 3 that's giving up 31.0 points a game in the early going.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harrison Butker missed a field goal for a second straight game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. A resurgent offense under a healthy Patrick Mahomes has given the veteran kicker a solid floor in terms of PATs, and he's a perfect 10-for-10 to begin the year with at least three in each contest. Butker's two FG misses have also been from 50-plus yards, and he's a perfect 8-for-8 from shorter distances. He may not be able to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Raiders team that's allowed 18.0 points a game, seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harrison Butker has been more floor than ceiling to begin the season. The Kansas City kicker has kicked at least three extra points in all four games, but he's logged more than one field goal only once, going 7-for-9 over that span with both his misses coming from 50-plus yards. With Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker having the offense operating at a very high level, Butker's mix of opportunities isn't likely to change much. He could be busy in Week 6 against a Chargers team allowing 25.8 points per game, tied for 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Harrison Butker missed two kicks in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, but he still came away with one of his more productive games of the season, connecting on three of four field goals and one of two extra points. It was the first time in 2026 that the veteran kicker had failed to convert multiple extra points, but his overall volume has been inconsistent, and through five contests he's gone 10-for-13 on FGs and 14-for-15 on PATs. Butker may not be able to afford to squander any chances in Week 7 against a Seahawks team allowing 20.3 points per game, tied for seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Harrison Butker went just 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, the first time he's missed multiple attempts in a single game since 2018. The veteran kicker has missed five of 16 FG attempts overall this season, including one from inside 50 yards, and he may need to turn things around quickly to prevent KC from beginning a search for his replacement. Butker will try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos team that's allowing 20.1 points a game, seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Harrison Butker's job security continues to shrink. The veteran kicker missed a 54-yard field goal in the fourth quarter of a Week 8 loss to the Broncos, forcing Kansas City to go for a touchdown on its next possession to try and overcome a four-point deficit, rather than give Butker a chance to play hero. He's missed at least one FG in three straight games, and his 66.7% success rate (12-for-18) through seven games is over 20 points lower than his 2025 performance. Head coach Andy Reid hasn't yet made a move to replace Butker, but the team did sign Justin Tucker to its practice squad last week. If Butker gets a chance to turn things around in Week 9, he'll be facing a Jets team allowing 23.5 points per game, 16th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Harrison Butker missed another field goal in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, but he converted all five of his extra points. The veteran kicker has an awful 63.2% success rate on field goal attempts through eight games, going just 12-for-19 including a weak 2-for-8 showing from 50-plus yards, but so far Andy Reid has stuck with him. Butker will try to regain some confidence indoors in a Week 10 road trip to Atlanta against a Falcons team that's given up 24.8 points per game this season, tied for 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Harrison Butker hasn't converted a field goal attempt in two straight games and hasn't kicked more than one in four straight, going a weak 2-for-6 on attempts during that stretch. The Kansas City offense has been providing him with more PATs, however, and he's gone 13-for-13 on extra points over the last three contests. Butker's struggles have left him with little job security, but for now he still holds the job. He could be busier in Week 11 against a Cardinals team allowing 28.9 points per game, tied for 31st in the league with the Raiders.
outlooksByWeek.12: Harrison Butker appears to be taking the threat to his job security seriously. The veteran kicker has been perfect over the last two weeks, converting both his field goal attempts and all nine of his PATs. He had missed seven FGs in 10 games, although six of those shanks have come from 50-plus yards out. With the Kansas City offense ramping up its efficiency, Butker's volume is likely to skew more toward extra points, giving him a safer floor at the expense of his ceiling. He'll look to stay locked in during a Week 12 clash with a Bills team that ranks ninth in points per game allowed.

outlooksByWeek.2: Geno Smith may be called upon more often in Week 2 when the Jets face the Packers. He wasn't asked to do much last week as the club played with a rare lead for the majority of the game, relying on the run-something unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Green Bay's secondary is vulnerable, allowing three touchdowns to Carson Wentz to start the year. With more volume, Smith can ascend to the second tier of quarterbacks in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Geno Smith will look to be the next quarterback to take advantage of the Lions' secondary when the Jets head to Detroit in Week 3. Smith hasn't topped 250 yards through two games and has just one touchdown pass, but he is in a very favorable spot in Week 3, with Detroit having allowed three touchdown passes in each outing thus far. Smith threw 41 times in Week 2, and so long as the Lions are scoring, Smith will likely have high volume again, putting him in a position to have his best showing of the year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Geno Smith is facing an uphill battle if he hopes to match his Week 3 success when the Jets face the Bears in Week 4. Smith is coming off a sterling outing where he threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, completing 84% of his passes against the Lions. While the Bears' secondary is vulnerable in individual matchups, their overall body of work has been stout. Chicago hasn't allowed more than 153 yards over the last two weeks, with no touchdowns and three interceptions. Despite Breece Hall's likely absence, the Bears are more suspect against the run, potentially setting Smith up for a game-management approach.
outlooksByWeek.5: Geno Smith hopes for more opportunities in the Jets' Week 5 game against a vulnerable Browns secondary. After completing 31 passes in Week 3, Smith went just 8-for-15 in Week 4 against the Bears. Despite the lack of volume, he has a 5:0 TD:INT ratio and a 7.7 yards-per-attempt average, his highest mark since playing just two games in 2016. Cleveland has allowed nine touchdown passes in four games and at least 291 yards in each of the last two weeks, putting Smith in a spot to exceed his season norms.
outlooksByWeek.6: Geno Smith faces an uphill battle for fantasy success when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Smith has been held to 182 yards or fewer in consecutive weeks and has multiple touchdown passes just once through five games. While the Patriots' secondary is banged up, they've still allowed just a 6:3 TD:INT ratio through five games while holding three quarterbacks to no more than 187 yards. The Jets hope to remain run-first, limiting Smith's opportunities.
outlooksByWeek.7: Geno Smith will look to buck his seasonal trends in an inviting Week 7 matchup when the Jets face the Dolphins. Smith has opened the year with one or zero touchdown passes in five of his six games, but Miami's defense has allowed 11 touchdown throws in five contests. Smith likely needs those timely scoring plays as Miami is allowing just 226 passing yards per game, with teams preferring to exploit its run defense, setting him up as a risky bye-week replacement option.
outlooksByWeek.8: Geno Smith is poised to build on one of his best outings of the year when the Jets host the Raiders in Week 8. He threw for three touchdowns in Week 7 against Miami, his second game in seven outings at that mark, while the other five have produced just one touchdown or none. Las Vegas has allowed multiple touchdowns in five straight games and 16 scores overall, the second-highest total across the league. Smith needs to find paydirt to be a viable option, as the Raiders have surrendered more than 255 passing yards just once.
outlooksByWeek.9: Geno Smith faces an uphill battle to continue his current form when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. Smith has thrown for multiple touchdowns and at least 287 yards in consecutive weeks after tossing only one or no touchdowns in five of his first six outings. Kansas City has allowed only seven touchdown passes, with only two opposing quarterbacks topping 222 yards against them, suggesting fantasy managers are better off looking for streaming options elsewhere.
outlooksByWeek.10: Geno Smith will look to bounce back in Week 10 when the Jets face the Bills. After averaging 288.5 passing yards over two promising showings, Smith managed just 165 yards in Week 9, failing to throw a touchdown for the second time this season. Buffalo's defense is middling in terms of fantasy points allowed to opposing quarterbacks, but they've given up 15 touchdown passes through eight games, and the game flow will likely force the Jets to throw frequently while trailing. Smith has thrown multiple touchdowns in just three games, but there is some streaming appeal given a favorable Week 10 matchup.
outlooksByWeek.11: Geno Smith will need to overcome an ankle injury if he's to help the Jets take down the Chargers in Week 11. Smith was in and out of the lineup in Week 10, his first time ceding snaps under center all season, resulting in his second straight game without a touchdown pass. Smith now has one or zero scores in seven of his 10 outings. While the Chargers have allowed at least 340 passing yards in consecutive games, they've also surrendered multiple touchdown passes just three times in nine games, not setting Smith up for high-end production in Week 11. Cade Klubnik will start if Smith isn't deemed fit.
outlooksByWeek.12: Geno Smith brings low-volume but surging efficiency into the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. While he hasn't topped 176 passing yards in three straight games and has failed to complete more than 18 attempts, Smith is coming off his third three-touchdown pass outing in Week 11. With the Jets preferring a run-first approach paired with an unhealthy receiving corps, Smith is not a fantasy option against a mid-tier secondary that's allowing 7.7 yards per attempt.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith was traded to the Jets following an unsuccessful one-year stint in Las Vegas. Smith, who began his career as a second-round pick with the Jets in 2013, is in line to start, though he's a long shot for consistent fantasy production. Smith peaked with a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game with Seattle in 2022, but he has finished no better than 16th over the past three seasons. He paced the NFL in both interceptions and sacks in 2025 after finishing third in both categories in 2024 and is no longer much of a factor with his legs. The 35-year-old might bring some stability to the fantasy outlook of the team's pass catchers, but we shouldn't expect much more than that. Consider Smith only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.9: Devin Duvernay could be in line for an expanded role in Arizona's offense beginning with a Week 9 clash in Seattle. After being limited to special-teams duties over the first seven weeks of the campaign, Duvernay logged a 42% offensive snap share against Dallas in Week 8 and caught both of his targets for 14 yards. Kendrick Bourne suffered a fractured tibia early in that game and will miss the rest of the season, so Duvernay could be asked to take on a larger role in the wideout corps moving forward. However, a matchup against Seattle isn't ideal, as the Seahawks are allowing the fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Devin Duvernay could be called upon to take on a larger role in the Cardinals' Week 10 matchup versus the Rams. Duvernay played only on special teams over the first seven weeks of the campaign, but he's logged over 40% of Arizona's offensive snaps over the past two weeks and has tallied four catches for 22 yards on four targets. He could be asked to do more beginning in Week 10, as both Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are expected to miss the rest of the season. Duvernay faces a tough opponent in the Rams, who have allowed a modest 116.4 receiving yards per game to wideouts, ranking in the top five leaguewide.
outlooksByWeek.11: Devin Duvernay may have an opportunity to seize the No. 1 wideout role for Arizona in Week 11 against Kansas City. Duvernay logged a modest 2-35-0 receiving line this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams, but his reception, receiving yardage and target (three) totals all paced Cardinals wideouts. If Duvernay can show continued rapport with rookie quarterback Carson Beck, he could begin to see more than the 29 percent offensive snap share he logged against Los Angeles. With that said, KC is a tough draw, as its secondary has given up the second-fewest receptions per game (10.1) to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Devin Duvernay's work in Arizona's wideout corps continues to dwindle ahead of a Week 12 matchup against Washington. After logging an offensive snap share of over 40% in Weeks 8 and 9, Duvernay sank to a 29% share in Week 10 and then a 4% share in Week 11. He continues to feature as the team's kick returner, but that isn't likely to yield much fruit in most fantasy formats. Duvernay thus isn't a recommended fantasy asset in Week 12 despite going up against a Commanders defense that has given up 10 receiving touchdowns to wideouts this season.

outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Goodson is the third backup running back already for the Cowboys this season. With Malik Davis injured and Emari Demercado deemed ineffective, Goodson had six carries for 22 yards in his season-debut versus the Ravens. However, Javonte Williams remains the undisputed starter, leaving Goodson and company picking up the scraps. In Week 4, the Cowboys will also face a rather stingy Texans run defense allowing 86.7 yards per game on the ground, which is fifth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Goodson managed three carries for 12 yards last game for the Cowboys. Meanwhile, starter Javonte Williams had 24 touches and three touchdowns in the comeback win over the Texans. In other words, Goodson's utility is extremely low barring injury. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Goodson did not receive a touch out of the backfield last game for the Cowboys. Meanwhile, starter Javonte Williams had 14 touches and a touchdown and continues to be the workhorse for the offense on the ground. If Goodson sees any touches in Week 6, he could find some room, though, as Green Bay's defense has been extremely suspect in defending the run. The Packers are allowing 127.6 rushing yards per contest, which is tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Goodson had just three offensive touches last game for Dallas. Goodson gained only nine yards, as he continues to be the primary, albeit little-used backup to Javonte Williams. Interestingly, though, Goodson returned five kicks for 122 yards after Kavontae Turpin went down with a rib injury. Goodson could reprise that role in Week 7 versus the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per contest, which is 19th in the league. The Eagles have also yielded eight rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 28th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Goodson has logged 17 carries over the last two games for Dallas. However, he has managed just 52 yards on the ground during that span. Meanwhile, starter Javonte Williams has rushed a staggering 49 times for over 200 yards during that same time period.  In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense that has been subpar against the run. Indy is allowing 131.8 rushing yards per tote, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Goodson is set to miss multiple weeks for the Cowboys due to a sprained knee. The timing is rough for Goodson, who is coming off his best performance of the season. Goodson rushed 12 times for 77 yards in the 27-23 win over the Colts. Either Israel Abanikanda or Jashaun Corbin will likely slide in as the backup running back, though neither is a reasonable option against a 49ers defense allowing just 80.9 rushing yards per game, which is second in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Williams' role could be elevated for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers with WR Omar Cooper (ankle) questionable. Williams logged just one Week 1 target despite playing 62% of the snaps in a game where the Jets led early and throughout-a script unlikely to materialize again in Week 2. With potential double-coverage on Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell running vertically, Williams could find ample space underneath without Cooper's presence, making him someone to consider in very deep formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Williams will look to build on an expanding role in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. Elevated to No. 3 on the depth chart with Omar Cooper landing on IR, Williams recorded six targets last week, catching them all for just 34 yards. The Jets' offense is unlikely to score enough to sustain a third viable receiver, but if there were such a matchup, it would be Week 3 against a secondary that's already allowed 437 yards to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Williams' role in the Jets' offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 tilt against the Bears. Despite the absence of Adonai Mitchell in Week 3, Williams logged only two targets in a game where the Jets threw 37 times. While the Bears are allowing 8.5 yards per target to receivers, Williams doesn't seem likely to garner enough looks to exploit a potentially favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Williams continues to amass minimal volume for the Jets as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. Williams flashed in Week 4, finishing with 73 yards and a touchdown, but it came on just three targets. While Cleveland has allowed three receivers to top 70 yards over the last two weeks, Williams' lack of opportunities makes for a boom-or-bust play in Week 5, and that assumes Adonai Mitchell doesn't return from a two-week absence.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Williams' role in the Jets offense may be declining ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Despite Adonai Mitchell's three-week absence, Williams has not logged more than three targets, and his snap share fell to a season-low 59% in Week 5 with the return of Tim Patrick. The Jets aren't throwing the ball enough to sustain secondary pass-catching options, and New England is allowing just 7.5 yards per target, the ninth-lowest in the league, leaving Williams with minimal appeal.
outlooksByWeek.9: Isaiah Williams isn't garnering substantial volume in the Jets' passing game ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Chiefs. While Williams caught his second touchdown of the season in Week 8, it was his first catch since Week 5. Kansas City has been stingy against opposing wideouts, allowing just two touchdown catches and the second-fewest fantasy points. With Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, and Omar Cooper all collecting more regular work, Williams lacks Week 9 fantasy charm.
outlooksByWeek.10: Isaiah Williams isn't collecting enough volume to help the Jets in Week 10 against the Bills. Despite the absence of Garrett Wilson (concussion) in Week 9, Williams failed to garner a target and has just one look over the last four weeks. The Jets likely will throw 30+ times Sunday assuming they fall behind early, but Williams remains unlikely to factor in those attempts.
outlooksByWeek.11: Isaiah Williams is trending upward in Week 11 when the Jets face the Chargers. Omar Cooper managed only one snap in Week 10 and is uncertain to play in Week 11 due to an ankle injury. This led to Williams logging a season-high seven snaps in Week 10, which he converted into just 24 yards. He has topped 34 yards on the year just once, but facing a secondary that is allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts, Williams could be a desperation play in deeper formats should Cooper be forced to sit.
outlooksByWeek.12: Isaiah Williams' involvement in the Jets' passing game is limited, and his availability for Week 12 against the Dolphins is uncertain due to a rib issue. Williams has topped two catches in just two of his 10 outings, and the Jets aren't throwing enough to sustain multiple receivers. Despite a favorable matchup against a Miami secondary that's allowing 9.2 yards per target, Williams is unlikely to produce for fantasy managers.

outlooksByWeek.4: Tory Horton is coming off his first catches of the season with Seattle set to host the Chargers in Week 4. Horton notched three catches on three targets for 48 yards in Sunday's Week 3 win over Washington, finishing as the Seahawks' third-leading pass catcher. However, his role makes for a limited fantasy ceiling at the moment, as he's logged less than one-third of Seattle's offensive snaps in each of his two games so far. The Chargers haven't done well against the pass this season, ranking 22nd in receiving yards allowed to wideouts through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tory Horton will look to get into the end zone for the second straight game when Seattle hosts San Francisco in Week 5. Horton caught just one pass against the Chargers in Week 4, but it was a six-yard touchdown. The second-year pro has otherwise struggled to make an impact so far in 2026, logging just four catches for 54 yards through three contests. His outlook isn't great against a San Francisco defense that has allowed the seventh-fewest receiving yards to wideouts so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tory Horton and the Seahawks host the undefeated Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He caught just one of five targets for 13 yards and returned one punt for 13 yards during Seattle's Week 6 overtime loss. Horton garnered his most looks of the season but wasn't able to make much of anything happen. The second-year wideout owns a 5-67-1 line on nine targets through five games in 2026. Despite the increased opportunities, Horton should remain on fantasy waiver wires versus Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tory Horton may move up in Seattle's wideout pecking order versus the Bears in Week 8. With Rashid Shaheed dealing with a knee injury and possibly set to miss time, Horton could be asked to step into a bigger role on offense. So far, Horton hasn't done much as a receiver, finishing with one or zero catches in five of the six games in which he's played. That makes him a volatile fantasy play even if Shaheed is ruled out despite facing a Bears defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards per game allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tory Horton may again get an elevated opportunity in Week 9 versus Arizona if Rashid Shaheed (knee) can't suit up for Seattle. With Shaheed out Week 8 against Chicago, Horton ranked second on his squad with six targets, and he tied a season high with three catches, which he turned into 26 yards. Given the target dominance of stud wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no Seattle wideout can be counted on for consistent production, but Horton should at least be involved against Arizona if Shaheed sits out again. He could also benefit from a favorable matchup, as the Cardinals are tied for last in the league with 11 receiving TDs allowed to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tory Horton may get another chance at an increased role in Seattle's Week 10 tilt against the Raiders. With Rashid Shaheed (knee) out the past two weeks, Horton has logged his two highest offensive snap shares of the season. He's managed a modest five catches for 48 yards on nine targets over that span, but those performances mark two of his three most productive outputs of the campaign. If Shaheed is out again, there's an opportunity for Horton to make some plays against a Las Vegas defense that has given up 9.52 yards per target to wideouts this year, third-worst in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Horton had the look of a Day 3 find by Seattle early on in 2025 prior to a season-ending shin injury suffered in Week 9. The 2025 fifth-round pick opened his career buried on the depth chart behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, but still found a way to make an impact while being limited to 46% of the offensive snaps. Though his production was volatile and he never cleared five targets in a game, he found the end zone five times on 23 targets. Despite the impressive showing, Horton's short-term outlook is dicey with JSN, Kupp and Rashid Shaheed presumably ahead of him on the depth chart. The 23-year-old's primary value is as a dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. St. Brown kicked off the season with a bang against the Saints, catching 10 of 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns. The star wide receiver continues to hold the monopoly in Detroit's passing game, and his production doesn't look to be taking a dip any time soon. He'll take on a Bills defense that ceded a seventh-most PPR points to Houston wide receivers (40.0) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. St. Brown finished with a monster performance in Week 2, bringing in nine of 13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns. Not only has the star pass catcher recorded back-to-back two-TD performances, but he's also now amassed 19 catches for 209 yards in that stretch. He should continue to benefit from Detroit's shaky defense, even against a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to bounce back from a quieter game as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. St. Brown finished Week 3 against the Jets with a touchdown, but other than that, he has just four catches for 19 yards. The eight targets he finished with did still tie  Jahmyr Gibbs for a team lead, so the volume remains for the pair of stars to both produce highly. St. Brown will face a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to find the end zone again as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. St. Brown returned to a solid eight catches for 75 yards against the Panthers in Week 4, but he also broke his three-game touchdown streak. The star pass catcher has now totaled 31 receptions for 303 yards and five touchdowns this season. He'll take on a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to find the end zone again as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. St. Brown has remained hot as of late with 14 catches for 144 yards in his last two outings, but he's been unable to find the end zone since Week 3. The star wide receiver will take a 37-372-5 receiving line into a big matchup versus a Green Bay secondary that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to heal from an ankle injury in time for Detroit's Week 8 matchup versus Minnesota. St. Brown played a full game in Week 7 against the Packers, finishing with nine catches for a season-high 153 yards. The star pass catcher also tweaked his ankle in the game, and while he's not expected to miss any time, his situation is worth monitoring. St. Brown will aim to expand on a 46-525-5 receiving line opposite to a Vikings defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to make a return to the end zone as the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9. St. Brown logged seven receptions for 46 yards and recorded one rush for 10 yards in a Week 8 win over Minnesota. The featured pass catcher has remained a dominant option week in and out, but he hasn't posted a touchdown since Week 3. He'll face a Miami defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs this season but 18th in the last three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.10: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to get back in the end zone as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. St. Brown led Detroit in all receiving categories against the Dolphins in Week 9, bringing in eight of 10 targets for 86 yards. The star wide receiver is on track for another dominant year, but he hasn't logged a touchdown since Week 3. He enters a favorable matchup versus a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. St. Brown finally broke his touchdown drought in a Week 10 blowout win over New England, catching four of five targets for 98 yards and two scores. The star pass catcher has now posted a 65-755-7 receiving line on 91 targets across nine contests. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. St. Brown punched in another score in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, which made up for his otherwise mediocre five catches for 37 yards. He's now brought in 70 of 97 targets for 792 yards and eight touchdowns this campaign. Chicago has ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: The only player in NFL history with 90-plus catches in each of his first five NFL seasons, St. Brown continues to assert himself as one of the league's best players. The 2021 fourth-round pick has finished exactly third among receivers in fantasy points three seasons in a row, ranking no lower than fourth in catches, yards and touchdowns each year. St. Brown actually enjoyed a career-high target share in 2025 (31.6%), which helped him to 13 top-20 fantasy outings. The 26-year-old has no added target competition and remains Jared Goff's clear No. 1 target. He should be off the board in the first round of your draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Nabers looked spry in his first game of the season for the Giants, a Week 1 victory over the Cowboys. Nabers led the G-Men in targets with nine, en route to six catches for 69 yards in the 28-20 triumph. Nabers showed no ill effects from his torn ACL and meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season, only needing to get tackled by his new head coach John Harbaugh to prove he could take a hit before suiting up. In Week 2, Nabers will face a Rams defense that struggled against the pass in Week 1, allowing 205 passing yards and three passing scores in its season opener. Nabers will likely be covered by all-pro cornerback Trent McDuffie, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Nabers injured his shoulder last game for the Giants. He was able to return, but still may undergo additional testing this week. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Nabers will likely see his stock take a hit. However, if Nabers can suit up in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Nabers shook off a shoulder injury to suit up last game for the Giants. He responded with five catches on six targets, though racked up a mere 26 yards in the 12-7 win over the Titans. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Nabers. However, Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Nabers exploded last game for 112 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants to victory. Nabers snagged six passes on seven targets for a season-high in terms of receiving yardage. He and quarterback Jameis Winston finally appeared to be on the same page. In Week 5, Nabers and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Malik Nabers saw a staggering 20 targets last game for the Giants. Nabers parlayed those ample opportunities into 11 grabs for 121 yards and a touchdown. It was the second-straight 100-yard outing for Nabers, who also scored for the second-consecutive contest. His newfound connection with starting quarterback Jameis Winston has been evident. In Week 6, the G-Men face a New Orleans defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Saints are allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Nabers continues his torrid stretch for the Giants. Nabers snagged 12 passes for 165 yards in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. Regardless of who has lined up under center for the Giants, Nabers has crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in three-straight contests. He has racked up a staggering 35 targets in his last two outings alone. In Week 7, Nabers has another favorable matchup against a leaky Texans secondary. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malik Nabers has crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in four-straight contests for the Giants. Nabers has racked up a staggering 36 catches for 509 yards and two touchdowns over that span. He has drawn an insane 51 targets during that time period, an average of nearly 13 opportunities per clash. In Week 9, the G-Men will face a scuffling Eagles squad. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Malik Nabers had a four-game 100-yard receiving streak snapped last game for the Giants. Nabers had five catches for 43 yards in the 19-11 win over the Eagles. He was targeted eight times. He will look to rebound in Week 10 against a porous Washington secondary. The Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Malik Nabers had a costly fumble last game for the Giants. Nabers had the ball punched out of his hands in scoring territory versus the Commanders, who ultimately defeated the G-Men by a score of 24-21. Nabers has now been held under 50 yards receiving in each of the last two outings following a dazzling four-game stretch of 100-yard outbursts. In Week 11, he will look to rebound against a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Malik Nabers snagged a touchdown pass for the Giants last game. Nabers finished the win over the Jags with seven catches for 55 yards and his third score of the season. Nabers was targeted 12 times, the third time in 2026 he received double-digit targets. In Week 12, the Giants will face a Colts defense allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, Indy has also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Nabers is on the comeback trail after a torn ACL limited him to only four appearances last season. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG. As a rookie, the 2024 sixth overall pick finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the 2024 season. He essentially has a new quarterback (Jaxson Dart threw only three passes his way last season), a new coach (John Harbaugh), a new offensive playcaller (Matt Nagy) and is recovering from the knee, so there are a lot of variables here, but the 23-year-old still holds elite upside. A healthy Nabers should be valued as a mid-to-back-end WR1, but the potential for a slow start needs to be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is expected to remain New Orleans' top running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Alvin Kamara (knee) being sidelined for the Week 1 overtime loss, Etienne only received nine carries, tying Kendre Miller for the most on the team. However, Etienne was busy as a receiver, catching seven of nine targets for 46 yards, which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. He could be in for another productive week, as Baltimore's defense allowed 28.1 PPR fantasy points to running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Etienne is expected operate as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite signing a big contract with the Saints this past offseason, Etienne saw just 10 opportunities in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He still leads the team in carries (17) but saw less work through the air, with Alvin Kamara (five catches on six targets) returning to the lineup. With Kamara back, Etienne may struggle to be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 17.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Travis Etienne (hamstring) will likely operate as New Orleans' top running back if active for the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Etienne has been sidelined for the Saints' last five games due to a hamstring issue, but his 21-day practice window is expected to be opened soon. If active for the Week 10 divisional matchup, Etienne is expected to thrive against a Panthers defense that's already allowed 12 touchdowns to opposing running backs in just eight games this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Travis Etienne will look to make a larger impact as the Saints' take on the Bears in Week 11. Etienne was relatively ineffective in his return from injury during the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, logging 11 touches for 34 yards. Despite Etienne serving as New Orleans' top running back, Audric Estime took most of the short-yardage work, and Alvin Kamara operated as the team's top red-zone back, scoring two touchdowns. Thus, Etienne's fantasy upside may be capped if his red-zone touches don't increase in the near future. He's set to face a solid Bears defense in Week 11 that's allowed just 20.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Travis Etienne is expected to remain the Saints' top rusher during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. In his two games since returning from a hamstring injury, Etienne has accumulated 90 rushing yards (4.1 yards per carry) and 20 receiving yards without finding the end zone. Despite his lack of production, Etienne was received 14 of the Saints' 16 running back carries during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, suggesting he's got a firm hold on the No. 1 role. Etienne is also in for an unfavorable matchup, as Cincinnati has allowed just 20.8 points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: DJ Moore will look to build on an impressive debut when the Bills host the Lions in Week 2. Despite new quarterback Josh Allen continuing to spread the ball around, Moore popped with a 100-yard outing on eight targets. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to open the year, but just 7.3 yards per attempt as New Orleans was forced to throw from behind. That may not be the case Thursday, and Moore is unlikely to garner high volume. Even so, facing a secondary void of high-end talent, Moore can get deep and provide big yardage without a lot of opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: DJ Moore will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he is to help the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. After showing sound chemistry with Josh Allen in his first action for Buffalo, Moore failed to haul in a touchdown late in the second quarter in Week 2, suffering the injury that forced him to miss the second half. The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.
outlooksByWeek.4: DJ Moore aims to remain heavily involved in the Bills' Week 4 game against the Patriots. In two healthy games, Moore has 18 targets as Josh Allen's top option, creating a stable floor. New England's secondary is middling, allowing the 18th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no one has topped 64 yards against them. Moore's potential could be further capped if he draws shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.5: DJ Moore continues to battle a shoulder issue as the Bills get set to travel in Week 5 to face the Rams. Moore exited Week 4's game against New England after aggravating the injury, his second early departure in four games. When playing an entire four quarters, Moore has dominated targets from Josh Allen, averaging nine looks. However, pairing injury concerns with the Rams' secondary not allowing an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, Moore could struggle in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: DJ Moore continues to battle through a shoulder issue that's cost him the better part of three games as the Bills head towards a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Moore has drawn 18 targets in his two healthy games, making his shoulder the only factor to worry about when considering him in lineups. The Raiders have allowed at least 91 yards to an opposing wideout in three straight weeks, adding confidence to Moore's viability if he proves healthy.
outlooksByWeek.8: DJ Moore hopes to be fully healthy following Buffalo's bye week in advance of their Week 8 matchup with the Ravens. Moore hasn't played since a brief appearance in Week 4 due to a shoulder injury that has lingered since Week 2. When on the field, he has been Josh Allen's favorite target, collecting 18 looks in two games. Baltimore has allowed four 100-yard receivers and an attractive 9.3 yards per target, the fifth-highest in the league, making Moore an attractive option if he suits up.
outlooksByWeek.9: DJ Moore will look to overcome a knee injury and help the Bills in Week 9 against the Vikings. It's been simple: when Moore plays, he's heavily involved, amassing 25 targets in three games. Minnesota is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, surrendering just four touchdown catches and 7.4 yards per target, but if he's on the field, Moore will have the volume necessary to be a viable lineup consideration.
outlooksByWeek.10: DJ Moore will look for increased volume when the Bills face the Jets in Week 10. Moore collected only five targets in Week 9, his lowest total in any healthy outing of 2026, in a game where Josh Allen had minimal time to throw. While he'll likely have more time Sunday and Moore has remained the preferred option on drop-backs, the Jets have allowed only nine touchdown receptions to wideouts, seemingly capping Moore's potential.
outlooksByWeek.11: DJ Moore will seek more big plays in Week 11 when the Bills face the Dolphins. Moore is averaging 16.3 yards per catch, the second-highest mark of his nine-year career, and gets an inviting matchup with a secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target to wideouts, the sixth-highest mark league-wide. Moore will need those big yardage chances as Buffalo threw only 21 times in Week 10 while blowing out the Jets, and a similar game script is likely against Miami.
outlooksByWeek.12: DJ Moore will try to maintain his recent scoring spree when the Bills face a strong Chiefs secondary in Week 12. Moore tied a season-high with 10 targets in Week 11, recording at least 82 yards receiving and scoring for the second time in as many games and third in four outings. Kansas City counters with only three touchdowns allowed to receivers in 10 contests, and a mere 6.6 yards per target. Moore will need steady volume to finish in the upper tier of receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rhamondre Stevenson will look for a heavier workload when the Patriots face the Steelers in Week 2. Stevenson notched 23 touches to open the year, and despite the potential return of TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), Stevenson should handle early-down work at a minimum. He's mainly an accumulator, averaging 4.0 yards per carry or less in two of the previous three seasons and just 2.8 to open 2026. But volume is king, and Stevenson likely has that since he also catches passes out of the backfield. Pittsburgh was vulnerable in Week 1 to receiving backs, plus Stevenson likely handles goal-line work, making him intriguing even in a difficult spot against a defense that allowed 3.8 yards per carry to open the year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rhamondre Stevenson's opportunities are questionable as the Patriots prepare for the Jaguars in Week 3. After a 23-touch season debut, Stevenson lost a fumble early in Week 2, an issue that's plagued him throughout his career, and ended with just seven touches. In a split backfield with Treveyon Henderson, New England will likely ride the Week 3 hot hand. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing rusher to go over 39 yards, both backs could be running uphill.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots offense is declining ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. The return of TreVeyon Henderson limited Stevenson to 13 rushes in Weeks 2 and 3, and unfavorable game flow and poor quarterback play are limiting his receiving opportunities. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but more receiving touchdowns (three) than rushing (two). Without certainty for double-digit touches, Stevenson comes with risk against a defense allowing a frugal 3.9 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rhamondre Stevenson continues to share work in the Patriots backfield ahead of an inviting Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. He amassed 13 carries in Week 4, one fewer than TreVeyon Henderson's 14, but Stevenson found the end zone while catching three passes for the third time in four weeks. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and was just solved by Kansas City's Kenneth Walker for 177 yards, so while split work will limit Stevenson's ceiling, his continued involvement as a pass-catcher paired with double-digit carries can result in fantasy-worthy production in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rhamondre Stevenson could garner workhorse carries in the Patriots' Week 6 match against the Jets with TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an ankle issue. Stevenson had 13 carries in Week 5 for the second straight week and now has double-digit carries in three of five games while adding at least three catches four times. With double-digit touches seemingly certain, Stevenson can exploit a defense that's allowing 4.3 yards per carry and one where he posted 102 yards and two touchdowns on only 13 touches last season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rhamondre Stevenson hasn't had much room to run for the Patriots in advance of a Week 7 clash with the Bears. Stevenson has logged double-digit carries in four of his first six games but is averaging a career-low 3.7 yards per carry while sharing time with TreVeyon Henderson, who surprisingly played in Week 6 despite a high-ankle sprain. Chicago has allowed only three rushing scores, and no opposing runner has topped 61 yards since Week 3, so while volume will remain Stevenson's friend, he'll likely need to find the end zone to provide fair returns.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rhamondre Stevenson's role in the Patriots' passing game will keep him active in Week 8 against the Dolphins. While he is coming off his third single-digit carry game of the season, he's caught at least three passes in five games and five in two outings, an area where Miami's defense is particularly vulnerable. The Dolphins allow a moderate 4.3 yards per carry and just three rushing touchdowns to backs, yet have given up 34 catches, including five touchdown receptions, to running backs in six games. Stevenson has multiple paths to meaningful production.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rhamondre Stevenson will look to lead the Patriots backfield again in Week 9 against a stingy Packers defense. Stevenson earned double-digit touches in seven of New England's first eight games and has at least 13 carries in four of his last five contests, despite sharing backfield touches with TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner. Green Bay has allowed 10 rushing touchdowns through eight games, which Stevenson may need for solid Week 9 production, as the Packers are allowing just 3.96 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rhamondre Stevenson is uncertain to suit up for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions due to a knee injury. New England fell into a big hole in Week 9, limiting Stevenson's carries prior to the injury, and he finished with a season-low six for the third time this season. His passing game involvement included a second touchdown reception in three weeks. If he plays, Stevenson figures to again lead the Patriots' backfield since TreVeyon Henderson will also likely be sidelined. Stevenson's rushing yard expectations can be tempered against a defense that's allowing a mere 3.9 yards per carry. Corey Kiner would be in line for lead back duties assuming both Stevenson and Henderson are sidelined.
outlooksByWeek.12: Rhamondre Stevenson could see heavy volume for the Patriots in Week 12 against the Chargers, with Tommy DeVito unlikely to spark the passing game. Emerging from a Week 11 bye, Stevenson can hopefully avoid an injury designation after a knee issue limited him to 36 yards on 12 carries over his last two outings. Facing a stacked front, Stevenson will rely on volume to beat a defense that's allowing 4.1 yards per carry and 10 touchdowns to backs in as many games, landing him in RB2/flex territory.

player.seasonOutlook: Stevenson will battle with second-year back TreVeyon Henderson for touches in the New England backfield. The duo shared the backfield at times last season, but it was the veteran Stevenson who usually operated as the lead back. He earned the role, ranking fifth among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF, second in yards after contact (2.82) and first in yards per target (9.1). Stevenson, who is entering his sixth season, did miss three games (he has missed time three seasons in a row), and his overall volume was limited (9.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game), which led to a 25th-place finish in fantasy points. Now 28 years old and with Henderson still very much in the mix, Stevenson, who has one top-20 fantasy campaign to his name, is a low-upside bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver as one of the hottest tight ends in the league. Following a quiet season opener in Australia, Kittle has put up 10 catches for 162 yards and three touchdowns over the subsequent two weeks. He's caught all but one of his 11 targets during that span, as he has been clicking very well with QB Brock Purdy. Kittle could continue rolling against a Broncos defense that has given up the eighth-most receiving yards (199) to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Kittle could again be a key component of San Francisco's offense in Week 5 against Seattle. Kittle has scored a touchdown in three straight games, and he got into the end zone on a game-sealing 56-yard reception in Week 4 versus the Broncos. The veteran tight end enters the clash against Seattle with 244 receiving yards on the season, third-most among NFL tight ends. With that said, the Seahawks' defense has given up the fourth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends, so Kittle has his work cut out for him in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Kittle should be past an illness by the time the 49ers face Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 6. Kittle suited up this past Sunday against Seattle despite falling under the weather near game day. He ended up with a modest five catches on six targets for 24 yards but logged his usual big workload with a season-high 93 percent offensive snap share. Kittle could be primed for a big game against the Commanders, who have surrendered 15.8 fantasy points per game -- second-most in the league -- to tight ends.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Kittle and the 49ers are in Atlanta as they look to stay undefeated in Week 7. He caught five of eight targets for 69 yards and a touchdown during San Francisco's 23-17 win in Week 6. Kittle finished second on the team in receptions, yardage and targets on a night where Brock Purdy attempted just 29 passes. The talented tight end boasts a 26-337-5 line on 36 targets through six outings, and he'll aim to keep rolling versus a Falcons defense tied for 23rd in fantasy points allowed per game (16.0) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 9 matchup versus the Raiders well-rested following his team's Week 8 bye. Kittle had his snaps managed each of the first two weeks following his January surgery to repair a torn Achilles tendon, but amid multiple injuries to the 49ers' WR corps, the star tight end logged at least an 85% offensive snap share (and at least six targets) in each of his past five games. San Francisco could get multiple of the injured wideouts back for Week 9, but Kittle should still be a big part of the passing game, as he ranks fifth among NFL tight ends with a 22.4% target share this season. He'll face a Las Vegas defense that has given up eight touchdowns to tight ends, tied for second-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: George Kittle's health and productivity have been huge this season for the 49ers heading into a Week 10 tilt against Dallas. After undergoing surgery in January to repair a torn Achilles, Kittle has played in every one of San Francisco's games this season and leads the club with 38 receptions, 483 receiving yards and five receiving touchdowns. His role in the passing game has been especially important of late, as Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) have been sidelined due to injuries, and the addition of veteran possession receiver Keenan Allen at the trade deadline isn't likely to impact Kittle's routes down the seams. Kittle will look to find success against a Dallas defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against tight ends, yielding 7.7 fantasy points per game to the position (tied for 12th in the league).
outlooksByWeek.11: George Kittle continues to be one of the NFL's most consistent tight ends ahead of the 49ers' Week 11 clash with Minnesota. Kittle tallied six catches for 74 yards this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, marking his eighth straight contest with at least four receptions. He's also registered at least 58 yards seven times during that span, giving him a very reliable weekly floor. Kittle could find the sledding tough against Minnesota, though, as the Vikings have given up the fewest fantasy points per game (5.1) to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 12 clash against Seattle fresh off a two-touchdown performance in Mexico City. While Kittle caught just three passes (on three targets) this past Sunday versus the Vikings, two of those receptions resulted in touchdowns. Kittle is up to seven scores on the season, tied for the most among NFL tight ends. With that said, Seattle has allowed just two TDs to tight ends this season and is giving up the third-fewest fantasy points per game (5.5) to the position, so Kittle faces a stiff task in replicating his Week 11 performance.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Jones will remain a high-usage option as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Jones saw a big workload in Week 4 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 20 times for 94 yards and recording four catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield shouldn't change with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Jones could be set to share the backfield in Week 7 as the Vikings play the Colts. Jones logged his best game of the season in Week 5 against the Saints before Minnesota's bye, rushing the ball 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown. The veteran could unfortunately now be in store for a shared role again, as position mate Jordan Mason is primed to return from IR, but the two have proven to be productive together in the past. Indy's defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Aaron Jones could be at risk of missing Week 8 as the Vikings travel to Detroit. Jones suffered a knee injury in Minnesota's Week 7 win over the Colts, and he's currently day-to-day. What this means for his status moving forward is unknown until practices start up this week, but it is promising that he avoided a significant injury. The veteran running back logged eight carries for 26 yards before his departure, and it appeared he was still holding a prominent role even with Jordan Mason back on the field. If Jones can get healthy, he'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Aaron Jones will aim to make the most of his opportunities as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jones shook off a knee injury and ended up playing in Week 8 against the Lions, but he logged a season-low five carries and 22 rushing yards, with two catches for 18 yards as well. The veteran's output moving forward is likely to remain capped with Jordan Mason sharing the backfield, but the pair could carve out some success versus a Buffalo defense that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Aaron Jones will look to make the most of his opportunities as the Vikings play the Packers in Week 10. Jones saw just five carries and one target in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, and he took them for 16 yards and five yards, respectively. The veteran running back has now seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, logging 18 carries in total during that stretch. He's not likely to see crazy value with Jordan Mason active, but a Green Bay defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to RBs is favorable.
outlooksByWeek.11: Aaron Jones will look to build off a solid showing as the Vikings travel to San Francisco in Week 11. Jones did well against his former squad in Week 10, logging 47 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, along with catching one pass for eight yards. The veteran remains in a timeshare with Jordan Mason, but he still holds some value moving forward. The 49ers have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.12: Aaron Jones will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Jones rushed the ball eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown, and he caught one pass for 13 yards in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. While the committee approach of Minnesota's backfield hasn't allowed for dominance for him or Jordan Mason, Jones has been the one to find the end zone more often. Atlanta has ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Blake Corum was one of few Rams players to have a good game on offense in their season-opening loss, and he'll look for more success in Week 2 against the Giants. Corum led Los Angeles with 54 rushing yards on just 10 carries versus San Francisco last Thursday, averaging 5.4 YPC after putting up an average of 5.1 YPC during the regular season last year. Kyren Williams remains the Rams' lead back, but there's little doubt that Corum has forced his way into a substantial role as well. The Giants held Dallas' No. 1 RB Javonte Williams to 3.4 YPC on 12 totes in Week 1, though Williams did score a rushing TD and put up a 5-31-1 line through the air.
outlooksByWeek.3: Blake Corum should continue to be a big part of the Rams' backfield versus the Broncos in Week 3. Against the Giants on Monday Night Football, Corum racked up 79 yards on 12 carries while adding a 13-yard reception. Through two weeks, Corum has 22 carries to Kyren Williams'  23, so the pair appear to be headed for a pretty even workload in 2026. Denver could be vulnerable to both ball carriers, as the Broncos have given up a whopping 5.40 YPC to RBs this season -- third worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Blake Corum will look to bounce back following a quiet Week 3 performance when the Rams visit Philadelphia in Week 4. Corum was held to season-low marks of six carries and 15 yards this past Sunday versus Denver while Kyren Williams put up 158 total yards. Though some expected Corum to challenge Williams for touches even more this season, the latter has emphatically cemented his No. 1 RB role with his strong early-season performance. Both Corum and Williams may need to rely on their work on the ground against the Eagles, who have given up the fewest receiving yards to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Blake Corum will aim to rebound from a pair of quiet games when the Rams host the Bills in Week 5. After after averaging 66.5 rushing yards in Los Angeles' first two games, Corum has totaled just 29 yards on the ground over his past two contests. He's been quite inefficient with his carries, logging just 2.6 yards per carry on his 11 totes while Kyren Williams has dominated backfield touches. Buffalo has given up six TDs to running backs this season, but three have come through the air. That's not Corum's forte -- he has just four catches for 20 yards with no scores as a receiver through four weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Blake Corum's role as a ball carrier seems to fading ahead of the Rams' Week 6 game versus Arizona. Corum rushed just five times for 19 yards Monday against Buffalo, marking his third straight contest with six or fewer carries after averaging 11 totes across the first two weeks. However, Corum did score his first TD of 2026 and had easily his best game this season as a receiver against the Bills, catching three passes for 53 yards. Given his recent downturn in carries, Corum may need to get into the end zone to come away with serviceable fantasy production, but the Cardinals have given up only four total TDs to running backs through five weeks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Blake Corum has developed into a legitimate complementary option in the Rams' backfield to star tailback Kyren Williams, rushing 47 times for 223 yards and a touchdown while adding nine receptions for 91 yards and another score through six games. His 4.7 yards per carry almost equals Williams' 4.9 mark, but the main difference is the touches, as Corum is averaging just 7.8 carries per game compared to Williams' 13.3. Still, Corum faces an encouraging Week 7 matchup against the Raiders, who have surrendered 19.6 fantasy points per game to RBs in 2026, the ninth-worst mark in the NFL.His limited receiving involvement and secondary role make him a touchdown-dependent flex option rather than a dependable weekly starter.
outlooksByWeek.8: Blake Corum is coming off his biggest workload of the campaign with the Rams' Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers on tap. After entering Sunday with fewer than 10 carries in four straight contests, Corum rumbled for 93 yards and a touchdown on a season-high 17 totes against the Raiders. Backfield mate Kyren Williams equaled Corum with 18 touches and figures to continue to lead the team's backfield, but Corum certainly reminded fantasy managers that he's worth consideration even in the No. 2 RB role. Both Corum and Williams could find room to run against a Chargers defense that ranks 21st in the league with 4.19 yards per carry allowed to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Blake Corum should continue to have a big role in the Rams' backfield in Week 9 against the Commanders. Corum logged five fewer carries than backfield make Kyren Williams this past Sunday versus the Chargers, but Corum led the team with 73 rushing yards and also scored a touchdown for the fourth straight contest. After taking fewer than 10 totes four straight weeks, Corum has averaged 14 carries across his past two contests and seems to have regained his role as Los Angeles' 1B option next to Williams' 1A role. Washington has been pretty tough on running backs so far this season, tying for 10th in the league with 15.5 fantasy points allowed per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.10: Blake Corum continues to get a hefty share of work out of the Rams' backfield heading into a Week 10 visit to Arizona. Corum led Los Angeles with 58 rushing yards and scored a touchdown on 11 carries in a Week 9 win against Washington. Though he remains marginally behind Kyren Williams in the Rams' backfield, Corum has logged double-digit carries in three straight games and has scored in each of those contests. There could be an opportunity for both Corum and Williams to succeed against a Cardinals defense that is giving up 99.6 rushing yards per game to RBs, ranking 19th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Blake Corum will look to build on a season-best performance when the Rams host the Packers in Week 12. Corum rumbled for a season-high 100 rushing yards and a touchdown in Week 10 against Arizona while adding three catches for 19 yards. He should be fresh with Los Angeles having been on bye in Week 12, and Corum could be even more important than usual if backfield mate Kyren Williams' sore toe inhibits him at all. Both ball carriers could be productive against a Green Bay defense that ranks 26th in the NFL with 21.1 fantasy points per game allowed to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a tough Week 2 matchup against the Ravens, whose defense gave up just 12.7 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite a poor first half, Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns in last week's overtime loss, making him the league's leading passer. However, Shough was prone to turnovers, throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble, which is something Baltimore could capitalize on. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup, as the Ravens allowed just 166 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Shough has been one of the NFL's most productive QBs through two weeks, leading the league in passing yards (662) while producing five total touchdowns. Despite throwing the ball 90 times in his first two contests, Shough remains one of the league leaders in completion percentage (68.9 percent). He's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, however, with the Raiders' allowing just one passing touchdowns this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Shough is expected lead the Saints' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14 points to the Packers in Week 3. Shough continued his stretch of impressive play in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, throwing for 255 yards, four touchdowns and an interception. Head coach Kellen Moore continues to put his faith in Shough, as the Saints' are throwing the ball 44 times per game through three weeks. Expect Shough to remain one of fantasy's best quarterbacks in Week 4 against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.6 fantasy points per game to the position this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Shough is expected to lead the Saints' offense into the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Despite a loss in Week 4, Shough remained productive, throwing for 286 yards and a touchdown with no turnovers. The second-year pro is now averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game, suggesting he'll remain productive for fantasy purposes as the season progresses. Despite this, he's in for a very tough Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's allowed just 15.7 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Shough is expected to remain productive in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Shough had his worst performance of the season in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, completing just 16 of 25 pass attempts for 96 yards and two interceptions. Despite this, he currently ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards (1,299) through five games, attempting a league-leading 205 pass attempts. He could definitely bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Shough will look to stay hot in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers.
