Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 5 against Buffalo, but the team was defeated in overtime. Still, it was an impressive showing for the reigning NFL MVP, as he posted his fourth consecutive effort of 300-plus passing yards. Stafford could be in for another big performance versus a Cardinals defense that has given up the second-highest passer rating (117.2) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Stafford enters the Rams' Week 7 matchup against the Raiders having completed 164 of 249 passes for 1,794 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions through six games. The veteran quarterback is averaging 299 passing yards per contest, but his production has been inconsistent, and Los Angeles has stumbled to a 2-4 record. The absence of Davante Adams, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, creates another obstacle for Stafford. However, Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, making Stafford an appealing bounce-back candidate despite the Rams' recent offensive struggles.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Stafford continues to put up prolific numbers for the Rams heading into a Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers. The reigning NFL MVP threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns against Las Vegas in Week 7, though he also tossed his seventh interception. Stafford has now compiled over 300 passing yards and/or multiple passing touchdowns in all but one game so far this season, and he leads the league with 1,989 total passing yards. The Chargers could at least offer some resistance, as they've allowed a modest 18.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, ninth-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Matthew Stafford will try to help the Rams move above .500 for the first time this season with a win in Week 9 against Washington. Stafford was pretty quiet against the Chargers this past Sunday, throwing for just 157 yards with one touchdown and one interception, but his performance was good enough to lead his team to a second straight victory. The veteran quarterback continues to rely heavily on star wideout Puka Nacua with Davante Adams (hamstring) expected to remain sidelined for multiple more games. Stafford has a prime matchup against the Commanders, who have given up the third-most fantasy points per game (24.6) to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Matthew Stafford will have to operate without his favorite target in the Rams' Week 10 tilt against Arizona. Puka Nacua, who Stafford has targeted at least 10 times in five of his past six games, has a knee injury that is expected to require a stint on IR. The Rams are also still without Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), so Stafford will have to look to other wideouts, as well as the tight-end corps, more often moving forward. He'll at least have a promising matchup in Week 10, as the Cardinals have allowed the third-most fantasy points (23.9) to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Matthew Stafford emerges from the Rams' bye with the prospect of facing Green Bay in Week 12 still without either of his two top wideouts. Davante Adams (hamstring) isn't expected to come off IR this week, and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss the remainder of the campaign. Stafford was able to guide Los Angeles to a win without both stars in Week 10 against Arizona, throwing for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception, but he'll likely face a tougher challenge this week. Whereas the Cardinals rank 30th in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks, the Packers sit at a very respectable eighth in that category.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: J.K. Dobbins wasn't a big part of the Broncos' game plan in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, as the veteran running back had only eight carries for 36 yards. RJ Harvey's volume was similar, with seven touches to Dobbins' eight, but turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Dobbins averaged over 80 scrimmage yards last season in the 10 regular-season games he was healthy, so better days should be ahead for Denver's lead back, although they may not come right away. In Week 2, he'll face a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: J.K. Dobbins' workload has been limited to begin the season, with just 18 carries for 72 yards through the Broncos' first two games. The veteran back also has yet to see a target, as RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman have been prioritized as pass-catchers. Dobbins picked up a minor hamstring injury in Week 2's win over the Jaguars, but the issue isn't expected to keep him out of the lineup in Week 3. The same can't be said for Harvey, however, who didn't play at all in Week 2 due to his own hamstring strain. Dobbins could split touches with Coleman again in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: J.K. Dobbins is coming off his largest workload of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams. He had 17 carries and 18 total touches but turned them into just 53 scrimmage yards. Dobbins has struggled out of the gate, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but he should continue to handle the majority of the early-down work while rookie Jonah Coleman is on IR. RJ Harvey, who compiled 47 scrimmage yards on just eight touches against the Rams, remains the primary passing-down back. Dobbins will look for his first touchdown of 2026 in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: J.K. Dobbins continues to struggle as the primary early-down back for the Broncos. In a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, he managed just 40 rushing yards on 11 carries. This marks the fourth straight game to begin the season he's failed to reach 50 rushing yards or get into the end zone. Dobbins' 3.5 yards per carry would be a career low; he's never had a mark below 4.6 in any year he's played at least eight games. The veteran RB has at least stayed healthy, but that hasn't led to much production. He'll try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: J.K. Dobbins scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, while also producing season highs in touches (20) and rushing yards (68). The veteran running back was one of the few players to clearly benefit from Sean Payton's return to play-calling duties, but Dobbins still managed fairly modest numbers. He's been able to stay healthy so far in 2026, but through five games he's averaged just 3.6 yards per carry, a mark that would be a career low if it doesn't improve. Dobbins will take on a Seahawks defense in Week 6 that's tied for 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but which has yet to allow any back to reach 70 rushing yards in a game.
outlooksByWeek.7: J.K. Dobbins scored a rushing touchdown for a second straight game in the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The veteran running back hasn't found much success overall in a struggling offense, averaging just 3.3 yards per carry with zero gains of 20-plus yards through six games, but his role as the goal-line back provides him with a consistent path to production. Dobbins is also more involved as a pass catcher in recent weeks, producing an 8-27-0 line while logging multiple targets in four straight weeks. He'll look to break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 28th in rushing yards per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: J.K. Dobbins may be in danger of losing his spot in the Broncos' offense. During a Week 7 win over the Cardinals, rookie Jonah Coleman led the backfield with nine carries compared to Dobbins' six, and Coleman's 11 touches were also more than RJ Harvey's five. Both Dobbins and Harvey got into the end zone while Coleman didn't, suggesting that this could be turning into a full-blown committee. Dobbins doesn't contribute as a pass catcher the way Harvey does, so if he gets supplanted on early downs by Coleman, he may fade out of the game plan entirely. Dobbins will have trouble producing on limited volume in Week 8 versus a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: J.K. Dobbins may have lost his hold on the top job in the Broncos' backfield. In a Week 8 comeback win over Kansas City, it was rookie Jonah Coleman who got the biggest workload and who scored the winning touchdown on a five-yard run. Dobbins recorded just seven carries, his second straight game getting single-digit touches, and his woeful 3.3 yards per carry doesn't make a strong case for a bigger role. With RJ Harvey on injured reserve, Dobbins should retain the No. 2 job for the next few weeks. The veteran might be able to make a splash on limited carries in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and which ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: J.K. Dobbins fell into a depth role behind rookie Jonah Coleman in the Broncos' backfield prior to the team's bye. Over the last three games, Dobbins has 17 carries to Coleman's 37, and the youngster is also seeing the bulk of the action at the goal line. Dobbins scored a rushing TD during that span, and he hasn't completely disappeared from the game plan, but it would likely take an injury to Coleman for him to log significant volume again. Dobbins will take on a Raiders defense in Week 11 that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: J.K. Dobbins has faded into a depth role in the Broncos' backfield with the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman. Dobbins has handled single-digit touches in four straight games, and in a Week 11 win over the Raiders, he saw only one snap on offense, gaining zero yards on his only carry. The veteran's main path to fantasy relevance was through volume, and that no longer appears to be open while Coleman is healthy and effective. Dobbins will try to win back a little more work in Week 12 against a Steelers defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dobbins re-signed with Denver and will attempt to fend off sophomore RJ Harvey for the team's lead-back job. With both active during Weeks 1-10 last season (10 games), Dobbins handled 153 carries (60% team share) and 15 targets (4%), compared to 50 carries (20%) and 29 targets (9%) for Harvey. Dobbins ran well (5.05 yards per carry) when healthy, but he was limited to four touchdowns and was a nonfactor as a receiver (37 yards on 15 targets) en route to averaging 11.6 fantasy points (27th). Dobbins enters his age-27 campaign having yet to play a full season in his career (seven-plus missed games in four of the past five years) and without much value even when active (he has never produced a top-20 fantasy campaign). Dobbins is an underwhelming flex option with added value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rachaad White missed Washington's last game due to a shoulder issue, leaving his status in question for Week 5 versus the Giants. An argument can be made that White has been more productive than fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt in 2026, though that point may be moot as long as White is sidelined. Austin Ekeler will be the backup to Bill if White remains shelved. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rachaad White returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a shoulder issue. However, White failed to have much of an impact. He rushed seven times for just 18 yards, while also catching a two-yard pass out of the backfield. Meanwhile, starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown. In Week 6, the Commanders face a 49ers defense that has been rather stingy against the run. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per clash, which is 10th in the league. In addition, San Fran has surrendered just three rushing scores to date, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rachaad White will serve as the No. 1 running back for the Commanders in Week 8, as starter Jacory Croskey-Merritt was placed on Injured Reserve with a groin injury. White has found the end zone in two of the last three games as a receiver out of the backfield, but is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as a rusher. Still, the expanded role should give him double-digit touches against a floundering Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rachaad White has scored in back-to-back games for Washington. White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. White has found the end zone in each of the last two contests since taking over the starting running back job for the injured Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Jeremy McNichols also left this game with an injury, leaving Austin Ekeler as the only other healthy option. In Week 9, Washington will face a Rams defense allowing 109.3 yards per tilt on the ground, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Rams have surrendered just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rachaad White continues to operate as the top back for the Commanders, though has found little room to roam on the ground. White has failed to rush for more than 55 yards in any game this season. However, he does have at least two receptions in three-straight contests. In Week 10, White will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Rachaad White is averaging at least four yards per carry over his last three games with the Commanders. Though White is technically the starting running back, he has only had double-digit carries twice this season. Moreover, Jacory Croskey-Merritt could return soon from Injured Reserve. For now, though, White remains the top dog in the backfield heading into a Week 11 clash with the Bengals. Cincy has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. The Bengals are allowing 123.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Rachaad White dressed last game for the Commanders, but did not record a carry. Perhaps his heel issue was more concerning than initially thought, as Jacory Croskey-Merritt had 13 carries against the Bengals, while Austin Ekeler registered seven. Croskey-Merritt's return from injury likely relegates White to backup duty in Week 12 versus Arizona anyway, though the matchup is extremely favorable. The Cardinals are allowing 128.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.
outlooksByWeek.4: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome Pittsburgh to town for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He caught just two of nine targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset victory in Week 3. Concepcion wasn't able to contribute much despite tying for the team lead in targets with Harold Fannin Jr., but it's still a positive sign that the Browns are looking to get the ball in his hands. He'll get his first chance to face the division-rival Steelers and their 14th-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed (403) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Jets for a Week 5 showdown. The rookie receiver finished second on the team in receptions (5) and yardage (64), while his eight targets led the way in Cleveland's Week 4 victory. Concepcion also returned two punts for 10 yards, as it remains clear the Browns want the ball in his hands in a variety of ways for him to shine as a playmaker. However, he'll face a talented Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome the division-rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He caught his lone target for five yards before leaving Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5 with a head injury after a hard hit. Concepcion has entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will have to be cleared by an independent neurologist before returning to the field. The promising rookie's status should be monitored leading up to a Week 6 showdown against Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Titans in Week 7. He hauled in four of six targets for 37 yards and rushed twice for two yards during Cleveland's 13-10 comeback win in Week 6. The rookie first-round pick led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and was second in yardage behind veteran Jerry Jeudy (69). Concepcion will look to deliver more, along with the entire Browns' offense, versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: KC Concepcion and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for a Week 8 divisional clash. He caught eight of 10 targets for 129 yards and had three carries for another 23 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 7. The rookie broke out with season highs in receptions, yardage and targets while leading the Browns in every category. Concepcion will aim to score his first touchdown of his career versus the Steelers 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (30.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, KC Concepcion and the Browns are home for the first time since Week 6 to host the Texans. He grabbed four of six targets for 85 yards, including a 64-yard touchdown, during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. The score was the rookie wideout's first of his young career, and he now sports a 37-437-1 receiving line on 55 targets to go along with 10 carries for 37 yards through nine games. Concepcion will aim to take advantage of a Houston defense allowing the third-most fantasy points per game (38.5) to opposing WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: KC Concepcion and the Browns are home for a Week 12 clash against Las Vegas on Sunday Night Football. He corralled three of eight targets for 21 yards and rushed once for a six-yard TD during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Concepcion finished second on the team in targets but was sixth in yardage, although he salvaged the outing with his first career rushing score. He draws a winnable matchup versus a Raiders defense allowing 33.5 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen McMillan (knee) will operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McMillan was unable to suit up in Week 1 due to a nagging knee injury, but he could have a valuable role in Tampa Bay's receiving corps once healthy. Outside of Emeka Egbuka, the Buccaneers' wideouts combined to catch seven of eight targets for 76 yards in Week 1, which suggests McMillan will have a large opportunity to contribute when available. He's in for a great Week 2 matchup as well, with Cleveland's defense allowing three touchdowns to WRs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: McMillan is a fascinating late-round sleeper after he impressed as a rookie before missing all but four games due to injury last season. The 2024 third-round pick was featured during the final five games of his rookie season and exploded for a league-high seven TD catches (at least one in all five outings) and 19.8 fantasy PPG (more than 16.7 points in all five) in that span. He was limited in his return to action late in 2025, but did flash with a 7-114-0 performance on nine targets in Week 17. The 24-year-old has a path to a near-every-down role in 2026 with only Emeka Egbuka and 30-year-old Chris Godwin ahead of him on the depth chart. McMillan is worth the inexpensive flier on draft day.

No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Loop and the Ravens look to keep rolling at home versus the Saints in Week 2. Baltimore put up 41 points in their Week 1 victory, and Loop was a perfect 7-for-7 on his attempts. He made all five PATs and drilled both field-goal attempts-one from 57 yards out and one from 45. As long as he's the starting kicker, Loop should see plenty of scoring chances in this high-scoring Ravens offense. He'll try to stay perfect against a New Orleans defense that gave up 31 points to the Lions in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the Cowboys for a Week 3 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on both PATs during Baltimore's 24-17 loss in Week 2. Loop's first attempt from 49 yards was blocked, but he followed up by making his second attempt from the same distance. He should have plenty of opportunities to score in what's expected to be a high-scoring contest versus Dallas inside the AT&T Stadium dome in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Loop and the Ravens return home to square off against the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was perfect again in Baltimore's dramatic 34-31 victory in Brazil in Week 3, making both of his field-goal attempts, including a 56-yard game-winning kick as time expired, and all four of his extra points. Loop is now 5-for-6 on field-goal attempts and 11-for-11 on extra-point tries in 2026. The Ravens are fifth in scoring at 30.7 points per game, so he should continue earning plenty of opportunities for one of the best offenses in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Loop and the Ravens pay a visit to the surging Falcons for a Week 5 interconference clash on Sunday Night Football. The second-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on all three PATs during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. Loop missed his second field goal of the season but set a new career high with his make from 64 yards out, and he's now 6-for-8 on field goals and a perfect 14-for-14 on extra points. Atlanta has scored the most points in the league over its last two games (80), meaning Loop and the Ravens will have to keep up in a potential high-scoring game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Loop and the Ravens travel to square off against the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime victory in Week 5. Two of Loop's makes came from 50-plus yards, and he's now 5-for-5 on kicks from that distance this season and 9-for-11 on field goals overall. He's turning into a very reliable fantasy asset for a Ravens team that scores 29.2 points per game, making him a strong play against Cleveland.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Loop and the Ravens host the division-rival Bengals for a Week 7 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and converted his lone PAT during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Through six contests this season, Loop is 10-for-13 (76.9%) on field goals and a perfect 16-for-16 on extra-point tries. He has three outings with 100% accuracy and three with 50% accuracy, making him an inconsistent fantasy option despite kicking for a Ravens offense that scores 26.0 points per game, which ranks seventh so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the 5-1 Bills in Week 8. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Following a 30-point outing in an overtime victory in Week 5, the Ravens' offense has struggled mightily over the last two games, combining for just 23 points over that stretch. However, with Lamar Jackson (ankle) progressing toward a return from a three-game absence, Loop could have more opportunities to score versus a Bills defense allowing 28.5 points per contest, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Loop and the Ravens are back home for a Week 9 clash against the 5-2 Jaguars. He went 1-for-2 on field goal attempts and converted his lone PAT during Baltimore's 36-10 loss in Week 8. Loop has attempted more than two FGs just once this season, and there's a good chance his limited involvement will continue with Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) probably done for the year. The Ravens have scored a combined 33 points over their last three outings, and their struggles are likely to persist versus a Jacksonville defense allowing just 15.9 points per game, the second-best mark in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep it rolling in Detroit's Week 2 matchup at Buffalo. Gibbs was the bell cow managers hoped for in Week 1 against the Saints, logging 29 rushes for 156 yards, two touchdowns and catching all five of his targets for 30 yards. He'll also face a Bills defense that fared badly against the ground game in their season opener, allowing Gibbs' former teammate David Montgomery to total 79 yards and three touchdowns off 23 touches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to keep things rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Gibbs finished with huge numbers once again in Week 2, but most of his output came from six catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The superstar running back has seen high volume so far, with 56 touches for 299 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to his name this season. He'll face a Jets defense that's been tough against the run in its first two games, but New York hasn't faced anyone of Gibbs' caliber.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his touchdown tear alive as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Gibbs was a beast once again in Week 3 against the Jets, turning 20 carries into 99 yards and two touchdowns, as well as catching the ball six times for 65 yards and another touchdown. The fourth-year star has now found the end zone six times across three games, and he's totaled 463 yards from scrimmage. He'll face a Panthers defense that's allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to return to dominance as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Gibbs produced for fantasy managers in Week 4, but he still rushed 15 times for a season-low 46 yards with a touchdown, tacking on four catches for 31 yards. Either way, the superstar running back has found the end zone in every game this season, and he's surpassed 100 total yards in three of four games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top five against fantasy RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to come out of the bye week with a bang as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Gibbs was a monster in Week 5 against the Cardinals, rushing 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns, with five catches for 56 yards as well. The premier running back has now surpassed 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season, and he's found the end zone nine times across five games. He'll face a Green Bay front that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to get back in the end zone as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Gibbs hit the century mark on the ground for the third time this season in Week 7 versus Green Bay, rushing the ball 29 times for 116 yards and adding five catches for 27 yards. The superstar unfortunately was held to zero touchdowns for the first time this season, with nine to his name across the first five games. He'll change focus now to a Minnesota defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to stay hot as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Gibbs recorded another monster performance on the ground in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, rushing the ball 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown, with two catches for 15 yards as well. The superstar has now surpassed 100 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's found the end zone in all but one outing this season. He'll take on a Dolphins defense that's ranked a favorable 27th in fantasy points allowed to running backs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jahmyr Gibbs will seek to return to dominance as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Gibbs punched in another rushing score alongside 74 yards on the ground in Week 9 against the Dolphins, but he was unable to record a catch for the first time this season. The star ball carrier has now recorded 20 or more carries in each of his last four outings, but he's seen his receiving work decline each week in that stretch. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep up his dominance as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. Gibbs had another monster performance in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, totaling 252 yards off 29 touches and tacking on two rushing touchdowns. The superstar has now amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine showings. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his tear going in Week 12 as Detroit faces Chicago on Thanksgiving. Gibbs eventually broke down an otherwise stingy Tampa Bay run defense in Week 11, rushing 23 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns and catching four passes for 20 yards. The superstar has now surpassed 95 rushing yards in seven of 10 games this season, and he's totaled 13 scores on the ground. He'll face a Bears defense that's ranked relatively middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this season, and that Travis Etienne averaged 5.42 yards per carry against this past Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.
outlooksByWeek.4: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.
outlooksByWeek.5: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Browns in the Jets' Week 5 matchup due to a quad injury. He missed Week 4 with the issue, and when healthy, he was limited to 32 or fewer yards in his last two outings. Should he suit up, it's possible he'd be eased into his return and share snaps with Braelon Allen, but it's a favorable spot if a normal workload can be anticipated. While Cleveland has yet to allow a running back to score, they're allowing 4.8 yards per carry, with the last three lead backs all reaching at least 82 yards.
outlooksByWeek.6: Breece Hall needs to overcome a quad injury to suit up for the first time in three weeks when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Braelon Allen has shouldered the load in Hall's absence, and a split workload can be anticipated once Hall returns. Hall would require an unlikely heavy volume to be a top option facing a New England defense that's allowed just 399 rushing yards through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Breece Hall has missed three straight games due to a quad injury as the Jets get set to face the Dolphins in Week 7. Braelon Allen has shined during Hall's absence, and should Hall be deemed healthy, it would appear safe to assume he'd be eased back into action. Miami's defense ranks in the middle of the pack against opposing rushers, allowing 4.0 yards per carry and three rushing scores, but five touchdowns through the air to opposing backs. With questionable volume if he returns to action, it's probably wise to wait one more week before deploying Hall.
outlooksByWeek.8: Breece Hall's role is uncertain if he returns from a quad injury in Week 8 when the Jets face the Raiders. Hall has not played since Week 3 and has topped 32 yards just once, while Braelon Allen has shined during his absence. Being eased back into action appears more likely than immediately commanding the Jets' backfield, but he may not require heavy volume to be an intriguing asset, as the Raiders are allowing the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs and 5.2 yards per carry. Five opposing backs have rushed for 94 yards or more against them.
outlooksByWeek.9: Breece Hall is poised to return from a five-game absence due to a quad injury when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. In Hall's absence, Braelon Allen shined and has likely earned at least a portion of the carries, leaving Hall's role uncertain. Pairing that with a matchup against a Kansas City defense that's allowing just 3.3 yards per carry, Hall doesn't offer a solid floor or much upside in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.10: Breece Hall's workload should be strong in the Jets' Week 10 matchup against a tough Bills run defense. Returning to action in Week 9 after a five-game absence, Hall collected 18 touches to Braelon Allen's 10, despite Allen's success while Hall was sidelined. Hall has logged at least 13 carries in all four games when healthy, adding 13 receptions. His viability in the passing game should allow him to be a fantasy factor despite facing a defense that's allowing just 3.8 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.11: Breece Hall brings steady volume into a somewhat challenging matchup in Week 11 when the Jets face the Chargers. Hall has amassed at least 11 carries in both games since returning from injury while adding seven receptions, tallying 195 total yards though not reaching the end zone and continuing to share reps with Braelon Allen. The Chargers are allowing the 10th most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but just 4.0 yards per carry and an even lower 3.9 yards per reception. Hall remains a lineup mainstay and could surge in the receiving game if Cade Klubnik is forced into action over Geno Smith (ankle).
outlooksByWeek.12: Breece Hall is slated for a heavy workload for the Jets' run-first offense entering an inviting matchup against the Dolphins in Week 12. Hall amassed 20 rushes in Week 11, adding three catches, and has now topped 100 total yards in consecutive outings. Miami is allowing a modest 4.3 yards per carry but 11 total touchdowns (six rushing, five receiving) to running backs. Braelon Allen excelled against the Dolphins in Hall's absence earlier in the season, so Hall should produce in Week 12, even if ceding some carries to Allen. Hall remains a must-start.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams is coming off an explosive Monday Night Football performance heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. With Puka Nacua sidelined by a hip injury, Adams starred Monday against the Giants, posting a massive 10-195-2 line. Nacua's status for Week 3 is up in the air, and Adams would logically stand to be Matthew Stafford's top target again if Nacua can't suit up. However, Denver is a tough matchup, as the Broncos have yielded just 6.55 yards per target to wideouts this season (fifth-best in the NFL).
outlooksByWeek.4: Davante Adams has looked resurgent of late ahead of the Rams' Week 4 tilt against the Eagles. With Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined the past two weeks, Adams has gone off for 15 catches, 332 yards and two touchdowns. However, Nacua has a chance to return to action against Philadelphia, which would potentially result in Adams seeing less attention from QB Matthew Stafford. With that said, both wideouts could feast against an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league by giving up an average of 157.7 receiving yards per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Davante Adams is coming off a quiet performance as the Rams prepare to host the Bills in Week 5. Against Philadelphia in Week 4, Adams was held to four catches for 32 yards. That was a substantial downturn after Adams averaged 7.5 catches and 166 yards over the previous two contests, though he still got a healthy nine targets against the Eagles. It has to be mentioned that star wideout Puka Nacua returned to action in Week 4 and posted a 9-125-0 line, while Adams' big performances the previous two weeks took place in games Nacua missed due to injury. Both WRs could find success against the Bills, who have allowed the fourth-most receiving yards to wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Davante Adams is coming off his second two-TD game of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 6 battle versus Arizona. Against Buffalo on Monday Night Football in Week 5, Adams recorded a 5-51-2 line on seven targets. While he lagged far behind Puka Nacua's 24 targets and massive 17-138-1 line, Adams continued to work as a top option for QB Matthew Stafford in the red zone. That could come in handy again versus the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-high 10 receiving touchdowns to wide receivers so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Davante Adams was placed on Injured Reserve due to a ruptured left hamstring in the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals and is expected to be sidelined until after the Rams' Week 11 bye in a best-case scenario. With Adams out, names such as Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell should be in line for more targets, while established threats in the passing game like Puka Nacua, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams will also be in line for an uptick in numbers. Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdonwns this season, and he will be sidelined for the time being, so he'll miss out on the chance of being productive in a favorable Week 7 matchup against a below-average Raiders defense.
outlooksByWeek.12: Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to remain sidelined for the Rams' Week 12 clash against Green Bay. That may be due in part to the game taking part on Wednesday, but even with an extended break afterward, the star wideout is currently thought to have just an "outside chance" to suit up in Week 13 against Kansas City. Los Angeles will turn to a hodgepodge of wideouts, including Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith, for wideout production in the absence of Adams and Puka Nacua (knee/toe).

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the Texans in Week 2. Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards with one TD and one INT, and he rushed five times for 20 yards in their season-opening win. Houston ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (39.0) to QBs after Josh Allen torched them for 357 scrimmage yards and four TDs. Burrow will look to get Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins more involved after the receivers combined for 71 yards on just five catches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are on the road to face the Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with back spasms in practice, Burrow was a full go in Week 2, throwing for 207 yards (20-for-31) with two TDs and no INTs in the 20-6 victory. He faces a stout Pittsburgh defense that ranks first in fantasy points allowed (11.6) to QBs and seventh in passing yards allowed. Burrow is one of the best at his position, but fantasy managers should approach this matchup with caution after the Steelers held Drake Maye to 208 passing yards (14-for-22) with one pick while sacking him three times in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Joe Burrow and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He threw for 282 yards (28-for-37) with three TDs and no INTs and added 13 yards on two carries during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Burrow also lost a fumble in the final minute of the contest, but he had a strong outing overall against a tough defense. Up next is another difficult task, as Jacksonville's defense is tied for fifth, allowing 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the 0-4 Dolphins in Week 5. He completed 39 of 54 pass attempts for 428 yards with one TD and two INTs while rushing three times for six yards and another score during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. The Bengals leaned on Burrow while playing from behind most of the game, but with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both questionable to suit up against Miami, they're hoping a better start will allow them to rely on the ground game a bit more. The Dolphins' defense is certainly beatable, allowing 21.2 fantasy points to QBs (T-18th) and 29.7 to RBs, which ranks dead last.
outlooksByWeek.7: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are in Baltimore for an AFC North clash in Week 7. During Cincinnati's Week 5 win over Miami, he threw for 190 yards (23-for-32) with four TDs and no INTs while rushing four times for 10 yards. Now coming off their bye week, Burrow will look to find holes in a tough Ravens defense that allows 17.5 fantasy points per game to QBs, which ranks seventh. The good news is that he'll have his vast array of complementary skill players available following a week of rest, headlined by Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
outlooksByWeek.8: Joe Burrow and the Bengals return home to host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He completed 22 of 30 pass attempts for 292 yards with four touchdowns and zero interceptions and rushed twice for 12 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. It was Burrow's second straight outing with four TDs and no INTs, as he threw all of his scores in the second half. Up next is a Tennessee defense allowing 19.2 fantasy points per game to QBs, which ranks 12th.
outlooksByWeek.9: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are in Spain for a Week 9 overseas tilt against the Falcons. In Week 8, he completed 38 of 48 pass attempts for 462 yards with five TDs and three INTs, and he had three carries for 10 yards and another score during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win. Burrow recorded season highs in passing yards, completion percentage, TDs, and INTs, and he has posted a 13:3 TD:INT ratio over his last three outings. Burrow faces a Falcons defense allowing 18.7 fantasy points per game (10th) to opposing QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Joe Burrow and the Bengals welcome the divisional-rival Steelers to town for a Week 10 meeting on Sunday Night Football. He stayed red-hot in Week 9, completing 24 of 29 pass attempts for 271 yards and three TDs with no INTs, while rushing three times for seven yards and another score. Burrow owns a 16:3 TD:INT ratio and has two rushing TDs over his last four outings, and he continues to lead the NFL with 23 passing TDs through eight games. He'll look to avenge a Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh, when he went 28-for-37 for 282 yards and three scores but lost a fumble with 53 seconds remaining and Cincinnati down by three.
outlooksByWeek.11: Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit the Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 11. His hot streak continued during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, as he threw for 409 yards with four TDs and no INTs while rushing once for eight yards. Over his last five outings, all Bengals wins, Burrow has compiled 1,624 passing yards with a 20:3 TD:INT ratio, while adding 47 rushing yards and another two scores. The NFL's leading passer in terms of TDs (27) will aim to keep rolling versus the Commanders' 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to opposing QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Joe Burrow and the Bengals host the Saints in an interconference clash. He completed 28 of 40 pass attempts for 300 yards with two TDs and zero INTs while rushing twice for minus-one yard during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss. Burrow delivered his fourth 300-yard outing of the season while extending his streak of games without an interception to three. He'll look to get his team back in the win column versus a New Orleans defense allowing 19.8 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Burrow will attempt to bounce back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. The 29-year-old has now missed at least six games in three of his six pro seasons, including two of his past three. Burrow was still a starting-caliber fantasy quarterback when active last season (top-12 scorer in five of his final six games), but his ceiling was limited by a near complete lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries). Burrow was a top-five scoring quarterback in each of his past two full seasons, and coach Zac Taylor cut back a bit on his extreme pass-heavy playcalling last season, so Burrow is best valued as more of a midrange QB1 than an elite option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tucker Kraft should continue to have a big role in Green Bay's offense as they face the Jets in Week 2. Kraft reeled in three of six targets for 65 yards against the Vikings in Week 1, but he was definitely a huge focus of their defensive scheme. The star tight end will luckily face a New York defense that should be less menacing this Sunday, as they ceded a lower-half 15.4 PPR points per game to tight ends in the 2025 campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tucker Kraft will look to get more involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Kraft was held to just two catches for 15 yards in Week 2, but Green Bay's passing attack was lacking for most of the game. The bruising tight end will seek to re-establish himself as a top outlet for quarterback Jordan Love. Luckily, an Atlanta defense that's allowed 20.7 PPR points per game to tight ends so far this season, 29th in the league, could be a great place to start.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tucker Kraft will seek to bounce back as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Kraft brought in four of eight targets for 26 yards against the Falcons in Week 3, with some drops that are usually caught. The fourth-year tight end has now posted a 9-106-0 receiving line on 17 targets across the first three games of the season, which is underwhelming considering his start to last year. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's been tough on all but tight ends, allowing a bottom-10 183 receiving yards to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tucker Kraft will seek to build on his best performance of the season as the Packers take on Chicago in Week 5. Kraft recorded a season-high six catches in Week 4 against the Buccaneers, which he converted for 42 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end has started the campaign with a 15-148-1 receiving line, which he could expand on well against Green Bay's biggest rival. Kraft will have a tough task against a Bears defense that's ranked top five against fantasy TEs across four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tucker Kraft will look to stay busy as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Kraft finished with a solid five catches for 64 yards and one rush for two yards against the Bears in Week 5, even with teammates Christian Watson and Matthew Golden combining for 12 receptions for 266 yards and two touchdowns. While the featured tight end has served a different purpose in Green Bay's passing game so far, he still holds a 20-212-1 receiving line on the year. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tucker Kraft will look to do more with his targets as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Kraft stayed involved in Week 6 against the Cowboys, catching five of eight targets for 37 yards. The fourth-year tight end has continued to get opportunities with a 25-249-1 receiving line off 37 targets, but he still sits behind the two-man punch of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson at this point in the year. Luckily for Kraft, the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game (31.9) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tucker Kraft will look to build off a solid showing as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Kraft brought in four of six targets for 48 yards and his second touchdown of the season in Green Bay's Week 7 loss to the Lions. The featured tight end has now put up a 29-287-2 receiving line through the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked 20th in fantasy points allowed to TEs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tucker Kraft will look to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Kraft found the end zone once again in Week 8 against the Panthers, finishing the game with six catches for 53 yards and his score. The tight end has now posted a 35-350-3 receiving line on 49 targets this season, and he's found the end zone in back-to-back games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack in fantasy points allowed to TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tucker Kraft will aim to get back on track as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Kraft didn't get to join in on any of the fun of Green Bay's offensive explosion in Week 9 over the Patriots, as he brought in just one of his three targets for one yard and rushed the ball twice for eight yards. He's now posted a 36-351-3 receiving line across the first nine games of the campaign. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he logged three catches for 65 yards against in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tucker Kraft will aim to get back on track as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Kraft entered Green Bay's bye with back-to-back one-catch games, which was even more disappointing given he looked to finally be getting on track prior. The fourth-year tight end has now sported a 37-370-3 receiving line over 10 outings this campaign. Los Angeles has also ceded the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Kraft's steady career progression had him on the cusp of a full-on breakout last season, but all was derailed by a torn ACL in Week 9. Prior to the injury, Kraft had seen 10 targets in consecutive games, one of which included a career-high 33.3 fantasy points. Through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points. Granted, Kraft took advantage of a super easy schedule and was way over his head in the TD department (six TDs with an expected total of 1.8 and only two end zone targets), but his boost in usage and terrific RAC skills (he has led the position in the category each of his three seasons) were enough to get him into the weekly TE1 mix. Kraft's recovery will need to be monitored, but even if he's ready for Week 1, a dip in production is possible in his first year back from the major injury. He's a risky middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jakobi Meyers maintains a high floor, though he's a low-ceiling fantasy WR3 or flex play for Jacksonville's Week 2 home game against Denver's elite defense. Meyers has posted at least 39 receiving yards in all 10 of his games with the Jaguars since coming over in a midseason trade last year, including 40 receiving yards and a TD in the Week 1 win over Cleveland. Parker Washington and Brian Thomas have more downfield playmaking capability, but Meyers should see his share of short targets with Trevor Lawrence likely looking to get the ball out quickly to counter a Broncos pass rush that led the league with 68 sacks last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jakobi Meyers has been targeted just three times through Jacksonville's first two games. That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jakobi Meyers led the Jaguars with seven catches for 64 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in Week 3 against the Patriots after catching all three of his targets for 68 yards and a TD across Jacksonville's first two games. The veteran wideout has been playing alongside Parker Washington in two-WR sets and working ahead of Brian Thomas, as Meyers' 79% snap share this season is nearly double Thomas' mark. Washington is the clear No. 1 receiving option for the Jaguars, but Meyers is shaping up as the team's next-most reliable pass catcher, which is enough to be deployed as a WR3 or flex option in Week 4 against the Bengals, who didn't allow a touchdown pass through Week 2 before giving up TDs to three separate Steelers wideouts in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jakobi Meyers has been efficient with his opportunities for the Jaguars, catching 13 of 15 targets for 165 yards and two touchdowns heading into a Week 5 trip to London to face the Eagles. His usage has fluctuated in a Jacksonville passing game with many mouths to feed, but Meyers is a viable flex option for Week 5, especially in deeper leagues. The Eagles are giving up 164 yards and one receiving touchdown per game to WRs, and they could be without top CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) in Week 5, which would make things easier for some combination of Meyers, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Josh Cameron.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jakobi Meyers is averaging 40 yards per game and has scored twice through five outings heading into Jacksonville's Week 6 matchup with the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to cover wide receivers, having allowed 193 yards per game and six TDs to the position through five games. Meyers is a distant second on the WR depth chart behind Parker Washington, but the plus matchup makes Meyers a viable flex option.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jakobi Meyers has established himself as the No. 2 WR for the Jaguars behind Parker Washington, putting Meyers firmly in the fantasy flex conversation for a Week 8 home game against the Colts. Meyers is averaging 48 receiving yards on 4.7 targets per game, and he set season highs in both of those categories with 83 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to the Texans prior to a Week 7 bye. The veteran wideout faced the Colts three times last season. Two of those meetings came after Meyers was acquired by the Jaguars in a midseason trade, and he mustered exactly 39 receiving yards in both games while scoring a touchdown in one of those matchups. He has five TDs in 15 regular-season games with Jacksonville.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jakobi Meyers was held to two catches in Week 8 while playing through a hamstring injury. He has had an up-and-down season for the Jaguars while working as the No. 2 WR behind Parker Washington. The Jaguars visit the Ravens on Thursday in Week 9, so Meyers may not have time to regain health on a short week. The injury risk lowers his floor, but he's a passable flex option against a Ravens defense that's giving up 177.6 yards per game to wideouts. Meyers is averaging 3.1 catches for 44.1 yards per game, with two TDs in seven outings.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jakobi Meyers is a strong Week 10 flex play against a Titans defense that has struggled to cover wide receivers. Tennessee is allowing a league-high 15.3 catches for 195 yards per game to the position. Meyers has had an up-and-down season as Jacksonville's No. 2 WR but has trended in the right direction recently, notching two of his three best performances this season for both receiving yards and targets within the last three games. He's more likely to produce a peak than a valley in the first of Jacksonville's two meetings this season against Tennessee's league-worst secondary.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jakobi Meyers ranks second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington in both receiving yards (408) and targets (43), but the gap between Washington and Meyers is far larger than the gap between Meyers and TE Brenton Strange for the role of Trevor Lawrence's No. 2 target. Meyers has exceeded 65 yards just once all season and hasn't scored since Week 3, so he has been a disappointment more often than not for fantasy managers plugging him into a flex spot. He'll have a decent opportunity to end his six-game touchdown drought in Week 11 against a Giants secondary that has allowed WRs to score 11 times in nine games, though the Giants hold wideouts to just 127 yards per game. As usual, Meyers is a fine deep-league flex but not a player to get particularly excited about.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jakobi Meyers has drawn at least six targets in four of Jacksonville's last five games, reaching 10 targets twice over that span. His decent volume as the Jaguars' No. 2 WR makes Meyers an appealing Week 12 flex option against Tennessee's league-worst secondary, which is allowing an average of 16 catches for 210 yards per game to wide receivers. Meyers turned six targets into just three catches for 34 yards in Week 10 at Tennessee, but he's capable of producing a more impressive stat line in this home rematch as he tries to snap a TD drought that dates back to Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Love should continue to lead a high-volume passing attack as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Love finished Week 1 with the second-highest passing yard total of his career (387), completing 21 of 42 passes with two touchdowns and one interception. Most of his success came in the first half, with then two turnovers and virtually no offensive prowess in the fourth quarter. With that being said, Green Bay should continue to rely on the passing offense, especially given that there's no return timeline for RB1 Josh Jacobs (personal). Given that Love was able to find success against one of the best defenses in the game, he should have no problem piecing up a New York unit that allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game (22.1) to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Love will look to make a statement as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Love snuck out a win for Green Bay in Week 2, but a 55.2 percent completion rate for 145 yards, even with a 2:0 TD:INT, was uninspiring against the Jets. The sixth-year gunslinger luckily still sits at 532 passing yards on the year with four touchdowns and one interception, and his high volume only looks to continue with Josh Jacobs' return date uncertain. He'll face an Atlanta defense that gave up 287 passing yards and three touchdowns to Bryce Young this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Love will look to get the Packers back in the win column against Tampa Bay in Week 4. Love posted friendly fantasy numbers in Week 3 even amidst a disappointing loss, completing 52.8 percent of passes for 312 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. The sixth-year quarterback has now thrown two touchdowns in every game so far this season, and he's eclipsed 300 passing yards twice. Love remains a solid, high-volume option moving forward, especially given the struggles of Green Bay's run game. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a top-10 18.3 fantasy points per game to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Love will look to deliver a big win for the Packers in Week 5 against the Bears. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT in a close win over Tampa Bay in Week 4. The veteran quarterback has now completed a career-low 56 percent of passes for 1,041 yards with eight touchdowns and three interceptions this season, with 300 or more passing yards in two of four outings. Love will take on a Chicago defense that's ranked 12th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jordan Love will look to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Love was on fire in a blowout win over the Bears in Week 5, completing 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. After a shaky but still touchdown-heavy start to the season, he's now completed 73 percent or more of his passes in back-to-back weeks and totaled 564 passing yards with a 4:1 TD:INT ratio in that stretch. Love will have the perfect opportunity to replicate his greatness again, as Dallas has ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks (23.8) so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Love will look to keep an electric stretch going as the Packers travel to Detroit in Week 7. Love was solid in another Packers win in Week 6, completing 23 of 41 passes for 276 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, and he also made some noise on the ground with two rushes for 14 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year starter has now thrown for more than 275 yards in four of six games this season, and he's thrown two touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll enter another favorable matchup as the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks on the year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Love will aim to get the Packers back in the win column in Week 8 versus the Panthers. Even with Josh Jacobs back on the field at Detroit in Week 7, Green Bay still leaned on the passing game, with Love completing 27 of 45 passes for 274 yards with a 2:1 TD:INT ratio. He's now thrown for two touchdowns in all but one game this season, but he's still totaled two in every outing. Love should have no problem continuing his success against a Carolina defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy quarterbacks.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jordan Love will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Love stayed hot in a Week 8 win over the Panthers, completing 30 of 41 passes for 288 yards with a 3:1 TD:INT ratio. He's now thrown for 250-plus yards in six of eight games and recorded two or more touchdowns in every outing of the season. Love will face a New England defense that ceded 211 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to his former backup, Malik Willis, this past weekend.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jordan Love will look to keep his MVP campaign rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Love was on fire again in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three passing touchdowns and a 13-yard rushing score. Green Bay's signal caller has now dished out two or more touchdowns and passed for 270 or more yards in each of his last three outings. He'll rematch a Vikings defense that he threw for 387 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against in a Week 1 loss.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jordan Love will travel to take on the Rams in a Week 12 matchup for Green Bay out of the bye. Love and the Packers went into their off week with many questions, with the starting quarterback throwing for 220 yards and a 1:1 TD:INT versus Minnesota in Week 10. Love has still put together an impressive first half of the season, with multiple touchdowns in all but one game and 2,838 passing yards across 10 weeks. Los Angeles has ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign, so Love might have his work cut out for him to return to dominance.

player.seasonOutlook: Love is back for his fourth season as the Packers' starting quarterback. The 2020 first-round pick has emerged as one of the league's best passers (he has finished ninth, fifth and third in QBR during his three seasons as a starter), but that hasn't converted to much fantasy production as of late. After finishing sixth in fantasy points per game in 2023, Love has finished 17th and 21st the past two seasons. A dramatic dip in both passing (19th in pass attempts both years) and rushing (282 yards and one TD total during the two seasons) has been the culprit. Love, who produced just five weekly finishes better than 16th last season, has a limited ceiling in Matt LaFleur's scheme. He's best valued as a back-end QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Spencer Shrader made a 58-yard field goal but also missed an extra point in a confounding performance during the Colts' season-opening loss. The big-legged kicker may not get many opportunities in Week 2 against the Chiefs, especially since the Colts are one of the league's most efficient red-zone teams thanks to the presence of star RB Jonathan Taylor. Shrader is a middling fantasy option, and you can likely find a kicker in a more appealing situation on your league's waiver wire.
outlooksByWeek.3: Spencer Shrader has made all four of his field-goal attempts and five of six extra point tries through two games this season. The Colts are averaging a robust 26.5 points per game, but their success on offense has been overshadowed by a league-worst defensive performance en route to a 0-2 start. Shrader is gaining some streaming appeal heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans, who are allowing 28.0 points per game in the early going after giving up just 17.4 points per game last season. He's a borderline fantasy starter at this point.
outlooksByWeek.4: Spencer Shrader is coming off a heroic performance in the Colts' 19-17 Week 3 win over the Texans, as the kicker overcame an early groin injury to make all four of his field-goal attempts, including a go-ahead 53-yarder with 16 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He's off to an 8-for-8 start this season and has made kicks from as deep as 58 yards. Shrader is making a case for a starting fantasy kicker role, and he'll have a chance to showcase his skills on the international stage in Week 4, when the Colts face the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Scoring opportunities are likely to be plentiful for Shrader since Washington is giving up 30.7 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Spencer Shrader has made all seven of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last two games and all 11 attempts this season. He has been one of the hottest waiver-wire options at kicker over the past couple of weeks and could be worth picking up if he's still available ahead of a Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. The Steelers have allowed eight made field goals in four games and 21.8 points per game. Those who streamed Shrader against Washington in Week 4 may as well keep rolling with him in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Spencer Shrader has emerged as an elite fantasy kicker through five weeks, converting all 12 of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last three games. He's 16-for-16 overall this season, including a perfect 6-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Indianapolis' offense generated plenty of field-goal opportunities in the first half of last season before falling off a cliff in the second half, so the risk of regression is substantial. However, Shrader has an excellent opportunity to keep rolling in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who have allowed 13 field goals through five games, tied with Pittsburgh for the most in the NFL. Keep starting Shrader if you have him.
outlooksByWeek.7: Spencer Shrader has been one of the few bright spots for the 2-4 Colts, converting all of his league-high 18 field-goal attempts through six weeks, including six from beyond 50 yards. His lone blemish on the season is a missed extra point. Indianapolis could struggle to consistently reach scoring range in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game, but Shrader has been too good recently to bench, and the Colts could find themselves kicking more field goals than PATs once again in this difficult matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Spencer Shrader leads the league in field goals made (19) and attempted (21), but he was just 1-for-3 in the Week 7 loss to Minnesota after starting 18-for-18 through six games. The Colts' kicker will attempt to bounce back in Week 8 against the Jaguars, who boast the league's third-stingiest scoring defense, allowing just 17.3 points per game. Shrader has earned some goodwill from fantasy managers with his hot start, but he could find himself back on the waiver wire before long if the misses start to pile up.
outlooksByWeek.9: Spencer Shrader is quickly losing his luster as the reeling Colts continue to struggle on offense. He still leads the league with 19 made field goals, but Shrader has slowed down significantly after an 18-for-18 start through Week 6. Shrader has gone just 1-for-3 on field goal attempts over the past two games while the Colts have been outscored 58-17 in that span. It's tempting to cut bait given his recent downturn, but fantasy managers should give Shrader one more chance to get back on track in Week 9 against the Cowboys, who are giving up 26.6 points per game, which is the sixth-most in the NFL.
