outlooksByWeek.10: Spencer Shrader leads the league in field goals made and attempted, even with his volume and effectiveness dropping off in recent weeks as the 2-7 Colts continue to struggle as a team. He's 22-for-24 this season but just 4-for-6 over the past three games. Indianapolis faces a Dolphins defense in Week 10 that has allowed 15 made field goals in eight games and 25.0 points per game. If you have Shrader on your roster, you may as well keep starting him.
outlooksByWeek.11: Spencer Shrader has made no more than one field goal in three of the last four games. His recent downturn has knocked Shrader out of first place in field goals made and attempted, though he's still top-three in both categories thanks to a torrid start that has the Colts' kicker at 23-for-25 through 10 games. That strong start included a 4-for-4 Week 3 performance against the Texans, whom Shrader will face again in Week 11. The Colts' offense has been depleted by a few trades and will likely struggle to generate consistent kicking opportunities moving forward, but Shrader is viable in Week 11 since Houston ranks in the middle of the pack with 24.3 points allowed per game and 18 made field goals against. If you see an enticing alternative on your league's waiver wire, it may be time to move on from Shrader.
outlooksByWeek.12: Spencer Shrader's stellar start is a distant memory. The struggling kicker has gone just 6-for-10 on field-goal attempts over the past five games after making all 18 of his attempts through Week 6. Indianapolis has switched QBs from Daniel Jones to Anthony Richardson after dropping six of its last seven games, but moving the ball will likely remain difficult for the Colts' underwhelming offense in Week 12 against the Giants, who allow the seventh-fewest scrimmage yards (310.5) and 12th-fewest points (21.4) per game. Shrader is a risky Week 12 fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashee Rice took advantage of his limited volume in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, catching both his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown. Patrick Mahomes didn't have to throw much, as Kenneth Walker had a career-best day on the ground and the team had a comfortable lead in the second half. Better performances should be ahead for Rice in more favorable game scripts, but returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy could also be planning to lean on his running game more heavily than in years past. Rice will look to follow in Zay Flowers' footsteps in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in points per game allowed to WRs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashee Rice's volume ticked up in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 4-83-0 line on six targets. Xavier Worthy has been getting more looks from Patrick Mahomes, and Rice's targets have mainly come very close to the line of scrimmage. He's got the run-after-catch ability to turn those short receptions into big gains, but he may not be a high-volume option in an offense that has prioritized Kenneth Walker and the running game. Rice will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashee Rice hasn't yet put together a breakout game for Kansas City in 2026. The fourth-year wide receiver has a solid 13-190-1 line on 17 targets through three weeks, but Patrick Mahomes hasn't focused on any one pass catcher and has been spreading the ball around effectively. Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets. Rice could have a hard time improving on his numbers in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashee Rice picked up a minor hamstring strain and was limited to just six snaps in Kansas City's Week 4 win over the Raiders, but coming out of a Week 5 bye, the issue may not cost him any further time. In his first three games of the season, Rice produced a 13-190-1 line on 15 targets, and his volume could increase with speedster Tyquan Thornton out due to an ankle injury that could sideline him for the remainder of the year. Rice could pop for big numbers in Week 6 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashee Rice wasn't able to get healthy over Kansas City's Week 5 bye, and the wide receiver sat out a Week 6 win over the Chargers due to knee and hamstring issues. His absence didn't significantly affect the offense as Kenneth Walker dominated against the Chargers. In his three full games this season, Rice has produced a 13-190-1 line on 17 targets. If he's able to return in Week 7, he'll have a tough matchup against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rashee Rice continues to work his way back from a hamstring strain, missing his second straight game in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. Before getting injured in Week 4, Rice had produced an 11-171-0 line on 15 targets over the prior two games. Once he's cleared to return, he should immediately be Patrick Mahomes' top option in the passing game. If Rice does get back in the lineup in Week 8, he'll be facing a Broncos secondary that could once again be without Pat Surtain but still ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rashee Rice returned in Week 8 from a two-game absence due to a hamstring issue and caught his second touchdown of the season in Kansas City's loss to the Broncos. In four full games this season, Rice has managed a 20-243-2 line on 25 targets as Patrick Mahomes' top downfield option, but he has yet to receive double-digit targets in any game. That's a volume he reached four times in eight contests in 2025. Rice will look to put the injury further behind him in Week 9 against a Jets secondary that ranks 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Rashee Rice put together another quiet performance in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, catching five of seven passes for 49 yards. The fourth-year wide receiver has a 12-102-1 line on 15 targets over the last two weeks since returning from a two-game absence due to lower-body injuries, and his breakout potential could be limited even further if Patrick Mahomes misses any time after picking up an elbow injury against the Jets. Rice will try to make a bigger contribution in Week 10 against a Falcons secondary that just traded away safety Jessie Bates and ranks 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Rashee Rice's role and volume did not change much in Week 10 against the Falcons, even with trade deadline acquisition Josh Downs in the lineup for Kansas City. Rice caught five of six targets for 82 yards, the third time in seven games he's recorded at least 80 receiving yards. The fourth-year wide receiver is the top downfield option for Patrick Mahomes, but his 30-374-2 line on 38 targets is far from elite production. Rice will look to take a step forward in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Rashee Rice continues to handle a steady role in the Kansas City passing attack. Over four games since returning from a hamstring injury, the fourth-year wide receiver has caught at least five passes each time out, producing a 23-237-1 line on 27 targets. Patrick Mahomes appears to be back in peak form, but that hasn't yet translated into a ceiling game for Rice, who has yet to haul in more than 88 yards in any game this year and has only two touchdowns in eight appearances. Rice will look to break out in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Rice enters Year 4 of his career still seeking his first full season as a starter. The 2023 second-round pick was sidelined for most of 2024 due to injury and missed nine games last season due to suspension (Weeks 1-6) and injury (Weeks 16-18). The good news is that Rice remained highly productive when active. He handled 9.8 targets per game and was a top-12 fantasy receiver in five of his eight outings in 2025. Rice is Patrick Mahomes' top target, and his 8.0 RAC is tops among qualified receivers over the past three seasons. With Mahomes (ACL recovery) ready to go in Week 1 as expected, Rice finds himself in the WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town for a Week 5 home tilt. He played 75% of snaps on offense and caught three of five targets for 17 yards and his second touchdown of the season. Fellow tight end Darnell Washington (3-27-1) was slightly more productive while playing 70% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like it'll be a toss-up between the two on any given week as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 6. He played 38 snaps on offense (70%) and was highly productive, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two of Aaron Rodgers' three TD passes during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Freiermuth finished third on the team in receptions and yardage, while his seven looks were the second-most. Fellow starting tight end Darnell Washington was on the field for 34 offensive snaps (63%) and caught two of three targets for 12 yards. Freiermuth recorded a second consecutive outing with a score and now has four TDs on the season, and he'll aim to take advantage of a Tampa Bay defense allowing 15.7 fantasy points per game (22nd) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers travel to Paris to take on the Saints in Week 7. He caught two of three targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime in Week 6. Freiermuth and fellow tight end Darnell Washington each played 71% of snaps on offense, but it was the latter who made the bigger impact in this one, as Washington tallied a 4-25-1 line on six targets. Freiermuth will try to rebound versus a New Orleans defense that just surrendered six receptions for 99 yards and a TD to Isaiah Likely.
outlooksByWeek.8: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers return home to host the Browns for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He caught two of four targets for 20 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 win in Paris. Freiermuth played 34 offensive snaps to fellow TE Darnell Washington's 36, but the two have been essentially neck-and-neck in playing time through seven outings this season. Freiermuth will aim to stand out versus Cleveland's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (13.9) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.10: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers travel to Cincinnati for an AFC North showdown in Week 10. He caught both of his targets for 35 yards and rushed once for a one-yard touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 8 victory. Freiermuth finished second on the team in yardage and accounted for one of three rushing TDs despite playing only 53% of the offensive snaps. Over his last three contests, he strung together a 6-66-0 receiving line on nine targets to go along with his one-yard TD run, securing two receptions in each outing. Freiermuth could struggle to hit paydirt for the sixth time this season in a matchup versus a Bengals defense that's given up only one score to opposing TEs through eight games.
outlooksByWeek.11: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Eagles for an in-state showdown in Week 11. He caught two of three targets for 35 yards and one touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss, making it two straight outings with a score. Freiermuth fought hard to break the goal line on his 27-yard TD reception, even with his team down big in the fourth quarter. He played 53% of the offensive snaps compared to 50% for Darnell Washington, so snap counts have essentially been a coin flip between the two tight ends. Freiermuth is a tough sell for fantasy managers in a matchup versus Philadelphia's defense, as they're tied for the fourth-fewest points allowed per game (10.5) to opposing TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers battle the Broncos at home on Black Friday in Week 12. He caught all five targets for 39 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Freiermuth has recently been more involved on offense than fellow tight end Darnell Washington as Washington finished with a 3-22-0 line on three targets. Freiermuth remains a TD-or-bust fantasy option and he'll face a Denver defense that's allowed the third-most receiving yards (702) and eight TDs (T-27th) to opposing TEs in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylin Noel finished second on the Texans with 53 receiving yards in the season opener despite being targeted just twice. Noel will need to earn a larger role to gain fantasy relevance, but he has a chance to do so given Houston's lack of a clear No. 2 WR behind Nico Collins. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte combined for eight targets in Week 1 but recorded only 53 receiving yards between the two of them, matching Noel's yardage total. Noel can't be trusted as a starter heading into a Week 2 home game against the Bengals, but the 2025 third-round draft pick could be worth stashing, especially in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylin Noel could see extra opportunities in Week 3 if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a second consecutive game against the Colts. Noel has just three catches this season, but two of them have exceeded 30 yards. The 2025 third-round pick's big-play ability makes him a viable deep-league option in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two games. Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jared Wayne are the other healthy options in Houston's WR room.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylin Noel is a deep-league dart throw for Week 4 against the Cowboys, especially if top Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) is sidelined for a third consecutive game. Noel is tied for fifth on the team with nine targets through three games, but he leads all of Houston's WRs with 11.2 yards per target. Given the Texans' lack of production from the position in Collins' absence, it would be sensible to give Noel more opportunities. Whether they materialize is another matter, and Noel's limited usage so far this season suggests he'll be tough to trust in Week 4, even against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 387 scrimmage yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylin Noel turned three targets into 85 yards for the Texans in their Week 4 loss to Dallas, and the 2025 third-round pick continues to make the most of his opportunities. Heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans, Noel has caught eight of 12 targets for 186 yards while leading the league with 23.3 yards per reception. Noel's big-play potential makes him worth a flier in deeper formats against a Titans secondary that has been prone to breakdowns, but he hasn't garnered consistent enough volume from C.J. Stroud to be started comfortably in any matchup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylin Noel continues to make the most of his opportunities for the Texans. The 2025 third-round pick has caught every pass thrown his way in four of five games this season, leads the team with 17.5 yards per catch and just scored his first TD of the campaign while tying his season high with five targets in the Week 5 win over Tennessee. Noel's arrow is pointing up ahead of a Week 6 matchup against a Jacksonville defense that's allowing a league-high 204 receiving yards per game to WRs, though his floor remains low due to modest volume, as he has earned just 17 targets through five games. He's a boom-or-bust Week 6 flex option for managers in deeper leagues or in search of a bye-week plug-in.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylin Noel has made the most of his opportunities all season, and Houston's 2025 third-round pick has started to earn a larger role in recent weeks. He takes a two-game touchdown streak into Week 7 against the Giants. Noel has caught all 12 of his targets for 233 yards over the past three games after posting five catches for 101 yards on nine targets through Week 3. Nico Collins remains the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game, and the role of trade acquisition Marvin Harrison should grow moving forward, but Noel's recent success makes him a viable Week 7 flex play against a Giants secondary that has allowed seven receiving TDs to WRs in six games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaylin Noel sustained a season-ending toe injury in Houston's Week 7 loss to the Giants. The 2025 third-round pick can be dropped in all redraft formats ahead of Houston's Week 9 road game against the Chargers. Noel was gaining momentum prior to getting hurt, so he has some forward-looking value in dynasty and keeper formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre Tucker was fairly quiet in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, catching two of four targets for 27 yards. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, project to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Tucker isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre Tucker produced his first ceiling game of 2026 in the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers. churning out a 5-119-1 line on seven targets. The volatile wideout is showing some early chemistry with new quarterback Kirk Cousins, and no one else has yet shown any indication that they'll be able to challenge him for the top spot on the depth chart, even if Tucker's skill set would be better suited for a WR2 or even WR3 role. Tucker will try to build on last week's effort in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre Tucker remains in the top spot on the Raiders' wide receiver depth chart, but he's a boom-or-bust option. After popping for a big game in Week 2, Tucker fell back to a 4-43-0 line on just four targets in a Week 3 win over the Saints. With Las Vegas off to a 3-0 start, changes in the offensive mix aren't likely, but Tucker simply doesn't have the physical tools to consistently get open and win 1-on-1 matchups in the NFL. Another rare ceiling game is unlikely in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre Tucker handled a season-high eight targets in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, but he turned them into just four catches for 44 yards. The fourth-year wideout has reached 50 receiving yards only once in four games to begin the season, producing a 15-233-1 line on 23 targets. With a healthy Brock Bowers back as Kirk Cousins' No. 1 option, Tucker's chances of another ceiling game have shrunk. He'll face a Patriots secondary in Week 5 that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tre Tucker has hauled in at least four passes in four straight games as the Raiders' top wide receiver, although he plays a clear second fiddle to tight end Brock Bowers in the passing game. Tucker has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in three of those games, and his only touchdown came during his Week 2 eruption against the Chargers. The fourth-year wideout will have a ceiling game once in a blue moon, but his weekly floor is low, at least while Kirk Cousins remains under center instead of rookie Fernando Mendoza. Tucker will try to get enough volume to take advantage of a Week 6 matchup against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tre Tucker continues to build chemistry with Kirk Cousins. The Raiders' No. 1 wide receiver hauled in two touchdowns in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, and through six games Tucker has produced a 24-371-3 line on 35 targets, putting him on pace for his first 1,000-yard effort. Tight end Brock Bowers remains the top option in the passing game, and Tucker has yet to record more than eight targets in a game in 2026. The prospect of Fernando Mendoza replacing Cousins under center at some point offers additional uncertainty for Tucker. He'll have a hard time delivering another ceiling game in Week 7 against a Rams secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tre Tucker is on his way to a career-best season with Kirk Cousins under center for the Raiders. The fourth-year wideout has caught 10 of 19 targets for 200 yards and three touchdowns over the last two games, and through seven contests Tucker sports a 29-474-4 line on 47 targets. Brock Bowers is still the team's top downfield threat, but Tucker is establishing himself as a strong No. 2 option, although the eventual switch at QB to rookie Fernando Mendoza could change things. Tucker will look to keep rolling in Week 8 against a Jets secondary that is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tre Tucker put his boom-bust tendencies on full display in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets, failing to catch his only look from Kirk Cousins one week after producing a 5-103-1 line on 12 targets against the Rams. Tucker is Las Vegas' top option at wide receiver, but Brock Bowers is the focal point of the passing attack, and Michael Mayer and Ashton Jeanty get their share of the target volume as well. Tucker is still on pace for a career-best campaign with a 29-474-4 line on 48 targets through eight games, but his floor will always be risky. He'll look to bounce back in Week 9 against a 49ers secondary that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tre Tucker caught at least four passes for the seventh time in the last eight games during the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers, hauling in four of eight targets for 55 yards. The fourth-year wide receiver has been a boom-or-bust option throughout his career, and 2026 is no exception. In his three best performances, he's amassed a 15-319-4 line on 26 targets, but he hasn't reached 60 receiving yards or found the end zone in any of his other six contests. Tucker isn't likely to deliver a ceiling game in Week 10 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tre Tucker didn't show much chemistry with Fernando Mendoza in the rookie quarterback's first NFL start, catching just one of two targets for nine yards in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. He remains the team's top wide receiver, and with Brock Bowers now dealing with an ankle injury, there could be less competition for targets in the short term. Tucker produced a 34-538-4 line on 58 targets through the first nine games of the year, mainly with Kirk Cousins under center. He'll try to establish that kind of rapport with Mendoza in Week 11 against a Broncos secondary that ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tre Tucker has yet to get on the same page as new starting quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Tucker recorded 10 targets in the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos, but he was able to haul in just two for 50 yards. Meanwhile, Jack Bech posted an 8-88-1 line on nine targets, and he may be making a push to replace Tucker as the team's No. 1 wide receiver. Tucker will attempt to prove he deserves to continue seeing high volume from Mendoza in Week 12 against a Browns secondary that ranks 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: A team's No. 1 wide receiver is often a household name, but that's certainly not the case for the underrated Tucker, Las Vegas' top wideout for most of the 2025 season. Tucker has finished in the top 10 among wide receivers in both snaps and routes each of the last two seasons and ranked just outside of the top 30 in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns in 2025. Tucker, who also contributes as rusher, has yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign while working in the Raiders' struggling offenses and would need a terrific rookie season from Fernando Mendoza to get there in 2026. That's a long shot for the undersized receiver, so he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keaton Mitchell couldn't capitalize on his preseason buzz in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. He got only four carries, turning them into a mere nine yards, and failed to see a target. The former Raven is the clear backup to Omarion Hampton in the backfield, but Mitchell may need much more favorable game scripts to get meaningful volume. He'll try to contribute in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keaton Mitchell has taken a clear backseat to Omarion Hampton in the Chargers' backfield to begin the season, getting 10 touches to his teammate's 37 through two games. Mitchell has yet to do much to earn a larger role, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, although he does have a 15-yard gain on his only catch. Hampton has lost a fumble in each game so far in 2026, and these ball security issues could open the door for Mitchell to get more involved. If he does see more volume in Week 3, Mitchell could hit paydirt against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keaton Mitchell could be moving into a bigger role in the Chargers' backfield. While the offense as a whole is struggling, the former Raven logged a season-high eight carries in Week 3 and turned them into 52 rushing yards. He also made his first trip to the end zone in 2026, getting a one-yard shovel pass from Justin Herbert on a jet sweep. Omarion Hampton is struggling to adapt to new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, and that's opening the door for Mitchell to push his way into a timeshare in the backfield. However, neither back is likely to make a splash in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keaton Mitchell's role in the Chargers' backfield continues to grow. The former Raven handled a season-high 15 touches in a Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, turning them into 63 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton produced 53 yards and a rushing TD on 11 touches, and Kimani Vidal added 36 yards and a receiving score on seven touches. That split points toward offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel moving into a full-blown backfield committee, and while Mitchell's volume has been trending up, he hasn't done much yet to make a case for the No. 1 spot on the depth chart. He'll look to make his own trip to the end zone in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keaton Mitchell is coming off a disappointing Week 5 performance against the Broncos, as he turned nine touches into a modest 29 scrimmage yards. He was outgained by both Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal as the Chargers' backfield devolves into a full committee, but none of the three have made a strong case to seize the clear No. 1 role. Mitchell flashed big-play potential during his time with the Ravens, but working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line won't generate many holes. He'll try to produce in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Keaton Mitchell's usage declined in Week 6, prior to the Chargers' bye. After averaging nearly 12 touches per game in the preceding two weeks, Mitchell had two carries for just four yards, while Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal handled bigger workloads. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is scrambling to find answers, so Mitchell is expected to get more chances to prove he deserves a consistent role. However, so far in 2026, he hasn't produced more than 52 rushing yards or 63 scrimmage yards in a game. In Week 8, he will take on a Rams defense that is tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Keaton Mitchell remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Omarion Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Mitchell got seven touches and Kimani Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Mitchell is still looking for his first rushing TD of the season, and his current usage holds little appeal. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Keaton Mitchell made a bit of noise as a pass catcher in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, catching three of four targets for 34 yards while turning seven carries into 33 yards. He remains mired in a backfield committee, with Omarion Hampton gaining a team-high 60 rushing yards on 13 carries while Kimani Vidal chipped in 36 scrimmage yards on eight touches. There have been few signs that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will shift away from the arrangement, either due to individual performance or game script, which limits the ceiling of all three backs. Mitchell will try to take advantage of what opportunities he gets in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Keaton Mitchell nearly disappeared from the Chargers' game plan in their first win of the season. During a Week 10 victory over the Ravens, he failed to catch his only target and eked out just four rushing yards on three carries, after handling 17 total touches in the prior two contests. Omarion Hampton, meanwhile, broke out for 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries, potentially ending the team's backfield committee in decisive fashion. Mitchell will try to make a splash on what touches he gets in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Keaton Mitchell has fallen into a depth role in the Chargers' backfield. After getting double-digit touches as recently as Week 9 against the Texans, he's handled just three carries and one catch over the last two games while Omarion Hampton re-staked his claim to the No. 1 job. Mitchell also picked up a knee injury in Week 11, which could leave Kimani Vidal without any competition in the short term for the backup role. If Mitchell is able to suit up in Week 12, he'll be facing a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell signed with the Chargers after spending his first three NFL seasons with Baltimore. The 2023 UDFA will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind starter Omarion Hampton. Mitchell has been limited to 140 touches over his first three NFL seasons, but he has been extremely productive when called upon. His career 6.34 yards per carry ranks second and his 2.50 YAC fourth among 89 backs with 100-plus carries since 2023. He has also put up 184 yards on 23 targets (8.0 YPT). Mitchell is on the small side, so his ceiling is likely capped (he has never cleared 11 touches in a game), but the 24-year-old would be worth adding should Hampton miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dylan Sampson and the Browns are in Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers in Week 2. Unfortunately for the second-year pro, he's expected to miss "significant time" with a left knee injury sustained in Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. The severity of his injury is still being evaluated, but there's a high chance of him being placed on IR once more information comes out.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. The second-year running back, who has been on injured reserve with a knee injury since September 15, could potentially return to practice ahead of their matchup with Baltimore. Head coach Todd Monken said Monday that there's a "possibility" Cleveland opens the 21-day practice window for Sampson this week. If he's able to get back on the field, it couldn't come at a better time for the Browns, as they're currently dealing with injuries to Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Raheim Sanders (hip) sustained in Week 5's loss. It would be wise to monitor the practice reps for the entire backfield as they prepare for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dylan Sampson and the Browns travel to face the division-rival Steelers in Week 8. He rushed six times for 45 yards and caught all three targets for another 32 yards during Cleveland's Week 7 win. Sampson made his first appearance since Week 1 due to a knee injury that forced him to be placed on IR. Quinshon Judkins (ankle) also returned from a one-game absence and out-touched Sampson 18-9, but it was still encouraging for Sampson to take advantage of his opportunities. He'll look to build upon this showing versus a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dylan Sampson and the Browns return home to face off against Houston in Week 10. He had eight carries for 21 yards and caught three of six targets for 27 yards during Cleveland's Week 9 overtime loss. Sampson finished tied for second on the team in targets, and with the Browns' offense likely to play from behind most weeks, he could provide a boost as the preferred back on passing downs. Sampson will aim to contribute more facing a Houston defense allowing 22.4 fantasy points per game (20th) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the Raiders on Sunday Night Football in Week 12. He rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Sampson was out-touched 13-8 by starter Quinshon Judkins, but Sampson continues to push closer to an even timeshare. Sampson will look to contribute more versus a Las Vegas defense allowing 26.9 fantasy points per game to RBs, the fifth most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Sampson is back for Year 2 in Cleveland after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he struggled on a small sample of work as a rusher (his 2.69 yards per carry was dead last among 65 qualified backs), but was a contributor in the passing game (23rd among RBs with 33 receptions). Sampson was a young rookie (he doesn't turn 22 until September), so there's still some room for growth, and he's positioned for a larger role behind Quinshon Judkins with Jerome Ford no longer on the roster. Expect Sampson to see some change-of-pace carries and a moderate pass-catching role in 2026. He'll land on the flex radar only if Judkins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Denzel Boston and the Browns travel to battle the Buccaneers in Week 2. The rookie pass-catcher corralled two of four targets for 59 yards and a TD during Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss. Boston's touchdown was a 46-yard dime from Deshaun Watson, and he finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He draws a tough matchup against Tampa Bay, which ranked fourth in receptions allowed to WRs (8).
outlooksByWeek.3: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Panthers in a Week 3 clash between 1-1 teams. The rookie followed up his 2-59-1 receiving line in the opener with an even better outing against the Buccaneers, tallying five catches on seven targets for 95 yards and another TD. Boston led the team in yardage and targets, as he's quickly becoming Deshaun Watson's preferred target, particularly downfield. He faces a vulnerable Carolina defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (30.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Steelers and their eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs in Week 4. The rookie wideout caught two of four targets for 41 yards and scored on a two-point conversion during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Boston finished second on the team in yardage behind Harold Fannin Jr. (51) as he continues to develop chemistry with QB Deshaun Watson. He's shaping up to be a boom-or-bust fantasy option but offers plenty of upside as the Browns' deep option for an improving offense.
outlooksByWeek.5: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road to take on the Jets in Week 5. He caught four of seven targets for a team-high 89 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. Boston tied for third in targets and continued to prove himself as a big-play option, generating 60 yards on one reception that helped set up a Browns' touchdown run. He'll face a strong Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 6. He caught three of seven targets for 46 yards, including a 29-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, during Cleveland's 17-12 Week 5 loss. The rookie wideout continues to shine for the Browns, as he now has a 16-330-3 line on 29 targets through five games to begin his career. With KC Concepcion (concussion) questionable for Week 6, Boston should remain Deshaun Watson's top target versus Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road for an interconference clash against the Titans in Week 7. He caught just one of five targets for 15 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 6. Boston tied for last in receptions but finished second in targets, as Deshaun Watson completed only 16 of his 26 pass attempts. It's still a positive sign that the Browns want to get the ball in the rookie's hands despite the meager offensive output. Boston will aim to bounce back versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Denzel Boston and the Browns head to Pittsburgh for an AFC North clash in Week 8. He hauled in three of eight targets for 27 yards in Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Boston finished third on the team in targets but was a distant fourth in yardage behind fellow rookie KC Concepcion (129), Harold Fannin Jr. (91) and Dylan Sampson (32). Boston will look to rebound against a Steelers defense he posted a 4-89-0 receiving line on seven targets back in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.10: Denzel Boston and the Browns welcome the 3-5 Texans to town in Week 10. He corralled six of seven targets for 98 yards during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. Boston just missed the 100-yard mark but established a new career high in receiving yards, pacing his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He showed great rapport with Shedeur Sanders, who earned his first start of the season, but Deshaun Watson (concussion) is likely to return from a one-game absence to face his former team. Boston will look to build upon this effort against a Houston defense allowing the third-most fantasy points per game (38.5) to opposing WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the 4-7 Raiders on Sunday Night Football in Week 12. He brought in one of two targets for 16 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 10. Boston struggled while appearing to aggravate a toe injury in the victory, but hopefully, the rookie has had enough time to get close to 100% following the team's bye. Boston will aim to find the end zone for the first time since Week 5 against a Las Vegas defense that's given up 13 TDs to the position, tied for fourth most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of April's draft. He is a big receiver with terrific ball skills and touchdown-scoring upside. He's not the fastest, but that didn't stop him from producing 62-plus receptions, 830-plus yards and nine-plus TDs during both of his seasons as a starter at Washington. He handled 45% of his team's air yards in 2025 (highest in this rookie class). Boston dropped only four of 209 career targets (1.9% drop rate is fourth best in this WR class) and has the look of a reliable possession receiver. He'll begin his career battling Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie KC Concepcion for targets in a Cleveland offense yet to sort out its quarterback situation. Boston is a fine late-round-upside flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ladd McConkey seemed headed for a big performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching five of seven targets for 81 yards and a touchdown. However, he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter after a big hit left him with a rib injury. McConkey still led the team in receiving yards and was on the receiving end of Justin Herbert's only TD pass, and the club doesn't seem to believe the injury is serious. His status for Week 2 will remain up in the air until later in the week, if not right up to kickoff. If he is able to suit up, McConkey will be facing a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ladd McConkey was clearly limited by a rib injury in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, catching all three of his targets for 35 yards. That was still good enough to tie for the team lead in receptions, however, as Justin Herbert and the entire offense continue to adjust to the new scheme instituted by OC Mike McDaniel. McConkey is Herbert's clear top downfield option, and as he gets healthier, his production should begin to look more like the 5-82-1 line he delivered in the season opener before getting hurt in the third quarter. McConkey will get a favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ladd McConkey seemed hampered by his rib injury in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, but he still managed to turn five targets into four catches for 66 yards. The clear top option for Justin Herbert, McConkey has 15 targets through three games despite missing most of the second half in Week 2 after getting hurt, turning that volume into a 12-183-1 line. That's the only touchdown Herbert has thrown to a wide receiver so far in 2026. McConkey should be a little healthier in Week 4, but he'll be facing a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ladd McConkey failed to catch either of his targets in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, leaving the game early after aggravating a foot injury he picked up in practice during the week. The third-year wideout was already playing through a rib issue, and an absence of one or more games seems almost assured. The Chargers' passing game has struggled with or without him on the field, but if McConkey does miss time, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris would become Justin Herbert's top downfield options in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ladd McConkey continues to deal with injuries, sitting out the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos with a foot issue after dealing with a rib injury earlier in the season. He hasn't caught a pass since Week 3, but in those first three games, McConkey managed a 12-183-1 line on 15 targets as Justin Herbert's clear No. 1 option. The rest of the team's wide receiver room is also banged up, which could give the team extra incentive to get McConkey back in the lineup as quickly as possible. Even if he suits up in Week 6, he'll struggle to contribute against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ladd McConkey has only missed one game so far in 2026, but injuries have marred the season for the Chargers' top wide receiver, and he comes out of the team's bye still in the league's concussion protocol. The offense as a whole has struggled, but McConkey's been productive when reasonably healthy, posting a 12-182-1 line on 15 targets over the first three weeks. If he's cleared to return in Week 8, he'll take on a stingy Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ladd McConkey came out of the Chargers' bye looking healthy, and he was one of the few bright spots on offense for the team in a Week 8 loss to the Rams. The third-year wideout caught four of six targets for 86 yards, and over six games this season -- only two of which he saw a full snap share in -- he's produced a 17-286-1 line on 24 targets. If McConkey can stay on the field, he figures to continue being Justin Herbert's top downfield option, on a winless team that's been trailing early and often in 2026. McConkey will face an underperforming Texans secondary in Week 9 that ranks a stunning 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ladd McConkey didn't log any snaps in the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, as back spasms during pregame workouts kept him on the sideline. The third-year wide receiver has seen a full workload in just two of the seven games he's been active for, and with the team winless on the season, there's little incentive for the Chargers to take any risks with his health. McConkey has been productive when he's been in the lineup, but it's becoming harder to predict when that will be. If he manages to play in Week 10, he'll be facing a Ravens secondary that's tied for 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ladd McConkey missed his third game of the season in Week 10, this time due to back trouble, as the Chargers' beat the Ravens for their first win of the season. McConkey's been fully healthy for only two games so far in 2026, posting an 8-152-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, and his only touchdown of the year came back in the first half of Week 1 before he suffered his initial rib injury, which was followed by a foot injury and a concussion. If McConkey is cleared to return in Week 11, he'll face a Jets secondary that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Ladd McConkey made his mark in the red zone during the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets, catching five of eight targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns. The third-year wide receiver hadn't found the end zone since Week 1 as he endures an injury-plagued season, but when he's been in the lineup, he's been Justin Herbert's clear top option. Unfortunately, it could be Herbert's turn on the sideline, as the quarterback was diagnosed with a concussion after the loss to the Jets. McConkey's outlook would get a big downgrade if DJ Uiagalelei is under center for his first career NFL start, but regardless of who is throwing him the ball, he'll be facing a Patriots secondary that ranks an enticing 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: McConkey is looking to rebound after falling short of high expectations in 2025. The 2024 second-round pick was terrific as a rookie (82-1,155-7 receiving line and a 12th-place finish among WRs in fantasy points), but dipped to 66-789-6 line and a 30th-place finish last season. Though he ran considerably more routes, saw similar target numbers and was used a lot more near the goal line (seventh among WRs with 12 end zone targets), McConkey's efficiency plummeted, with his catch rate dipping from 74% to 62% and his yards per target from 10.4 to 7.4. The good news is that there's reason for optimism that he'll bounce back, as he has a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel, the Chargers' offense figures to improve with a much healthier line, and Keenan Allen is out of the picture. McConkey, 24, makes for a fine fantasy WR3.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Jefferson will look to keep it rolling in Week 2 as Minnesota takes on the Bears. Jefferson returned to a fantasy level in Week 1 that he didn't see much of in 2025, reeling in eight of nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns. The star wideout also had a solid connection with veteran Carson Wentz, who came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion). Given that Jefferson still produced with the Vikings' QB2, he could be in line for big games no matter who lines up under center, so long as it isn't J.J. McCarthy. He'll face a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Jefferson will look to rebound from a quieter week as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jefferson was held to three catches for 55 yards against the Bears in Week 2, but the game was played in bad weather and ended with a 9-3 score. The superstar pass catcher has 11 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he could increase those numbers twofold against a Bucs defense that ceded 95 yards and a touchdown to Cleveland receiver Denzel Boston this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justin Jefferson will look to return as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Jefferson exited Week 3 against the Buccaneers with an ankle injury, but there don't appear to be any concerns beyond a sprain at this point. The star wideout has totaled 13 catches for 179 yards and two touchdowns on the season even in just five halves, and he's been a major piece of Minnesota's 3-0 start. If he is healthy, Jefferson will face a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against wide receivers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justin Jefferson will aim to make a return for Minnesota's Week 5 clash at New Orleans. Jefferson sat out of the Vikings' Week 4 win over the Dolphins with an ankle injury, but the hope is that his absences will be limited to that game. The star pass catcher has totaled a quieter 13-179-2 receiving line over his first two-plus games, so he'll look to make a bang if he does return to action. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this season, which could provide everything Jefferson needs to deliver.
outlooksByWeek.7: Justin Jefferson remains Minnesota's top target in Week 7 against the Colts. Jefferson put together a solid performance against the Saints in Week 5 before the Vikings' bye, recording six catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. The star pass catcher looks to have a solid connection with quarterback Kyler Murray, which could be even more solid after a week of rest. Indianapolis ceded a 6-70-1 receiving line to Titans' WR1 Carnell Tate in Week 6, which could bode well for Jefferson.
outlooksByWeek.8: Justin Jefferson will look to get back in the end zone as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Jefferson had a quiet performance out of the bye in Week 7, reeling in four of seven targets for 44 yards, which was his second-lowest yardage total of the year. The star wideout has now pieced together a 23-302-3 receiving line across five games this season. He'll have plenty of chances to carve up a Detroit secondary that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Justin Jefferson will aim to ramp up his output as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jefferson brought in five of nine targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in Week 8 against the Lions, finding the end zone for the fourth time this season. The superstar wide receiver is on pace to finish the season with the fewest catches and yards of his career, and he's yet to record a 100-yard receiving game. Luckily, he'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Justin Jefferson will hope to see better play at the QB position in Week 10 as the Vikings travel to Green Bay. Jefferson reeled in just three of his whopping 11 targets for 58 yards in a Week 9 loss to the Bills. The all-out struggles of Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (hamstring), were fully seen in Jefferson's receiving line, but the trade deadline acquisition of Kirk Cousins re-united him with the QB he's had the most success with. The talented wideout doesn't have any 100-yard games and has posted less than 60 yards in five of seven games. Jefferson will face a Packers defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to the wide receiver position this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Justin Jefferson could be in store for better output again as the Vikings play San Francisco in Week 11. Jefferson benefited from the addition of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota in a Week 10 win over Green Bay, logging season highs in catches (9) and targets (13). The star wideout's 74 yards were also his best total since Week 5, further supporting that he may be in store for a return to dominance. He'll take on a 49ers defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.12: Justin Jefferson will look to get back in the end zone as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Jefferson has benefited greatly from the reintroduction of Kirk Cousins in the last two weeks, totaling 16 catches for 142 yards in that stretch. The star pass catcher has now put together a 47-553-4 receiving line over nine games, which could be greatly improved in the coming weeks if he keeps a strong connection with Cousins. He'll shift his attention to an Atlanta defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After finishing in the top 10 among receivers in fantasy PPG during each of his first five seasons, Jefferson plummeted to 30th in 2025. The fall was, of course, unrelated to Jefferson's ability, as the team's quarterback woes limited the star receiver to career-low showings in yardage (1,048), touchdowns (two), catch rate (60%) and yards per target (7.4). Jefferson's fall came despite him seeing a career-high 30.1% target share and ranking in the top six at the position in targets (141) and end zone targets (15). The 27-year-old remains an elite player, but the quarterback concerns aren't fully solved, with dual-threat Kyler Murray (one receiver managed a top-25 fantasy campaign during his time as a starter in Arizona) set to work as the starter. Perhaps Murray can ignite Jefferson similar to how he did DeAndre Hopkins at times, but there's certainly some risk. Jefferson is best considered as a mid-range WR1.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens was second on the Cowboys in targets last game.  Pickens managed six catches for just 40 yards, though, as CeeDee Lamb went wild for Dallas. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. The task may not get easier in Week 3, as Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Pickens is coming off his best game of the season for the Cowboys. Pickens led Dallas in targets with 11 opportunities, parlaying those looks into seven grabs for 82 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone this season, and his overall numbers remain disappointing following a standout 2025 campaign. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL. Moreover, teammate CeeDee Lamb could be guarded by all-pro corner Derek Stingley Jr., which could free up Pickens for more targets.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Pickens has had back-to-back games with at least 75 yards receiving for the Cowboys. On the downside, Pickens was targeted just three times last game as compared to a staggering 21 targets for fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb. The targets are unlikely to be so lopsided in Week 5 versus the Bucs, but Pickens certainly appears to be playing second-fiddle to the aforementioned Lamb in 2026. Tampa Bay's defense has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Pickens stepped up last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards as he was dealing with a quadriceps issue. As a result, Pickens was the primary target in the passing game and corralled nine of 13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown.  Lamb is not expected to miss the Week 6 clash versus the Packers, though Pickens would benefit even if Lamb is limited. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Pickens led the Cowboys in receiving last game. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly still struggled. Despite 11 looks, Pickens managed just 73 yards on six catches in the 23-13 loss to the Pack. Pickens has an impressive 24 targets over his last two contests alone. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: George Pickens found the end zone last game for Dallas. Pickens snagged four passes for 57 yards and the touchdown. It was his second score in three outings. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: George Pickens was held to just 48 yards receiving last game for Dallas. This was his lowest receiving total since the second week of the season. Pickens has just 10 targets combined over the last two games and was seen leaving the field early following the OT loss to Arizona, meaning there could be trouble in paradise. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: George Pickens did not suit up last game for Dallas due to a hamstring ailment. His status for Week 10 versus the 49ers remains up in the air. Even if Pickens is able to play, he will face a difficult task. The Niners are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: George Pickens snagged three touchdowns last game for the Cowboys. Pickens racked up an incredible 18 targets, parlaying those looks into 11 grabs for 145 yards and the three scores. The targets and receptions set career highs, while the yardage total was his best on the season. In Week 11, Pickens has a delectable matchup against the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: George Pickens crossed the 100-yard threshold yet again for the Cowboys last game. Pickens caught seven passes for 102 yards and a touchdown in the 51-30 dismantling of the Titans. Pickens has gone over the 100-yard receiving mark in two-straight contests, having scored a gaudy four touchdowns during that span. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Saints to town for a Week 2 matchup. Flowers left Baltimore's 41-23 Week 1 win in the second quarter and did not return. He is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury, per head coach Jesse Minter. Soft tissue injuries can be tricky, especially for someone as shifty as Flowers, but it sounds like the issue is not considered serious. He's fresh off posting a career-high 150 receiving yards on five catches (six targets) and a TD, so if the speedster is active against New Orleans, he should see plenty of looks from Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 matchup between 1-1 teams. He was ruled out of Baltimore's Week 2 loss with a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, so his status in practice this week will be something to monitor. If he's able to suit up in Week 3, Flowers will face a Cowboys defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) and 13th in receiving yards allowed to WRs. In his absence, Rashod Bateman put up a 7-88-1 receiving line on nine targets as Lamar Jackson's No. 1 receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Titans to town in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and handled a full workload, catching five of six targets for 84 yards while taking his lone carry for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 3 victory. Flowers led the team in receptions, targets, and yardage, and that should remain the same against Tennessee, which has the 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs. The hamstring issue appears to be behind him for now, but managers will want to keep an eye on his practice reps leading up to Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Zay Flowers looks to continue his hot start in 2026 when the Ravens visit the Falcons in Week 5. He grabbed eight of 10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. The fourth-year wideout owns an 18-352-2 receiving line on 22 targets across three contests. However, if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to suit up, Flowers will be catching passes from Tyler Huntley, who completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson. He'll have the added benefit of facing an Atlanta defense that allows 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs and gave up eight receptions for 116 yards to Chris Olave.
outlooksByWeek.6: Zay Flowers and the Ravens travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He hauled in eight of nine targets for 53 yards during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Flowers paced the team in receptions and targets and was second in yardage, showing a strong rapport with Tyler Huntley, who started in place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle). No matter who's under center, Flowers remains the top receiving threat against Cleveland's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (36.4) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zay Flowers and the Ravens return home for a divisional showdown against the Bengals in Week 7. He caught six of 11 targets for 66 yards and had one carry for one yard during Baltimore's Week 6 loss. Flowers led Baltimore in receptions, yardage, and targets, with no other player earning more than five looks from Tyler Huntley. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question for a third consecutive week, Huntley is in line for his second start under center. Regardless of who is at QB, Flowers will continue operating as the clear-cut No. 1 option in the passing game versus Cincinnati's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (29.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to halt a two-game losing skid when they visit the Bills in Week 8. He caught eight of 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown in Baltimore's 35-13 Week 7 defeat. Flowers led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets by a wide margin, recording the Ravens' only touchdown in the loss. There's a good chance Lamar Jackson (ankle) will return from a three-game absence in Week 8, but Flowers has proven to be a fantasy stud this season no matter who's under center. He'll face a Buffalo defense that surrenders 42.3 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs, the most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Zay Flowers and the Ravens host the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. He was held without a catch on five targets during Baltimore's 36-10 Week 8 loss. With Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both leaving the game with injuries, Flowers struggled mightily to get anything going. The Ravens could be forced to start Joe Fagnano (knee) against the Jaguars' 29th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs, but the uncertainty at the QB position greatly lowers Flowers' fantasy appeal.
outlooksByWeek.10: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are at home to take on the Chargers in Week 10. He brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for another 17 yards during Baltimore's defeat in Week 9. Flowers and his fantasy managers are hoping the acquisition of Jacoby Brissett will provide a boost for the Ravens' passing game, as the former Cardinal will get his first Ravens start on Monday Night Football. Flowers does have a favorable matchup against a Chargers defense allowing 36.9 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to snap a five-game losing streak when they visit the Panthers in Week 11. He corralled six of seven targets for 74 yards but lost a key fumble during Baltimore's Week 10 loss. Flowers turned it over with 2:11 remaining, ultimately ending his team's chance to tie or take the lead. On a brighter note, Jacoby Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards, meaning Flowers should have no shortage of opportunities to make up for the costly mistake versus Carolina's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (31.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Zay Flowers and Baltimore travel to square off against the Texans in Week 12. He caught eight of 11 targets for 97 yards and rushed once for minus-13 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Flowers led his team in receptions, yardage and targets, but it was Rashod Bateman who was on the receiving end of Jacoby Brissett's 52-yard TD pass. Flowers' fantasy stock is on the rise with Brissett under center, and they'll face a favorable matchup against Houston's 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.7) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Flowers' emergence into a star continued in 2025, as the 2023 first-round pick posted career-best marks in target share (29%), targets (118), catches (86) and yardage (1,211). Despite still lacking a role near the goal line (he has never cleared seven end zone targets or six touchdowns in a single season), Flowers finished seventh among receivers in fantasy points (13th PPG), which marks his first finish better than 25th (31st PPG). A highly targeted, short-range RAC specialist, Flowers' ceiling is lower than other top receivers, but the 25-year-old remains positioned as Lamar Jackson's top target in Baltimore's new-look offense. Flowers makes for a solid fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Daniels overcame a slow start to nearly lead the Commanders to a comeback win against the Eagles in Week 1. Daniels finished the contest with 164 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with an additional 31 yards rushing for the game. Daniels will look to build some momentum in Week 2 versus an extremely suspect Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed the most yards in the NFL last season, and the supposedly revamped defense was trounced by the Giants in their 2026 opener. The Cowboys allowed 394 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns in an ugly 28-20 loss to Jaxson Dart and company.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow against the Cowboys in Week 2, the same elbow he injured last year for the Commanders. While the elbow is not fractured, Daniels is almost certain to miss Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. Veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jayden Daniels is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4.  Daniels is unlikely to play versus the Colts due to his dislocated elbow, though, and especially since backup Marcus Mariota just led an improbable victory over the defending Super Bowl champions. Mariota tossed three touchdowns in the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Whoever lines up under center in Week 4 will have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Colts pass defense. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jayden Daniels could return in Week 5 for the Commanders from a dislocated elbow. Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota left Washington's last game with a knee injury, which could hasten the need for Daniels to return versus the Giants. if neither quarterback can suit up, seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis would get the nod. The defense for the Giants looks totally revamped in 2026, allowing 205.3 yards per tilt through the air, which is 10th in the league. The Giants are tied for the league-lead with six interceptions.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jayden Daniels returned from injury and appeared to show no ill effects regarding his previously dislocated elbow. Daniels rushed for over 100 yards and two touchdowns, while also passing for 199 yards against the Giants. Unfortunately, poor game management at the end of overtime cost the Commanders the win, and overshadows what was otherwise a solid return to the lineup for Daniels. Unfortunately, a tall task lurks in Week 6 on the road versus the 49ers. San Francisco is undefeated and allowing just 297.2 scrimmage yards per tilt, which is sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jayden Daniels produced one of his best games of the season before the bye for the Commanders, and will look to build off of that performance in Week 8 versus the Eagles.  Daniels completed 72.5-percent of his passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in a narrow loss to the 49ers. In fact, it was the first time in 2026 that Daniels threw for even 200 yards in a contest. Daniels will face an Eagles defense that has been better against the run than the pass this season.  Philadelphia is allowing 244.5 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.  However, Philadelphia is still surrendering 119.3 yards per game on the ground, which is just 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jayden Daniels has thrown for at least 215 yards in each of the last two games for Washington. He also has three touchdown passes over that span. However, in Week 9, Daniels will face a stellar Rams pass defense.  Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jayden Daniels threw for 274 yards and a touchdown last game for Washington. He has passed for at least one touchdown in three-straight outings, and thrown for at least 270 yards in two of those three contests. In Week 10, he will face a Giants defense that has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL. However, the Giants are surrendering 123.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the league, and Daniels ran for 103 yards and two scores when the two teams met earlier this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jayden Daniels tossed three touchdown passes last game for the Commanders. He also threw his first two interceptions of the season in the thrilling 24-21 win over the Giants. Daniels has thrown for at least 215 yards in four-straight contests. He may be more successful with his legs than with his arm in Week 11 versus the Bengals, though. Cincinnati is allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. By contrast, Cincy is surrendering 123.9 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jayden Daniels did not record a touchdown last game for the Commanders.  However, he threw for 289 yards and rushed for an additional 55 yards in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals. It was the second-highest passing total of the season for Daniels, and his third-highest rushing total of the year. Daniels has a tasty matchup in Week 12 versus a suspect Cardinals defense allowing 355.2 scrimmage yards per game, which is 26th in the NFL. In addition, Arizona is allowing 29.4 points per tilt, which is 31st in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Daniels is looking to bounce back after appearing in only seven games due to injury last season. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year began his career with a bang, tossing 25 touchdowns and adding 891 yards and six scores with his legs in his first season. He wasn't quite as dominant when healthy last season (16.3 points per game, compared to 20.9 in 2024), but he remained a major factor with his legs (58-278-2 in seven games, three of which were partial appearances). Daniels' supporting cast is underwhelming and he'll be working with a new playcaller (David Blough), but the dual-threat ability supplies the 25-year-old with elite upside. He's a strong QB1 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference showdown in Week 2. Jackson was stellar in the opener despite losing a fumble, throwing for 324 yards (17-for-25) with one TD and no picks while rushing seven times for another 40 yards and a TD. Although he still offers elite upside at the QB position, it's important to note that his favorite receiver, Zay Flowers, is dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Jesse Minter considers "day-to-day." The two connected on five of six targets for 150 yards and a score in the victory. The New Orleans defense ranks 12th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.5) to QBs after Jared Goff's 206 yards and two TDs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens look to bounce back after a tough loss when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. Jackson threw for 235 yards (21-for-31) with one TD and one INT while rushing four times for 34 yards in Week 2's 24-17 loss. Baltimore draws a favorable matchup against a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed (27.2) and 31st in rushing yards allowed to QBs. Zay Flowers (hamstring) missed Week 2's contest, but the hope is that Jackson's speedy receiver makes it back on the field in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the 0-3 Titans for a Week 4 showdown.
