In Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win over Dallas in Week 3, he connected on 15 of 20 throws for 186 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 50 yards, including a 27-yard strike to Zay Flowers that helped set up the game-winning field goal as time expired. Tennessee's defense has been stingy, allowing just 13.9 fantasy points per game to QBs through three games, which ranks first. Jackson should have his full complement of receivers available as the Ravens aim to improve to 3-1 on the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens travel to face the Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 5. Prior to missing the entire second half of Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4, the two-time MVP threw for 222 yards (15-for-20) with two TDs and no INTs while rushing twice for 20 yards. Jackson was well on his way to a stellar outing with his team up 24-7 at halftime, but an ankle injury forced him out early and has him in jeopardy of missing the upcoming road tilt in Atlanta. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that the Ravens are uncertain of Jackson's status for Week 5, and if he's unable to suit up, Tyler Huntley will get the nod at quarterback.
outlooksByWeek.6: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. The two-time league MVP sat out Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5 with a sprained left ankle. Head coach Jesse Minter relayed Monday that Jackson is "definitely doing better" in his recovery, but there's still no guarantee that he'll be ready for the trip to Cleveland. Tyler Huntley filled in admirably as the starting QB, throwing for 201 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 20 yards and another score in the OT victory. Jackson will need to practice in some form before the Ravens can determine his status against the Browns' 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Bengals for an AFC North showdown in Week 7. He missed a second consecutive game in Week 6, a 13-10 loss to Cleveland, due to an ankle injury sustained in Week 4. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Jackson could potentially get back on the practice field during Week 7 prep, but Baltimore is still considering their star quarterback day-to-day. If he's unable to suit up for the third straight contest, Tyler Huntley will continue to start under center versus Cincinnati's 19th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.5) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the Bills in Week 8. After missing the last three contests with an ankle injury, he appears to be headed in the right direction, as head coach Jesse Minter stated Jackson is "in a decent spot" to return to action against Buffalo. His practice participation bears monitoring following his limited activity prior to Baltimore's Week 7 loss. If active, Jackson will aim to snap a two-game losing streak versus a Bills defense allowing 26.5 fantasy points per game (30th) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Lamar Jackson is heading to the IR after taking just one snap for the Ravens in Week 9. He missed the prior three contests with a high-ankle injury, and now thumb surgery could end his season. Tyler Huntley took over, but he had to exit with a toe injury, forcing emergency third-string QB Joe Fagnano into action. More will be known about Jackson's status after he goes under a very small knife.

player.seasonOutlook: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel in Week 2 to face the Patriots, who have the ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to RBs. He rushed 10 times for 46 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 20-13 win against Atlanta. Warren lost a fumble, but he still out-touched fellow RB Rico Dowdle 15-10 and had much better results from those opportunities. If the Steelers continue to favor the passing game against New England, or if they're forced into it via game flow, Warren would carry a bit more value in what looks to be a true timeshare.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He rushed 17 times for 127 yards and caught three of four targets for 49 yards during Pittsburgh's thrilling 30-27 victory in Week 3. Warren handled a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out, and it looks like that could again be the case with a short turnaround for Week 4's Thursday Night Football showcase in Cleveland. He'll face a tough matchup as the Browns rank sixth in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs and are one of seven teams yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town in Week 5. He tallied 17 carries for 93 yards while catching three of six targets for 33 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Warren handled a massive workload for the second straight week with Rico Dowdle (toe) on the sidelines. There's a chance Dowdle remains out against Indianapolis, leaving Warren as the unquestioned lead back versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense, which has allowed 24.2 fantasy points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and caught all six of his targets for 87 yards, including an 80-yard TD reception, during Pittsburgh's Week 5 win. Warren continued to handle a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out for the third straight contest. He compiled 490 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 61 touches over that stretch, and head coach Mike McCarthy stated Monday that Warren is viewed as "our featured player right now." Even if Dowdle can suit up versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) in Week 6, Warren is likely to keep working as the lead back for a Steelers offense averaging 29.3 points through their last three outings.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers face off against the Saints in Paris in Week 7. He had 14 carries for 50 yards and caught two of four targets for 28 yards during Pittsburgh's overtime victory in Week 6. With Rico Dowdle (toe) back on the field, Warren's opportunities dipped noticeably despite out-touching Dowdle 16-10. He should still handle a larger volume than Dowdle going forward, but managers should certainly temper expectations as long as both backs are healthy. Warren draws a very favorable matchup against a New Orleans defense that ranks dead last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 divisional clash. He had 18 carries for 101 yards and corralled three of four targets for 36 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 victory in Paris. Fellow running back Rico Dowdle amassed 86 scrimmage yards on 15 touches, and it appears he's rounding into form after missing nearly a month with a toe injury. Warren remains atop the backfield hierarchy, but he'll face a tough test against Cleveland's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Jaylen Warren and the Steelers visit their divisional-rival Bengals on Sunday Night Football. He rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown while catching one of two targets for no gain during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 9. Warren matched his career high for rushing yards and produced his third 100-plus-yard effort in his last four games. In Week 3, he generated 176 scrimmage yards on 20 touches in his first matchup against Cincinnati, so he'll be hungry to put up similar numbers on the road.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Eagles in Week 11. He had seven carries for 15 yards and caught five of six targets for 26 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss. Warren and the entire Steelers offense found little success until the game was already out of reach, as several backups took the field in the fourth quarter. Warren will look to shake off the tough outing, but he'll have to do so against Philadelphia's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to opposing RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Jaylen Warren and the Steelers aim to snap a two-game losing streak when they host the Broncos on Black Friday. He had nine carries for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Warren got 11 touches compared to nine for backfield mate Rico Dowdle, but it was an overall quiet outing for both. The Steelers have shifted to more of a timeshare with Dowdle now fully healthy, leaving Warren as a TD-or-bust option versus Denver's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (24.9) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to serve as one of the Saints' top running backs if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Kamara was sidelined for Week 1 but is expected to return for Week 2, likely operating as the Saints' top receiving back. He could take work away from Travis Etienne, who caught seven of eight targets in last week's overtime loss. Tyler Shough attempted 56 passes in Week 1, which bodes well for Kamara's potential upside as a receiver. He's in for a solid Week 2 matchup as well, with the Ravens defense giving up 5.3 yards per touch to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alvin Kamara is expected to operate as the Saints' top pass-catching back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. In his return from a sprained MCL in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Kamara led the Saints' backfield in carries (nine), targets (six) and receptions (five). Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Even so, the Saints' backfield is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that's allowed just 3.8 yards per carry thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Alvin Kamara will likely be in for a larger offensive role with Travis Etienne (hamstring)  sidelined for New Orleans' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Kamara has received nine carries in each of the last two weeks after sitting out Week 1, but he's struggled with efficiency, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry. Additionally, he saw just one target in the Week 3 loss to the Raiders, suggesting he may not have the same receiving volume as in past years. Regardless, this receiving volume should increase with Etienne out for Week 4. Kamara could still struggle against a Falcons defense that's given up 13.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top running back while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is sidelined during the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. In his first game without Etienne this season, Kamara totaled 58 yards on 12 touches, but his workload was largely impacted by the game script. He led New Orleans' backfield in targets (seven), which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara is in for a tough Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 14.7 fantasy points per game to running backs this season, the fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Despite operating as New Orleans' No. 1 RB over the last two weeks, Kamara logged fewer snaps (12) and carries (three) than Kendre Miller (six carries on 13 snaps) in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings. Additionally, he got fewer targets than Miller (two to three), which is a very negative sign for his outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara could be productive against a Giants defense that's given up just 94 receiving yards but two receiving touchdowns to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Kamara had his best game of the 2026 campaign in a Week 6 win over the Giants, accounting for 69 yards and a touchdown on nine touches. Despite this, he logged just 18 offensive snaps, which is fewer both than Kendre Miller (31) and CJ Donaldson (22). Kamara dealt with an injury in the first half, but with Miller receiving 20 carries, it appears as if Kamara's upside is limited, operating primarily as a receiver out of the backfield. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up just 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top pass-catching running back in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Kamara has received seven targets in two of New Orleans' last four games, proving his value to the team's passing attack. While not the most effective rusher at this stage in his career, Kamara has averaged 43 total yards on 10.5 touches per game through six contests this season. He could struggle against a tough Browns defense that's allowed just 28 total receptions to running backs through eight games this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top pass-catching running back in the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Kamara received fewer than 10 touches for the third time in New Orleans' last four games during the Week 9 win over the Browns, despite backfield mate Kendre Miller being release prior to the contest. Regardless, Kamara ranks first amongst Saints RBs in targets (31), receptions (25), receiving yards (150) and receiving touchdowns (one) in seven appearances this year. He could find success against a Panthers defense that's allowed 230 yards and a touchdown through the air to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Alvin Kamara will remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Kamara was limited to just five touches while Travis Etienne returned from injury in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers. However, Kamara scored two touchdowns on those touches and appeared to be operating as New Orleans' top red-zone RB. With Kamara, Etienne and Audric Estime all playing roles in the Saints' backfield, it may be hard to trust any of them going forward. Kamara could take advantage of a Chicago defense that's allowed 7.3 yards per target and two receiving touchdowns to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Alvin Kamara will likely play a minimal offensive role during the Saints' Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Despite finding the end zone during the Week 11 loss to the Saints, Kamara played just eight offensive snaps while Travis Etienne and CJ Donaldson each played 32. Additionally, Kamara has received just seven touches over the Saints' last two games, suggesting his role in the offense has diminished. Expect Kamara to have minimal value in Week 12 against a Bengals defense that's given up just 294 receiving yards to RBs through nine games this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Kamara is entering his age-31 season set to play a change-of-pace role behind Travis Etienne and is unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue shining in Carolina's Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Coker has shown out in the Panthers last two games (including their wild-card loss to end last season), having recorded a combined 17 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He's outproduced 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and looks to be a major part of Carolina's offense going forward. However, Coker is dealing with an ankle issue and could struggle against a tough Falcons defense that gave up just 5.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's favorite targets in Carolina's Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Coker has been incredibly productive, leading the Panthers in receptions (16) and yards (204) while being tied for first in targets (18) through two weeks. Across his last three games (including playoffs), the third-year pro has caught 25 of 30 targets for 338 yards and two touchdowns, emerging as one of the NFL's top young wideouts. He's in for a very favorable matchup in Week 3 as well, as the Browns' defense has surrendered 7.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top targets if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Coker has dealt with three separate injuries through three weeks this season (ankle, hamstring and quadriceps). Despite this, the third-year wideout has amassed 222 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 18 catches, leading the Panthers in yards and touchdowns. If Coker is able to suit up in Week 4, he's in for an incredibly favorable matchup, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 31.7 points and 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to the WR position this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to return for the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Coker was on a tear to start the season, catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina's first two games. He's expected to continue benefitting from the new, aggressive Panthers offense, led by Bryce Young, who's averaging 40.5 passing attempts per game this year. Coker will likely find success if active in Week 6 against an Eagles defense that's given up seven touchdowns to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. In Coker's three full games this season, he's caught 22 of 31 targets for 301 yards and two touchdowns. With Young averaging 40.2 passing attempts per game, it appears as if Coker will continue to produce at a high level going forward. Additionally, he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Tampa Bay secondary that's allowed five touchdowns to wideouts through six games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jalen Coker (shoulder) is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's top targets if active for Carolina's Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Coker underwhelmed in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, catching just one of four targets for nine yards, his least productive game since Week 7 of 2025. Coker has been one of the league's best wideouts when healthy this season, averaging 5.8 receptions and 77.5 yards per game in his four full games in 2026. If active for Week 8, he could have plenty of scoring opportunities against a Packers secondary that's allowed 35.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Carolina's top receivers in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Coker has been relatively quiet since returning from injury in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, catching just nine of 22 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown over his last three contests. Despite this, Coker ranks second on the Panthers in targets (7.3), receptions (4.5) and receiving yards per game (60.7) this season, suggesting more production could be in the near future. Coker could struggle in Week 9, however, as Denver's secondary has allowed just 6.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top receiving options in the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Coker has cooled down along with the majority of Carolina's offense over the last three weeks, catching just seven of 14 targets for 74 yards and a touchdown during that span. Despite this, Bryce Young is still tied for the most pass attempts per game in the NFL (38.5), which bodes well for Coker's fantasy outlook going forward. Coker could take advantage of a New Orleans secondary that's given up 11.1 yards per completion this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jalen Coker will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. After catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns across Carolina's first two games this season, Coker has managed just 15 receptions on 35 targets for 189 yards and one touchdown over his last six contests. He remains second on the team in receptions (31), targets (53) and receiving yards (393) but likely can't be trusted after four consecutive performances of less than 10.0 fantasy points. However, Coker is in for a favorable Week 11 matchup against a Baltimore secondary that's allowed 9.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts through nine contests this year.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jalen Coker (concussion) is expected to remain one of Carolina's top weapons if active for the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Coker entered concussion protocol following a four-catch, 47 yard performance in a win over the Ravens in Week 11, putting his availability for Monday night's contest in jeopardy. He's been relatively underwhelming over his last five games, catching 11 of 25 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown. If active, Coker will likely struggle against an impressive Tampa Bay secondary that's given up just 7.6 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 2 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14.8 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite Carolina's defensive struggles, Young threw for 361 yards, the third-most in the NFL during Week 1, and led the offense to 37 points. Additionally, he added a touchdown on the ground as the Panthers offense looked more aggressive than in 2025. Young is also in for a favorable matchup, as he threw for 569 yards and accounted for four total touchdowns in two games versus the Falcons in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns, whose defense has surrendered 22.1 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Young has been one of the most productive QBs in the NFL through two weeks, as he's tied for the most touchdown passes in the league (six) while ranking second in passing yards (648). He's also threatened defenses with his legs, adding 16 yards and a score on the ground. Young could very well finish as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks again in Week 3 while playing a Browns defense that's allowed five touchdown passes this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bryce Young is expected to lead the Panthers' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Despite a Week 3 loss, Young remained productive, throwing for 291 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Through three weeks, the Alabama product has accounted for eight total touchdowns and two turnovers while leading Carolina's offense to 29.7 points per game. He's dealing with injuries to Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee), which could result in the Panthers leaning more on the ground game in Week 4. Regardless, Young should be in for a favorable matchup against a Lions defense that's given up the most fantasy points per game to opposing QBs (35.3) this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading Carolina's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Young has performed very well to start the season, leading the NFL in passing yards per game (317) while accounting for 10 total touchdowns. In his most recent performance, a Week 4 win over the Lions, Young threw for a whopping 329 yards and two touchdowns. He's expected to remain one of fantasy's top quarterbacks while facing an Eagles defense that's allowed 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bryce Young is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Through five games this season, Young has thrown for 1,549 yards and accounted for 12 touchdowns with just two interceptions, leading the league with 309.8 passing yards per game. He's emerged as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks while leading the Panthers' offense to 29.2 points per game, the fourth-best mark in the NFL. Expect Young to remain productive in Week 7 against a Buccaneers defense that's given up just 18.7 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bryce Young will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Young underwhelmed for the first time all season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, completing 14 of 27 passes for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Despite this, Young has been one of the league's most productive quarterbacks this season, throwing for an average of 285.3 yards and 2.0 touchdowns per game. He'll look to rebound in Week 8 against a strong Packers defense that's given up just 17.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bryce Young will look to bounce back from a tough Week 8 performance in the Panthers' Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Young has really struggled over Carolina's last two contests, completing just 37 of 68 pass attempts for 372 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. Young has been playing through a knee injury since the Week 3 loss to the Browns, which could be hindering his performance. However, he could bounce back in Week 9, as Denver's defense has given up 20.7 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading the Panthers' offense during the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. Young played well despite a loss in Week 9 against the Broncos, throwing for 276 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. He remains tied for the league-lead in passing attempts per game (38.5) and fourth in passing yards per game (274.6). which are both positive signs for his outlook going forward. Additionally, Young is in for a favorable Week 10 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 21.2 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading the Panthers' offense during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Young had a relatively underwhelming performance in the Week 10 win over the Saints, completing 17 of 30 passes for 200 yards without a touchdown or interception. Despite this outing, Young ranks sixth in the NFL in pass attempts (37.6) and yards (266.3) per game, suggesting a positive fantasy outlook moving forward. However, Young could struggle against a solid Ravens defense that's given up just 20.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through nine games this year.
outlooksByWeek.12: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading Carolina's offense into the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Young performed well during the Week 11 win over the Ravens, throwing for 254 yards, two touchdowns and an interception while posting his best single-game completion rate of the season (73.3%). Although Carolina has relied more on Chuba Hubbard and the rushing attack over the last couple of weeks, Young remains eighth in the NFL in pass attempts per game (36.8), which bodes well for his fantasy outlook rest-of-season. Despite this, Young could struggle against a solid Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 18.3 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Young has yet to find his way to any sort of fantasy relevance during his first three NFL seasons. The 2023 No. 1 draft pick has yet to finish a season better than 20th in passing yards, 10th in rushing yards or 24th in fantasy points per game. Efficiency has been a problem, as last season's career-high 6.3 yards per attempt was barely up from 2024 and still among the worst in the NFL. Young's 47.6 QBR last season ranked 22nd among 28 qualified quarterbacks. Perhaps the 25-year-old will make a leap in top target Tetairoa McMillan's second season and Brad Idzik's debut as the offensive playcaller, but it will be asking a lot to expect QB1 production. Young is best viewed as a fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.3: Ollie Gordon's workload could increase if Jaylen Wright misses the Dolphins' Week 3 game against the Chiefs. Despite being No. 3 on the depth chart, Gordon has outsnapped Wright behind Miami's workhorse, De'Von Achane. Kansas City allowed stud Jonathan Taylor to rush for two scores in Week 2 but kept Denver's backs under control in Week 1. Barring an injury to Achane, it's difficult to envision a path to meaningful production for Gordon.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out in Week 3. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins often falling behind in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the preferred pass-catching option. Confidence isn't inspired facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 yards per carry and 11 catches to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ollie Gordon could be emerging in the Dolphins' backfield heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. With De'Von Achane (knee) out, Gordon ran for 100 yards on just nine carries in Week 4, vastly outperforming Jaylen Wright, while also scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. Touches figure to remain low if the Dolphins are forced to play from behind early, but facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry could lead to steady yardage without high volume, and Gordon will remain an option near the goal line.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ollie Gordon will likely continue to serve as the lead back for the Dolphins in Week 7 against the Jets. Prior to Miami's Week 6 bye, Gordon had 17 or 18 carries in two of three games. The lone outing with a decrease in carries was also his only 100-yard game, and he scored in each contest. Though he hasn't factored into the passing game, volume remains king for running backs, and Gordon appears to have that in a matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, resulting in the 11th-most fantasy points allowed.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ollie Gordon may be hindered by an unfavorable game flow in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He has scored in four straight games, topping 100 yards twice while amassing at least 17 carries three times. Jaylen Wright is uncertain to play in Week 8, which could result in 20-plus carries for Miami's only option in the backfield if they remain competitive and aren't forced to throw the entire second half. New England brings a mid-tier run defense into Week 8, allowing 4.1 yards per carry but just five rushing scores in seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ollie Gordon will bring consistent volume into the Dolphins' Week 9 matchup with the Lions. Since taking over as the team's lead back, Gordon has at least 17 carries in four of his last five games, though he's seen a minimal amount of work in the passing game, snagging just six passes. Detroit has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs, mainly due to opponents passing on them at will, which Miami isn't equipped to do. With volume paramount for the position, Gordon is a safe bet to pile up carries, creating a nice floor that can be elevated if he finds the end zone.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ollie Gordon should log heavy volume again in an inviting Week 10 matchup when the Dolphins face the Colts. Gordon has 16 or more carries in three straight games and five of his last six, scoring four times and topping 100 yards twice. He has no major competition for carries with Jaylen Wright injured and sparingly used even when healthy. Indianapolis is allowing 4.8 yards per carry, the third-highest mark in the league, setting Gordon up to take advantage of a big workload.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ollie Gordon will have a heavy workload for as long as the Dolphins remain competitive in Week 11 against the Bills. Gordon has at least 16 carries in five straight games and caught a season-high four passes in Week 10, though Miami was in a four-quarter game against the Colts. Buffalo figures to be a far more difficult opponent, which could force a heavier pass-game script. With Buffalo allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, Gordon could be touchdown-dependent for top-end fantasy scoring.
outlooksByWeek.12: Ollie Gordon will look to repeat prior success when the Dolphins face the Jets for the second time this year in Week 12. He drew only 11 carries in Week 11, his lowest total since Week 4, but burst through for 6.3 yards per carry, also his best mark since Week 4. Gordon rushed for 103 yards on 25 carries against the Jets in Week 7. Their defense has allowed 4.6 yards per carry and eight rushing scores through 11 games, surrendering an additional four touchdown receptions, and Gordon is more involved in the passing game with McCord under center.

player.seasonOutlook: Gordon is battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind lead back De'Von Achane in Miami. Gordon was used sparingly as a rookie and didn't exactly move the needle. The 2025 sixth-round pick averaged an ugly 2.84 yards per carry on 70 attempts and 3.6 yards per target on the nine balls thrown his way. Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase McLaughlin will look to remain perfect in the Buccaneers' Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McLaughlin made all five of his kicks during last week's loss, including a 51-yard field goal. With the Browns defense allowing 34 total points and 10 kicking points in a Week 1 loss, McLaughlin is likely in for lots more scoring opportunities in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase McLaughlin could remain one of the top kickers in fantasy despite the Buccaneers' tough Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, as he's now converted on all six field-goal tries this season, including two from 50-plus yards. Despite McLaughlin being tied for the league-lead in field-goals made this season, he could struggle against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 6.5 kicking points per game thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 4 matchup against the Packers. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, converting on all four of his kicks, including a 54-yard field goal. He's now made all nine of his field-goal tries and all five point-after attempts through three weeks. If Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to miss the Week 4 contest, McLaughlin may have fewer scoring opportunities. However, he's still in for a relatively favorable matchup with the Packers allowing 7.0 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase McLaughlin is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal in the Week 4 loss to the Packers but made both of his point-after attempts. On the season, he's converted on all nine of his field-goal tries, including three from beyond 50 yards. McLaughlin could get fewer kicking chances with Jalon Daniels starting at quarterback for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb), but the Cowboys remain a favorable matchup, allowing 8.5 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chase McLaughlin will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. McLaughlin impressed during the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, converting on his lone field-goal try and all three point-after attempts. He remains perfect on the season, making all 20 of his kicks this season (10 field goals and 10 extra points). He could have plenty of scoring chances against a Steelers defense that's given up 9.8 kicking points per game this season, tied for the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. McLaughlin had an impressive showing in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Buccaneers, converting on all four of his field-goal tries, including three from 40-plus yards. The veteran kicker is perfect on the season, making 14 field goals and 11 extra points. He'll likely have multiple scoring opportunities in Week 7, as the Panthers defense has allowed 7.4 kicking points per game this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chase McLaughlin could have few scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. McLaughlin converted on all seven of his kicks in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, making two field goals and five extra points. On the season, McLaughlin has been perfect, making all 16 of his field-goal tries and all 16 of his point-after attempts. Despite this, McLaughlin could struggle against a solid Falcons defense that's allowed just 6.4 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He made all three of his field goal attempts despite the heavy rain in the Week 8 win over the Falcons. On the season, he's converted all 19 of his field goal tries and all 17 of his point-after attempts. Despite his incredible season, McLaughlin is in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Bears defense that's allowed just 5.0 kicking points per game through seven weeks this year.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chase McLaughlin could have limited scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 11 matchup against the Lions. McLaughlin has been one of fantasy's top kickers through nine games this season, converting on all 22 of his field-goal tries and all 18 of his point-after attempts. Despite this, he could have few scoring chances in Week 11 against a Detroit defense that's given up just 5.3 kicking points per game on the season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chase McLaughlin could receive few scoring chances during Tampa Bay's Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal during the Week 11 loss to the Lions but converted on all three of his extra points. On the season, the veteran has been perfect, making all 22 of his field-goal tries and all 21 of his point-after attempts. Despite his impressive season, Carolina has held opponents to just 7.1 kicking points per game, making this an unfavorable matchup for McLaughlin.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Schultz was second on the Texans in targets behind Nico Collins during the season opener, which matched Schultz's usage last season. After being thrown to eight times in Week 1 against a Bills defense that allowed the fewest yards in the NFL to TEs last season, Schultz is poised for a hefty Week 2 workload against a Bengals defense that surrendered the most yards to his position in 2025. Schultz's role and matchup make him a top-10 fantasy TE for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Schultz paced the Texans with 12 catches for 140 yards on 14 targets in the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati, working as C.J. Stroud's top target in the absence of WR Nico Collins (hamstring). The veteran TE is the favorite to lead the team in targets if Collins sits in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most yards and TDs in the NFL this season. Indianapolis just allowed nine catches for 101 yards and a TD to Chiefs TE Travis Kelce in Week 2. Schultz is locked in as a fantasy TE1 for Week 3 if Collins sits and has a strong argument to stay in that range even if Collins suits up.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Schultz is coming off a disappointing 30-yard outing in Week 3 against the Colts, but he'll remain a fantasy TE1 in Week 4 against the Cowboys if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game. Schultz had 12 catches for 140 yards in Week 2 and is averaging 85 receiving yards per game since Collins got hurt. The Cowboys have struggled to defend TEs, allowing three TDs while forcing only two incompletions on 19 passes to the position. If Collins returns, Schultz will maintain fantasy starter-level upside but with a lower floor due to dropping a spot in the pass-catching hierarchy.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Schultz has recorded just 39 yards in two games since his 140-yard outburst for the Texans in Week 2. He's back to working as a supporting piece in Houston's passing game now that Nico Collins has recovered from a hamstring injury. The 30-year-old TE's inconsistent workloads keep him from being a reliable fantasy starter, and Schultz will be tough to trust in Week 5 against a Titans defense that's holding his position to 27 receiving yards per game, fourth-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Schultz leads the Texans with 24 catches heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Jaguars in London, though half of those receptions came in Week 2 against the Bengals. Jacksonville has been among the five stingiest defenses against TEs, limiting the position to 3.6 catches for 34 yards per game. The Jaguars have allowed two TDs to the position, but Schultz has scored only five times in 39 regular-season games since the start of the 2024 season and is still searching for his first TD of the season. Despite Schultz's respectable target volume, he's best left on the bench in single-TE formats in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dalton Schultz has exceeded 35 receiving yards just once through Houston's first six games of the season and has yet to score a TD heading into a Week 7 home game against the Giants. He's a secondary option in a Houston passing game that has gotten more production out of its WRs in recent weeks, and Schultz's lack of red-zone involvement compared to other middling TE options makes him an unappealing fantasy play. The Giants have limited TEs to two TDs this season, so Schultz is best left on the bench or waivers since his TD drought is unlikely to end in Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dalton Schultz isn't a recommended Week 9 fantasy option in most formats for Houston's road game against the Chargers. The veteran TE has 33 catches for 322 yards through Houston's first seven games of the season, but Schultz has yet to score this season, and the Chargers have allowed just one TD to a TE. Frustratingly for Schultz's fantasy managers, backup TE Foster Moreau has scored three TDs on 11 catches this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dalton Schultz is a borderline fantasy starter at TE for Week 10 against the Browns. He ranks ninth among TEs with 46 receiving yards per game but has yet to score this season and has a meager five TDs in 42 regular-season appearances since the start of the 2024 season. Cleveland has allowed five TDs to the position in nine games, as well as 58 yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.11: Dalton Schultz is coming off a bittersweet Week 10 performance against the Browns. He scored his first touchdown of the season on his only catch but was held to a single reception for the first time all season. The reliable TE is a borderline fantasy starter for Week 11 against the Colts; however, there are certainly higher-upside options to be found at the position. Schultz hasn't topped 45 yards since his 140-yard Week 2 outburst, which occurred while the Texans were without top WR Nico Collins, who has since recovered from a hamstring injury. The Colts have allowed seven TDs in 10 games to TEs, which is tied for fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Dalton Schultz has been held to one catch for 11 yards in each of Houston's last two games, though one of those receptions was his first touchdown of the season. He has been utilized primarily as a blocker in Houston's recent games, so Schultz hasn't benefited much from the strong play of QB C.J. Stroud. In Week 12, Schultz will face a Ravens defense that has struggled to defend TEs, allowing 54 yards per game and seven TDs in 11 games to the position. He's a viable low-end starter at a position that lacks depth, but nobody's getting excited about starting Schultz these days.

player.seasonOutlook: Schultz has been one of the league's most consistent tight ends over the past six years, but with the exception of one season, he hasn't been overly useful in fantasy. Schultz was fantasy's No. 3 tight end in scoring while he was in Dallas in 2021, but he has finished 10th or worse in his other eight campaigns (that includes exactly 10th in three of the past four seasons). In 2025, Schultz ranked sixth or better at the position in targets, catches and yards, but he found the end zone only three times and has now cleared five touchdowns once in his career (eight in 2021). Schultz is a reliable target for QB C.J. Stroud, but with Houston's depth at wide receiver, he simply doesn't offer much upside. Consider him a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Evans seems likely to continue playing through an injury to his ribs for San Francisco's Week 5 matchup against the Seahawks. The veteran wideout toughed out the injury in Week 4 and posted a 5-76-0 receiving line against a tough Broncos secondary. That receiving yardage was a season-high mark for Evans, as were his eight targets. Seattle could pose a significant challenge to the 49ers' receiving corps, however, as the Seahawks have yielded just 12.8 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season -- third-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Evans is coming off his best game as a member of the 49ers heading into a Week 6 tilt against Washington. Evans posted a 7-113-1 receiving line and added a two-point conversion in a tight win over the division-rival Seahawks this past Sunday. Fellow wideout Deebo Samuel injured his hamstring in the victory, and if he's unable to return for Week 6, Evans' importance in the passing game could be elevated even higher. The Commanders may be ripe for the picking, as they've given up the seventh-most fantasy points per game (25.0) to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Evans and the 49ers are in Atlanta for a Week 7 road tilt. Unfortunately for him, he'll likely be spending it, and possibly more, on the sidelines after aggravating his Achilles injury in San Francisco's Week 6 win. Evans is expected to sit out the contest against the Falcons with a Week 8 bye on the horizon, giving him extra time and recovery for a chance to suit up in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.9: Mike Evans is expected to return from a one-game absence for the 49ers' Week 9 matchup against Las Vegas. Evans was held out of the Week 7 loss to Atlanta due to a lingering Achilles issue, but San Francisco's Week 8 bye enabled him to get some much-needed rest. It still bears monitoring the veteran wideout's practice participation throughout the week, though, as Achilles injuries can be tricky. Should Evans indeed suit up, he'll face a struggling Raiders defense that has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game (23.9) to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Mike Evans continues to tend to an Achilles injury and is iffy to suit up for San Francisco in Week 10 against Dallas. The injury has prevented Evans from playing in each of the 49ers' past two games despite the team's bye being sandwiched between those contests. Fellow starting wideout Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has also been out, but the 49ers did add depth at the trade deadline by bringing in Keenan Allen. If Evans can return in Week 10, he'll square off against a Cowboys defense that ranks a poor 25th in the league with 23.4 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.11: Mike Evans reportedly has a chance to return from an Achilles injury for San Francisco's Week 11 tilt against the Vikings. Evans has missed the 49ers' past three games while dealing with right Achilles tendinitis. San Francisco recently acquired veteran Keenan Allen to bolster the wideout corps, and Deebo Samuel returned in Week 10 from a multi-game absence caused by a hamstring injury, but Evans' ability to get back on the field would still be a big boost given his chemistry with QB Brock Purdy this season. The 49ers can use all the help they can get on Sunday Night Football, as Minnesota has been tough on opposing passing games this season and has allowed just 16.2 fantasy points per game to wideouts -- fourth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Mike Evans will look to move further past his Achilles injury when the 49ers host Seattle in Week 12. Evans returned from a three-game absence this past Sunday against Minnesota and posted a 6-109-1 receiving line on seven targets. The veteran wideout did log just a 42% offensive snap share, so San Francisco may have been easing him back in workload-wise despite his big stat line. Evans could find the sledding tougher against the Seahawks, who have allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (12.8) to wideouts this season, though Evans burned Seattle for a 7-113-1 receiving line in their first meeting this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Woody Marks is set to occupy a change-of-pace role behind David Montgomery in Week 2, when the Texans host the Bengals. Marks turned 11 touches into 40 scrimmage yards in Week 1 against the Bills, while Montgomery had 79 yards and three TDs on 23 touches. Cincinnati had the worst run defense in the league last season, but Marks' modest usage makes him no better than a deep-league flex play as long as Montgomery is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.3: Woody Marks capitalized on a negative game flow in Week 2, out-touching David Montgomery 13-8. The 0-2 Texans will face a Colts team that's also 0-2 in Week 3, and Montgomery is likely to reclaim the lead role unless Houston falls into a multi-score hole again. Marks is averaging just 2.9 yards per carry and 4.2 yards per catch in 2026 after averaging a modest 3.6 yards per carry during his 2025 rookie season. He has RB3/flex upside in Week 3 against a Colts defense that's giving up 177 rushing yards per game, but Marks' uncertain role and poor efficiency this season cap his value despite the intriguing matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Woody Marks is the 1B option in Houston's backfield, which is enough to earn flex consideration in deeper formats for Week 4 against the Cowboys. The Cowboys are giving up 114 rushing yards per game to RBs and have surrendered four TDs to the position. Marks has 29 touches this season to David Montgomery's 44. Neither RB has found much running room behind Houston's weak offensive line, as Marks is averaging 3.0 yards per carry, while Montgomery is at 2.8 yards per carry. Marks scored his first touchdown of the season in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, while Montgomery has three TDs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Woody Marks takes a two-game touchdown streak into the Texans' Week 5 trip to Tennessee, though he has been out-touched 54-35 by David Montgomery in Houston's backfield. Marks has pulled within one touchdown of Montgomery this season, and neither running back has been efficient behind Houston's struggling offensive line, as Marks is averaging 3.1 yards per carry to Montgomery's 2.7. The Titans are giving up 100 yards per game on the ground to RBs, but Marks' position on the short end of a backfield platoon makes him a deep-league flex candidate at best for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Woody Marks is set to lead Houston's backfield in Week 6 against the Jaguars, as fellow Texans RB David Montgomery (groin) is considered week-to-week. Marks racked up 85 scrimmage yards on 19 touches in the Week 5 win over Tennessee, a game Montgomery exited in the first half. Jacksonville is allowing a league-low 63.8 rushing yards per game, but RBs are averaging 40 receiving yards per game against the Jaguars. Expectations should be tempered due to the difficult matchup, but Marks is projected to get plenty of touches, making him a high-end Week 6 flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Woody Marks has averaged 18 touches and 83 scrimmage yards over Houston's last two games, leading the team's backfield since David Montgomery sustained a groin injury early in Week 5. Prior to that point, Marks averaged nine touches for 30 yards per game. If Montgomery is unable to play in Week 7, Marks would be a fantasy RB2 in the lead role against a Giants defense that has allowed three rushing scores and three receiving TDs to RBs through six games this season. Jawhar Jordan, who had six carries for 43 yards and a TD in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville, would likely work in a change-of-pace role again. If Montgomery returns, Marks would still be a viable flex option, albeit with a far lower floor.
outlooksByWeek.9: Woody Marks looks set to retain the lead role in Houston's backfield for a juicy Week 9 matchup with the Chargers, leaving him firmly in the fantasy RB2 range. David Montgomery hasn't played since getting banged up early in Week 5 against the Titans, and he may not be ready to return after Houston's Week 8 bye. Marks has averaged 18.7 touches over the past three games while recording at least 81 scrimmage yards in each of those three games. He should continue to pile up yardage against a Chargers defense that is allowing 124.6 rushing yards per game, and Marks has a nice opportunity to find the end zone for the first time since Week 4, as RBs have produced nine TDs in seven games against the Chargers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Woody Marks has recorded between 17 and 20 touches for 74-85 yards in each of Houston's last four games, working in a bell-cow role in the absence of David Montgomery (groin). Montgomery looks likely to remain sidelined in Week 10 at Cleveland, which should keep Marks in the fantasy RB2 range thanks to his high touch floor against a Browns defense that's allowing 115 rushing yards per game to running backs. Marks hasn't scored since Week 4, while Cleveland has given up seven TDs to RBs in nine games.
outlooksByWeek.11: Woody Marks entered concussion protocol during Houston's Week 10 loss to the the Browns. He isn't expected to be cleared in time to face the Colts on Thursday Night Football in Week 11. David Montgomery (groin) would likely assume the lead role in Houston's backfield if he gains clearance for his first action since Week 5. Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale are Houston's other options at RB.
outlooksByWeek.12: Woody Marks missed Houston's Week 11 win over the Colts due to a concussion. If he clears protocol in time to face the Ravens in Week 12, Marks would be a decent flex option while splitting carries with David Montgomery, who returned from a groin injury in Week 11. Marks has exceeded 40 scrimmage yards only once in five games alongside Montgomery, and that was a game in which Montgomery exited early due to an injury, but Houston's entire RB room should benefit from facing a reeling Ravens defense that has allowed multiple rushing touchdowns in four consecutive games. Baltimore is giving up 29.2 points per game during its current six-game losing streak.

player.seasonOutlook: Marks, a fourth-round NFL draft pick in 2025, played a substantial role as a rookie, soaking up 220 touches (22nd among RBs), but he struggled with efficiency (his 3.59 yards per carry and 1.61 yards after contact both ranked near the basement) and found the end zone only five times. The result was 9.4 fantasy points per game and one top-10 fantasy outing. Marks appears ticketed for a lesser role in 2026 now that David Montgomery was brought in to serve as the likely leader of a backfield committee. Especially in an offense that doesn't use backs in the passing game very much, Marks is no more than a bench/insurance stash.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for those matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Pitts will look to rebound for a disappointing Week 1 performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Pitts failed to haul in his lone target during last week's loss, with Bijan Robinson and Drake London combining for a 73.6% of Cooper Rush's targets. Despite this, Pitts could very well rebound against a Panthers defense that just allowed a whopping 59 points in Week 1, as they also gave up 11.5 PPR fantasy points to tight ends. His rebound could depend on Atlanta's quarterback situation, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) looking to return from injury in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Pitts has really struggled along with the majority of Atlanta's offense throughout the first two weeks, catching just one of four targets for 15 yards. However, he could really benefit from the return of Michael Penix as the team's starting quarterback heading into Week 3. While Penix was healthy during the 2025 season, Pitts averaged 4.2 receptions and 41.7 yards per game -- a vast difference from his 2026 production thus far. He's also in for a favorable matchup, as the Packers' defense has allowed 12.0 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a disappointing start in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite Michael Penix returning to the field in the Week 3 win over the Packers, Pitts' role remained limited, catching just one of two targets for five yards. He was overshadowed by Drake London (9-194-0) and appears to be operating as the Falcons' No. 3 pass catcher, also behind Bijan Robinson (16 targets to Pitts' six). However, Pitts could rebound in Week 4, as the Saints' defense has allowed 20.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Pitts had his most productive game of the season in the Week 4 win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 47 yards. Despite this, he played just 50% of Atlanta's offensive snaps and has now logged an average of 2.3 targets per game, suggesting he may not be as involved in the team's offensive game plan as he has been in past years. Additionally, Pitts in in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 10.4 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Pitts will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Pitts had his best game of the 2026 season during the Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens, catching five of six targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. Since the return of quarterback Michael Penix (ribs) in Week 3, Pitts has caught nine of 11 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown. Pitts could struggle in Week 6, however, as he's set to face a Chicago defense that's allowed just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top offensive weapons in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Pitts is coming off his best performance of the season in a Week 6 loss to the Bears, catching five of seven targets for 60 yards and two scores. It appears as if he's been more involved in Atlanta's offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching 10 of 13 targets for 102 yards and three touchdowns after receiving just nine targets in his first four contests. However, Pitts could struggle against a solid 49ers defense that's given up just 8.4 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs through five games this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyle Pitts will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Pitts has really found a rhythm over the last three weeks after a slow start to the season, catching 15 of 18 targets for 124 yards and four touchdowns over that span. Despite ranking fourth on the team in yards, Pitts has tallied the third-most targets (27) and the most touchdowns (four) on the Falcons through seven weeks. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with the Buccaneers' defense giving up 16.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top pass catchers in the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Despite catching just two of five targets for six yards in the Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, Pitts finished tied for the most receptions in the game. Prior to last week's loss, Pitts appeared to be finding his groove, averaging 5.0 receptions, 41.3 yards and 1.3 touchdowns per game from Weeks 5 through 7. He's expected to bounce back against a Bengals defense that's given up 15.9 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this year.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kyle Pitts will look to rebound from a poor performance in Atlanta's Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. After catching 15 of 18 targets for 122 yards and four touchdowns from Weeks 5 through 7, Pitts has really struggled. In his last two games, the Florida product has hauled in just five of 10 targets for 29 yards and no scores, making him too inconsistent to be a week-in and week-out starter going forward. However, he's in for a favorable Week 10 matchup against a Kansas City defense that's allowed 17.0 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of Atlanta's top pass catchers during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Pitts has been relatively inconsistent this year, catching 29 of 42 targets for 270 yards and four touchdowns. He's tallied fewer than 10 fantasy points in seven of 10 games this season, making him hard to trust as a weekly fantasy starter. This is especially true due to a difficult matchup in Week 12, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season, the best mark in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Right when it seemed like Pitts might never live up to the hype, the 2021 No. 4 pick put together the best season of his career. Pitts finished second among tight ends in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points, setting career highs in all but the yardage category. He scored five touchdowns and has increased his total in that category (by exactly one) each season in the league. Pitts did a big chunk of his damage with Kirk Cousins under center (some with WR Drake London sidelined), which is notable as Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. are set to battle for the Atlanta QB job. There's some obvious risk here considering Pitts finished 17th or lower in PPG three straight seasons before 2025, but he nonetheless enters his age-25 season as a priority target in the Atlanta offense. Consider him a midrange TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyren Williams enters the Rams' Week 5 matchup against the Bills with plenty of momentum. Williams totaled 147 yards and two touchdowns in a comeback win over Philadelphia in Week 4, pushing him up to four total TDs on the season. The star running back has logged at least 80 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's averaged 68.5 receiving yards across his past two contests. Buffalo has yielded 22.2 fantasy points per game to running backs so far, sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyren Williams will take aim at the end zone again in the Rams' Week 6 matchup versus the Cardinals. Though Williams was held to 49 yards on 16 carries against Buffalo in Week 6, he added 27 yards as a receiver and scored his fifth touchdown of the season. He also continued to put plenty of space between him and No. 2 RB Blake Corum, logging 11 more totes than his backup. Williams could find ample running room against an Arizona defense that ranks 19th in the league by allowing 4.17 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyren Williams remains the Rams' leading running back entering Week 7 against the Raiders, having rushed 80 times for 393 yards and four touchdowns while adding 30 receptions for 217 yards and another score. He's averaging an efficient 4.9 yards per carry, and his Week 6 showing against the Cardinals was right in line with that, as he notched 50 rushing yards in just 10 carries. Williams' receiving involvement provides a dependable fantasy foundation, particularly with Davante Adams sidelined for an extended period, and this looks like a favorable matchup on paper for the star tailback since Las Vegas has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyren Williams will look to continue his consistent campaign when the Rams face the Chargers in Week 8. Williams posted 121 total yards Sunday against Las Vegas, marking the third time this season's he's logged over 100 total yards in a game. While his backfield mate Blake Corum has at times impacted Williams' workload, the latter has made the most of his carries, averaging a career-best 5.1 yards per rush, and he's also having his best season as a pass catcher. Williams could feast on a Chargers defense that's giving up 20.1 fantasy points per game to running backs to rank 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyren Williams will likely continue to share the Rams' backfield in Week 9 against Washington. Williams tallied a modest 56 yards on 16 carries against the Chargers in a win this past Sunday, but he managed to get into the end zone for the fifth time over his past five games. He's faced competition for carries of late from Blake Corum, who has tallied 28 totes for 166 yards and two TDs over the past two weeks. Both Williams and Corum could battle for running room against the Commanders, who are yielding just 3.63 yards per carry to running backs, which ranks seventh-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kyren Williams may be asked to log a heftier workload than usual for the Rams in Week 10 against the Cardinals. Williams rushed for just 45 yards -- his second-lowest mark of the season -- on 15 carries against Washington in Week 9, adding 16 yards on three catches. However, Los Angeles is going to be without wideout Puka Nacua (knee) for multiple weeks, and with Davante Adams (hamstring) still on IR, the team may turn more to its ground game  -- led by Williams and Blake Corum -- to carry the load. Arizona's defense has been middling against the run this season, allowing 18.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, tied for 18th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kyren Williams has been dealing with a sore toe but is expected to play in the Rams' Week 12 matchup versus Green Bay. Williams logged a season-low 32 total yards (23 rushing, nine receiving) versus Arizona his last time out, so he'll be looking for a big bounce-back performance against the Packers. With that said, Blake Corum -- who went off for a season-best 119 yards and scored a touchdown in that game against the Cardinals -- continues to get double-digit touches every week, denting Williams' ceiling to an extent. Both backs could find success against a Green Bay defense that has given up 12 rushing TDs to running backs, tied for fourth-most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameson Williams will look to build off a big outing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. Williams had his best game of the year in Week 4 against the Panthers, bringing in six of eight targets for 102 yards. The speedster has still posted just a 16-229-0 receiving line to start the season, but he has seen eight or more targets in two games, which could bode well for his output. He'll also face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jameson Williams will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Williams found the end zone twice in a Week 5 win over the Cardinals before Detroit's bye week, which was done with two catches for 47 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now totaled 18 grabs for 276 yards and two scores on the season. He'll face a Green Bay secondary that's ranked in the middle versus fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jameson Williams will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Williams produced his best fantasy performance of the year in a Week 7 win over Green Bay, hauling in five of nine targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns. The speedy wideout has now produced four touchdowns in his last two games, along with seven catches for 138 yards in that stretch. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jameson Williams will look to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Williams kept his touchdown streak and recent dominance alive in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, reeling in four of six targets for 70 yards and a touchdown. The speedy wideout has now logged 11 catches for 208 yards and a whopping five touchdowns in his last three outings.
