He'll face a Dolphins defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jameson Williams will look to get more volume as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Williams struggled to get touches with a stagnant passing game against the Dolphins in Week 9, recording one catch for 31 yards and one rush for nine yards. The speedy wideout has now posted a 28-468-5 receiving line on 44 targets across eight games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jameson Williams will remain a flashy option in Detroit's offense heading into Week 11 against the Buccaneers. Williams didn't benefit, like some of his teammates, from an offensive explosion in a Week 10 win over New England, but he still hauled in four of seven targets for 50 yards. The speedy wideout has now logged 32 catches for 518 yards and five touchdowns so far this season. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jameson Williams will seek to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. Williams led Detroit in receiving yards against the Buccaneers in Week 11, bringing in all four of his targets for 93 yards and a touchdown. The speedster has now posted a 36-611-6 receiving line across 10 games, and he's logged 50 or more yards in four of his last five outings. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Purdy and the 49ers head into a Week 2 tilt against Miami fresh off a big season-opening win over the Rams. Purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns in that contest, connecting with wideouts Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson for the three scores while adding 29 yards on five rushes. It was a big victory against a vaunted NFC West rival that many have pegged as Super Bowl favorites, so San Francisco will look to avoid a letdown in Week 2 against a much less revered Dolphins team. Miami was beaten soundly by the Raiders in Week 1 while allowing QB Kirk Cousins to toss three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Purdy will look to build upon a historic performance when San Francisco faces Arizona in Week 3. Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers against Miami on Sunday, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That stat line made Purdy the second passer in NFL history with 250 passing yards on a 90 performance completion rate in multiple games. The fifth-year signal caller may be without some of his weapons in Week 3 if Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) need to sit out, though early reports suggest Evans isn't dealing with a serious injury. The Cardinals could have a hard time containing Purdy after giving up 235 passing yards and three TDs to Seattle QB Drew Lock in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Purdy will lead the 3-0 49ers in a Week 4 matchup against the Broncos. Purdy threw for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions in a Week 3 win against Arizona, and he currently holds the highest passer rating (133.1) in the NFL. Purdy is also tied for the league lead with nine TD passes, three of which have gone to star tight end George Kittle. However, Denver figures to pose a tough challenge, as the Broncos' defense -- led in the secondary by star cornerback Patrick Surtain -- has limited opponents to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Purdy will look to help keep San Francisco's perfect record alive with a win over Seattle in Week 5. Purdy has been outstanding to the begin the campaign, completing 70% of his passes and recording an 11:1 TD:INT. He's also getting great protection from the offensive line, as he's yet to take a sack this season. The Seahawks could pose a stiff challenge, however, as they've collected seven sacks through five games and have allowed the fifth-lowest passer rating (76.2) in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brock Purdy and the 49ers will look to remain perfect with a Week 6 win over Washington. Purdy was sacked for the first time this season and threw his first pickoff since Week 1 this past Sunday against Seattle, but he also threw two touchdowns to help guide San Francisco to victory. He was especially synched up with veteran wideout Mike Evans, with whom he connected seven times for 113 yards and a score. Purdy could feast on a Commanders defense that has given up 14 passing touchdowns (tied for most in the NFL) and 27.9 fantasy points per game (second-most in the league) to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brock Purdy and the 49ers travel to take on the Falcons in Week 7. He completed 21 of 29 pass attempts for 264 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing five times for 28 yards during San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Purdy found seven different receivers as the 49ers improved to 6-0 on the season, but it sounds like they could be without Mike Evans (Achilles) for an extended period of time. Purdy will take aim at Atlanta's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.6) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brock Purdy should be well-rested off the 49ers' bye week for a Week 9 clash against Las Vegas. Purdy will be looking to bounce back from his first multi-turnover game of the campaign, as he threw two interceptions in a Week 7 loss to the Falcons. Despite that performance, Purdy still ranks in the top five leaguewide with a 110.1 QB rating in 2026. He could also be getting a big boost Week 9, as injured wideouts Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) all have a chance to return from absences. Purdy should be able to find success against the Raiders, who have allowed a 103.2 QB rating this season, third-worst in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brock Purdy will continue to push toward MVP consideration when the 49ers face Dallas in Week 10. Purdy helped San Francisco improve to 7-1 this past Sunday with a win over the Raiders during which he threw for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception despite working without the team's top two wideouts, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Purdy also ran for 40 yards and a score in the victory, and he currently ranks sixth among NFL quarterbacks with 201 rushing yards on the campaign. Even if Evans and/or Samuel remain out for Week 10, the addition of Keenan Allen at the trade deadline should provide him with a reliable fallback option. Purdy is primed for a big day against a Cowboys defense that ranks 25th in the league by allowing a 99.1 quarterback rating this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brock Purdy is coming off one of the best performances of his career as the 49ers prepare to host Minnesota in Week 11. Purdy threw for a career-best 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions this past Sunday in a win over Dallas. The star quarterback now ranks second among QBs with at least 100 pass attempts in QB rating (115.2) and has posted an impressive 20:5 TD:INT. However, Purdy faces a tough test in the Vikings, who lead the NFL with 37 sacks and have allowed only six passing touchdowns while recording 10 interceptions.
outlooksByWeek.12: Brock Purdy will face another tough defense when the 49ers host Seattle in Week 12. The star quarterback solved Minnesota's previously stingy defense this past Sunday in a 35-10 victory in Mexico City, throwing for 255 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Purdy and San Francisco's offense seems to be firing on all cylinders right now, especially after the return of All-Pro wideout Mike Evans. Still, the Seahawks could present a stiffer test than most, as they have yielded the fewest fantasy points per game (14.1) to quarterbacks and held Purdy to a season-low 189 passing yards in their first meeting Week 5.

player.seasonOutlook: Purdy enters his fifth NFL season looking to rebound after injuries caused him to appear in only nine games in 2025. The good news is Purdy played well, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of the nine games, including 26-plus points in three straight games during Weeks 15-17. A highly effective passer and solid contributor as a rusher, Purdy has quietly finished in the top 10 in fantasy points per game in each of the past three seasons. With a good supporting cast led by Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and free agent additions Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, Purdy is an underrated mid-to-back-end QB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.
outlooksByWeek.4: Patrick Mahomes continued his strong start to the season in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, producing multiple touchdowns for a third straight game. The two-time MVP has a 7:2 TD-to-INT ratio in those three contests while adding another score on the ground, and his 8.3 yards per attempt would be his highest mark since 2019. He's done it without the benefit of a single dominant receiver, as Travis Kelce, Kenneth Walker, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy have all logged between 15 and 18 targets. Mahomes will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Patrick Mahomes comes out of Kansas City's bye with a strong 9:2 TD:INT and 8.1 yards per attempt through four games. The presence of Kenneth Walker in the backfield has opened things up for the team's passing game, but Mahomes did lose Week 4 breakout Tyquan Thornton to a dislocated ankle that could potentially sideline the speedy wideout for the rest of the season. Rashee Rice also picked up a minor hamstring strain prior to the bye, which could leave Mahomes working with a very inexperienced group of WRs, although he still has Travis Kelce to fall back on. Mahomes will be facing a Chargers defense in Week 6 that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Patrick Mahomes didn't have much to do in Kansas City's Week 6 easy win over the Chargers. With Kenneth Walker and the defense doing most of the work in a 22-6 victory, Mahomes failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time this season, although he did rack up 272 passing yards and 9.1 yards per attempt. His 8.3 mark on the year is his best since 2019, and through five games he's produced 10 TDs-nine passing and one rushing-against three turnovers. Mahomes faces a much tougher test in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Patrick Mahomes is coming off one of the worst performances of his career in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. The two-time MVP threw for a season-low 165 yards with zero touchdowns and failed to get his team into the red zone for the first time in 153 career starts, including regular season and playoffs. With his wide receiver room thinned by injuries, Mahomes is again having a tough time stretching the field or taking advantage of a defense's focus on Kenneth Walker. He'll try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos defense playing below expectations, which sits tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Patrick Mahomes bounced back from a two-game touchdown drought to throw three TDs in Week 8, but it wasn't enough as Kansas City lost to the Broncos and ceded first place in the AFC West. Despite a lack of consistent help at wide receiver, something that could be addressed at the trade deadline, Mahomes is on pace for his best passing yards total since 2021. With a 12:4 TD:INT ratio through seven games, he could produce 30-plus touchdowns for the first time since 2022. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 9 against a Jets defense that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Patrick Mahomes put together another strong performance in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, completing 74.2% of his 31 pass attempts with two touchdowns and zero interceptions, but he suffered an elbow injury during the contest. He finished the game, but the team is awaiting the results of testing to determine the severity. For now, Mahomes has been deemed day-to-day. If he's cleared to play in Week 10, he'll be facing a Falcons defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs but just traded starting safety Jessie Bates. If Mahomes is held out, Justin Fields would get his first start of the season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Patrick Mahomes is coming off a huge performance in a Week 10 win over the Falcons, as he threw five touchdown passes for the first time since Week 1 of the 2022 season. The trade-deadline addition of Josh Downs revitalized the passing game, as four different Kansas City players had receptions of 30-plus yards. Mahomes has a 10:0 TD:INT ratio over the last three games with two 300-yard performances, giving him significant momentum heading into a Week 11 clash with a Cardinals defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Patrick Mahomes continues to roll, tossing multiple touchdowns for a fourth straight game and topping 300 passing yards for the third time during that stretch in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals. The two-time MVP finally seems to be back in top form after last season's knee injury, and the trade deadline addition of Josh Downs has given him another downfield option. Mahomes will need to stay hot in Week 12 in a marquee AFC clash against the Bills, who rank 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.10: Chimere Dike stepped up in Week 8 with five catches for 71 yards and a TD in the absence of Carnell Tate (shoulder). Tate is expected to return after Tennessee's Week 9 bye, which will likely bump Dike back to a bench role on offense against the Jaguars in Week 10. Dike can be ignored in standard fantasy formats but remains an elite option in leagues that reward return yards on special teams, as the 2025 fourth-round pick leads the NFL with 3,517 all-purpose yards since entering the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chimere Dike had 71 receiving yards and a touchdown catch in Tennessee's Week 8 loss to the Bengals, but that performance accounts for more than half of his 140 receiving yards this season. Dike could be ticketed for a larger role in Week 11 against the Cowboys if at least one of Carnell Tate (shoulder) or Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) doesn't play. The 2025 fourth-round pick has stepped up when given more opportunities before, but Dike remains a deep-league dart throw at best in most formats, even against a weak Dallas secondary that's allowing 158 receiving yards per game to WRs, considering Tennessee's passing game has ranged from putrid to inconsistent. In fantasy formats that reward punt and kickoff return yards, you're probably starting him for his special-teams contributions regardless, with any offensive output just a nice bonus.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chimere Dike has led Tennessee's wide receivers in receiving yards twice in the past three games, posting 71 yards in Week 8 against the Bengals and 69 yards in Week 11 against the Cowboys. He was held to just 16 receiving yards by the Jaguars in between, and Dike will face Jacksonville again in a Week 12 road rematch. He looks poised to remain a staple in three-receiver sets while working out of the slot since Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of the season. Dike has shown enough in recent weeks to earn flex consideration against a Jacksonville defense that is around league-average against WRs but excels at stopping the run.

player.seasonOutlook: A first-team All-Pro in his first professional season, Dike broke Tim Brown's NFL rookie record for all-purpose yards. Most of that damage came as a returner (398 yards and two TDs on punts, 1,588 yards on kicks), but Dike also produced a bit as a receiver (423 yards and four TDs) and rusher (18 yards). The versatile Dike will remain a major factor in the return game, but he has added competition at wide receiver with Calvin Ridley healthy, Carnell Tate drafted fourth overall and target hog Wan'Dale Robinson signed during free agency. The 23-year-old will handle situational short-area targets and a few carries, but he's not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kavontae Turpin managed just one catch for eight yards in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Turpin remains mostly utilized as a kick returner at this stage, though the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: KaVontae Turpin did not even garner a target last game for Dallas. Turpin continues to be utilized largely in the return game. Meanwhile Ryan Flournoy is the clearcut No. 3 wideout behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: KaVontae Turpin continues to flash his versatility for the Cowboys. In addition to his standard role as the primary returner for Dallas, Turpin also rushed for a nine-yard touchdown and even caught a nine-yard pass. Despite this, Turpin remains a boom-or-bust candidate in an offense with so much firepower ahead of him on the depth chart. In Week 4, the Cowboys face a Texans defense allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt through the air, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: KaVontae Turpin remains buried on the depth chart for the Cowboys, at least in terms of receiving. Turpin is the primary returner but has just two catches for 17 yards through four contests. Barring injury, Turpin's impact will mostly be felt on special teams. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KaVontae Turpin saw a season-high four targets last game for the Cowboys.  CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to the additional looks for Turpin. However, Turpin managed just two catches for 22 yards in the loss, and Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Turpin back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: KaVontae Turpin left the last game for the Cowboys due to a rib injury, leaving his status in question for Week 7 versus the Eagles. Tyler Goodson handled kick return duties, while Jonathan Mingo caught punts in Turpin's absence. His targets on offense appear to have been gobbled up by No. 3 wideout Ryan Flournoy. If Turpin can return in Week 7, he would face an Eagles defense allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: KaVontae Turpin did not suit up last game for the Cowboys due to a rib injury.  Turpin has been more of an ancillary part of the offense even when healthy, as he has just four catches and two carries on the season. CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy handle most of the targets from quarterback Dak Prescott.  However, if Turpin somehow can suit up, he could have a favorable matchup if targeted. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: KaVontae Turpin missed last game for Dallas with a rib injury. In fact, it was the second-straight absence for Turpin. His status remains up in the air for Week 9 versus the Colts. If he can somehow suit up, the Colts defense is allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: KaVontae Turpin has missed each of the last three games for Dallas due to a rib ailment. His status remains up in the air for Week 10 versus the 49ers. If Turpin does suit up, his opportunities will likely be limited against a Niners defense allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: KaVonte Turpin returned from a three-game absence due to a rib ailment, but failed to make much of a mark in the passing game. Turpin was targeted three times, though managed just one catch for 10 yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers in Week 10. Meanwhile, the trio of CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy combined for a staggering 38 targets in the high-scoring affair. In other words, Turpin is largely depth at the position, even in Week 11 versus a Titans defense allowing the most passing yards in the NFL per game.
outlooksByWeek.12: KaVontae Turpin found the end zone last game for the Cowboys. Turpin took a handoff 22 yards for a touchdown in the 51-30 thrashing of the Titans. He finished with two carries for 41 yards and the score, as well as 134 return yards. Turpin has just five catches on the season but will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense in Week 12. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Skattebo showed no ill effects from last season's injury in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in he stunning 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys. With the Giants poised to possess the ball and feed the running game under new coach John Harbaugh, Skattebo should continue to be in line for a heavy workload. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Skattebo managed just 55 yards from scrimmage last game for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, teams will likely gameplan to stop the run, which starts with Skattebo. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Skattebo racked up 100 yards from scrimmage in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Skattebo took 20 carries for 60 yards while also catching three passes for 40 yards out of the backfield. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely on the running game led by Skattebo in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Skattebo has struggled to find room to roam for the Giants thus far this season. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 58 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals last game. He is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston. In Week 5, Skattebo will face a rather stingy Washington run defense as well. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Skattebo was mostly a non-factor last game against the Commanders, at least until the end of a wild contest which resulted in a tie. Skattebo managed 40 of his 71 scrimmage yards in overtime, though coughed up the ball as the Giants were in field goal range to potentially win the game. Skattebo would have truly been the goat for this contest had Washington not botched the final seconds of overtime. Skattebo has had 60 rushing yards or less in four-straight games, and has failed to score since the opener. However, in Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Skattebo had zero touches last game for the Giants. One week after losing a key fumble, Skattebo was removed from his starting job as the Giants backfield devolved into a four-man committee. Tyrone Tracy was the team's most productive back, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown, but managed just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches and Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries. Skattebo could return to a more significant role in Week 7 against the Texans, but it will be hard to trust any New York running back until one emerges from the pack. Houston is also allowing just 83 rushing yards per contest, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cam Skattebo retained his starring role for the Giants last game, gaining 121 scrimmage yards and scoring a touchdown in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. Tyrone Tracy went on Injured Reserve following the victory, leaving Devin Singletary as the only other legitimate option at running back behind Skattebo. Though talks of a trade for Jonathan Taylor have intensified, nothing appears imminent heading into a tasty Week 9 clash with Philadelphia. The Eagles have been torched on the ground in 2026, allowing 131.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. Likewise, the Eagles have given up 10 rushing scores, which is tied for 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cam Skattebo did not suit up in New York's last game due to a hamstring issue. However, Skattebo pushed to play in the contest, and as a result looks primed to return to the starting lineup in Week 10 versus the Commanders. Washington has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026, though, allowing just 102.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the league. In addition, the Commanders have yielded just seven rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Cam Skattebo scored twice last game for the Giants. He also gained over 120 scrimmage yards for the second-straight contest. Following being benched versus the Saints, Skattebo has responded with 39 touches in the subsequent two tilts, though he did miss the win over Philadelphia due to a hamstring ailment. He will have his work cut out for him in Week 11 versus the Jags. Jacksonville is allowing just 91 rushing yards per clash, which is sixth in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have surrendered only five rushing touchdowns this season, which is tied for fourth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Cam Skattebo fumbled yet again for the Giants last game. The turnover ultimately did not cost his team the win this time, though Skattebo managed just 34 yards on 14 carries overall versus a stout Jacksonville run defense. If Skattebo can hold onto the ball, he should have better luck against the Colts in Week 12. Indianapolis is allowing 134.4 rushing yards per tilt, which is 29th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Skattebo is a Year 2 breakout candidate following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season. The fourth-round pick first played a significant offensive role in Week 2 and went on to average 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards while scoring six TDs during his six full games. His 19.1 fantasy points per game during the span would've ranked sixth over the full season. The 24-year-old enters 2026 with a new coach (John Harbaugh) and playcaller (Matt Nagy), but his competition for touches are Najee Harris and the same guys he beat out for work in 2025 (Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary). Assuming his ankle heals up as expected, Skattebo will be on the RB2 radar with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Olave definitely benefitted from Tyler Shough's 56 pass attempts during the Week 1 overtime loss. However, New Orleans averaged 34.8 pass attempts per game in 2025, so Olave will likely continue to see loads of volume. Additionally, he saw a 25 percent target share, which should remain steady until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns later this season. Olave is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to WRs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top receivers in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Olave ranks second in the NFL in both receptions (18) and receiving yards (268) through the first two weeks, cementing himself as New Orleans' top wideout. Currently, he's received a 25.6 percent target share, which should continue proving valuable with the Saints high-volume of pass attempts (90 through two weeks, second-most in the NFL). Olave could struggle against the Raiders, however, whose defense has allowed just 21.9 PPR fantasy points to wideouts per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Olave has surpasses 100 receiving yards in two of three games this season, catching 27 of 36 targets for 373 yards and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from New Orleans' pass-happy offense that has averaged 44 pass attempts per game through three weeks. Additionally, Olave is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a struggling Falcons secondary that's allowed 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Olave is expected to lead New Orleans' receiving corps again in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Olave has been spectacular through the Saints' first four games this season, catching 35 of 48 targets for 491 yards (second in the NFL) and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense, which has led to ample opportunities for Olave this season. Despite this, Olave could struggle in Week 5 against a tough Vikings secondary that's given up just 30.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Olave will look to return to form in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Olave struggled along with the rest of New Orleans' offense in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for 46 yards. On the season, Olave ranks second in the NFL with 537 receiving yards and will likely continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's aggressive style of offense (averaging 41 pass attempts per game). Expect Olave to bounce back against a solid Giants defense that's allowed 30.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Olave didn't receive his usual volume in Week 6 but remained productive, catching four of seven targets for 43 yards and a score. He's expected to continue benefitting from Kellen Moore's aggressive offense that's averaged 39.2 pass attempts per game through six weeks. However, Olave is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, as Pittsburgh's defense has given up just 29.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Olave ranks fifth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (90.9) and sixth in receptions per game (7.0) through seven contests. Additionally, quarterback Tyler Shough is averaging a league-high 39.0 pass attempts per game, which suggests Olave will continue to produce at a high level going forward. He's in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 29.8 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top pass catcher in the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Olave added another productive outing to his impressive 2026 campaign during the Week 9 overtime win against the Browns, catching seven of 12 targets for 98 yards. On the season, Olave ranks sixth in the NFL in targets per game (10.4) and seventh in receiving yards per game (91.8). Olave's high volume will likely continue as well, with Tyler Shough tied for the most pass attempts per game (38.5) in the league through eight games. Expect Olave to succeed against a depleted Panthers secondary that's allowed 31.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Chris Olave is expected to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Saints' Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Olave was overshadowed by 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, as he logged season-lows in targets, receptions and yards. Despite this poor showing, Olave remains eighth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (84.9) and 10th in targets per game (9.7), so his fantasy outlook remains very positive going forward. However, he's set to face a tough Bears defense that's allowed just 29.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Olave bounced back from a poor Week 10 performance in last week's loss to the Bears, catching nine of 15 targets to 102 yards. He remains one of seven NFL players to average 10-or-more targets per game (10.2) while ranking seventh in the league in receiving yards per game (86.6). Despite his impressive season, Olave could struggle in Week 12 against a solid Bengals secondary that's given up just 29.7 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through nine games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Reichard converted his lone field-goal attempt and four PATs in a come-from-behind Week 1 win over Green Bay. The third-year kicker was only on the field for extra-point tries after nailing a 38-yard field goal in the first quarter, but the nature of the game made Minnesota more ambitious with their offensive scheme. This could give Reichard more opportunities against a Chicago defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack seven points to Ryan Fitzgerald this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Will Reichard will look to stay hot as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Reichard converted all three of his field-goal attempts in a bad-weather win over the Bears in Week 2. The third-year kicker has now nailed four field goals and all four of his PATs this year. He'll face a Bucs squad that's tied for the most fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (13.0) so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Will Reichard will look to stay perfect as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Reichard finished with his best game of the season in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts (including two 50-plus-yarders) and knocking in two extra-point tries. The third-year kicker will now focus on a Miami team that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 6.7 fantasy points per game to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Will Reichard should be a high-volume option once again as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 4 against the Dolphins, scoring all 15 of Minnesota's points from field goals. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last three games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Saints squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against kickers this season,
outlooksByWeek.7: Will Reichard remains a high-volume option once again as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 5. Reichard stayed busy in Week 5 before Minnesota's bye, nailing all three of his field-goal attempts and two XPAs. The third-year boot has now made three or more field goals in each of his last four games, and he's yet to miss a kick this year. He'll face a Colts squad that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to kickers (10.3) this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Will Reichard should remain a high-usage option as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Reichard stayed busy in Week 7 against the Colts, but he did miss his first kick of the season going 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts. Even so, the third-year boot has now gone 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including six makes from 50-plus yards, and nailed all nine of his XPAs this season. Detroit has ranked a tough third in fantasy points allowed to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Will Reichard will aim to get back on track as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Reichard didn't get much usage in a Week 8 loss to the Lions, missing a field goal attempt from 57 yards and converting his sole extra-point try. Even with a field goal miss in each of the last two weeks, the third-year kicker still sits at 18 of 20 on the year, and he's gone a perfect 10-for-10 on XPAs. Buffalo has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Will Reichard will look to stay involved as the Vikings play the Packers in Week 10. Reichard got back on track in a Week 9 loss to the Bills, making both of his two field-goal attempts. The kicker has now made two or more field goals in all but two of his eight outings this campaign, but the efficiency of the Vikings' offense could improve with Kirk Cousins taking over as the starting QB, turning some of his FG volume into PATs. Green Bay has also ranked a tough first in fantasy points allowed to kickers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.11: Will Reichard will seek to stay hot as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Reichard was perfect in a Week 10 win over Green Bay, nailing all six of his kicks with three field-goal makes. The third-year kicker has now converted 23 of 25 field-goal attempts and made all 13 of his XPAs across nine showings. The 49ers have allowed a middle-of-the-pack 8.0 points per game to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Will Reichard will look to bounce back as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Reichard went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made one XPA in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. Fortunately, those misses were just his second and third of the season, so there aren't currently any blaring warning signs of regression. He'll face a Falcons squad that's ranked top 10 versus fantasy kickers this campaign.

outlooksByWeek.7: Kaden Wetjen and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 meeting against the Saints. He did not record a target but accrued 105 yards on four kickoff returns and also had two punt returns for zero yards. Wetjen has only played on special teams through six outings in 2026 and thus remains off the fantasy radar despite the plethora of injuries to the Steelers' wide receiver corps.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kaden Wetjen and the Steelers host a Week 8 AFC North clash against the Browns. He did not register any offensive snaps but returned two kickoffs for 60 yards and one punt for 13 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 win in Paris. Wetjen has not been able to contribute on offense despite WRs Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) landing on IR.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emmett Johnson contributed in his NFL debut, gaining 24 yards on eight carries and catching both his targets for 44 yards in a season-opening win over the Broncos. Kansas City leaned heavily on its ground game, with Kenneth Walker having a career-best day on 26 touches. Johnson's volume may be repeatable if this proves to be the team's offensive formula in 2026 and they continue building big second-half leads. Johnson will look to take advantage of his opportunities in Week 2 against a Colts defense that was just steamrolled by Derrick Henry but ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emmett Johnson remains in a limited role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Through three games, the fifth-round rookie has only 20 touches-16 carries and four receptions-but has managed to turn that into 120 scrimmage yards. Coach Andy Reid has hinted that Johnson's workload will increase as the season wears on, but as yet there's been no actual sign of that happening. Johnson will be a dart throw, albeit one with big-play upside, in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emmett Johnson has seen little work to begin his career as the No. 2 running back for Kansas City behind bell cow Kenneth Walker. Johnson is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but the fifth-round rookie has teased his big-play potential as a pass catcher, catching all five of his targets for 74 yards. As long as Walker remains healthy, Johnson will remain little more than an upside bench stash. He could get some garbage-time touches in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emmett Johnson remains stuck in a low-volume role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Johnson hasn't logged double-digit touches since Week 1, and his three targets in a Week 6 win over the Chargers were a season-high. The rookie running back will likely need an injury to Walker to contribute. Johnson will look for his first NFL touchdown in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Emmett Johnson continues to work his way into the Kansas City game plan as a pass-catcher. Over the last two games, the rookie has corralled four of six targets for 35 yards while the team deals with injuries to its wide receiver corps. Johnson will not challenge a healthy Kenneth Walker as the lead back, but Andy Reid is trying to find ways to get Johnson the ball in space. The result has been a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through his first six NFL games. Johnson will look to score his first career touchdown in Week 8 against a Broncos defense that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Emmett Johnson took advantage of his opportunities again in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, scoring his first career rushing touchdown while gaining 34 yards on six carries. Kenneth Walker, who found the end zone three times in the victory, remains firmly on top of the depth chart, but Johnson is beginning to earn a steady workload as the No. 2 option in the backfield. The rookie is averaging a tidy 4.3 yards per carry on the ground, while adding a 14-237-1 line on 16 targets over eight games. Johnson could make an impact on limited touches again in Week 10 against a Falcons defense that's tied for 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Emmett Johnson was incredible in his first career NFL start in Week 10 against the Falcons, leading Kansas City to a big win with 171 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The opportunity came with Kenneth Walker sidelined by a groin injury, but the issue isn't expected to keep the former Seahawk sidelined for long. Johnson's performance does make a case for him to take on a bigger workload as the No. 2 option in the backfield once Walker is back. Johnson will look to exploit what volume he gets in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Emmett Johnson has taken full advantage of Kenneth Walker's absence from the Kansas City backfield due to a groin strain. Over two games with Walker on the sideline, Johnson has erupted for 206 rushing yards and a touchdown while adding a 10-108-2 line on 11 targets. While the rookie running back will return to the No. 2 role once Walker is cleared to return, Johnson's performance could encourage Andy Reid to use more of a timeshare between them in order to keep both fresh ahead of the playoffs. Walker is expected to return in Week 12 against the Bills, but Johnson might be able to make a difference on limited touches against a defense that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson and Brashard Smith are set to handle No. 2/3 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. Smith will be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2, facing the 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (25.1) to TEs. The second-year pro managed two catches on three targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 loss in the season opener. Fannin has the perfect chance at a rebound performance against Tampa Bay, as Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki cooked their defense with five receptions for 78 yards and a TD in Week 1. Even with poor quarterback play, Fannin has the talent and opportunity as the focal point of an offense that might not be good but will be forced to throw the ball plenty while playing from behind.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harold Fannin and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3 for their 2026 home opener. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with five catches on six targets for 54 yards. Fannin is still searching for his first TD of the season after collecting six as a rookie, as fellow tight end Blake Whiteheart was on the receiving end of a 17-yard score from Deshaun Watson. Fannin looks to find the end zone against Carolina's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4 for an AFC North clash between two 2-1 teams. He caught seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two TDs during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3, including the game-winning score. Fannin led the team in receptions and yardage while tying KC Concepcion for first in targets. He now has a 12-126-2 line on 18 targets across three contests as one of Deshaun Watson's favorite receivers. Fannin will have a tough matchup against Pittsburgh's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.3) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to stay hot and earn a fourth consecutive victory against the Jets in a Week 5 road clash. He caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. The second-year tight end now has three combined TDs over his last two outings. Fannin should once again be a featured target for Deshaun Watson versus the Jets' ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (10.2) to TEs. They have yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are back home to host the Ravens for an AFC North divisional tilt in Week 6. It was a quiet day for the sophomore tight end, as he caught just one of four targets for four yards during Cleveland's 17-12 defeat in Week 5. Fannin notched at least 50 receiving yards or caught a touchdown in three straight outings prior to this dud, so fantasy managers can blame the poor showing on weather. He'll look to get back into the end zone versus a Baltimore defense that surrendered five receptions for 42 yards and a TD to Kyle Pitts Sr. in their last outing.
outlooksByWeek.7: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are in Tennessee for an interconference clash in Week 7. He caught one of three targets for nine yards during Cleveland's 13-10 Week 6 win. Following a three-game stretch in which he recorded a 15-132-3 receiving line on 20 targets, Fannin has now gone two straight outings with one reception and fewer than 10 yards. The second-year TE will try to bounce back versus a Titans defense allowing 10.5 fantasy points per game (T-7th) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns visit the Steelers for an AFC North battle in Week 8. He brought in six of nine targets for 91 yards and also lost a fumble during Cleveland's 27-24 Week 7 win. Fannin finished second behind KC Concepcion (8-129-0 on 10 targets) in receptions, yardage, and targets while setting a new season high in receiving yards. Fannin will look to exploit the Pittsburgh defense again after he recorded a 3-27-1 line against them in a Week 4 victory.
outlooksByWeek.10: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns welcome the Texans to town for a Week 10 AFC clash. He caught both of his targets for 42 yards, including an impressive 39-yard touchdown in overtime, during Cleveland's 23-22 OT loss in Week 9. Fannin was quiet until the extra frame, a disappointing development after he erupted for a 10-154-0 line on 12 targets in his previous outing. He'll look to stay hot despite a difficult matchup versus Houston's fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (10.1) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to go 5-0 at home when the Raiders visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught seven of nine targets for 91 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Fannin paced his team in every receiving category, finishing as the leader in yardage for the second time in three games. Over his last four outings, he's registered a 25-378-1 line on 32 targets. Fannin will look to stay hot against a Las Vegas defense allowing 16.7 fantasy points per game (28th) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

outlooksByWeek.5: Kimani Vidal is coming off his most productive game of 2026, taking five carries for 25 yards and turning three targets into a 2-11-1 line during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. While the seven touches represented a season high for Vidal, they still trailed Keaton Mitchell's 15 and Omarion Hampton's 11. Mitchell led the trio with 63 scrimmage yards, while Hampton scored a rushing TD. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is drifting toward a full-blown committee as he searches for a spark, but it would likely take an injury ahead of him for Vidal to gain significant volume on a consistent basis. He'll try to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kimani Vidal posted a season-high nine touches in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos, turning eight carries into 57 yards and his first rushing touchdown of the season while also catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. The third-year back has gotten into the end zone in back-to-back games, but Vidal remains firmly in a committee with Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell, and none of the three would seem to have a significant ceiling while working behind a patchwork offensive line. Vidal will try to keep his TD streak going in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kimani Vidal was seeing his usage increase prior to the Chargers' Week 7 bye, with the third-year running back handling a season-high 10 touches in a Week 6 loss to Kansas City, although he turned that volume into just 40 scrimmage yards and zero TDs. Omarion Hampton remains the back with the biggest upside on the roster, but Vidal and Keaton Mitchell are also in the mix, and Mike McDaniel may deploy a full-blown committee in his backfield as he searches for answers. Vidal will face a Rams defense in Week 8 that's tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kimani Vidal remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Omarion Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Keaton Mitchell got seven touches and Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Vidal does have two TDs in the last four games, one rushing and one receiving, but his current usage gives him little upside. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Kimani Vidal remains stuck in a committee in the Chargers' backfield. While Vidal turned eight touches into 36 scrimmage yards in a Week 9 loss to the Texans, Omarion Hampton gained a team-high 60 rushing yards on 13 carries, and Keaton Mitchell put together 67 scrimmage yards on 10 touches. That leaves Vidal dependent on TDs or injuries around him on the depth chart for value. He'll try to make a splash in Week 10 against a Ravens defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kimani Vidal nearly disappeared from the Chargers' game plan in their first win of the season. During a Week 10 win over the Ravens, he gained zero yards on two carries while catching both his targets for 14 yards, his lowest touch volume since Week 3. Omarion Hampton, meanwhile, broke out for 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries, potentially ending the team's backfield committee. Vidal will try to make a splash in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kimani Vidal has remained a steady part of the Chargers' game plan in recent weeks. The third-year running back has handled at least eight touches in five of the last six games, managing 167 rushing yards and a touchdown over that stretch on 4.3 yards per carry while adding an 11-63-0 line on 15 targets. While Omarion Hampton has reasserted himself as the top back, a knee injury to Keaton Mitchell could reduce Vidal's competition for backup snaps. Vidal will try to take advantage of what volume he gets in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Returning for his third year with the Chargers, Vidal is set to compete with newcomer Keaton Mitchell for change-of-pace touches behind Omarion Hampton. Vidal had some big moments in 2025, clearing 17 fantasy points in four games, but the notable disclaimer here is that Hampton was sidelined for all of those outings. In fact, Vidal scored only 4.1 fantasy PPG in his other nine games. The 2024 sixth-round pick is a fine depth player who showed he can handle big workloads when needed, but he'll be worth rostering only should Hampton miss time and, even then, Mitchell figures to play a role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Bass continues to be busy for the high-scoring Bills' offense as they enter a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. In Week 1, Bass made three extra points and three field goals, though none were 50-plus yards. Detroit's defense, particularly the secondary, was suspect a week ago, and the Bills should score plenty, making Bass appealing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Bass will attempt to bounce back from his first miss of the season when the Bills host the Chargers in Week 3. Bass wasn't afforded a field goal try in Week 2, with Buffalo's offense finding the end zone with ease, but still provided a reasonable floor, hitting five of six extra points. The Bills' offensive efficiency could cap Bass' scoring potential, but historically, the highest-scoring kickers come from the highest-scoring teams.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Bass' opportunities have been limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup between the Bills and Patriots. Through three weeks, Bass has attempted only four field goals, though Buffalo's high-powered offense has generated 12 extra points. New England's defense remains stingy, allowing just 15 total points to opposing kickers, likely keeping Bass out of Week 4 consideration.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Bass remains a stable floor, low ceiling kicking option for the Bills as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. Bass has collected 14 extra points through four weeks as Buffalo routinely converts drives into touchdowns, but only six field goal attempts, where he's perfect, keeping his scoring capacity limited. The Rams' defense has been stingy to opposing kickers, so don't expect Week 5 to be Bass' breakout party.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Bass is trending up as the Bills get set to face the Raiders in Week 6. Extra points will remain consistent in Buffalo's efficient offense, as Bass has at least three attempts in four of five games, but his field goals increased each of the last three weeks. Las Vegas, however, has been stingy to opposing kicker scoring, surrendering 16 PATs but just six field-goal tries as teams routinely convert drives into touchdowns. Bass' floor Sunday looks stable, but the ceiling may be low.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Bass has increased his workload over the last three weeks as Buffalo gets set to face Baltimore in Week 8. Always a steady source for PATs in Buffalo's high-scoring offense (Bass has made at least two in every game), he went from four field goals across his first three games to nine over his last three. None have come from 50-plus yards, potentially keeping bonus scoring off the table. Baltimore is a mid-tier defense for points allowed to kickers, but they've allowed as many field goal attempts as extra points through seven games, setting Bass up for a strong Week 8.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Bass has been busy for the Bills ahead of a difficult Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. He has multiple field goals in four straight weeks, 12 in total. Bass has added upside to his stable floor in Buffalo's high-scoring offense, which has yielded 21 extra points in seven games. Minnesota has allowed only six field goals and 11 made PATs all season, putting Bass' hot streak in jeopardy.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Bass continues to see heavy volume in the Bills' prolific offense ahead of a Week 10 matchup with the Jets. Seemingly always assured of a handful of PATs, making at least two in every game, Bass has at least three field goals in four straight games, creating double-digit scoring upside with consistency. The Jets are allowing the ninth-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing kickers however, largely due to opponents converting drives into touchdowns, surrendering just 13 field goal attempts in nine games, which should test Bass' current form.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Bass faces unsettled scoring chances when the Bills host the Dolphins in Week 11. After attempting multiple field goals in five straight games, Bass tried just one in Week 10 with Buffalo coasting to a win and converting drives into touchdowns. That script seems likely to manifest again in Week 11 against an overmatched Miami defense, so while Bass will have a multi-PAT floor, his ceiling could be capped.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tyler Bass continues to thrive in the Bills' potent offense ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. He converted four of five field goal attempts and two extra points in Week 11, his fifth game in his last six with at least three field goals. While the Chiefs have allowed only 12 PATs in 10 games, they've surrendered 22 field goals, and with Buffalo likely to test that defense more than other opponents, Bass should again earn enough scoring chances to merit heavy fantasy consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Saints and their defense, which ranks 13th in fantasy points allowed per game (11.3) to TEs, in Week 2. Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. With Flowers and a host of other receivers dealing with injuries, Andrews could be in line for additional looks as a safety net for Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to rebound from an upset defeat when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. He caught six of seven targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss, making it two straight outings with exactly 49 receiving yards for the 31-year-old. Andrews draws a favorable matchup versus a Dallas defense that surrendered eight receptions for 78 yards and two TDs to Isaiah Likely in the season opener. The Cowboys rank 26th in fantasy points allowed (16.9) and are one of two teams with a catch rate of 100% to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mark Andrews and the Ravens welcome the 0-3 Titans to town for a Week 4 showdown. After missing some time with a hand injury during Baltimore's 34-31 Week 3 win, Andrews returned and ultimately finished with three catches for 24 yards on five targets. He's still in search of his first TD of 2026, but he's been consistently involved on offense, totaling 18 targets across three contests. Andrews could find it difficult to break through in the scoring department against the Titans' third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (7.4) to TEs, as they're one of nine teams yet to surrender a receiving touchdown to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are on the road for the first time since the season opener to face the Falcons in Week 5. He corralled five of six targets for 27 yards and his first touchdown of the season in Baltimore's Week 4 win. Andrews has yet to top 50 yards receiving through four outings to date, and that trend could continue if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to play on Sunday Night Football. The veteran tight end will aim to find paydirt for the second straight week against Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (15.9) per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are in Cleveland for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He caught four of six targets for 28 yards and lost a fumble during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Andrews is averaging a solid six targets through five outings in 2026, but he's yet to top 50 receiving yards, only has one touchdown, and tallies 35.4 yards per contest. He'll look to break out versus a Browns defense that's tied for 19th in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are back home to square off against the Bengals in Week 7. He caught one of three targets for four yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Andrews turned in his worst performance of the season on a day the Ravens tallied a meager 252 total yards of offense. Fellow tight end Josh Cuevas, a rookie fifth-round pick in 2026, recorded a 4-44-1 line on five targets, finishing second on the team in yardage while tying for second in receptions and targets. Andrews will look to rebound versus Cincinnati's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (16.2) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Mark Andrews and the Ravens travel to face the Bills in Week 8. He caught three of four targets for 23 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 defeat in Week 7. Andrews was unable to take advantage of game flow, as Tyler Huntley attempted 34 passes and threw for a career-high 298 yards. Andrews has failed to top 30 receiving yards in five straight outings, making him a tough start in fantasy despite the potential return of Lamar Jackson (ankle).
outlooksByWeek.9: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Jaguars for an AFC showdown in Week 9. He caught three of four targets for 14 yards during Baltimore's 36-10 Week 8 defeat. Andrews finished second on the team in receptions and third in targets, but the entire Ravens offense struggled with Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both forced out with injuries. Andrews has compiled an underwhelming 29-218-1 receiving line on 41 targets through seven games this season. Fantasy managers should look elsewhere, with the 31-year-old squaring off against Jacksonville's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (11.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Mark Andrews and the Ravens welcome the winless Chargers to town. He caught both of his targets for 19 yards during Baltimore's Week 9 loss. Andrews actually led the team in receiving yardage and was second behind Zay Flowers and Justice Hill in receptions, who each recorded three. Jacoby Brissett will earn his first start for the Ravens after being acquired via trade, but Andrews could find it difficult to operate versus a Chargers defense allowing 10.0 fantasy points per game (3rd) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to snap a five-game losing streak when they visit the 4-5 Panthers. He's coming off easily his best outing of the season in Week 10's loss, as he caught all eight of his targets for 82 yards while leading the team in receptions and yardage. Andrews established new season highs in each receiving category with the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett making his first start for Baltimore. Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards, and if that trend continues for the Ravens' offense, Andrews could be primed for a much larger role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Mark Andrews and the Ravens are back on the road to battle the Texans. He brought in two of three targets for 14 yards during Baltimore's loss in Week 11. Andrews' follow-up to his season-best performance in Week 10 was disappointing, especially when considering Jacoby Brissett attempted 37 passes and the Ravens scored 33 points. Next up for Andrews is a Houston defense allowing 10.0 fantasy points per game to TEs, the second-lowest mark in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

outlooksByWeek.2: James Cook will seek higher volume when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Cook logged just 13 carries in a surprisingly high-scoring opener in Houston, going for 57 yards while adding three catches on four targets but failing to reach the end zone after scoring 32 times over the last two seasons. Detroit's defense allowed a fair 4.0 yards per carry last week but is far more vulnerable through the air. Cook's bulk role is unquestioned, keeping his floor stable while a potential shootout creates more chances for him to reach pay dirt.
outlooksByWeek.3: James Cook faces a challenge for fantasy managers in the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Cook and Buffalo's offense motored through Detroit last week, their lead back finishing with 139 total yards and a touchdown. The Chargers have been stingy against the run, allowing a mere 2.98 yards per carry to the likes of Ashton Jeanty and Jeremiah Love. Teams beat them through the air with far greater ease. Cook's role in this potent offense is unquestioned, but tempered expectations in Week 3 appear prudent.
outlooksByWeek.4: James Cook figures to see a heavy workload in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Cook has consecutive games with at least 21 carries, topping 134 yards in each while scoring twice. He's not heavily involved in the passing game, with just four catches after at least 32 grabs the last two years, and the return of Ty Johnson doesn't inspire confidence. New England just allowed a season-high 73 yards to Jacksonville's lead back Bhayshul Tuten, but they held Cook to 156 yards in two meetings last year. There's little doubt Cook will be heavily featured, but he may need to reach the end zone for a massive Week 4 contribution.
outlooksByWeek.5: James Cook will likely require volume to exploit a Rams defense when the Bills face them in their Week 5 Monday night affair. Cook has now scored in three straight games, but his workload was minimal in Week 4 against New England, rushing a season-low 12 times. The Rams have been stout against the run, not allowing a running back to score through four games and allowing just 3.9 yards per carry, and Cook's lack of involvement in the passing game further dampens the outlook. So long as Buffalo doesn't fall behind early and is forced to throw often, Cook remains stable, but Week 5 profiles as a night to temper lofty expectations.
outlooksByWeek.6: James Cook will seek the end zone for the fifth straight week when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. While Cook hasn't been heavily targeted in the passing game, he's posted 100-plus yard rushing efforts in three of his last four outings, garnering at least 21 carries at the same rate. Buffalo is a run-first offense, and the Week 6 matchup is very appealing; Las Vegas allows 5.2 yards per carry, again setting up Cook to be a top-tier option.
outlooksByWeek.8: James Cook needs heavy volume in Week 8 to bolster Buffalo's offense against the Ravens. That hasn't been a problem, as he's amassed 20-plus touches in four of the Bills' first six outings, and he's continued scoring, finding the end zone in each of his last five games. Prior to a Week 7 bye, Cook had his best game as a receiver, possibly elevating his floor even higher. Baltimore is a stout defense against the run, allowing just 3.8 yards per carry, the eighth-lowest total in the league, but they have surrendered 86 yards or more to an opposing back three times. Barring an unexpected change in usage, Cook should be able to flirt with those numbers in Week 8.
outlooksByWeek.9: James Cook brings a six-game scoring streak into the Bills' Week 9 matchup against a stingy Vikings defense. He topped 20 carries in three straight contests and five of seven overall. Cook added five catches for 79 yards in his last two games after just 31 yards in his first five. Minnesota has allowed only four rushing scores through seven games, but a healthy 4.6 yards per carry in a blitz-heavy scheme. With Cook assured of heavy usage, he appears poised for solid production.
outlooksByWeek.10: James Cook's high volume creates a high floor and ceiling heading into the Bills' Week 10 matchup with the Jets. Cook amassed a season-high 31 carries in Week 9, his sixth game in eight outings with 20-plus touches, and has topped 100 total yards at the same ratio while scoring in seven straight games. While the Bills have a short week coming off a Monday night game, nothing has been shown to suggest Cook's role will be reduced. This suggests he'll run wild on a Jets defense that's allowing the eighth-most fantasy points to opposing running backs and one he posted 132 yards and two touchdowns against in one healthy outing in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.11: James Cook brings an eight-game scoring streak into the Bills' Week 11 matchup with the Dolphins. He has at least 18 carries in five straight games and has topped 100 rushing yards in five of nine outings overall. Cook hasn't caught a pass in two weeks, an area where Miami has been vulnerable, allowing five touchdown receptions to running backs, the same number of rushing touchdowns they've surrendered. A quick turnaround to a Week 12 Thursday night game is the only concern for Cook's workload and high-end production.
outlooksByWeek.12: James Cook brings his usual heavy workload and a nine-game scoring streak into the Bills' challenging Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. Cook collected 22 carries (on only 40 snaps) in Week 11 and is averaging 20.9 carries through 10 games. Despite a short turnaround to Thursday in Week 12, Cook's bell-cow role is secure, and he'll need that volume against a Kansas City front that's allowing just 3.5 yards per carry and six touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: Cook signed a contract extension last offseason and was immediately vaulted into the biggest role of his career. The 2022 second-round NFL draft pick finished in the top five among backs in carries, rushing yards (league-high 1,621), touchdowns and yards per carry (5.25). The one limiting factor in Cook's fantasy output was a minimal receiving role (his 40 targets ranked 26th among RBs), but he still came through with a sixth-place finish in fantasy points. The 26-year-old is set to play the same role in Joe Brady's scheme and will be a candidate for his third straight double-digit touchdown campaign as long as Josh Allen is under center. Consider Cook a midrange RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ashton Jeanty looked like a franchise back in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins, turning 29 touches into 147 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The ankle injury that limited him in training camp and the preseason was no longer an issue, and the second-year RB dominated the workload, as rookie backup Mike Washington notched only seven carries. Jeanty's pass-catching role could be cut back once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to return, but he will remain a focal point of the offense heading into a Week 2 clash with a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
