outlooksByWeek.3: Ashton Jeanty has looked the part of a bell-cow running back to begin his second NFL season, amassing 54 touches through two games and turning them into 210 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The 2025 first-round pick is still only averaging 3.4 yards per carry however, and the Raiders' offseason upgrades to the offensive line haven't yet led to better efficiency on the ground for Jeanty. He'll try to take advantage of a Week 3 clash with a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ashton Jeanty continues to garner a big workload for the Raiders, but he isn't yet consistently producing big numbers. Through three games, the second-year back is tied for third in the NFL in touches with 76, behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson, but Jeanty's averaging just 3.3 yards per carry and his 303 scrimmage yards are only 14th in the league. He also has yet to score a rushing touchdown in 2026, although he did haul in two TD catches in Week 1. Jeanty will try to improve his efficiency in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ashton Jeanty continues to bolster his lackluster rushing numbers with big production through the air. In the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, the second-year RB managed just 58 rushing yards on 15 carries, but he added six catches for 68 yards on a season-high eight targets. Jeanty's 3.4 yards per carry and zero TDs on the ground through four weeks are a concern, but his 19-165-2 line on 24 targets softens the blow. He'll take on a Patriots defense in Week 5 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ashton Jeanty continues to keep his production afloat via his skills as a pass-catcher. The second-year running back is averaging just 3.3 yards per carry after another poor showing on the ground in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, but he's supplied a 22-215-2 line on 30 targets through five games. The 30 targets are third in the league among RBs, behind the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs and the Rams' Kyren Williams, while Jeanty's receiving yards are third behind Gibbs and the Steelers' Jaylen Warren. Jeanty will try to deliver a more well-rounded line in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and 31st in receiving TDs allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ashton Jeanty scored his first rushing touchdown of the season in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, but it was otherwise another lackluster performance for the second-year running back. Jeanty is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry, and the inefficiency is costing him volume, as he hasn't handled 20-plus touches in a game since Week 4. He remains involved as a pass catcher, however, hauling in at least three passes in every game this year while compiling a 26-251-2 line on 36 targets through six contests. Jeanty could contribute through the air in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but 29th in receiving yards per game allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground while making an impact as a pass catcher. In the Raiders' Week 7 loss to the Rams, the second-year player gained a season-low 15 rushing yards on eight carries, but caught all eight of his targets for 61 yards and a touchdown. Jeanty has gotten at least six targets in six of seven games so far in 2026, turning that volume into a 34-312-3 line on 44 looks. but his 3.1 yards per carry suggests he simply isn't cut out to be a No. 1 back. He'll try to bring some balance to his stat line in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Ashton Jeanty is coming off another poor effort, managing just 20 scrimmage yards on 11 touches in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers. This time, he wasn't overshadowed by rookie Mike Washington, who lost a total of three yards on his six carries. Jeanty maintains a shaky hold on the top spot in the backfield, but he hasn't reached 30 rushing yards in a game since Week 4, and his contributions of late have been limited to his usage as a pass-catcher. Jeanty isn't likely to turn things around in Week 10 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Ashton Jeanty failed to generate much production in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, gaining 18 rushing yards on nine carries and catching all four of his targets for 46 yards. It's the sixth time in the last seven games he's generated more yards through the air than on the ground, but his hold on the No. 1 job in the backfield may have tightened a bit with Mike Washington struggling over the last two weeks as well. Jeanty's outlook as a pass-catcher could improve if Brock Bowers misses time due to an ankle injury. During the two games the star tight end sat out at the beginning of the season, Jeanty caught 10 of 13 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Ashton Jeanty finally had a breakout performance in the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The second-year running back gained 79 yards on the ground on just 11 carries, while adding a 5-90-1 line on eight targets. With the Las Vegas offense looking like it will stay effective with rookie Fernando Mendoza at quarterback, Jeanty should get more opportunities to establish himself as a three-down threat, but his primary strength still appears to be as a pass catcher, and he leads all RBs this season in targets, catches and receiving yards. In Week 12, Jeanty will take aim at a Browns defense that has been among the stingiest in the NFL in receiving production allowed to backs, but which ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeanty is eyeing a leap forward in his second NFL season after an uneven rookie campaign in which the first-round pick enjoyed a ton of volume (seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions) and played fairly well (eighth among RBs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF) but struggled to overcome the shaky Las Vegas offense. The good news is that the Raiders' offense should improve in 2026 with a better/healthier offensive line, a new coach in Super Bowl champion Klint Kubiak and a new quarterback in projected No. 1 NFL draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Jeanty has a clean path to a massive offensive role and is a strong bet for a leap forward. The 22-year-old is a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for Dallas. Williams rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, while catching five passes for 31 yards and a second score, though the Cowboys fell to the Giants by a score of 28-20. Nevertheless, Williams appears to have picked up right where he left off in 2025 during his career year. In Week 2, Williams will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL in that category currently.
outlooksByWeek.3: Javonte Williams was rather quiet last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 50 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone versus Washington, as the passing game took the spotlight in the 37-20 win. Williams may also have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL. However, Baltimore has allowed three rushing touchdowns already, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 98 yards last game for the Cowboys. Williams also found the end zone for the third time this year. He has received at least 15 touches in every game this season. In Week 4, WIlliams should continue to remain heavily involved against the Houston Texans. The Texans have been extremely stingy against the run, though. Houston is surrendering just 86.7 rushing yards per clash, which is fifth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Javonte Williams scored three times in the second half of the last game for the Cowboys, leading a thrilling comeback victory over the Texans. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote this season, but has six combined touchdowns through four outings. He has also made his presence felt in the passing game with 15 receptions over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again last game for Dallas. Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and the score, notching his sixth rushing touchdown of the young season. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote, but has received double-digit carries in every contest in 2026. In Week 6, Williams looks primed for another jaunt to the end zone versus the Packers. Green Bay has given up eight rushing touchdowns already this season, which is 31st in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again for Dallas last game. Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Williams has scored in four-straight games for the Cowboys, though is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote overall. In fact, he has failed to cross the 50-yard rushing mark in two-straight games. In Week 7, Williams will face a sliding Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per contest, which is 19th in the league. The Eagles have also yielded eight rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 28th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Javonte Williams was largely held in check last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 56 yards rushing on 24 carries. He was also held out of the end zone for just the second time all season. The workload remains stellar, though, as Williams now has a staggering 49 carries in the last two contests alone. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense that has been subpar against the run. Indy is allowing 131.8 rushing yards per tote, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Javonte Williams got back into the end zone last game for Dallas. Williams scored his ninth rushing touchdown of the season in the 27-23 win over the Colts. Williams also crossed the 100-yard rushing plateau for the second time in 2026. Williams has at least 20 carries in each of the last three outings. However, in Week 10, he will face a difficult task versus the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 80.9 rushing yards per game, which is second in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for second in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Javonte Williams was held out of the end zone for the second time in three games for the Cowboys. Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Williams was also held under 65 yards rushing for the second time in three contests. However, his usage remains high, as he has received double-digit carries in every game in 2026. In Week 11, Williams will face a Titans squad that has been lackluster against the run. Tennessee is allowing 124 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Javonte Williams scored twice last game for the Cowboys.  Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and one touchdown on the ground, while also catching three passes for 24 yards and a second score during the 51-30 blowout of the Titans. Williams has 12 combined touchdowns through 11 contests for Dallas. In Week 12, he will face an Eagles defense allowing 120.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL.  Likewise, Philadelphia has surrendered 10 rushing scores this season, which is tied for 18th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carnell Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards during his NFL debut, but he had just 38 yards on six targets as Titans QB Cam Ward threw for a meager 140 yards. Tennessee's passing game is likely to struggle again in Week 2 against Philadelphia's excellent secondary, led by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Tate is likely to maintain a prominent role on the rebuilding Titans after being drafted fourth overall out of Ohio State, but the rookie WR is hard to trust as anything more than a fantasy WR3 or flex play until Tennessee's offense shows some life.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carnell Tate is off to an uninspiring start, with seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets through two games with the Titans. A Week 3 road game against the injury-riddled Giants presents a nice opportunity for the rookie fourth overall pick out of Ohio State to break out, as the Giants just allowed 195 receiving yards and two TDs to Rams WR Davante Adams. Tate leads his team in targets through two games, but the Titans have struggled to move the ball through the air. Given Tate's draft pedigree and matchup, he's a high-ceiling fantasy WR3 for Week 3, though it's fair for fantasy managers to be hesitant given the highly touted rookie's lackluster production so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Carnell Tate has 20 targets through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 road game against the Ravens, turning that decent volume into a pedestrian 13 catches for 123 yards, averaging 41 yards per game. Tennessee's entire passing game is tough to trust given the struggles of QB Cam Ward, but Tate has the most upside among the team's pass catchers. A Week 4 breakout is possible against a Ravens defense that has given up the second-most catches to WRs, especially if the Titans fall behind and are forced to air it out, but Tate can't be trusted as anything more than a flex option until Ward shows signs of progress.
outlooksByWeek.5: Carnell Tate broke out in Week 4 against the Ravens, recording 145 receiving yards after totaling just 123 yards over his first three games for the Titans. The rookie fourth-overall pick has been limited by the struggles of second-year QB Cam Ward, who is averaging just 182 passing yards per game. Tate is likely to match up frequently with top Texans CB Derek Stingley in Week 5, but Stingley and company have allowed the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and touchdown receptions (six) to wide receivers. With Tate trending in the right direction, he's a high-upside flex option for Week 5 as the promising rookie continues to search for his first NFL touchdown.
outlooksByWeek.6: Carnell Tate crashed back down to earth in Week 5, producing just one catch for six yards against the Texans while playing through a back injury after breaking out for a career-high 145 receiving yards against the Eagles in Week 4. Tennessee's fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will likely remain a boom-or-bust fantasy option throughout his rookie campaign while occupying a starting role in what has been the worst offense in the league. A Week 6 road game against the Colts appears more likely to deliver a peak than a valley, assuming Tate is close to full health, as Indianapolis is giving up 160 receiving yards per game and 15 yards per catch to wideouts. Tate is a high-ceiling Week 6 flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Carnell Tate had 70 receiving yards and his first NFL touchdown in Tennessee's Week 6 win over the Colts and broke out for 145 receiving yards against the Ravens in Week 4, but he was held to just six yards by the Texans in between. The rookie, fourth overall pick is still searching for consistency in a Titans passing game that ranks among the league's worst, but Tate has shown enough upside to warrant a lineup spot as a flex option in most formats heading into a Week 7 home game against the Browns. Cleveland has been weaker than league average at defending wide receivers, allowing 157 yards per game and seven TDs in six games to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Carnell Tate has recorded at least 69 receiving yards in three of his last four games, establishing himself as a reliable fantasy option despite the ongoing struggles of Titans QB Cam Ward. Facing a Bengals defense that just allowed eight catches for 137 yards and a TD to top Ravens WR Zay Flowers, Tate is a high-end flex option for Week 8. The rookie fourth overall pick is averaging more than seven targets per game and could get plenty of opportunities if the 1-6 Titans fall behind as expected on the road against the 4-2 Bengals.
outlooksByWeek.10: Carnell Tate sat out Tennessee's Week 8 loss to the Bengals prior to a Week 9 bye due to a shoulder injury. The rookie, fourth overall pick is expected to return in Week 10 against the Jaguars and will likely reprise his role as the top option in Tennessee's underwhelming passing offense. Tate racked up at least 69 yards in three of his last four appearances, making him a strong flex play in a game that's likely to feature a negative game script for the 1-7 Titans, leading to more passes. The 6-2 Jaguars are allowing 175 yards per game to WRs, though they have limited the position to four TDs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Carnell Tate hasn't played since Week 7 due to a shoulder injury. Prior to his absence, the rookie fourth overall pick had at least 69 receiving yards in three of his last four appearances. If Tate gets the green light to play in Week 11, he would be a high-end flex option against a Dallas defense that's allowing 158 yards and a TD per game through the air to wide receivers. Titans QB Cam Ward is coming off his two best outings of the season in Tate's absence.
outlooksByWeek.12: Carnell Tate got into his first game action since Week 7 and scored a 59-yard touchdown in his return from a shoulder injury in Week 11 against the Cowboys. His other four targets went for a combined minus-1 yard, and Tate finished third on the Titans in both receiving yards and targets, trailing Chimere Dike and Calvin Ridley. Tate continues to have the highest ceiling among Tennessee's pass catchers, and the team's entire offense has been trending up lately, even though that improvement hasn't translated to wins heading into a Week 12 trip to Jacksonville. This will be Tate's first encounter with a Jaguars defense that's allowing 162 yards per game to WRs but has held the position to five TDs, as he missed the Week 10 meeting between these AFC South rivals. The rookie, fourth overall pick is a solid fantasy WR3 or flex option.

player.seasonOutlook: Tate was selected by the Titans with the fourth overall pick of April's draft. He didn't see a ton of volume at Ohio State, but he was efficient, averaging 13.1 yards per target (first in this rookie WR class) and 3.06 yards per route run (third) in 2025. He also paced the class in YPT for his career (11.6) and caught an impressive 75% of his targets during the 39-game span. Tate underwhelmed in the 40-yard dash at the combine (4.53 at 192 pounds), but he measured in with big hands and a large wingspan. Wide receivers selected in the top 10 handle, on average, one-quarter of their team's targets and generally deliver WR2/3 fantasy production. Cam Ward's development will be key here, but Tate's combination of talent and projected target volume is enough to make him an appealing WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake Maye will hope to clean up mistakes when the Patriots host the Steelers in Week 2. Maye threw three interceptions in the season opener while under constant pressure, and Pittsburgh's defense, led by T.J. Watt, recorded four sacks last week. While the chemistry was still developing, Maye is now also without No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) for the immediate future, leading to questionable receiving options. While Maye remains a dangerous runner that will keep his floor reasonable, this likely low-scoring game may not be ideal for a true bounce-back performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake Maye will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. He is averaging just 183 passing yards through two weeks, with only one touchdown pass and four interceptions. Maye was picked off just eight times all last season. Opponents seem to be pressuring Maye, though Jacksonville is middling at getting after the passer. However, they've allowed only two touchdown passes while limiting quarterbacks to 44 rushing yards. With A.J. Brown still sidelined, Maye will be challenged to exhibit his 2025 form.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake Maye's confidence appears shaken in the face of pressure ahead of the Patriots' Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Maye has a 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, completing just 14 passes in each of his last two games while posting a season-high of 208 yards in Week 2. While he remains dangerous with his legs, he's been held to 18 yards or fewer in Weeks 2 and 3. Buffalo's defense is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks, giving up seven touchdowns with just one interception. The game could be high-scoring or at least force the Patriots to try and match points, but Maye didn't throw a touchdown pass against this unit a year ago.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake Maye will look to carry momentum in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders. After a dismal 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, Maye provided a season-high 269 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 yards on eight rushes in Week 4 against Buffalo. Las Vegas is surrendering a 7:4 TD:INT ratio through four games, with six of those touchdowns coming in the last two weeks, suggesting Maye can provide the 2025 version expected by his fantasy managers in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake Maye will look to extend his hot streak to three games in Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets. After a terrible start to his season (one touchdown, six interceptions), Maye has produced eight touchdowns and one interception over the last two weeks. The Jets are statistically stout against the pass, allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks (195.4 yards per game), but it's come against the likes of Cam Ward, Deshaun Watson, and the Bears' backups. Maye averaged 268.5 yards and threw six touchdown passes in two games against the Jets last season, suggesting his surge can continue in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake Maye hopes to extend his hot streak to four games when the Patriots face the Bears in Week 7. After throwing just one touchdown in his first three games, Maye has burst out with 10 touchdown passes and a scoring rush over his last three games. He now has his full complement of receivers with A.J. Brown returning from an ankle injury. Chicago has allowed two 300-yard passers and multiple touchdown passes three times to date, giving Maye an opportunity to continue his current form Thursday night.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake Maye's recent surge should continue when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. In Week 7, he topped 300 passing yards for the second time in three weeks and also added a rushing touchdown for the second time in three games, bringing his total to 14 touchdowns over his last four games. Miami's secondary has been decimated by opposing signal-callers, allowing seven touchdown passes in the last two weeks, multiple touchdown passes in five of six games, and the third-worst yards per attempt at 8.1. This firmly entrenches Maye in Week 8 lineups.
outlooksByWeek.9: Drake Maye will look to continue providing elite production when the Patriots face the Packers in Week 9. While his volume was low, Maye completed a season-high 80% of his passes in Week 8, tossing multiple touchdowns for the fifth straight week while running for a score for the third time in four games. The Packers figure to offer fair resistance, allowing multiple touchdown passes just twice all season, snagging as many interceptions as touchdowns (10) while surrendering just 6.2 yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Drake Maye appears poised for a busy outing in Week 10 when the Patriots face the Lions. Maye has tossed multiple touchdown passes in six straight outings (17 total), three times going for 299 yards or more, and could be asked to throw at a high rate with running backs TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson uncertain to suit up. Pair that with a matchup against a Lions secondary that's allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks, and Maye could provide elite numbers in Week 10's Sunday morning affair in Germany.

player.seasonOutlook: Maye is entering his third NFL season and second full season as New England's starter. The 2024 No. 3 draft pick is fresh off a breakout 2025 campaign in which he finished in the top five among quarterbacks in pass completions, yards and TDs, as well as rush attempts and yards. Maye, who led the league in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9), trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points (351.9), fantasy points per game (20.7) and top-10 fantasy weeks (10). The NFL MVP runner-up will need to overcome a tougher schedule, but he has a better supporting cast (including A.J. Brown) and the 24-year-old's combination of passing talent and rushing ability have him well positioned for another top-five fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in New England to face the Patriots in Week 2. The veteran wideout corralled four of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win against the Falcons. He led the team in targets by four but finished third in receiving yards. Metcalf has a hypothetical advantage over Michael Pittman after playing last year with Aaron Rodgers, and there's a good chance he'll be his favorite target against New England's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional clash. He caught four of a team-high nine targets for just 27 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Metcalf finished fifth in yardage despite tying Germie Bernard and Pat Freiermuth for second in receptions, and he now has an 8-67-0 receiving line on 19 targets through two outings. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense have been underwhelming to begin the season, and they'll face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North clash between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught three of five targets for 31 yards and his first TD of the season during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. Metcalf has an 11-98-1 receiving line on 24 targets through three contests, as he and Aaron Rodgers have had a hard time connecting in their second season together. With that being said, it'll be difficult to trust Metcalf until the duo is on the same page, even against a beatable Cleveland secondary allowing 36.7 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 26th.
outlooksByWeek.5: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Colts in a Week 5 clash between 2-2 teams. He caught five of nine targets for 115 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Metcalf turned in his best performance of the season by far while leading his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He'll look to stay hot against a beatable Indianapolis secondary that allows 35.0 fantasy points per game (20th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are on the road to take on the Buccaneers in Week 6. He caught three of four targets for 12 yards and rushed once for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Metcalf and Darnell Washington tied for the fewest receiving yards on the team, while the veteran wideout finished fourth in targets. He'll try to rebound against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs and just gave up nine receptions for 130 yards and a TD to George Pickens.
outlooksByWeek.7: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 showdown against the Saints. He caught 11 of 15 targets for 93 yards in Pittsburgh's gritty comeback victory in Week 6. Metcalf led the team in yardage and targets while tying with rookie Germie Bernard (11-87-1) for first in receptions. The 11 catches were a product of game flow with the Steelers playing from behind most of the game, and they were Metcalf's most on the season by far, as he had the same number of receptions over his previous three games combined. He'll look to take advantage of a New Orleans defense that just allowed Malik Nabers to record a 12-165-0 line on 15 targets.
outlooksByWeek.8: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 showdown with first place in the AFC North on the line. He brought in two of six targets for 56 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 win in Paris. Metcalf tied for the lead in targets while pacing the team in yardage despite his low reception count. He'll be ready to face a Cleveland defense he cooked for a season-high 115 yards on five catches in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.10: DK Metcalf and the Steelers travel to Cincinnati for a divisional clash in Week 10. He caught just one of six targets for four yards during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 8, giving the 28-year-old a 3-60-0 receiving line on 12 targets over his last two contests. Metcalf and the Steelers didn't have to throw much while playing most of Week 8 with a double-digit advantage, but that could change in Week 10 versus a high-powered Bengals offense on Sunday Night Football. In his first matchup against Cincinnati, Metcalf corralled three of five targets for 31 yards and his only TD of the season.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, DK Metcalf and the Steelers visit an Eagles defense allowing 37.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs. In Week 10, he hauled in two of six targets for 54 yards, including a 32-yard touchdown, during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss. Metcalf found the end zone for just the second time all season and the first time since Week 3. Despite the favorable matchup, Metcalf remains an inconsistent fantasy option for a team that prefers to run the ball.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, DK Metcalf and the Steelers look to stay undefeated at home when they battle the Broncos on Black Friday. He caught one of four targets for two yards before being ejected in the third quarter of Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Metcalf's season continues to spiral out of control, and luckily for him, the veteran receiver will not face a suspension from the league following the scuffle. Metcalf will be on the field versus Denver, but he should remain on fantasy benches.

player.seasonOutlook: Metcalf returns for Year 2 in Pittsburgh after a solid but unspectacular debut season. The ex-Seahawk missed two games and finished outside the top 20 receivers in targets, catches and yardage (career-low 850), but still did just enough to produce a 21st-place finish in fantasy PPG (his fifth top-25 in his last six seasons). Metcalf soaked up 11 end zone targets and is up to 107 for his career, which leads the NFL since his debut in 2019. The 28-year-old has added target competition this season in the form of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, so while he'll certainly remain busy, a slight dip in usage is probable. Metcalf should be valued as a back-end WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Kelce showed he still has plenty left in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, leading the team with 71 receiving yards while catching three of five targets. The veteran tight end's production tailed off the last couple years, but he still topped 800 receiving yards in 12 straight seasons, and Week 1's performance moved him past Jason Witten into second place on the NFL's all-time list for TEs with 13,073 yards, trailing only Tony Gonzalez's 15,127. Kelce will take on a Colts defense in Week 2 that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to tight ends in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Kelce continued a strong start to his 14th NFL season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 9-101-1 line on 11 targets. The future Hall of Famer last delivered a 1,000-yard campaign in 2022, but he's jumped out to an early pace in 2026 that would see him top 1,400 receiving yards and set a new career high. With Patrick Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Kelce may need to rely on spike games rather than steady production for his fantasy value. He'll take on a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's allowed 10.2 yards per target to tight ends through two weeks, 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Kelce notched just two targets in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, but he caught both for 59 yards and a touchdown. The future Hall of Famer seems revitalized in his age-36 season, and he's already hauled in two catches of 40 or more yards, just one short of the career-high three he produced way back in 2016. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around effectively, and Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets through three games. The tight end has turned his volume into a strong 14-231-2 line. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs and has already coughed up five TDs to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Travis Kelce remains on pace for a bounce-back season coming out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye. Through four games, the veteran tight end is on pace for his first 1,000-yard season since 2022, although it's fair to wonder if he can keep that up given his reduced volume, as he's also on track to fall short of 100 targets for the first time since 2014. With Kenneth Walker having rejuvenated the team's rushing game and Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy both capable of handling underneath and intermediate routes, there isn't a clear niche for Kelce to thrive in. He remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, and that should keep his floor relatively high. Kelce will take on a Chargers defense in Week 6 that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Travis Kelce wasn't needed much in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, catching four of five targets for 53 yards. The veteran tight end has slowed down after a fast start to the season, and through five games he's produced a 20-299-2 line on 27 targets while the offense has leaned heavily on Kenneth Walker. Kelce remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, especially while Rashee Rice is sidelined. Kelce faces a tough matchup in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that's allowed the fewest receiving yards in the league to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Travis Kelce made history again in Week 7, moving into fifth place on the NFL's all-time reception list with 1,104 as Kansas City fell to the Seahawks. The veteran tight end remains Patrick Mahomes' most reliable pass catcher, and through six games, Kelce's delivered a 24-343-2 line on 35 targets. The 37-year-old is no longer as dangerous with the ball in his hands, but he can still move the chains consistently. Kelce will take on a Broncos defense in Week 8 that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Travis Kelce caught five of seven targets for 67 yards in Kansas City's Week 8 loss to the Broncos, his best performance since delivering a 9-101-1 line in Week 2. The veteran tight end remains one of Patrick Mahomes' most trusted options, and Kelce has a shot at his first 1,000-yard effort since 2022 if he can maintain his current pace. He could be poised for solid numbers again in Week 9 against a Jets defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Travis Kelce produced his highest yardage total since Week 2 in Kansas City's Week 9 win over the Jets, hauling in four of six targets for a team-high 72 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2021 on a one-yard plunge. Kelce has delivered a 33-482-2 line on 48 targets through eight games, but his outlook would suffer if Patrick Mahomes ends up missing time due to an elbow injury he picked up against the Jets. Regardless of who's under center, Kelce will face a Falcons defense in Week 10 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Travis Kelce is coming off his least productive game of the season, catching both his targets for 30 yards in Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons. The veteran tight end hasn't caught a touchdown pass since Week 3, and he hasn't hauled in more than five passes or 72 receiving yards since Week 2, but his role as Patrick Mahomes' most reliable security blanket gives him a fairly secure floor. Kelce will look to make a bigger contribution in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Travis Kelce is coming off one of his best games of the season, catching six of seven targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals. The future Hall of Famer snapped a six-game TD drought with the performance, and with 586 receiving yards through 10 contests, he's still got a real shot at his first 1,000-yard campaign since 2022. Kelce is Patrick Mahomes' most reliable option, but he has plenty of competition for targets in a passing game that features plenty of depth but no clear No. 1 threat. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against a Bills defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sam LaPorta should remain a big part of Detroit's offense in Week 2 at Buffalo. In Week 1 against the Saints, LaPorta's 5-48-0 receiving line put him second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receiving yards while tying Jahmyr Gibbs for second in catches. The fourth-year tight end will face a Bills defense that allowed 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday, so he'll have plenty of opportunities to build on his season-opening performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sam LaPorta will look to remain a top target as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. LaPorta recorded six catches for 52 yards and his first touchdown of the season against the Bills in Week 2. The starting tight end has now been targeted 15 times across two games, and he's converted these into 11 grabs for 100 yards and a touchdown. He'll face a New York defense that held Green Bay's Tucker Kraft to just two catches for 15 yards this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sam LaPorta should remain a complementary option as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. LaPorta caught three of four targets for 44 yards against the Jets in Week 3, which was his quietest game of the year. Detroit's ability to score and defensive problems keep the passing game alive even when running back Jahmyr Gibbs is tearing it up on the ground, so there don't look to be any issues with LaPorta's usage moving forward. He'll face a Carolina defense that ceded a 7-51-2 stat line to Harold Fannin in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Sam LaPorta will look to build on a season-best showing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. LaPorta impressed even in a Week 4 loss to Carolina, reeling in eight of 13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year tight end has now registered a 22-228-2  receiving line this season, and he remains a consistent option for Jared Goff, especially in important situations. LaPorta will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Sam LaPorta will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. LaPorta recorded another statement performance in Week 5 over the Cardinals heading into Detroit's bye, bringing in all five of his targets for 88 yards and a touchdown. The featured tight end has now surpassed 50 yards in three of his last four games, and he's found the end zone in each of those outings as well. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Sam LaPorta will aim to bounce back as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. LaPorta was silenced in a Week 7 win over the Packers, catching one of two targets for 18 yards. The starting tight end's performance will hopefully be an anomaly, and he still has a 28-334-3 receiving line through six outings this season. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked a tough first in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Sam LaPorta will look to get back on track as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. LaPorta had another quiet performance in Detroit's Week 8 win over the Vikings, bringing in three of five targets for 33 yards and logging one rush for two yards. After an impressive stretch heading into a Week 6 bye, the starting tight end has now logged just four catches for 51 yards in the last two weeks. LaPorta will face a Miami defense that's ranked a favorable 30th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Sam LaPorta will look to get back on track as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. LaPorta was quiet again in Week 9 versus the Dolphins, amid a struggling Detroit passing offense, recording four catches for 32 yards. The starting tight end has totaled just 83 receiving yards in his last three games after going back-to-back weeks with 80-plus receiving yards and a touchdown heading into the Lions' bye. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Sam LaPorta will aim to get back on track as the Lions return home against the Patriots in Week 11. LaPorta has had an extremely dry stretch ever since Detroit's bye week, failing to reach 40 yards in four straight games. The starting tight end has now recorded 36 receptions for 415 yards and three touchdowns, with most of his volume coming from the first five outings of the season. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Sam LaPorta will look to build off a bounce-back showing as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. LaPorta hauled in three of six targets for 62 yards in a Week 11 win over Tampa Bay, with most of his output coming from a 47-yard catch early in the game. Still, this receiving line included his best yardage total since before Detroit's bye in Week 5, so he'll hopefully be able to build on it in the weeks to come. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy tight ends in the last four weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: LaPorta has settled in as one of the league's top tight ends, but the 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't been able to match the fantasy success he enjoyed as a rookie. Since posting an 86-889-10 receiving line in 17 games that first season, LaPorta has totaled a 100-1,215-10 line in 25 games over the past two seasons. LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short by a back injury, otherwise he was well on his way to his third straight top-10 fantasy campaign (he finished seventh in PPG). The 25-year-old joins Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs as the clear "Core Four" targets in a good, pass-friendly Detroit offense, and is thus a solid fantasy TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season. However, he was overshadowed by Bucky Irving in Week 1, who caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards, while Gainwell was targeted just once. He will likely need more receiving work to be fantasy relevant in a Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed just two receptions for 22 yards to RBs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Gainwell is likely to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Gainwell has logged just 10 rush attempts for 21 yards through three games this season, confirming he's firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. The first-year Buccaneer has yet to score a touchdown as well, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a score. Despite this, Gainwell is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Packers defense that's already given up six rushing touchdowns this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Gainwell found the end zone for the first time this season during the Week 4 loss to the Packers. However, he remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield, as Irving out-touched Gainwell 16 to five. Gainwell will likely struggle maintaining fantasy relevance in Week 5 without scoring another touchdown, though the Cowboys defense has already allowed four rushing TDs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Gainwell has operated as Tampa Bay's top receiving back over the last two weeks, getting more targets (six), receptions (five) and yards (32) than Bucky Irving (two catches on three targets for 10 yards). Despite this, Gainwell will likely struggle finding fantasy relevance without scoring a touchdown. He could thrive against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed 200 receiving yards to RBs through five contests, tied for the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Gainwell was given few opportunities in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, accumulating 24 total yards on just three touches. Additionally, Gainwell was on the field for just 15% of Tampa Bay's offensive plays, his lowest mark of the season. It appears as if Gainwell is trending toward receiving less work as the season progresses, but he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Panthers defense that's allowed 5.1 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kenny Gainwell is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Gainwell had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, rushing 14 times for 88 yards. Despite his productive day, Gainwell still tallied 10 fewer carries than Bucky Irving (24 rushes for 106 yards and two touchdowns), suggesting he remains firmly behind Irving in Tampa Bay's backfield. However, Gainwell could remain successful in Week 8 against a Falcons defense that's given up 10 total touchdowns to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kenny Gainwell will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He racked up a career-high 140 rushing yards on 25 carries in the Week 8 win over the Falcons, bringing his season total to 289 yards (5.0 yards per carry). Despite Gainwell's huge performance, he still remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. Gainwell could struggle, especially against a strong Bears defense that has allowed just three rushing touchdowns to RBs all season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back in the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Despite Gainwell playing behind Bucky Irving, he's tallied 304 yards from scrimmage over the Buccaneers' last three games. Additionally, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Monday that the team will aim to lessen Irving's workload going forward, suggesting Gainwell's role on the offense could expand as the year progresses. However, Gainwell may struggle against the Lions in Week 11, as the Detroit has allowed just 3.7 yards per carry to opposing running backs this year.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kenny Gainwell is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bucky Irving, Gainwell has emerged as one of the top playmakers on this Buccaneers offense. Over the team's last four contests, Gainwell has averaged 90.8 scrimmage yards per game but hasn't found the end zone. He could be a valuable fantasy asset in Week 12, as Tampa Bay is set to face a Carolina defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs (28.6) in the NFL this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Gainwell signed with the Buccaneers following a second-half breakout with Pittsburgh last season. After playing sparingly during the first four-and-a-half years of his career, Gainwell averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on last season (eight games). Only five backs scored more points than Gainwell after Week 10. He did most of his damage as a receiver (top six among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards) and will now look to earn a similar role alongside Bucky Irving in Tampa Bay. Gainwell's strong season suggests he'll have a role, but the 23-year-old Irving is likely to operate as the lead back. Gainwell is best valued as a bench/insurance stash with some flex appeal in deep PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Williams' snaps could increase for the Patriots in Week 2 against the Steelers. Despite not drawing a target to open the season, Williams will likely ascend the depth chart following A.J. Brown's ankle injury that will sideline him for at least a month. Williams has shown big-play potential, so he may not require heavy volume to contribute, but until New England reveals its new receiving rotation, Williams can only be considered in the deepest of formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Williams hopes for more opportunities in Week 3 as the Patriots face the Jaguars. Rising up the depth chart with A.J. Brown on IR, Williams still only recorded a 21% snap share, registering two targets and a 10-yard catch in Week 2 where New England completed only 14 passes. Williams has big-play potential, but the passing game isn't operating at a high enough level to sustain a No. 4 WR despite facing a defense that's allowing 10.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Williams remains a low-volume, big-play option for the Patriots entering Week 4 against the Bills. Serving as the No. 4 WR following the ankle injury to A.J. Brown, Williams caught one of three targets for 34 yards in Week 3. He's logged five targets in the two games since Brown went down and has a favorable matchup against a Bills' secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target. With Drake Maye struggling, Williams likely won't have enough opportunities to be a Week 4 option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyle Williams hasn't been heavily involved in the Patriots passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. Williams amassed a mere two targets in Week 4 while Efton Chism appeared to overtake him as the team's No. 4 receiver. Williams likely won't garner enough attention to be a reliable Week 5 option, despite facing a Raiders secondary that's allowing a generous 8.2 yards per target to receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyle Williams hopes to maintain his big-play ability in Week 6 when the Patriots host the Jets. Williams hauled in three passes for 91 yards in Week 5, despite a 32% snap share even with Mack Hollins's absence, making Williams reliant on chunk plays for fantasy production. The Jets have allowed just 644 yards to opposing wideouts over five games (128.8 per game), and with New England spreading targets, Williams won't have volume on his side in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyle Williams could factor into the Patriots' receiving rotation in Week 7 against the Bears if Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is unable to play. Williams has three or fewer targets in every game to date, but averaging 24.5 yards per catch, he's proven capable of doing more with less. While more volume can be anticipated, Williams will have a chance to stretch the field against a defense that's allowing 9.8 yards per target, the third-highest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyle Williams will likely remain a low-volume, field-stretching option for the Patriots in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Williams has only two targets over the last two weeks with A.J. Brown back to full health. Miami is vulnerable against the pass, but has been exploited by tight ends and running backs more than receivers, a recipe New England cooked up in Week 7 and seems probable to follow again in Week 8. This leaves Williams with far too few chances to exploit a secondary that's allowing 8.8 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyle Williams continues to provide a low-volume, field-stretching role for the Patriots ahead of their Week 9 tilt with the Packers. Williams has just one target in each of New England's last three games and has only seven catches all season, but he's averaging a robust 27.1 yards per reception. Green Bay has allowed just 14 catches of at least 20 yards this season, the fourth-lowest across the league, limiting Williams' Week 9 appeal.
outlooksByWeek.12: Kyle Williams slides up the Patriots' depth chart with A.J. Brown (hamstring) unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Chargers. Williams doesn't have more than three targets in a game, with only 16 looks all season, and is working with Tommy DeVito at the helm. However, Williams has shown chunk-play potential with a robust 27.1 yards per catch. The Chargers are allowing a generous 9.1 yards per target, the seventh-highest in the league. There is a pathway for Williams to produce, but the risk isn't worth the reward.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams showed some flashes as a rookie, but he has a tough path to a Year 2 breakout. The 2025 third-round pick didn't see the field much (31% snap share), but he scored three touchdowns on 21 targets, all of which came from Week 10 on. He was utilized as a situational deep threat (17.6 aDOT), which led to a low catch rate (48%) but plenty of big plays (20.9 YPR). That role may not change much in 2026, as Williams will now compete with newcomers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, as well as incumbents DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins for targets in a good New England offense led by Drake Maye. Unfortunately, he doesn't have a path to fantasy consistency and is best stashed only in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Seth McGowan had the only touch by a Colts RB other than Jonathan Taylor in the season opener. McGowan and fellow backup DJ Giddens are irrelevant for fantasy purposes as long as Taylor is available. Taylor handled 22 touches in Week 1 and is expected to maintain a workhorse role in Week 2 at Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.3: Seth McGowan is locked in as the little-used backup to workhorse Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, having beaten out DJ Giddens (knee) for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. McGowan has just two carries and one target through two games. With Taylor healthy for a Week 3 home game against the AFC South rival Texans, McGowan remains a non-factor in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Seth McGowan has seven career touches heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London, four of which came in the Week 3 win over Houston. With star RB Jonathan Taylor healthy, McGowan's workload is expected to remain limited in Week 4 against Washington's stout run defense. McGowan's fantasy value is purely as a bench insurance policy in case of a Taylor injury.
outlooksByWeek.5: Seth McGowan got seven touches in the Week 4 win over the Commanders, as the Colts built a big enough lead to give Jonathan Taylor some late-game rest for the first time this season. Those seven touches equaled McGowan's touch total from his first three games combined. The rookie seventh-round pick remains a distant second behind Taylor on the Colts' RB depth chart heading into a Week 5 road game against the Steelers. McGowan has minimal standalone fantasy value as long as Taylor is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.6: Seth McGowan has 20 touches for 71 yards through five NFL games with the Colts. The rookie seventh-round pick is a distant second on Indianapolis' RB depth chart behind Jonathan Taylor. There is a greater chance than usual of the Colts pulling away and resting Taylor in a Week 6 home game against the 0-5 Titans, but banking on a lopsided game is an unreliable strategy, so McGowan is best left out of fantasy lineups in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Seth McGowan has turned 21 carries and four targets into 98 scrimmage yards through six NFL appearances with the Colts. With starter Jonathan Taylor healthy heading into a Week 7 trip to Minnesota, McGowan projects to remain in a low-volume, change-of-pace role. The rookie seventh-round pick has minimal standalone fantasy potential and isn't a recommended option against the Vikings, who boast the league's stingiest scoring defense at 12.8 points allowed per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Seth McGowan set career highs with 48 scrimmage yards on 12 touches in the Colts' Week 7 loss to Minnesota, but the rookie seventh-round pick has yet to score a TD and is averaging a meager 21 scrimmage yards per game as Jonathan Taylor's backup. McGowan has become a popular fantasy waiver target as the possibility of Taylor being traded comes into focus, but McGowan is nothing more than a speculative bench stash as long as Taylor stays put and is healthy. The rookie's standalone appeal for Week 8 is minimal against a league-best Jaguars run defense that's yielding just 72 yards per game on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.9: Seth McGowan is averaging fewer than five carries per game while posting just four catches in his first eight NFL games. The rookie seventh-round pick won't be a recommended fantasy option for Week 9 against the Cowboys if it's business as usual in the Colts' backfield, but trade rumors have been brewing around star RB Jonathan Taylor. If Taylor is traded or held out in anticipation of a trade, McGowan or DJ Giddens would be the next man up. Should McGowan garner a starter's workload, he would be a serviceable fantasy RB2 in Week 9 against a dreadful Dallas defense that's allowing 144.5 scrimmage yards per game to RBs and has given up 11 TDs to the position in eight games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Seth McGowan is poised to remain the Colts' No. 2 RB with Jonathan Taylor staying with the team. The rookie seventh-round pick is averaging a solid 4.8 yards per carry, though he has exceeded six rushing attempts in a game just once in his young career. It would have been a juicy introduction to the lead role in a favorable Week 10 matchup against a Dolphins defense that has allowed nine TDs to RBs in eight games en route to a 1-7 record. Now, he's only a deep-league flex option.
outlooksByWeek.11: Seth McGowan set career highs with 12 carries and 77 rushing yards in the Colts' Week 10 win over the Dolphins while scoring a touchdown for the second consecutive game. Indianapolis has deployed McGowan as the 1B option behind Jonathan Taylor over the past couple of weeks, and the rookie seventh-round pick is quietly averaging an impressive 5.2 yards per carry in his young career. McGowan has yet to catch multiple passes in a game and has just nine career receiving yards, so he'll be tough to trust as a flex option, even in deeper formats, until he shows more receiving capabilities. He'll face a Texans defense in Week 11 that has been much more vulnerable through the air than on the ground, limiting RBs to 89 rushing yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.12: Seth McGowan injured his hamstring in the Colts' Week 11 loss to Houston and is expected to sit out Week 12 against the Giants. The rookie had been earning a larger share of carries in a change-of-pace role behind Jonathan Taylor. DJ Giddens moves up to the second spot on Indianapolis' RB depth chart, but he may not get as many opportunities as McGowan did.

player.seasonOutlook: McGowan was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. McGowan is an older prospect (25), having bounced around five schools due to an off-field issue in 2021 that led to jail time and a dismissal from Oklahoma. He slowly rebuilt his career and peaked with 1,100 yards and six TDs at New Mexico State in 2024 prior to delivering 851 yards and 12 TDs at Kentucky last season. His efficiency is hit or miss, as his career 2.65 YAC is very poor, but his 4.2 forced missed tackle rate is strong. He's been effective in the passing game, as well, so there's some hope for a pro level impact. McGowan impressed at the combine, posting the top vertical and broad jump in this RB rookie class and running a solid 4.49 40-yard dash at 223 pounds. McGowan will battle DJ Giddens for primary backup duties behind Jonathan Taylor, so it's possible he finds his way to some value as an insurance hold.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jadarian Price injured his shoulder in the Seahawks' Week 2 win over Arizona, and it's unclear if he'll be able to play in Week 3 against Washington. The rookie RB was injured in the fourth quarter versus the Cardinals and finished the game with 13 carries for 52 yards and one catch for eight yards. Should Price not be able to play in Week 3, Emanuel Wilson would be he lead candidate to take over as the Seahawks starting RB. The Commanders have been awful against the pass but decent against the run this season and are yielding just 3.79 YPC against running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jadarian Price heads into Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers with potentially a lot on the line. After fumbling early in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Commanders, the rookie ended up logging just five totes for 15 yards while adding one catch for seven yards. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three carries and five catches) each out-touched Price, casting uncertainty about the Seahawks' backfield plans moving forward. Price would benefit from a productive (and fumble-free) performance against the Chargers, who rank 19th in the league in giving up 17.2 fantasy points per game through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jadarian Price (chest) is eligible to return from IR for Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Price hasn't played since Week 3, but he's expected to be designated to return this week. It remains to be seen if the rookie will be able to suit up against the Bears, and even if he does play, he may be part of a backfield committee that also includes Emanuel Wilson and the potentially returning Zach Charbonnet (knee). With that said, Seattle's backfield could find success against a Chicago defense that has given up 4.33 yards per carry to running backs, 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jadarian Price is coming off an inefficient return from IR heading into Seattle's Week 9 clash against the Cardinals. Price moved past a chest injury to lead Seattle's backfield in carries against Chicago on Monday Night Football, but he garnered just 29 yards on 10 totes and eight yards on two catches. He shared RB snaps fairly equally with Zach Charbonnet, and if the duo continues in a timeshare, both players may have a limited week-to-week fantasy ceiling. The Cardinals do present a relatively favorable matchup, as they're middling or worse in most statistical categories versus running backs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jadarian Price looks to be settling in as Seattle's No. 2 RB ahead of a Week 10 clash against Las Vegas. The rookie running back handled 13 touches this past Sunday in a win over Arizona while Zach Charbonnet logged 17 touches. However, Charbonnet had 16 carries to Prize's nine, suggesting that the former may be leaning more toward a change-of-pace role. Both Charbonnet and Price could be utilized heavily against the Raiders, who have given up the second-most fantasy points per game (23.1) to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jadarian Price's role at running back for Seattle could gain further clarity in Week 12 against San Francisco. Though he scored his first career touchdown in Week 10 against Las Vegas, Price's 10 touches lagged well behind those of Zach Charbonnet, who rushed 20 times for 94 yards. Seattle was on bye Week 11, so if Charbonnet again gets the lion's share of work this weekend, it could be an indication that Price is locked into the team's No. 2 RB role. Both he and Charbonnet could face tough sledding against a 49ers defense that has given up the fourth-fewest yards per carry (3.55) to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Hutchinson remains off the fantasy radar in most formats heading into Houston's Week 2 home game against the Bengals. He was third on the Texans with six targets in the season opener but finished with just three catches for 32 receiving yards. Hutchinson has topped 42 yards just twice through 50 career regular-season appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Hutchinson drew nine targets in Nico Collins' (hamstring) absence in Week 2 but turned that into just three catches for 37 yards. Hutchinson figures to maintain a prominent role in Houston's passing game against the league-worst Colts defense in Week 3, especially if Collins remains sidelined. Whether Hutchinson can turn that significant usage into production is another matter, as he has usually failed to capitalize on such opportunities in the past, with only two career regular-season games of 42 or more receiving yards. Hutchinson is in the Week 3 deep-league flex conversation, but his lack of prior production is concerning.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Hutchinson continues to do little with substantial volume, and that seems unlikely to change in Week 4, even with Houston hosting a weak Cowboys defense surrendering 27.3 points per game. Hutchinson has caught just nine of 21 targets this season and is averaging 40 receiving yards per game. Houston's lack of capable alternatives at WR figures to keep Hutchinson involved enough in Week 4 to earn deep-league flex consideration, especially if top wideout Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Xavier Hutchinson has exactly three catches in every game this season for the Texans and is averaging 42 receiving yards per game heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans. He has drawn 11 targets in two games playing alongside Nico Collins and 15 targets during the two games Collins missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins should continue to work as C.J. Stroud's No. 1 option against Tennessee's beatable secondary, while the remainder of Houston's receiving corps is best left on the bench or waiver wire, Hutchinson included.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Hutchinson set season highs with four catches and 65 yards in Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, but he has yet to score this season and has just three touchdowns in 54 career regular-season games. He's likely to slide down a spot on the WR depth chart once trade acquisition Marvin Harrison is up to speed, but that may not happen in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Hutchinson should get enough opportunities against a Jaguars defense that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers to warrant Week 6 flex consideration in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Hutchinson had season-low totals across the board with two catches for 10 yards on three targets in Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars, and he won't be a recommended Week 7 fantasy play against the Giants, even in deeper formats. He was earning decent volume while Houston's WR room was banged up, but the return of Nico Collins from a hamstring injury, coupled with the trade for Marvin Harrison and emergence of Jaylin Noel, have relegated Hutchinson to a depth role. Hutchinson doesn't have the talent to find consistent success with limited usage, as he has just three TDs in 55 career regular-season games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Xavier Hutchinson is likely to continue sliding down the depth chart at wide receiver as Marvin Harrison and Tank Dell get acclimated in Houston. The Texans traded for Harrison prior to Week 6 and activated Dell from injured reserve prior to Week 7. Hutchinson has just 27 receiving yards in two games since Harrison's arrival, though Hutchinson scored his first TD of the season in Week 7 against the Giants, marking just his fourth TD in 56 regular-season appearances for the Texans. Following a Week 8 bye, the Texans take on the winless Chargers in Week 9. Hutchinson isn't a recommended fantasy option against a Chargers defense that has been more stout against the pass than the run.
outlooksByWeek.10: Xavier Hutchinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Houston's Week 10 road game against the Browns, but he has just 46 receiving yards over that span and is averaging a meager 36 receiving yards per game this season. He has maintained a prominent role in a high-ceiling Houston passing offense, drawing at least five targets in all but one game, but Hutchinson hasn't done much with those opportunities and had just three career TDs in 3.5 seasons prior to his current two-game scoring streak. Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison, and Kayshon Boutte all have higher upside among Houston's WRs for Week 10 and beyond.
outlooksByWeek.11: Xavier Hutchinson has scored in three consecutive games heading into Houston's Week 11 home game against the Colts. He's averaging six targets per game, and while his paltry average of 6.4 yards per target suggests C.J. Stroud would be better off distributing those looks elsewhere, Hutchinson's volume has propelled the 26-year-old wideout into the weekly flex conversation. Perhaps Hutchinson is just a late bloomer who is finding his groove, but it's fair to remain skeptical considering his three TDs in the last three games match his total of three TDs from 55 regular-season appearances before this streak. The Colts have limited WRs to eight TDs in 10 games, though Indianapolis is allowing 149 yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.12: Xavier Hutchinson has topped 30 yards just once in Houston's last five games. He had a three-game touchdown streak to buoy his stat line during that stretch, but the scoring binge was likely fool's gold for a fourth-year player who had just three career TDs prior to that streak, which was snapped in the Week 11 win over Indianapolis. Starting a new scoring streak won't be easy in Week 12 against a Ravens defense that has held WRs to just seven touchdowns. While the Ravens are giving up 162 yards per game to the position, Hutchinson is competing for targets with Nico Collins and Tank Dell, as well as possibly Kayshon Boutte (hip) and Marvin Harrison (hamstring). Considering that Hutchinson's 6.3 yards per target are second-fewest among that group, ahead of only Harrison, it's tough to trust Hutchinson as anything more than a deep-league flex-spot flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Ward threw for just 140 yards in Tennessee's 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, bringing the 2025 first-overall pick's career average down to 184 passing yards per game. He's best avoided for fantasy purposes, even in multi-QB formats, for the Titans' Week 2 home game against the Eagles. Philadelphia's stingy pass defense limited Jayden Daniels to 164 passing yards and 4.8 yards per pass attempt in the Eagles' season-opening win over Washington.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Ward has been arguably the worst starting QB in the NFL since entering the league as the Titans' first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. In the first three games of his sophomore season, Ward hasn't thrown for more than 183 yards or recorded multiple touchdown passes in a game. Dynasty managers can continue to stash him on the bench for the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore in hopes of future improvements, but Ward's fantasy value in the present is negligible. The Ravens rank in the middle of the pack against the pass.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Ward hasn't thrown multiple touchdown passes in a game during the Titans' 0-4 start, and he's just 3-18 as a starter with 18 touchdown passes in 21 games. The 2025 first overall pick isn't an advisable fantasy option in Week 5 against the Texans, who have surprisingly surrendered the third-most passing yards in the league this season but still boast plenty of talent on defense and allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards in 2025. Dynasty managers looking for a silver lining with Ward can point to his season-high 222 passing yards in the Week 4 loss to Baltimore, 145 of which went to rookie fourth overall pick Carnell Tate.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Ward dropped to 3-19 as a starter for the Titans with a 26-3 loss to the Texans in Week 5, throwing an interception that dropped his season TD:INT to 3:3. He has declined in his second season after posting a 15:7 TD:INT as a rookie, while his passing yards per game have dropped from 186 in 2025 to 179 this year. Even against a Colts defense that's giving up the fifth-most passing yards per game, Ward can't be trusted in Week 6 fantasy lineups outside of deep superflex or multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Ward and the Titans finally earned their first win of the season in Week 6 against the Colts, though the second-year QB certainly wasn't the primary driving force in the victory, as he threw for just 102 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. Ward has mustered just four touchdown passes through six starts in his sophomore season while averaging 166 passing yards per game. He'll face a franchise that's all too familiar with subpar QB play in Week 7, taking on a Browns team that's off to a surprisingly strong 4-2 start this season while boasting one of the league's 10 stingiest defenses in terms of both passing yards and points allowed per game. Between Ward's own shortcomings and the tricky matchup, it's best to avoid him in fantasy for Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Ward has yet to throw multiple touchdown passes in a game heading into the Titans' Week 8 trip to Cincinnati. The second-year QB has an ugly 4:5 TD:INT while throwing for just 168 yards per game. Cincinnati's defense has limited QBs to a 6:4 TD:INT, but the Bengals allowed Baltimore's Tyler Huntley to throw for a career-high 298 yards in a Week 7 game that the Bengals won by 22 points. Until Ward shows signs of progress as a passer, he'll remain a fantasy non-factor, even in superflex formats.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cam Ward had his best game of the season in Tennessee's 43-36 Week 8 loss to the Bengals, prior to a Week 9 bye. He threw for 300 yards for the first time in his career and delivered a pair of touchdown passes for his first multi-TD performance through the air all season. Ward has a chance to build on that effort in Week 10 against a Jaguars defense that has been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground. The far larger sample of subpar football from the 2025 first overall pick prior to his strong outing last game suggests Ward remains tough to trust for now, even in superflex formats. The Jaguars are giving up the 11th-most passing yards per game, though they have more interceptions (11) than touchdown passes allowed (eight).
outlooksByWeek.11: Cam Ward has taken a noticeable step forward in Tennessee's last two games, even though the Titans lost both to drop to 1-8. After throwing for a career-high 304 yards and tossing multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season against the Bengals, Ward threw for 231 yards and two TDs in the Week 10 loss to Jacksonville, his second-highest passing yards total of the campaign. His four touchdown passes in that two-game stretch match Ward's total from his first seven starts of the season. The improving 2025 first overall pick has a nice opportunity to keep building momentum in Week 11 against a dreadful Dallas defense that has surrendered a 19:4 TD:INT ratio en route to allowing 28.2 points per game. Ward's underwhelming larger body of work leaves him out of the starting mix in most single-QB formats, but he's a sneaky-good Week 11 superflex option.
