outlooksByWeek.12: Cam Ward has thrown for at least 231 yards and two TDs in three consecutive games after failing to hit either of those passing benchmarks in any of his first seven starts this season. The 2025 first overall pick is growing in confidence, and he's also being forced to air it out as the 1-9 Titans consistently play catch-up. That's unlikely to change in Week 12, when the Titans face a Jaguars team that can put up points in bunches and is better at stopping the run than the pass. Ward's recent uptick in production has him in the conversation as a starter in superflex leagues, but there remain plenty of more reliable options in single-QB formats.

player.seasonOutlook: Ward is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an underwhelming rookie campaign, albeit under tough circumstances. The 2025 No. 1 draft pick was plenty busy as a rookie (eighth in the league in dropbacks and pass attempts), but he struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Ward was rarely a factor with his legs (more than 12 yards three times) and produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 12th. The good news is that a tough rookie year isn't overly damning for a quarterback's career trajectory, and he'll be in a better spot in 2026 with new playcaller Brian Daboll and an improved supporting cast (Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson join a now-healthy Calvin Ridley). Ward will need to run more to become an elite fantasy option, but Year 2 is the breakout season for many quarterbacks, so he's well worth a late flier.

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to face the Patriots in Week 2. He finished Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win versus the Falcons 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on PATs. Boswell's first miss of the season was from 56 yards out, but he was able to connect from 43 and 28 yards. The Steelers have several talented players on offense, but until they prove they can consistently put up 24-28 points a week, Boswell may not generate enough scoring opportunities to warrant a roster spot.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Boswell and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. The 12th-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Both of Boswell's attempts came from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 1-for-3 from that distance and 3-for-5 overall through two outings in 2026. He'll look to get back on track this Sunday versus a Cincinnati defense allowing 16.5 points per game, tied for eighth.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Boswell and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. It was Boswell's first perfect outing through three games, and his 33-yard kick just before the two-minute warning gave the Steelers the lead for good. He'll look to stay hot against Cleveland's 18th-ranked scoring defense, which is allowing 23.7 points per game thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Boswell and the Steelers return home to take on the Colts in Week 5. He finished Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4 converting one of two field-goal attempts while connecting on his lone extra-point try. Boswell's miss came from 48 yards out, and he's now 1-for-4 on kicks equal to or longer than that across four games in 2026. He'll aim to bounce back versus an Indianapolis defense giving up 26.0 points per contest, which ranks 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to battle the Buccaneers in Week 6. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and went 4-for-4 on extra-point tries during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Over his last three outings, Boswell is 6-for-7 on field goals while making all eight of his PATs. He's on the fantasy radar with the recent strong performances by the Steelers offense, as they've averaged 29.3 points during this three-game stretch. Boswell will try to make an impact against a Tampa Bay defense allowing 22.4 points per game in 2026, but just 15.0 PPG over their previous two.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 clash against the Saints. He converted four of five field-goal attempts, including a season-long 58-yarder, and both of his PATs during Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime win in Week 6. Boswell missed his first kick from 48 yards out, but he made up for it by making four in a row, with three of those makes coming in the fourth quarter to help send the game to OT. He'll get another chance to make an impact versus a New Orleans defense that allows 29.7 points per game, which is tied for the most in the NFL in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chris Boswell and the Steelers play host to the division rival Browns in Week 8. He went 3-for-3 on field goals and converted his lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory over the Saints in Paris. Boswell is looking to avenge his underwhelming performance against Cleveland in Week 4, as the 35-year-old missed one of two FGAs in the 27-24 defeat. Since then, Boswell is 9-for-10 on FGs and 7-for-7 on extra points. He'll try to keep rolling versus a Browns defense allowing 20.9 points per game, the 12th-fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 10 AFC North showdown against the Bengals. In Week 8, he went 2-for-3 on field goal attempts and connected on all three of his PATs to help Pittsburgh win its fourth straight game. Boswell misfired on a 57-yarder to end their first offensive possession, as the 35-year-old is now 4-for-7 on kicks from 50-plus yards out in 2026. However, he's had three or more FGAs in three consecutive outings, a trend that is likely to continue versus a Cincinnati team scoring the second-most points per game (30.0).
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Chris Boswell and the Steelers are back on the road to face the 2-7 Eagles. He connected on his only field goal attempt and lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss in Week 10. The Steelers offense struggled mightily to gain any traction until the game was well out of reach, leaving Boswell on the sidelines while his team opted to go for two on their final touchdown. He'll look to get more involved against a Philadelphia defense giving up 24.6 points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chris Boswell and the Steelers aim to improve to 5-0 at home when they host the Broncos in Week 12 on Black Friday. He went 3-for-3 on field goal attempts and drilled his lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss in Week 11. Boswell has now converted all of his field goals in consecutive games for the first time all season. The veteran kicker will try to stay perfect versus a Denver defense allowing 21.0 points per game through 10 outings.

outlooksByWeek.2: CeeDee Lamb found the end zone for the Cowboys while leading the squad in receiving in Week 1. However, Lamb finished with five catches for just 44 yards in the dismal 28-20 loss to the Giants. Still, Lamb led the team in targets, and the touchdown salvaged his day from a fantasy perspective. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: CeeDee Lamb went wild last game for the Cowboys. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Lamb had nine targets for the game. He has scored three touchdowns in his first two contests of the 2026 campaign. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard mark for the second-straight week for the Cowboys. Lamb snagged seven balls for 112 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Unfortunately, Lamb was held out of the end zone for the first time all season. However, Lamb has at least eight targets in each of the first three games for Dallas, and should stay in busy in Week 4 versus the Texans, even if he is guarded by all-pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. The Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: CeeDee Lamb is coming off a game for the ages. Lamb was targeted a staggering 21 times en route to an absurd 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown in the comeback win over the Texans. It was the third-straight 100-yard outing of the season for Lamb, and he scored for the fourth time in four contests. Following this outing, Lamb leads the NFL in receiving yards and receptions, and is tied for third in the NFL with four receiving scores. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: CeeDee Lamb is said to be dealing with a bruise of his quadriceps, but he is not expected to miss any time for the Cowboys. Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards last game as he was dealing with the issue. That snapped a three-game streak for Lamb of at least 112 yards receiving. He will look to get back on track in Week 6 versus the Packers. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: CeeDee Lamb was targeted a staggering 18 times last game for Dallas. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly had a difficult time. Despite the bevy of looks, Lamb managed just 70 yards on nine catches in the 23-13 loss. Lamb has an absurd 44 targets over his last three contests. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: CeeDee Lamb scored twice last game for the Cowboys.  Lamb led the Cowboys receivers in all categories, snagging five passes for 74 yards and the two touchdowns. He has found the end zone six times in seven contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: CeeDee Lamb led the Cowboys in receiving last game. Unfortunately, he managed just 58 yards and failed to find the end zone in the 33-30 OT loss to Arizona. Lamb has accumulated a staggering 41 targets over the last three contest, though has failed to cross 75 yards receiving in any of those contests. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: CeeDee Lamb took advantage of the absence of George Pickens last game for Dallas. While Lamb is always the top target in the offense, with Pickens out of the lineup Lamb was targeted even more frequently than usual, a total of 16 times against the Colts. Lamb responded with 10 catches for a staggering 195 yards and a touchdown. Lamb has double-digit targets in four-straight games, and Pickens remains questionable for the Week 10 clash with the 49ers. However, the Niners are allowing just 211 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just 11 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for seventh in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: CeeDee Lamb continues to pile up statistics for the Dallas Cowboys. Lamb found the end zone for the second-straight game and eighth time overall in 2026 in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Lamb finished with seven catches for 72 yards and the score. Lamb has drawn double-digit targets in five-straight contests, a trend that should continue in Week 11 versus the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard threshold yet again for the Cowboys last game. Lamb caught 11 passes for 132 yards and a touchdown in the 51-30 dismantling of the Titans. Lamb has scored in three-straight contests, and has gone over the 100-yard receiving mark in two of those outings. He is second in the NFL in receiving yardage overall, and first in receptions. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Lamb is eyeing a bounceback season following a 2025 campaign in which he finished 12th among receivers in fantasy PPG � his worst finish since 2021. Lamb did go over 1,000 yards for the fifth season in a row, but he missed three games, led all receivers with eight drops and was unlucky in the TD department, having scored three touchdowns (6.6 expected) despite seeing 11 end zone targets. Lamb, 27, remains in his prime and he was fantasy's top-scoring receiver the last time he played a full season (2023). As long Dak Prescott is on the field with him, Lamb will be a solid fantasy WR1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London looks poised to bounce back from a tough Week 1 in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina's defense just allowed a whopping 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, giving up 42.2 PPR fantasy points to wide receivers. London's rebound could depend on the quarterback play, as Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) are both questionable for Sunday's contest. However, with Carolina's defensive struggles during Week 1, London should be in for a fantastic matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake London will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. With Michael Penix returning from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London had one of the best performances of his career, catching nine of 10 targets for 194 yards. With Penix on the field, London has averaged 6.7 receptions, 98.7 receiving yards and 0.6 touchdowns per game, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as long as Penix remains healthy. Despite this, London is in for a tough Week 4 matchup against a Saints secondary that's given up 29.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. London has excelled since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, catching 14 of 16 targets for 290 yards across his last two contests. With Penix at the helm, London has averaged a whopping 6.6 receptions and 98.5 yards per game, suggesting that he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as the season progresses. Additionally, London is in for a terrific matchup against a Ravens secondary that's allowed 37.9 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake London will likely remain the Falcons' top pass catcher in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. London impressed in the Week 5 loss despite not finding the end zone, totaling 118 yards on seven receptions. He's been one of fantasy's top wideouts since Michael Penix (ribs) returned in Week 3, averaging seven receptions and 136 yards per game across three contests. As long as Penix is healthy for the Week 6 contest, London should have another fantastic opportunity to put up big numbers against a Bears defense that's given up 32.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Despite logging double-digit targets for the third time in his last four games, London recorded just four receptions and 62 yards in the Week 6 loss to the Bears. Since Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged 9.3 targets, 6.3 receptions and 117.5 yards per game, making him one of fantasy's most productive receivers. Even so, London could struggle against a tough 49ers defense in Week 7 that's given up just 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake London is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. London paced Atlanta's pass catchers in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, catching seven of nine targets for 66 yards and a score. Since quarterback Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged a whopping 6.4 receptions and 107.2 yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive WRs. He's in for a tough matchup in Week 8, however, as Tampa Bay's secondary has allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Drake London will look to bounce back from a tough Week 8 performance when the Falcons plays the Bengals in Week 9. London struggled along with the rest of Atlanta's offense in a rainy loss to the Buccaneers, catching just one of six targets for eight yards. However, he's still been one of the NFL's most productive receivers with Michael Penix at quarterback this year, averaging 5.5 receptions and 90.7 receiving yards per game. London will have a good opportunity to rebound against a Cincinnati secondary that's allowed 33.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top pass catcher during the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. London has cooled down after a terrific stretch of games from Weeks 3 through 5, averaging just 4.3 receptions and 52.8 receiving yards per game over Atlanta's last four contests. He's also averaging just 7.6 targets per game this season, his lowest mark since 2023, so it appears the Falcons are struggling to get him involved. Additionally, London is in for a difficult Week 10 matchup against a Chiefs secondary that's allowed just 23.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.12: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Prior to Atlanta's Week 11 bye, London had one of his best performances of the 2026 season, catching six of 12 targets for 109 yards. With Michael Penix at quarterback this year, London has averaged 5.5 receptions and 90.1 receiving yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive receivers. Despite this, London could definitely struggle against the Vikings in Week 12, as they have allowed just 27.8 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

player.seasonOutlook: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024. Last season, he missed five games and fell to 19th in fantasy points, but he was actually better on a per-game basis (seventh) and was the top scorer among receivers three times between Weeks 6 and 10. London remains heavily targeted (career 28% share) and sees plenty of work near the goal line (25 end zone targets over the past two seasons). As long as one of Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can play somewhat competent ball, the 25-year-old London shouldn't have trouble providing fringe-WR1 fantasy production.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Jacobs will look to ramp it up even more as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Jacobs carved out a solid performance in his return to the field against the Lions in Week 7, rushing the ball for 36 yards off 11 carries but catching five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown. While the rushing efficiency wasn't there, the usage definitely was, which bodes well for the veteran ball carrier. He could also be in store for a better outing on the ground, as Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Jacobs will again have an asterisk next to his name as the Packers face the Patriots in Week 9. Jacobs has been active the last two weeks, and while he's averaged an inefficient 2.3 yards per carry on 32 attempts, he's salvaged his performances with three total touchdowns in this stretch. The veteran ball carrier also could be at risk of not playing in the near future, as the NFL continues to investigate his alleged physical incidents. This makes him an uncertain play, especially against a New England defense that's ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in Week 10 as the Packers take on the Vikings. Jacobs hurt his finger in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, and he's now set to undergo surgery, which will keep him out for a maximum of three weeks. The veteran ball carrier has now recorded 36 rushes for 80 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches for 68 yards and two touchdowns as well. Kaleb Johnson, Pierre Strong, and banged-up Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd will be Green Bay's available running backs against a tough Minnesota defense.
outlooksByWeek.12: Josh Jacobs will look to make a return as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Jacobs missed Week 10 against Minnesota with a finger injury, and while he's had a week off to get back to full health, he was unable to practice fully on Monday. If the veteran ball carrier is good to go, he'll look to come out on top of a crowded backfield against a Los Angeles defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Allen brings a multi-touchdown streak into the Bills' Week 5 matchup at the Rams. Allen has provided multiple scores in each of Buffalo's first four games, throwing six scores while rushing for seven, though his yardage has topped 253 just once. The Rams, however, have allowed only one rushing touchdown and a mere 4.84 yards per pass attempt in what looks to be a battle of elite versus elite.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Allen looks to continue to provide elite returns when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Allen is coming off his best rushing effort of the year in Week 5, finishing with 121 yards while scoring on the ground for the eighth time in five games, adding further upside to his reliable passing efforts. Facing a Raiders defense in Week 6 that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks likely won't hinder Allen's appeal, as he's set for top-tier dual-threat production Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Allen hopes to have his full complement of receivers when the Bills come out of their bye to host the Ravens in Week 8. He failed to record a rushing score in Week 6 for the first time all season, but threw multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 2, maintaining his elite fantasy scoring. This game could bring shootout potential if Baltimore gets Lamar Jackson back under center. Baltimore's defense has been solid against opposing passers, allowing just five touchdown passes in six games before being solved by Joe Burrow for four in Week 7. They've also allowed just one rushing touchdown to the position, but Allen is matchup-proof.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Allen has his work cut out for him when the Bills face the Vikings in Week 9. He ran for his ninth touchdown in seven games during Week 8 and tossed two touchdown passes for the fourth time this season. He's matchup-proof, but Allen will face constant pressure from Minnesota's heavy blitzing scheme that's allowed only four touchdown passes and 81 rushing yards to opposing quarterbacks through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.10: Josh Allen will seek a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Jets in Week 10. In Week 9 at Minnesota, Allen, in the face of constant pressure, had his first game of the year with just one touchdown while being held under 250 yards for the fourth time. The Jets have allowed a 16:1 TD:INT ratio through nine games, but Allen threw for only 148 yards and no scores against them in his lone 2025 matchup, suggesting a lower-than-usual ceiling for arguably the league's best quarterback.
outlooksByWeek.11: Josh Allen faces potential workload limitations in the Bills' Week 11 game against the Dolphins. Allen completed only 11 of 21 passes against the Jets in Week 10, his second-lowest volume of the season, as Buffalo was able to get out to a comfortable lead and not challenge the Jets through the air. Another potentially uncompetitive game seems to be looming, and while Allen has 11 rushing touchdowns to go with his 13 passing scores, Miami has allowed quarterbacks to run for just two touchdowns all season. Allen routinely gets his fantasy points, but Week 11 expectations can be tempered slightly.
outlooksByWeek.12: Josh Allen will look to steal the spotlight in a marquee Week 12 Thursday matchup when the Bills face the Chiefs. Allen is coming off a curious outing in Week 11 against the Dolphins, throwing a season-high 45 times while not attempting a rush and tossing a season-high two interceptions. Kansas City has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, with just eight touchdown passes and no rushing scores through 10 games. Allen is a touch more vulnerable than his typical elite status.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.
outlooksByWeek.5: Luther Burden will aim to stay involved as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Burden tied his season high of 63 receiving yards in Week 4 against the Jets, and he's now recorded 60 or more yards in all but one game this season. The second-year wide receiver appears to be a pivotal part of Chicago's offense, and he could be a key piece towards a win in Tundratown. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Luther Burden will continue to be a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 6 at Atlanta. Burden brought in four of six targets for a team-high 47 receiving yards and rushed the ball four times for two yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers. The second-year pass catcher has been unable to get things going in multiple games this season, but this can be attributed to the struggles at the quarterback position. No matter who is throwing him the ball, the Falcons ranking 27th in fantasy point allowed to wide receivers this campaign could be favorable for Burden.
outlooksByWeek.7: Luther Burden will seek to stay busy as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Burden secured all eight of his targets for 95 yards in a Week 6 win over the Falcons, leading Chicago in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The second-year wideout has a 31-361-1 line on 43 targets across six games this season, and a dominant connection looks to be growing with quarterback Caleb Williams. Burden will now turn his sights to a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.8: Luther Burden will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Burden was on fire in Week 7 against the Patriots, turning four catches into 130 yards and a touchdown and taking his one carry for seven yards. The second-year pass catcher has now totaled 35 receptions for 491 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he's becoming Caleb Williams' favorite option in the passing game. Burden will now shift focus to a tough Seattle defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Luther Burden will look to stay busy as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Burden stayed hot in a Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, bringing in seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets across the last three games, and he's surpassed 50 receiving yards in all but two games this season. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Luther Burden will aim to recover from a concussion ahead of Chicago's Week 11 game against the Saints. Burden got concussed in the fourth quarter of a Week 9 win over the Buccaneers before the Bears' bye week, so hopefully he's had enough time to heal. The second-year star has now posted a 49-644-4 receiving line across nine games with career highs in catches and touchdowns, with one more game likely to get him over the hump in yards as well. If he's active, Burden will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked a tough eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Luther Burden will look to bounce back as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Burden posted a season-worst performance in Week 11 against the Saints, hauling in two of three targets for just 10 yards. Either way, he's posted a career-best 51-654-4 receiving line across just 10 games this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bhayshul Tuten is likely to get the majority of touches in Jacksonville's backfield in Week 2 against the Broncos, just as he did in the season-opening win over the Browns. Tuten turned 16 touches into 88 yards in Week 1, while Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah combined for 55 yards on 11 touches, though Rodriguez siphoned some valuable goal-line work. Denver's defense gave up the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL last season but just allowed Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson to combine for 259 scrimmage yards and two TDs in a Week 1 loss. Tuten has RB2 upside given his prominent role in a high-powered Jaguars offense, but he's more of a flex/RB3 for Week 2 against a talented Broncos defense searching for a rebound in their home opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bhayshul Tuten emerged as the clear No. 1 option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, ahead of Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialists LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah. Through the first two games of his sophomore season, Tuten turned 28 carries and three targets into 150 scrimmage yards and one TD. The speedster is a viable RB3/flex for Week 3, though expectations should be tempered against a New England defense that's off to an elite start, having allowed just 16 points through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 80 scrimmage yards and takes a two-game touchdown streak into Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals. Tuten is locked in atop the running back depth chart in one of the league's best offenses, which makes him a reliable fantasy RB2, even with Chris Rodriguez, LeQuint Allen, and Ameer Abdullah siphoning touches here and there. Cincinnati has been better than average against the run, but the Bengals have allowed a league-high 141 receiving yards to RBs, so Tuten is likely to make some plays as a pass-catcher even if running room is hard to come by.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bhayshul Tuten has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in three of the first four games of his second season with the Jaguars. The 2025 fourth-round pick has thrived in the lead role, establishing himself as an every-week fantasy RB2. He'll face an Eagles defense in Week 5 that's allowing 106 rushing yards per game to RBs and just surrendered a pair of late rushing scores to the Rams' Kyren Williams in a Week 4 loss. Tuten and the Jaguars will have a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff Sunday in Week 5 when they face the Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bhayshul Tuten remains Jacksonville's starting RB heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans. He has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in four of five games while occupying that role and has two rushing TDs this season. Houston has been among the league's stingiest defenses against RBs, limiting the position to 89 scrimmage yards per game and allowing only three TDs on 103 carries. Tuten's prominent role in an above-average offense keeps him in the fantasy RB2 range despite the tricky Week 6 matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bhayshul Tuten scored two receiving TDs against the Texans in Jacksonville's last action prior to a Week 7 bye. The well-rested lead back is a high-end fantasy RB2 for his return to action in Week 8 against the Colts, who are allowing 134 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Tuten is averaging 86 scrimmage yards on 18 touches per game and has scored four total TDs through six outings. His well-rounded skill set gives him a high touch floor regardless of how the game unfolds.
outlooksByWeek.10: Bhayshul Tuten played through foot and ankle injuries in Jacksonville's Week 9 win over the Ravens. He scored his fifth touchdown in the past three games but was held to a season-low 29 scrimmage yards, less than half of his previous low of 62 yards from Week 2. Tuten has had a few extra days to recover since last Thursday's win and should be ready to assume his usual role as Jacksonville's top RB for a juicy Week 10 road matchup against the Titans, who are allowing 135 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. He profiles as a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2 in fantasy for Week 10, especially if his practice participation levels indicate that Tuten's injury scare is behind him.
outlooksByWeek.11: Bhayshul Tuten has scored six times during his current four-game TD streak, and he has mustered at least 87 scrimmage yards in seven of Jacksonville's nine games this season. The second-year stud has crept into fantasy RB1 territory ahead of Jacksonville's Week 11 road game against the Giants, who have allowed just four rushing TDs to RBs but also three receiving TDs to the position through nine games. Tuten has five rushing TDs and three receiving scores this season while notching at least 12 carries in every game and two-plus receptions in all but two outings. His well-rounded skill set allows Jacksonville's lead back to maintain a prominent role regardless of the score.
outlooksByWeek.12: Bhayshul Tuten aggravated an ankle injury in Jacksonville's previous game. However, he reportedly avoided a serious injury and could still suit up in Week 12 against the Titans. The 2025 fourth-round pick hasn't missed a game during his second NFL year, though Tuten had a season-low 29 yards in Week 9 while playing through this ankle injury and just posted his second-lowest total of the season with 53 scrimmage yards in Week 11. If Tuten gets the green light, he can be plugged in as a fantasy RB2 against a Titans defense that's allowing 133 scrimmage yards per game to RBs, despite his injury concerns. Should Tuten sit, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead Jacksonville's ground game, while LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah offer receiving upside out of the backfield.

player.seasonOutlook: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 tilt against the Patriots. The former Indianapolis Colt secured all three targets for a team-high 58 yards in his debut for Pittsburgh. Pittman finished sixth in targets but still did plenty of damage with his opportunities, and if the Steelers want to throw the ball 40-plus times a game, he could develop into a reliable fantasy receiver. New England's defense ranks 21st in receiving yards allowed to WRs (161), but they will be playing at home with a rest advantage.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. After dealing with a foot injury during training camp and the preseason, he suffered a new foot ailment that forced him to miss Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss in New England. Pittman will have to practice in some capacity in order to return for Sunday's contest, but it sounds like his status for Week 3 is very much in question. Consider him doubtful to suit up until we hear otherwise.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Pittman and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence and caught two of five targets for 16 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Pittman tied for second on the team in targets but was unable to make much of an impact, as Aaron Rodgers continued spreading the ball around on offense by hitting nine different receivers. However, he has an opportunity to break out against Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the receiver's former team when the Colts come to town in Week 5. He hauled in two of four targets for 15 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, giving him a 7-89-0 receiving line on 12 targets across three contests. It's been a slow start for Pittman in his debut season for the Steelers, but Week 5 offers a shot at some payback against the team that drafted him in 2020. Indianapolis' defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs, a matchup that could help Pittman's chemistry with Aaron Rodgers.
outlooksByWeek.12: In Week 12, Michael Pittman and Pittsburgh aim to snap a two-game losing skid when they host the Broncos on Black Friday. He hasn't played since Week 4 after being placed on injured reserve due to a foot injury, but the first-year Steeler is ready to make his return versus a talented Denver secondary, which is allowing 28.1 fantasy points per game to WRs. Pittman hasn't played in nearly two months, so fantasy managers needing help at receiver should look elsewhere until he can prove otherwise.

player.seasonOutlook: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Parker Washington can safely be started as a fantasy WR2 in Week 2, even with the Jaguars facing a stout Broncos secondary. Washington paced Jacksonville's pass catchers with five catches for 83 yards and a TD on six targets in the season opener. In his last five games, including the playoffs, Washington has racked up 31 catches, 537 yards, and four TDs. Fellow Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) tends to draw significant defensive attention, which should keep top Broncos CB Patrick Surtain from shadowing Washington as long as Thomas suits up.
outlooksByWeek.3: Parker Washington has established himself as the No. 1 WR for the Jaguars and is headed toward weekly fantasy WR1 territory ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Patriots. New England has one of the league's best secondaries, led by CB Christian Gonzalez, but Washington appears largely matchup-proof considering the 24-year-old WR just accounted for 98 of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards in a Week 2 loss to Denver that could wind up being Lawrence's worst performance of the season. Washington has at least five catches and 83 receiving yards in each of his last five games, as well as three touchdown catches over that span, so the breakout star can be started with confidence regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Parker Washington has entered set-and-forget fantasy WR1 territory. Jacksonville's top wideout is likely to thrive in Week 4 against a suspect Bengals secondary that just allowed touchdowns to Steelers WRs Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek. Despite facing the strong Cleveland, Denver, and New England secondaries, Washington is averaging 74 yards per game with two TDs through three weeks to start 2026 after averaging 116 receiving yards and scoring twice in the final three games of the 2025 regular season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Parker Washington has recorded just 47 receiving yards on eight targets over Jacksonville's last two games after turning 18 targets into 181 yards over the preceding two games. Washington could have an easier time getting back on track in Week 5 if the Eagles are without top cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee). Philadelphia's secondary still has plenty of talent but hasn't been nearly as effective this year, allowing four touchdown catches to WRs after holding the position to six TDs in the entire 2025 regular season. Washington leads the Jaguars in all receiving categories and remains a fantasy WR2 at worst despite the recent hiccup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Parker Washington bounced back from a seven-yard Week 4 dud with his best game of the season in Week 5, racking up 124 yards and two TDs against the Eagles. Jacksonville's No. 1 receiver is averaging 70 yards per game and has four TDs through five outings while leading the Jaguars in every receiving category. Washington can be penciled in as a fantasy WR1 for Week 6 against a Texans pass defense that has been surprisingly weak, allowing 193 receiving yards per game to wideouts and six TDs in five games to the position, making it one of the five most generous defenses against wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.8: Parker Washington leads the Jaguars with a 26-416-4 receiving line on 46 targets through the Week 7 bye, and he has a nice opportunity to add to his team-best receiving totals in Week 8 against a Colts defense that may remain without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf) for a second consecutive game. Indianapolis ranks in the middle of the pack against WRs, allowing 142 yards per game to the position, though the Colts give up 25.7 points per game overall, ranking among the league's 10 most generous scoring defenses. Washington is on the fantasy WR1/WR2 borderline for this Week 8 home game.
outlooksByWeek.9: Parker Washington has been held to a single catch twice in Jacksonville's last four games but is averaging a team-high 61.7 receiving yards per game and has four TDs through seven games. His occasional down games keep Washington out of the set-and-forget WR1 range, but he's a high-end fantasy WR2 for a Week 9 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 177.6 yards per game to WRs. Baltimore has given up plenty of yards to the position but has held wideouts to just five TDs. There are numerous mouths to feed in Jacksonville's high-octane passing game, but Washington continues to have the most upside among the team's pass catchers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Parker Washington has had some quiet second halves with the Jaguars building big leads lately, and a similar scenario could be on the table in Week 10 against the 1-8 Titans. Washington remains a fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside for this matchup, as Trevor Lawrence's top target should feast as long as this game is competitive against a Titans secondary that has surrendered some big individual performances to WRs, allowing at least 117 yards to six different players this season, including a combined 296 yards and three TDs to Cincinnati's WR duo of Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase in Tennessee's most recent game. Washington has failed to exceed two catches in three of his last five games but easily leads the Jaguars with 493 receiving yards and five touchdown catches.
outlooksByWeek.11: Parker Washington capitalized on a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Titans, dissecting Tennessee's league-worst secondary for seven catches, a season-high 152 receiving yards, and a touchdown. Heading into a Week 11 road game against the Giants, Washington leads the Jaguars in all major receiving categories with a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets. He has had some down games with Trevor Lawrence spreading the ball around, as Washington has finished with a single catch on two occasions this season. That lower floor, compared to some of the elite wideouts around the NFL, makes Washington more of a fantasy WR2, but he offers weekly WR1 upside. The Giants are holding wideouts to 127 yards per game but have allowed 11 touchdown catches to the position in nine games.
outlooksByWeek.12: Parker Washington had a career-high 152 receiving yards and a touchdown on seven receptions against the Titans in Week 10, and he'll face the AFC South's cellar-dwellers again in Week 12, this time in Jacksonville. Another fantasy WR1 performance is on the table for Washington against Tennessee's reeling secondary, which has allowed the most catches and receiving yards to wideouts this season. The Titans are giving up 16 catches for 210 yards and 1.1 TDs per game to WRs, while Washington leads the Jaguars with a 44-748-6 receiving line through 10 games, with two of his three 100-yard receiving performances this season coming in the last two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dallas Goedert was the leading receiver for the Eagles in Week 1. Goedert snagged four passes for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the 24-22 win over Washington. Goedert was targeted five times. With A.J. Brown no longer in the fold, Goedert could see even more touches in the red zone. In Week 2, the Eagles will face the Tennessee Titans.  Tennessee was a tad frisky against the pass in Week 1, allowing just 215 yards passing to the Jets.  In addition, the Titans did not allow a passing touchdown for the game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dallas Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. Johnny Mundt caught two apsses in Goedert's place, and would be the next man up if Goedert cannot suit up. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dallas Goedert did not suit up last game for the Eagles due to a knee injury, and his status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. In his place, Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt combined for just two catches for 13 yards. Even if Goedert can suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.2 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dallas Goedert missed last game for the Eagles with a knee issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Goedert misses additional time, Zach Ertz would be the next man up.  An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dallas Goedert led the Eagles in targets and receptions last game. Returning from a two-game absence due to a knee injury, Goedert responded with six catches on nine targets. Unfortunately, Goedert gained just 38 yards, and the Eagles lost by a score of 19-17. If both DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley continue to be sidelined due to their respective hamstring injuries, though, Goedert should see plenty of looks, including in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dallas Goedert caught six passes for 61 yards last game for the Eagles. Goedert was second on the team in targets behind DeVonta Smith. Even with Tanner McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Goedert should still have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dallas Goedert finished second on the Eagles last game in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Goedert caught five passes on seven looks for 48 yards in the 38-21 loss to the Cowboys. Goedert has at least seven targets in three-straight outings. If DeVonta Smith and/or Dontayvion Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, Goedert should remain a focal point of the passing attack, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dallas Goedert has caught at least four passes in four-straight games for the Eagles. He has amassed 28 targets over that span. Unfortunately, Goedert is averaging less than 45 yards receiving per contest during that time period. He has also been held out of the end zone. With backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center, Goedert's prospects may not be getting any better. In Week 9, the Eagles will face a Giants defense allowing just 184.9 passing yards per tilt, which us third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Dallas Goedert collected five catches last game for Philadelphia, and continues to operate as a steady safety valve no matter who lines up under center. Goedert has at least four catches in all but one game played in 2026. In Week 11, Goedert will have a tasty matchup against a surprisingly porous Pittsburgh pass defense. The Steelers are surrendering 242.2 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Dallas Goedert had a rather quiet output for the Eagles with the return of DeVonta Smith. While Smith managed a healthy 12 targets in the 19-16 win over the Steelers, Goedert had just one look for the entire game. However, said target did gain 38 yards through the air.  Brighter days could be ahead for Goedert, though, as the Eagles face a porous Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 12. Dallas is allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. "America's Team" has also given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Worthy captured three of his six Week 1 targets for only 18 yards. The workload was low, but Kansas City QB Patrick Mahomes completed only five passes to wideouts in the Monday night opener. The third-year pro has the speed to stretch the field, but he's generally used more underneath, along with occasionally carrying the ball. Worthy is a Week 2 flex option when the Chiefs host the Colts. Indianapolis was one of five defenses to allow over 300 yards passing in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Worthy scored his first touchdown of the season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter. Worthy has notched steady target volume early in the season, with 13 total looks, but that has resulted in just an 8-43-1 line, and he has yet to get a carry. With Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Worthy will need some big plays to make a real fantasy contribution. The third-year speedster will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Worthy has struggled to break free for a big gain for Kansas City this season. The third-year speedster has managed just a 10-63-1 line on 15 targets, and surprisingly, he has yet to get a carry, perhaps to keep him healthy. Patrick Mahomes has also spread the ball around effectively, as Worthy, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets, so a big volume increase isn't likely. Worthy faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Worthy comes out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye still looking to establish himself as a consistent part of the passing attack. With both Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton getting hurt during a Week 4 win over the Raiders, Worthy caught four of seven targets for a season-high 70 yards. Rice appears to be on track to return quickly, but Thornton is likely to miss the rest of the year, which could open up some downfield routes for Worthy. The third-year speedster will face a Chargers secondary in Week 6 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Worthy is coming off his most productive game of the season, catching all seven of his targets for 73 yards in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers. With Rashee Rice sidelined, Worthy's volume has ticked up, but he hasn't been targeted more than seven times in a game this season. The third-year speedster also hasn't been able to break many big gains, with only one of his 21 catches going for 20-plus yards after nine of his 42 receptions in 2025 went for 20-plus. Worthy isn't likely to produce a ceiling game in Week 7 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Xavier Worthy struggled in Week 7 while filling in as Kansas City's No. 1 wide receiver, catching just three of six targets for 11 yards in a loss to the Seahawks. The third-year speedster has yet to reach 80 receiving yards this season, and it's looking increasingly like he won't live up to the billing of being the 28th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Once Rashee Rice is cleared to return from a hamstring strain, Worthy might benefit from returning to a more comfortable supporting role. He'll try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos secondary that could again be without Pat Surtain, but still ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Xavier Worthy continues to struggle in his third NFL season. The Kansas City wideout has handled at least six targets in four straight games and six of seven in 2026, but that steady volume has resulted in just a 27-230-1 line on 41 total targets. Worthy is being used on downfield routes less often this year, with his 8.8 aDOT being a career low, but Andy Reid hasn't been able to consistently scheme him into open space where he can use his elite speed. If the front office adds reinforcements at wide receiver by the trade deadline, Worthy's role could be squeezed further. He'll try to put together a breakout performance in Week 9 against a Jets secondary that ranks 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: Xavier Worthy was one of several Kansas City players to emerge from a Week 9 win over the Jets with an injury. The speedy wideout grabbed at his hamstring late in the victory after catching all six of his targets for 48 yards. Patrick Mahomes also suffered an injury to his throwing elbow, so even if Worthy doesn't end up missing time, his fantasy outlook could be affected by having Justin Fields under center instead. Worthy has struggled this season even when healthy, managing just a 33-278-1 line on 47 targets over eight games. If he's in the lineup in Week 10, he'll face a Falcons secondary that just traded away safety Jessie Bates and ranks 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Xavier Worthy could be in danger of vanishing from the Kansas City game plan. In a Week 10 win over the Falcons that marked the debut of trade-deadline acquisition Josh Downs, Worthy registered only three targets and failed to catch any. Downs, meanwhile, caught four of five targets and got into the end zone despite playing just 10 snaps. As the former Colt's role increases, Worthy could be squeezed further for looks from Patrick Mahomes, with Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, and the team's running backs also seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order. Worthy will try to bounce back in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Xavier Worthy was finally able to make a splash in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals, scoring his first touchdown since Week 2 on an 18-yard connection with Patrick Mahomes. Worthy caught just two of four targets for 38 total yards, and he's gone five straight games without reaching 50 receiving yards. The third-year speedster still has big-play upside, but he appears to be lost in the shuffle while Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson, and newcomer Josh Downs all get prioritized ahead of him. Worthy will try to build on last week's effort in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing as a rookie with 101 touches and 12 touchdowns in 20 games (including the playoffs), Worthy had the look of an emerging star. Things didn't go as planned in Year 2, though, as the 2024 first-round pick was injured on his third snap of the season and wasn't productive or utilized as much as expected upon his return. Worthy was limited to one touchdown (Week 6) and reached 12 fantasy points once in 14 games (Week 4). The speedy Worthy is still only 23 years old, so a Year 3 breakout is certainly possible, especially with Rashee Rice and 36-year-old Travis Kelce as his only legit target competition. He's worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to match a career outing when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Kincaid had a personal-best 130 yards in his season debut but, more importantly, played 77% of the team's snaps after topping 50% just three times last year. If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. He'll face a defense on Thursday night that allowed 87 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends in Week 1, suggesting his statistical surge can continue.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Kincaid brings momentum into the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. After a 130-yard opener, Kincaid posted seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against Detroit, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps. Opportunity, not talent, has been an issue as he hasn't played over a 50% snap share since Week 5 in 2025. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Part of the decrease in volume could be DJ Moore's return to health, but Buffalo remains run-heavy, limiting Kincaid's looks. He recorded a 67% snap share, more than usual, so opportunity remains. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Kincaid faces an uphill battle for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Rams in Week 5. He is coming off a season-low seven yards on two targets (one catch), and after a productive two-game start, has only five targets in Weeks 3 and 4. The Rams have defended tight ends at an elite level, allowing a mere 2.9 yards per target and only 85 total yards through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills' passing game is shrinking ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. After snagging 12 of 14 targets in his first two games, Kincaid has been limited to four catches on seven targets over the last three weeks, amassing just 52 yards. His snap share remains strong and elevated from 2025; Buffalo just seems more inclined to be a run-first offense. Las Vegas has allowed six touchdowns to opposing tight ends, resulting in the fifth-most fantasy points allowed to the position. Kincaid can be a viable starting option in a favorable bounce-back matchup.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dalton Kincaid hopes to rediscover some early season success with the Bills coming out of a bye week to host the Ravens in Week 8. After snagging 12 of 14 targets for 225 yards in his first two games, Kincaid has not topped 38 yards or scored in his subsequent four outings, despite maintaining a higher snap share than last season. Baltimore is allowing only 39.0 yards per game to opposing tight ends, setting up Kincaid for another quiet week, but the Ravens allowed two touchdowns to the position last week and five overall, potentially helping Kincaid break his scoring drought.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dalton Kincaid faces a challenging matchup in Week 9 when the Bills face the Vikings. He has 11 catches over the last two weeks, scoring in Week 8 for the first time since Week 2, and finished with 86 yards after hauling in just 90 total yards in his previous four games. Minnesota has allowed the fewest points per game to opposing tight ends, surrendering only 6.2 yards per target and no touchdowns through seven games. Kincaid needs volume to be productive in the Week 9 Monday night affair, and that's not a sure thing.
outlooksByWeek.10: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills offense may be sliding as they enter a Week 10 matchup against the Jets. In Buffalo's first six games, Kincaid garnered less than a 66% snap share just once, but since the team's Week 7 bye, he's been under 60% in two outings, resulting in just nine targets. The Jets have been vulnerable against tight ends, allowing at least 72 yards in three straight weeks, but Kincaid's recent workload is a concern.
outlooksByWeek.11: A lack of opportunities could keep the Bills' Dalton Kincaid from exploiting the Dolphins' defense in Week 11. He had just three targets for the second straight game in Week 10, and his snap share has declined in each of the last three games since Buffalo's Week 7 bye, reaching a season-low 46% in Week 10. Buffalo has been a run-heavy offense, often leaving Kincaid off the field in favor of more traditional blocking tight ends. With declining snaps, he will be left with too few chances to beat a defense that's allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.12: Dalton Kincaid will need to overcome thumb and ankle injuries if he's to help the Bills in a promising Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. His playing time and production have slid over the last three weeks coming out of Buffalo's Week 7 bye. Kincaid's snap share has dropped to around 50%, ceding his slot role to Dawson Knox, who is serving as an additional blocker on the line. If Kincaid plays, opportunities await, with Kansas City allowing tight ends to catch at least four passes in three straight games and five overall touchdowns. They have also yielded the seventh-most fantasy points per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 2 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's now been placed on IR for the injury. The fifth-year running back (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps against the Packers, with Mason leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Unfortunately, Mason will now be out for at least the next four weeks, priming Jones for a bigger role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 3 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's been placed on IR for the injury. Mason will remain sidelined for at least the next three weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 4 as the Vikings take on the Dolphins. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next two weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 5 as the Vikings travel to New Orleans. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next week, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Mason could be set to return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Mason has been sidelined since Week 1 with a thumb injury that landed him on IR, but he's set to return to practice this week. The fifth-year running back's return should put him at least in a complementary role with veteran Aaron Jones. Indianapolis' defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Mason could be in line for a workhorse role as the Vikings travel to Detroit in Week 8. Mason made his return from IR in Week 7 against the Colts and logged 15 carries for 68 yards, leading the ground game with Aaron Jones hurting his knee in the matchup. Jones' status is up in the air moving forward, so Mason's role could be even bigger if he has full command of the backfield. The Lions have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jordan Mason should remain a part of a two-punch backfield in Week 9 as the Vikings play the Bills. Mason led Minnesota's backfield with eight carries in a Week 8 loss to the Lions, but he finished with just 20 yards compared to Aaron Jones' five carries for 22 yards. The current timeshare between the two could continue to keep both in check, but Buffalo ranking 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs is favorable.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jordan Mason will look to see a more favorable game script in Week 10 as the Vikings travel to Green Bay. Mason rushed just six times for 35 yards and reeled in two of three targets for seven yards in a Week 9 loss to the Bills. As expected, the fifth-year ball carrier has been a part of a two-pronged backfield approach next to Aaron Jones this season, but it appears Mason might be the more efficient of the pair. The Packers have ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jordan Mason will aim to make the most of his situation as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Mason led Minnesota's backfield with 16 carries for 59 yards in a Week 10 win over the Packers, but teammate Aaron Jones punched in the only touchdown from the pair. Mason has yet to record a score in four outings since returning from a thumb injury, but he's put together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry. He'll face a San Francisco defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jordan Mason will aim to make the most of his usage as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Mason rushed the ball 11 times for 38 yards and logged one catch for minus-1 yard in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. He's now been unable to find the end zone since returning from injury in Week 7, and his receiving work has yet to make up for otherwise subpar rushing totals. Luckily, Atlanta has ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Daniel Jones is unlikely to post gaudy passing numbers in the Colts' run-first offense, and he doesn't appear interested in using his legs as much after tearing his Achilles in Week 14 of last season. His fantasy appeal is limited to multi-QB or superflex formats, and Jones is a low-end option even in those leagues for a Week 2 matchup against a Chiefs defense that held Bo Nix to 131 passing yards in Week 1. Jones had just 166 passing yards with a 1:1 TD:INT and one carry for four yards in the Colts' 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Ravens.
outlooksByWeek.3: Daniel Jones is averaging 188 passing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 3 home game against the Texans. Houston gave up two touchdown passes apiece to star QBs Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, but Jones will be hard-pressed to post his first multi-TD performance of the season considering the Texans boast one of the league's best defenses, having allowed the fewest yards in the NFL last season. The Colts will continue to rely primarily on the legs of star RB Jonathan Taylor, and Indianapolis has an underwhelming group of pass catchers that's expected to be without last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel) for several weeks. Jones has been a non-factor as a rusher since returning from a torn Achilles, with just 14 rushing yards this season. His mediocre passing stats make him an unappealing Week 3 fantasy option, even in multi-QB formats.
