outlooksByWeek.6: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Johnson tallied just 16 yards on four receptions in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, struggling alongside the rest of New Orleans' offense. Despite this, he's tied for the second-most receptions (25) on the Saints through five weeks, accumulating 248 yards and three touchdowns. Expect Johnson to bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's allowed 14.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Juwan Johnson will look to bounce back from a lackluster performance in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Johnson has struggled over the last two weeks, catching just four of seven targets for 16 yards. Despite this, he remains third on the team in targets (35), receptions (25) and yards (248) through six games, suggesting more fantasy production in the near future. Johnson is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, however, as Pittsburgh's defense has allowed just 11.7 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Johnson has really underperformed in the Saints' last two games, catching just one of five targets for seven yards during that span. Despite this recent lack of production, Johnson ranks third on the team in receiving yards (255), targets (38) and receptions (26) while catching three touchdowns across seven contests. Johnson could bounce back against a Cleveland defense that's given up 15.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers during the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Johnson saw little volume but saved his fantasy day with a score in Week 9, catching two of three targets for 34 yards and a touchdown. He's been relatively underwhelming over the last three contests, catching just three of seven targets for 41 yards and a touchdown. This is especially concerning due to the return of 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson, who will likely take more receiving volume away from Johnson as the season progresses. However, Johnson could thrive against a Panthers defense that's allowed 13.5 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Johnson has really struggled over New Orleans' last four games, catching just five of 10 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown. With Jordyn Tyson breaking out in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers (11-80-0), Johnson will likely receive even less opportunities going forward. He likely needs to score a touchdown to find fantasy relevance in Week 11 against a Bears defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to tight ends all season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) is expected to remain the Saints' top tight end if active for the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Johnson sustained a hamstring injury during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, and the extent of the issue remains TBD. Johnson struggled to find fantasy value before sustaining this injury, catching just five of 10 targets for 69 yards and one touchdown from Weeks 7 through 10 (three games). If active, Johnson could find fantasy value but is likely still too inconsistent to start, even with a favorable matchup against a Bengals defense that's given up 15.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson's impressive progression continued in 2025, as the converted wide receiver posted career-high marks in targets, catches, yardage and fantasy points (all four were eighth or better among tight ends). Johnson produced nine top-12 fantasy weeks, which tied for second at the position. He has finished in the top 12 in aDOT each of the past four seasons but hasn't been much of an option near the goal line (no more than four TDs or end zone targets in each of the past three seasons). The 29-year-old has added target competition, including eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy), but he very well could settle in as high as third in target priority in the Saints' Tyler Shough-led offense. Johnson is a fine TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Gay was perfect in his Raiders debut, converting field goals from 30 and 47 yards and all three extra points in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. A rebuilding opponent certainly provided Gay with extra opportunities, but the Las Vegas offense could also be better than expected. New head coach Klint Kubiak and an improved quarterback situation, with Kirk Cousins steadying the ship until rookie Fernando Mendoza is ready, should help. The pending return of Brock Bowers will also help generate more scoring drives. Gay may not be able to squander any chances in Week 2 against a Chargers team that ranked ninth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matt Gay has been busy to begin his Raiders' career, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and all six of his extra points through the first two games of the season. The outlook for the offense should improve once Brock Bowers is cleared for his 2026 debut, and while there's additional uncertainly on the horizon once first overall pick Fernando Mendoza is deemed ready to replace Kirk Cousins under center, Gay could actually benefit if the young QB struggles to get the ball into the end zone while he figures out NFL defenses. Gay will face a Saints team in Week 3 that's allowed an exact mirror to his production so far, with opposition kickers getting three FGs and six PATs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matt Gay has been both busy and perfect for the surprising 3-0 Raiders, connecting on all six of his field goal attempts and all eight of his PATs. The veteran kicker was also successful on his only attempt from 50-plus yards, as he looks to boot at least three long-range FGs for a sixth straight season. Gay has also benefited from a favorable early schedule, as all three of Las Vegas' games so far have been played indoors. The team will get a fourth straight game under a roof in a Week 4 home tilt against Kansas City, but Gay likely won't be able to afford to squander any opportunities versus an opponent that has given up just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matt Gay continues to benefit from the Raiders' surprisingly strong start to the season on offense with Kirk Cousins under center. In a Week 4 loss to Kansas City, Gay was a perfect 4-for-4 on FG tries while also converting his only PAT. The veteran has yet to miss an attempt in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 9-for-9 on extra points, putting him third in the NFL in kicker scoring behind the Vikings' Will Reichard and the Colts' Spencer Shrader. Gay likely won't be able to afford to start squandering opportunities in Week 5 against a Patriots team that's allowed 19.3 points per game so far, tied for sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matt Gay missed his first kick of the season in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, pinging the upright on a field goal attempt from 48 yards out. He's still having a strong season, converting all 11 of his PATs and going 11-for-12 on FG attempts, including his only attempt from 50-plus yards. Gay has benefited from a surprisingly potent offense under Kirk Cousins, but the veteran QB may be reverting to his usual level, perhaps opening the door for first overall pick Fernando Mendoza to take the reins, so it's not necessarily bad news for Gay's long-term outlook. Gay will take on a Bills team in Week 6 that's allowing 28.2 points per game, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matt Gay stayed busy in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, going a perfect 3-for-3 on both field goal attempts and extra points. The veteran kicker has benefited from the team's offensive resurgence under new head coach Klint Kubiak, and Gay sits third in scoring in the NFL behind the Colts' Spencer Shrader and the Bills' Tyler Bass. Gay will face a Rams team in Week 7 that's allowed 23.0 points per game, tied for 17th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Matt Gay was perfect in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets, converting all five of his PATs and his only field goal attempt. The veteran kicker has missed just two FGs through eight games this season, going 18-for-20 (90.0%), and he's drilled all 19 of his extra points. Playing his home games indoors appears to suit Gay, after he connected on just 13 of 19 field goals during his 10-game stint with the Commanders in 2025. Gay likely can't afford to squander any opportunities in Week 9 against a 49ers team allowing just 19.9 points per game, tied for sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Matt Gay was afforded few opportunities in the Raiders' Week 9 loss to the 49ers, connecting on a 50-yard attempt for his only field goal and converting both his PATs. The veteran kicker has a 90.5% FG success rate on the season, going 19-for-21, and he has yet to miss an extra point in 2026, but his erratic weekly volume limits his fantasy utility. Gay isn't likely to see much volume in Week 10 against a Seahawks team allowing 18.0 points per game, tied for fourth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Matt Gay didn't get much volume in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, as he converted both his field goal attempts and his only PAT. The veteran kicker has handled two or fewer FG attempts in four of the last six games, but with rookie Fernando Mendoza replacing Kirk Cousins under center, the offense's efficiency could take a step backward and give Gay more field goal chances. He may not be much busier in Week 11 against a Broncos team allowing 20.7 points per game, ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Matt Gay has been perfect over the last four weeks, going 5-for-5 on field goal attempts and 11-for-11 on PATs. The veteran kicker's volume hasn't been significantly affected by the switch at quarterback from Kirk Cousins to Fernando Mendoza, and the Raiders' offense might actually take a step forward once Brock Bowers gets healthy, with young skill players Ashton Jeanty and Jack Bech showing signs of breaking out. Gay will look to stay locked in during Week 12's clash with a Browns team that's allowing 22.0 points per game, tied for 14th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: After a miserable 2025 that saw them surrender the most yards while scoring the third-fewest fantasy points, the Commanders brought in a slew of offseason reinforcements, though it was more of a quantitative than qualitative process. There's no reason to trust this D/ST in Weeks 1 and 2, which are road matchups with the Eagles and Cowboys, but if the Commanders show midseason promise, bear in mind its most favorable matchups come during the season's second half.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel will look to build upon a strong season-opening performance when the 49ers face Miami in Week 2. In Samuel's return to San Francisco following a one-year hiatus, he caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in last Thursday's win over the Rams. Samuel and Mike Evans finished with nearly identical receiving lines, suggesting that both veteran wideouts can thrive with QB Brock Purdy. The Dolphins were beat handily by the Raiders in Week 1 while giving up three TDs through the air (though two were to RB Ashton Jeanty).
outlooksByWeek.3: Deebo Samuel is coming off a quiet game heading into San Francisco's Week 3 matchup against the Cardinals. Samuel caught three passes for 31 yards and rushed once for four yards in Sunday's rout of Miami. However, fellow wideouts Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both exited that contest due to injury, and though early reports suggest Evans should be fine for Week 3, Samuel could see more looks come his way given his comparatively good health. Arizona has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts so far this year and was just torched by Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) on Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deebo Samuel could take on the 49ers' No. 1 WR role in Week 4 against Denver if Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) is unable to play. Though Evans left in the second quarter in this past Sunday's win over Arizona, Samuel ended the contest without seeing a target. However, he still had a good fantasy line thanks to an 80-yard TD on a hook-and-ladder play, and Samuel also gained 14 yards on two carries. Should Evans be unable to suit up against Denver, Samuel could face the daunting task of trying to beat star cornerback Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deebo Samuel has been a versatile cog for the 49ers heading into a Week 5 matchup against Seattle. Samuel has scored three receiving TDs though four games, and he's also racked up 185 receiving yards, 74 rushing yads and 231 kick-return yards. The veteran wideout has drawn a modest 17 targets so far, but he's been very efficient in hauling in 14 of them. San Francisco may look to use Samuel creatively against a Seahawks defense that is allowing just 246.8 yards per game this season, fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Deebo Samuel is dealing with a hamstring injury and may not be able to play in San Francisco's Week 6 matchup against Washington. Samuel was hurt in the third quarter of this past Sunday's win over Seattle and was quickly ruled out. The veteran receiver is slated for imaging, which should provide clarity about the extent of the injury and a potential return timeline. If Samuel can't play in Week 6, he'll miss the opportunity to feast on a Commanders defense that has struggled mightily against the pass this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Deebo Samuel and the 49ers travel to face the Falcons in Week 7. The veteran receiver missed San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6 with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 5. Head coach Kyle Shanahan stated they would "hold off" on placing him on injured reserve with the Week 8 bye approaching, so it sounds like Samuel is in jeopardy of missing the road tilt against Atlanta. Expect him to work towards a Week 9 return, as long as he doesn't suffer any sort of setback.
outlooksByWeek.9: Deebo Samuel has a chance to return from a two-game absence for San Francisco's Week 9 tilt against Las Vegas. Samuel hurt his hamstring in Week 5 against Seattle and hasn't played since, but the 49ers' Week 8 bye allowed him time for extra rest. Mike Evans (Achilles) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) also have a chance to return to San Francisco's wideout corps following absences of their own, so the team's passing game could be getting a big boost. The outlook is positive for all of the 49ers' wide receivers given that the Raiders have allowed 10 receiving touchdowns to the position this year, tied for third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will look to return from a four-game absence when San Francisco travels to Dallas in Week 10. Samuel hasn't been placed on IR, and the expectation is that he'll return before the end of the season, but his status for this week is hazy, at best. With No. 1 wideout Mike Evans (Achilles) missing the past two games, the 49ers acquired Keenan Allen at the trade deadline to provide additional depth. If Samuel is able to get back on the field against the Cowboys, he could find success against a defense that has given up 159.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, ninth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Deebo Samuel will look to build on his best performance of the season when the 49ers  host the Vikings in Week 11. Samuel compiled 109 total yards and two touchdowns this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, with most of that yardage coming on a 70-yard rushing score. It was Samuel's first game if five weeks, as he had been sidelined due to a hamstring injury. His versatility could come in handy against a Vikings defense that is tied for the third-fewest receiving TDs (five) allowed to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Deebo Samuel continues to be a Swiss Army knife for San Francisco heading into a Week 12 tilt against the Seahawks. In this past Sunday's win over the Vikings, Samuel recorded two carries for 27 yards, caught three of four targets for 20 yards and returned two kickoffs for 57 yards. While that might not add up to substantial fantasy production, Samuel's skill set could be invaluable for the 49ers against a tough defense like the Seahawks'. Seattle has given up the fewest yards per target (5.89) to wideouts this season, so San Francisco may look to be creative in order to push the ball downfield.

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith broke loose last game for the Eagles, snagging 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Titans. Smith saw a team-best 13 targets for the game, a pace which should continue in the absence of A.J. Brown. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeVonta Smith unsurprisingly led the Eagles in targets, receptions and receiving yardage last game. Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Smith managed six catches and 65 yards on eight targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Smith has been held under 70 yards receiving in two of his three games this season. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeVonta Smith missed last game for the Eagles with a hamstring issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Smith misses additional time, Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon will have some big shoes to fill. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeVonta Smith has missed two-straight games for the Eagles. Smith has been nursing a hamstring ailment, and his status for Week 6 versus the Panthers remains up in the air. The Eagles offense has struggled mightily without Smith and running back Saquon Barkley. If Smith can return to the lineup, he would provide a major boost against a Carolina defense allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league. If Smith cannot suit up, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would see added work.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeVonta Smith returned to the Eagles lineup with a bang. Smith snagged seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown following a two-game absence from a hamstring issue. Even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center, Smith was targeted a staggering 14 times. As a result, even with McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Smith should have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: DeVonta Smith missed Philadelphia's last game after aggravating a hamstring injury. Smith has played in just four games this season due to the nagging issue, which could also leave him sidelined in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If he is able to suit up, Smith could have a tasty matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: DeVonta Smith missed yet another game for the Eagles due to a balky hamstring. Smith has played in just four contests in 2026 in what has been a lost season overall for 2-6 Philadelphia. If he is somehow able to suit up in Week 9, he would be facing a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 184.9 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: DeVonta Smith could return from a hamstring issue for the Eagles following their bye. Smith has missed five of the last six games for Philadelphia due to the ailment. His return, along with that of Dontayvion Wicks, would bolster an extremely depleted wide receiving corps. If he can suit up, the matchup could also be favorable in Week 11, as the Steelers defense has been surprisingly vulnerable to the pass in 2026. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: DeVonta Smith returned from injury for the Eagles and immediately received a heavy workload. Smith saw a team-high 12 targets in the 19-16 win. However, he managed just five catches for 41 yards for the game. Still, he retained his spot as the top target in the offense, and could find more success in Week 12 versus a porous Dallas Cowboys defense. "America's Team" has given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL. Dallas is also allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devin Singletary acted as the No. 2 back for the Giants in their season-opening win in Week 1 over Dallas. He received the second-most carries out of the backfield behind starter Cam Skattebo, while also catching four passes for 22 yards and a touchdown in the 28-20 triumph. Fellow rusher Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble in this game as well, which could further solidify Singletary's role, though veteran Najee Harris also looms. In Week 2, the Giants will be facing a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season. The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men to give the defensive line a boost.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devin Singletary managed just three carries for nine yards last game for the Giants. He remains firmly behind Cam Skattebo on the depth chart. Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury, so teams will likely gameplan to stop the run. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Singletary scored the winning touchdown last game for the Giants, and could have a larger role in the backfield moving forward. Tyrone Tracy was placed on Injured Reserve following the most recent contest, leaving only Singletary and Cam Skattebo as the healthy options out of the backfield. Though talks of a trade for Jonathan Taylor have intensified, nothing appears imminent heading into a tasty Week 9 clash with Philadelphia. The Eagles have been torched on the ground in 2026, allowing 131.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. Likewise, the Eagles have given up 10 rushing scores, which is tied for 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Singletary got the starting nod for the Giants last game, but did not find much room to roam. Singletary had a season-high 21 carries due to the injury to Cam Skattebo, though managed just 31 yards in the 19-11 win over the Eagles. Skattebo looks poised to return in Week 10 versus the Commanders, so Singletary's touches will likely take a massive hit as a result. In addition, Washington has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026, allowing just 102.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the league. In addition, the Commanders have yielded just seven rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Devin Singletary played just five snaps last game for the Giants. With Cam Skattebo healthy, Singletary was left largely riding the pine, a spot he will likely continue to occupy in Week 11 versus the Jags. The matchup versus Jacksonville is also far from ideal. Jacksonville is allowing just 91 rushing yards per clash, which is sixth in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have surrendered only five rushing touchdowns this season, which is tied for fourth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Devin Singletary managed just two touches last game for the Giants. Singletary has just three touches over the last two contests, and even with starter Cam Skattebo fumbling, Singletary continues to serve mostly as depth. Singletary is also averaging just 2.9 yards per carry this season, which has not helped his cause. In Week 12, he could find some room to roam against the lowly Colts, though.  Indianapolis is allowing 134.4 rushing yards per tilt, which is 29th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cameron Dicker didn't get many chances to hit the scoreboard in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, converting both his extra points but failing to see a field-goal attempt. The team's offense didn't quite look in sync yet under new coordinator Mike McDaniel, and top wideout Ladd McConkey was knocked out of the game early with a rib injury, so scoring drives could be tough to come by for the club in the short term. Dicker will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Raiders team that finished 25th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cameron Dicker has had a rough start to the season as the Chargers adjust to a new offensive scheme under Mike McDaniel. The fifth-year kicker has converted all four of his PATs through two games, but his only field-goal attempt so far came from 58 yards out, and he clanked it off the upright. Better days should be ahead for Dicker and the offense, but his streak of seasons with 40-plus FG attempts could be about to come to an abrupt end. Dicker could be a little busier in Week 3 against a Bills team that's allowed 31.0 points a game in the early going, tied for the third-worst total in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cameron Dicker has had a shaky start to the season as the Chargers struggle to put points on the board. The fifth-year kicker has seen just five extra points in three games, converting all five, and he's connected on just three of five FG attempts, with all three makes coming in a Week 3 loss to the Bills. That volatility isn't fantasy-friendly, and until the team's skill players begin to get the hang of new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, Dicker's volume is likely to remain limited. He probably won't be able to afford to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Seahawks team allowing just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cameron Dicker's volume increased for a second straight week in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his PATs. While the team's offense continues to struggle, Justin Herbert is at least putting together longer drives, and during those two contests Dicker has gone 6-for-7 on FG tries with all of his attempts coming from inside 50 yards. He likely won't be able to squander many chances in Week 5 against a Broncos team allowing 23.5 points per game, 17th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cameron Dicker's opportunities continue to be inconsistent due to the struggles of the Chargers' offense. The kicker hasn't attempted more than two PATs in any of the team's first five games, going a perfect 9-for-9, and he's seen one or fewer field goal attempts in three of those five contests. With the offensive line in shambles and Justin Herbert running out of healthy targets, Dicker's volume doesn't seem likely to pick up anytime soon. He'll face a Kansas City squad in Week 6 that's allowing 19.3 points per game, seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cameron Dicker failed to get an extra-point attempt in Week 6 for the first time this season, accounting for all the Chargers' points with two field goals in a 22-6 loss to Kansas City. Coming out of a bye, the offense will hopefully be a bit healthier and energized, providing Dicker with more opportunities, but he has kicked multiple field goals in three of the last four contests. In Week 8, he'll take aim at a Rams team that's allowing 22.7 points per game, 16th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cameron Dicker hasn't missed a kick in four straight games, converting all three of his field goal attempts in a Week 8 loss to the Rams but failing to even see a PAT for a second straight contest. The Chargers' offensive struggles limit Dicker's opportunities despite his accuracy, and the advantage of playing his home games indoors. Dicker will look for a little more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans team that's giving up 24.3 points per game, 18th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Cameron Dicker continues to benefit from the Chargers' inability to finish drives. The 26-year-old kicker has booted multiple field goals in five of the last six games, going 15-for-16 on FG attempts over that stretch but attempting just six extra points, converting them all. The steady volume gives Dicker a solid floor heading into a Week 10 clash with a Ravens team allowing 26.2 points per game, tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Cameron Dicker booted three field goals for a third straight game, and the fifth time in the last seven, as the Chargers recorded their first win of 2026 in a Week 10 victory over the Ravens. The team's offensive struggles have created extra FG opportunities for its kicker, and Dicker has yet to kick more than two PATs in a game even as his field goal volume remains steady. That gives him a somewhat reliable floor, but a questionable ceiling, heading into a Week 11 clash with a Jets team allowing 25.4 points a contest, 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Cameron Dicker hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, going 16-for-16 on field goal attempts and 10-for-10 on PATs over the last seven games. The Chargers' struggling offense hasn't provided him with consistent opportunities, but Dicker's reliability provides him with a solid floor. With Justin Herbert in the concussion protocol, DJ Uiagalelei could be in line to make his first career NFL start at quarterback, adding a lot more uncertainty to the picture. Even if Herbert plays, Dicker will be a volatile option at kicker in Week 12 against a Patriots team allowing 24.2 points per game, 19th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will likely have Drew Lock throwing balls to him when Seattle faces Arizona in Week 2. Lock took over for an injured Sam Darnold (glute) in the Seahawks' season-opening win, and Darnold is expected to miss Week 2. However, the QB change didn't impact Smith-Njigba's stat line in Week 1, as he finished with eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown. He's as matchup-proof a WR as there is in the NFL, and he's set to take on a Cardinals defense that allowed Ladd McConkey (ribs) to put up a 5-82-1 line in less than a full game during a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington riding the wave of a three-touchdown performance. That effort came Sunday versus Arizona, when the star wideout also caught nine passes for 155 yards. Smith-Njigba worked with backup QB Drew Lock in that victory due to Sam Darnold being sidelined with a glute injury, and it seems that the reigning AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year is more than capable up dominating regardless of who is throwing him the ball. Smith-Njigba could be in for another huge effort against a Commanders defense that has surrendered the 10th-most receiving yards (337) to wideouts through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off another huge game as Seattle prepares to host the Chargers in Week 4. Versus Washington in Week 3, Smith-Njigba recorded 10 catches on 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The star receiver has logged at least eight catches, 120 yards and one score in each of his first three games this season, making him among fantasy's most valuable assets once again. The Chargers don't figure to be able to contain Smith-Njigba given that they're allowing 9.76 yards per target to wideouts, fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should once again be the centerpiece of Seattle's passing game in a big Week 5 clash against the 49ers. The star wideout posted a fine 5-76-0 receiving line against the Chargers this past Sunday, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. It's telling that despite his final stats being quite adequate, Smith-Njigba's targets, catches and yards were each a season-low mark in what has been a standout campaign thus far. San Francisco is allowing just 6.96 yards per target to wideouts though four weeks (fifth-best in the league), though Smith-Njigba has proven to be essentially matchup-proof since the beginning of last season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is arguably the most matchup-proof wideout in the NFL, but he could be challenged in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Smith-Njigba caught five of eight targets for 102 yards and a touchdown against San Francisco in a loss this past Sunday. He's now recorded at least 100 receiving yards and one touchdown in four of his five games this season, and Smith-Njigba leads the league with 583 receiving yards. He'll be matched up Week 6 against a Broncos defense that has allowed the third-lowest catch rate (54.5%) to wideouts, but Smith-Njigba figures to get a big boost by not having to face star cornerback Patrick Surtain, who is expected to miss the contest due to an ankle injury.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks return home for a Week 7 interconference clash against the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. He corralled 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6, setting season highs in receptions and targets. Smith-Njigba paced his team in all receiving categories despite a quiet first half, and he now owns a 49-717-7 line on 65 targets through six outings. Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs will try to make it tough on the 2025 Offensive Player of the Year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to look like an unstoppable force for Seattle with a Week 8 matchup against the Bears on tap. Smith-Njigba caught nine of 12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City this past Sunday, marking his sixth performance of 100-plus receiving yards through seven weeks. The budding superstar leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns through seven weeks. He'll next face a Chicago defense that ranks 30th in the NFL with 9.51 yards per target yielded to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on a record-setting pace heading into Seattle's Week 9 game against the Cardinals. Though the Seahawks were crushed by Chicago in Week 8, Smith-Njigba put up another big game with six catches for 118 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets. The star wideout is up to a league-leading 985 receiving yards through eight weeks, putting him on pace to break the NFL's all-time record for receiving yards in a season. He'll have a prime opportunity to add onto his impressive stat line in Week 9, as the Cardinals are tied for 25th in the league with 23.7 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off a rare quiet game with Seattle's Week 10 matchup in Las Vegas on tap. The All-Pro wideout logged a season-low 51 yards on seven catches this past Sunday against Arizona, though he still drew a healthy 10 targets. Drew Lock (oblique) started at quarterback for the Seahawks in that contest and is expected to do so again in Week 10, as Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib) is likely to remain sidelined. Regardless, Smith-Njigba could feast against a Raiders defense that ranks 26th in the league with 23.6 fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will look to continue his dominant campaign in Seattle's Week 12 matchup versus San Francisco. Prior to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, Smith-Njigba had one of his biggest games of the season, posting an 8-171-1 receiving line against the Raiders. The talented wideout has worked with QB Drew Lock over Seattle's past two games, but Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) is expected to be back for this Sunday's NFC West clash. Smith-Njigba recorded 102 receiving yards and a touchdown when Seattle and San Francisco battled in Week 5, and the 49ers have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is fresh off a breakout season in which he paced all receivers in target share (36%), receiving yards (1,793), air yards (1,858) and yards per route run (3.8), while finishing no lower than fourth in targets, catches, touchdowns and fantasy points. JSN delivered top-10 fantasy weeks 10 times throughout 2025 and scored at least 13 points in 16 of 17 games. The 24-year-old is just now entering his prime and remains well positioned to handle one-third of the targets in Seattle's Sam Darnold-led offense. Smith-Njigba is an elite fantasy option who should be off the board in the early-to-middle part of Round 1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 showdown versus the Texans. He rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a TD and brought in five of six targets for another 22 yards during Cincinnati's Week 1 victory over Tampa Bay. Brown is the clear-cut lead back on a high-powered offense, and he should continue to see a hefty workload on the ground and in the passing game. However, Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, so consider this a less-than-favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to battle their division rivals in Week 3. He tallied 20 carries for 80 yards and corralled three of five targets for two yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win. Brown handled 23 of 26 touches out of the backfield, and he should continue to dominate those looks again in Week 3. The Steelers' defense ranks 26th in fantasy points allowed (27.5) to RBs after giving up 136 rushing yards and 4.9 yards per carry to the Patriots in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town for an AFC clash in Week 4. He rushed 13 times for 61 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. It was a quiet afternoon for Brown, with his 15 total touches well below his average of 22 accrued over his first two outings. He'll face another stout defensive unit, as Jacksonville ranks seventh in fantasy points (17.2) and fourth in rushing yards allowed (57.7) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase Brown and the Bengals visit the 0-4 Dolphins for a Week 5 showdown. He had nine carries for 10 yards but caught all 11 of his targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. Brown set a career high in receptions with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) leaving in the first half, and with Tee Higgins (adductor) picking up a questionable tag, the running back could again get high volume through the air while still handling the bulk of carries. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) and receiving TDs (4) allowed to the position, giving Brown a very favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase Brown and the Bengals are on the road for a divisional clash against the Ravens in Week 7. He registered 13 carries for 39 yards and caught three of four targets for 21 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Brown took a backseat to Samaje Perine, who had 14 carries for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a touchdown. Over his last two outings, he's rushed 22 times for 49 yards, a miserable 2.2 yards per carry. Next up is another difficult matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 18.6 fantasy points per game (7th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Titans to town for a Week 8 showdown. He rushed 11 times for 39 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Over his last three outings, Brown has 33 carries for 88 yards (2.7 yards per carry). He'll look to bounce back against a Tennessee defense that gave up 183 rushing yards and three total TDs to the Browns in Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chase Brown and the Bengals take on the Falcons for a Week 9 showdown in Spain. He rushed 12 times for 55 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 46 yards during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in Week 8. Brown lost a fumble but managed to out-touch Samaje Perine 20-5, a good sign for Brown's fantasy outlook. Next up is a Falcons defense allowing 28.1 fantasy points per game (30th) to opposing RBs after giving up 324 rushing yards in their last outing.
outlooksByWeek.10: Chase Brown and the Bengals host the division-rival Steelers for an AFC North clash in Week 10. In Week 9, he had nine carries for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for another 18 yards to help Cincinnati win a fourth straight game. Brown's production has been somewhat underwhelming from a fantasy perspective, as he's registered just one touchdown across eight outings in 2026. He'll look to find the end zone against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed just four TDs to the position and is coming off a bye.
outlooksByWeek.11: In Week 11, Chase Brown and the Bengals travel to face the Commanders on Monday Night Football. In Week 10, during Cincinnati's victory, he rushed 10 times for 44 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 39 yards and two TDs. Brown finally found paydirt, doing so for the first time since Week 1, while recording his first two receiving scores of the season. He'll look to exploit a Commanders defense that gave up 78 yards and two TDs to Cam Skattebo in their previous outing.
outlooksByWeek.12: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Saints to town for an interconference showdown in Week 12. He had six carries for six yards and caught five of eight targets for 30 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Brown watched as Samaje Perine erupted for 97 scrimmage yards on 10 touches, as Brown was unable to build upon his two-TD performance from the previous outing. Next up is a juicy matchup against New Orleans' 31st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (28.5) to opposing RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth NFL season and third as Cincinnati's lead back. His 2025 season got off to a rocky start (10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown during his first seven games), but it turned around drastically down the stretch (21.2 points per game and 10 TDs during his final 10 games). The improvement coincided with Cincinnati's improved QB play, which should continue into 2026 with a healthy Joe Burrow. Brown has yet to finish a season higher than 16th in carries or rushing yards, but he has scored exactly 11 TDs and has finished fifth in receptions in each of the past two years, both of which have resulted in top-10 fantasy campaigns. The 26-year-old once again has minimal competition for touches in a very good Bengals offense. He's best valued as a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to operate as Carolina's top pass catcher in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. McMillan caught just five passes for 75 yards and lost a fumble in last week's loss, despite the game ending with the most points ever scored in a Week 1 contest. He was out-shined by third-year wideout Jalen Coker, who paced Carolina's receiving corps in targets (nine), receptions (eight), yards (138) and touchdowns (two). McMillan will look to return to form in Week 2, but he's in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that gave up just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top receiving option in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. McMillan is coming off the best performance of his young career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, recording career highs in targets (16), receptions (14) and yards (192) while scoring two touchdowns. He ranks ninth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (96.3) through four appearances this season, leading Carolina in yards, targets and receptions. Expect McMillan to remain productive in Week 6 against an Eagles secondary that's allowed 38.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of Carolina's top wideouts in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan has been one of the league's most productive wideouts this season, catching 32 of 48 targets for 471 yards and two touchdowns in just five contests. He's averaged 94.2 receiving yards per game, the seventh-best mark in the NFL, and is expected to continue benefitting from the Panthers' aggressive style of offense (40.2 pass attempts per game). Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers secondary that's allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Despite Carolina's offensive struggles in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, McMillan was relatively productive, catching four of six targets for 40 yards. On the season, the second-year pro has nabbed 36 of 54 targets for 511 yards (11th-most in the NFL) and two touchdowns in just six contests. He could find success in Week 8 against a Packers secondary that's given up six receiving touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Following his huge performance against the Lions in Week 4 (14-192-2), McMillan has cooled off, catching just 16 of 26 targets for 184 yards and no scores over Carolina's last three games. Despite this, McMillan ranks 11th in the NFL in receiving yards per game (81.1) 12th in targets per game (9.3), which suggests more production is coming in the near future. However, he's in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Denver secondary that's allowed just 27.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout during the Week 10 matchup against the Saints. McMillan salvaged his fantasy day with a late score in the Week 9 loss to the Broncos, catching four of six targets for 56 yards. The Arizona product has cooled down since his monstrous performance in Week 4 (14-192-2), averaging 5.0 receptions and 60.0 receiving yards per game over his last four contests. Despite this, McMillan could find success against a Saints secondary that's allowed 31.7 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain Carolina's top wideout during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. McMillan was limited to just three catches on seven targets during the Week 10 win over the Saints, his fewest reception total since the Week 3 loss to the Browns. However, he ranked first on the team in targets while the rest of Carolina's receiver room combined for five targets, which is positive sign for McMillan's fantasy outlook going forward. McMillan could thrive against the Ravens in Week 11, as they have given up 34.3 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through nine games this season.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan had a nice bounce-back performance in the Week 11 win over the Ravens, catching six of nine targets for 71 yards and a score. The second-year pro is averaging team-highs in targets (8.7), receptions (5.5) and receiving yards per game (73.1), which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. McMillan is in for a tough Week 12 matchup, however, as the Buccaneers' defense has allowed just 30.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wide-receiver rooms this year.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Warren salvaged his fantasy day in the Colts' season-opening loss with a nine-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, but he had only four receiving yards across the rest of the game. The 2025 first-round pick has just 213 receiving yards in his last eight games after recording 617 yards in his first 10 outings. Warren did enough in Week 1 to warrant another fantasy start in most formats for a Week 2 road game against the Chiefs, but his lack of yards since the halfway point of his rookie season is becoming a worrying trend.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Warren has started his second NFL season on a two-game TD streak but has a meager 34 receiving yards on 12 targets. The Colts' 2025 first-round pick is poised to keep logging plenty of targets in Week 3 against the Texans, as Indianapolis is running out of NFL-caliber pass catchers in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Warren had six catches in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City, a game Pierce exited early. Given Warren's mix of talent and usage, he remains a top-10 fantasy TE in Week 3 against Houston's talented defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Warren has increased his catch total by three with each subsequent game this season, and he has scored in two of the Colts' three games heading into a Week 4 international game against the Commanders in London. Coming off a nine-catch game, Warren is a set-and-forget starting fantasy TE against a Washington defense that has allowed five TDs to the position through three games. The 2025 first-round pick is a key part of a Colts passing game that's missing top WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on injured reserve.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Warren has emerged with a consistent role as a short outlet for Colts QB Daniel Jones. Warren has caught 23 of 27 targets for 130 yards and two TDs, averaging almost six catches per game but just 5.7 yards per catch. His floor is high enough to be trusted as a weekly fantasy starter at TE, as Warren leads the Colts in catches and is one target shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. Week 5 at Pittsburgh is no exception, even though the Steelers are tied for the fourth-fewest catches allowed to TEs with 13. Two of those 13 receptions have resulted in touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Warren had a season-high 83 receiving yards and a short rushing TD in the Colts' Week 5 loss to Pittsburgh. The versatile TE has been the team's second-best offensive player behind star RB Jonathan Taylor. Warren has accounted for three of the team's five non-Taylor touchdowns and leads the Colts with 30 catches through five games. Warren remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter in Week 6 due to his prominent involvement in the game plan every week, even against a Titans defense that has allowed the third-fewest receiving yards to TEs at 29 per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Warren sat out the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans after being a late addition to the injury report due to a groin injury. If the 2025 first-round pick is cleared to return in Week 7 against the Vikings, he would reclaim his role as a key cog on offense for the Colts and a borderline top-five fantasy TE. Jonathan Taylor has seven of the Colts' 13 offensive TDs this season, and Warren has scored three of the other six while averaging six receptions per game. Minnesota hasn't allowed a TE to score this season while giving up 44 receiving yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Warren hasn't suited up since Week 5 due to a groin injury. He leads the Colts with 30 catches despite missing the past two games, so Warren would immediately return to the fantasy starting range if he gains clearance to return in Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that has been much more vulnerable through the air than on the ground. Jacksonville is holding TEs to 35 yards per game but has allowed the position to score four times in six outings, and Warren has accounted for three of the six TDs scored by Colts other than Jonathan Taylor.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Warren turned 10 targets into just 18 yards in his return from a two-game absence due to a groin injury in the Colts' 42-7 Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. That performance sums up the sorry state of Indianapolis' passing game, but Warren's volume remains elite for a TE. He's back to being a set-and-forget starting option at the position now that he's healthy, especially with a favorable Week 9 home matchup on tap against the Cowboys. Dallas' defense is allowing 51 yards per game to TEs and has given up four TDs to the position, surrendering 26.6 points per game overall.
outlooksByWeek.10: Tyler Warren has drawn at least seven targets in five of his last six appearances. The 2025 first-round pick remains a weekly fantasy starter at TE thanks to his hefty volume, even though he's averaging just 5.2 yards per target in the Colts' low-octane passing offense. Warren and the Colts will face a Dolphins defense in Week 10 that has allowed six receiving TDs in eight games to TEs. In addition to two touchdown catches, Warren has one rushing score this season.
outlooksByWeek.11: Tyler Warren had a season-low three targets in a head-scratching Week 10 performance against the Dolphins after the Colts traded away starting WRs Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Even after that dud, Warren is still averaging a healthy seven targets per game, and his 276 receiving yards and two receiving TDs lead all players still rostered by the Colts. Warren had a season-high nine catches when the Colts faced the Texans in Week 3 and should be similarly busy in the Week 11 rematch against a Houston defense that ranks among the league's 10 most generous units through the air. Don't let Warren's down game in Week 10 dissuade you from continuing to deploy him as a high-floor fantasy starter at TE.
outlooksByWeek.12: Tyler Warren has been held to just three catches in two games since the Colts traded starting WRs Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Rather than collecting even more targets as the team's top remaining pass catcher, Warren has struggled to create separation as defenses have focused on stopping him. Warren can't sink much lower following the Colts' QB change from Daniel Jones to Anthony Richardson, even though Richardson's 15-game sample as an NFL starter suggests he's more likely to air it out deep to wide receivers or take off running than find his TE on a short or intermediate route. Week 12 against the Giants will mark the first time that Warren, a 2025 first-round pick, and Richardson, a 2023 first-round pick, start in the same game. Benching Warren is justifiable if you have a solid alternative, but leaving him in and hoping for a spark with Richardson is defensible.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren put together a solid rookie season, but it could've been even better. In 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, Warren scored five touchdowns and averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG. In five games without Jones, Warren fell to 6.3 PPG and failed to find the end zone. In fact, the 2025 first-round pick was unlucky in the scoring department, ranking fifth among tight ends in end zone targets (seven) and expected TDs (7.5). Warren finished the season third among tight ends in targets and also had three goal-line carries. The 24-year-old was already a featured target and might see even more work with Michael Pittman Jr. shipped to Pittsburgh. Warren is a quality TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift will be a top option in Chicago's offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Swift cooled down in Week 2 after a monster opener, logging 16 rushes for 45 yards on the ground. The veteran RB did see success in the passing game, logging five catches for 54 yards. With Tyson Bagent expected to start at quarterback for the Bears, Swift could be utilized more heavily on the ground. Philadelphia has also allowed 216 rushing yards to running backs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: D'Andre Swift should remain Chicago's top option in the rushing game against the Jets in Week 4. Swift saw a season-high 20 carries in Week 3 versus Philly , taking them for 84 yards and adding on two catches for four yards. The veteran ball carrier eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign, but he's seen his only end zone appearances come from Week 1. He'll now turn his attention to a Jets defense that ceded 99 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 20 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in their most recent outing.
outlooksByWeek.5: D'Andre Swift will seek to get back on track as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Swift rushed the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught two targets for 16 yards against the Jets in Week 4, but he also lost a fumble and was stopped at the goal line twice. The veteran was outplayed by his younger counterpart, Kyle Monangai, who posted a 30-146-2 rushing line. Either way, Swift should still get plenty of usage against a Packers defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: D'Andre Swift could be in line for a featured role once again as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Swift should have benefited hugely from Kyle Monangai being out with a toe injury in Week 5, but he rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 30 yards in a blowout loss. The status of Monangai remains up in the air ahead of Chicago's away bout, and Swift's value is very much contingent on his position mate's status. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: D'Andre Swift could see his workload take a hit as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Swift was inefficient on the ground in Week 6 with 16 carries for 44 yards, but he was able to salvage his outing with two rushing touchdowns and four catches for 26 yards. The veteran has benefited from Kyle Monangai being out the last two weeks with turf toe, especially given that three of his six touchdowns this season have come in that stretch. Whether Monangai plays or not, Swift will face a New England front that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: D'Andre Swift's role will be up in the air heading into Week 8 as the Bears travel to Seattle. Swift produced once again in Week 7, tallying 22 rushes for 78 yards and a touchdown, along with catching four passes for 12 yards. The veteran has benefited from a workhorse role with Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) out the last three weeks, finding the end zone four times and averaging over 19 touches per game in that stretch. Monangai could be in line to return this week, but the pair of running backs have proven to both hold value even when both active. Either way, Swift will face a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs (15.4).
outlooksByWeek.9: D'Andre Swift will look to build on a high-volume performance as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Swift was, for the most part, stymied by a tough Seattle front in Week 8, averaging just 2.6 yards per carry, but he still put together a monster game with three touchdowns and 69 yards off a season-high 27 rushes. The veteran has directly benefited from the absence of position mate Kyle Monangai in the last four weeks, which can especially be seen through his seven touchdowns in that stretch. With or without Monangai active, Swift should have a tough time, especially if he can't find the end zone, against a Tampa Bay front that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.11: D'Andre Swift will look to bounce back from a tough showing as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Swift was shelled by a tough Tampa Bay front before Chicago's Week 10 bye, rushing the ball 12 times for 31 yards. The veteran still racked up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games without Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) out, so there is still hope for him to deliver moving forward. Even if Monangai returns, New Orleans ranking 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs could allow for an entire backfield to eat.
outlooksByWeek.12: D'Andre Swift will aim to continue to lead Chicago's running game in Week 12 at Detroit. Swift remained the top running back in a Week 11 win over the Saints even with Kyle Monangai back from a turf toe injury. Swift's 15 touches easily outweighed Monangai's eight touches, but it wouldn't be crazy if the Bears ramped up the younger running back in the upcoming away matchup. Swift will look to build on a career-high 11 touchdowns versus a Lions defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Williams is set to miss another game as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is set to get the start again versus a Packers defense that gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Caleb Williams' status is up in the air ahead of Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Williams has been sidelined since he injured his hamstring against Minnesota in Week 2, but he could be ready to return if he has a favorable practice week. If he plays, the starting quarterback will face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Williams will aim to build on a stellar return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Williams had no struggles in Week 6 against the Falcons in his first game since Week 2, completing 83 percent of passes for 305 yards and one touchdown. The third-year quarterback has now surpassed 250 passing yards in both games that he's played through this season, and the sky's the limit now. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Caleb Williams will aim to stay hot as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Williams impressed in his second game back from a hamstring injury in Week 7, completing 67 percent of passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns over the Patriots. The third-year quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in back-to-back weeks, and he hasn't committed a turnover in that stretch. He'll take on a Seattle defense that's been tougher on QBs, ranking second in fantasy points allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: Caleb Williams will look to stay solid as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Williams pieced together another solid outing in Chicago's Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown. The starting quarterback has now thrown for 860 yards and four touchdowns in his last three games, and he's passed for 240 or more yards in all but one outing this season. He'll shift focus to a Tampa Bay squad that's ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Caleb Williams will look to lead a more efficient Chicago offense in Week 12 at Detroit. Williams put together a passable stat line in a Week 11 win over the Saints, but the Bears offense looked sluggish in the matchup. The third-year quarterback has dished out two touchdowns in three of his last four games and thrown for 240 or more yards in all but one of his last five. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked a favorable 31st in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brandon Aubrey was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. With New York dominating time of possession, Aubrey did not even attempt a field goal. He also missed one of his extra points when Javonte Williams was assessed a taunting penalty following a touchdown, leading to a 48-yard PAT try. Aubrey has nowhere to go but up in Week 2 versus the Commanders, though. Washington allowed 26.5 points per game just a season ago, which was 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brandon Aubrey connected on all three of his field goals last game for Dallas, including a 60-yarder. Aubrey also booted four extra points, shaking off a surprising miss in Week 1 versus the Giants. In Week 3, the Cowboys clash with the Ravens. Baltimore is allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is in the middle of the pack so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and two extra points last game for Dallas, but his missed three-pointer will likely be the most talked about boot. Aubrey was blocked from 59 yards out, a makeable distance for the strong-legged kicker, and the Cowboys lost to the Ravens by that margin. However, Aubrey has made six field goals in the last two games, and remains a standout option kicking for one of the top offenses in the league. In Week 4, Dallas will face a disappointing Houston squad allowing 25 points per contest, which is 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brandon Aubrey missed two field goals last game for Dallas. Such a sensational headline needs explanation, though, as both of Aubrey's misses came from over 60 yards away. Aubrey had a 62-yarder blocked, and missed a 65-yarder wide left. Otherwise, Aubrey connected on two field goals from 50 yards and in, while also making all four of his extra points. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay squad allowing 24.0 points per clash, which is tied for 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brandon Aubrey did not have much work last game for Dallas. Aubrey connected on one field goal and one extra point in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Aubrey has made just nine field goals through five games for Dallas, which is tied for 10th in the league. In Week 6, the Cowboys face the Packers. Green Bay is allowing 22.4 points per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brandon Aubrey managed one single, solitary extra point last game for Dallas. The Cowboys offense has sputtered of late, scoring a combined 29 points over the last two contests. Aubrey has registered just one field goal and two PATs over that span. In Week 7, Dallas will look to right the ship against another struggling NFC East squad, the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per tilt, which is 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and three extra points for Dallas last game. Unfortunately, Aubrey also missed a kick from 50-plus yards out, and the Cowboys ended up losing to Arizona by three points in overtime. Still, Aubrey has now made three field goals and three extra points in each of the last two games for the Cowboys. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 9 versus the folding Colts. Indy is allowing 27.8 points per clash, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brandon Aubrey missed yet another long field goal last game for Dallas. Aubrey did make two other tries, though pulled a 50-yarder wide left in the 27-23 win over the Colts. Aubrey is now 3-for-8 on attempts from 50-plus yards out this season. In Week 10, the Cowboys will face the 49ers. Points may be hard to come by, as San Fran is allowing just 19.5 points per tilt, which is sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brandon Aubrey connected on two field goals and two extra points for the Cowboys in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Aubrey did miss an extra point, his second of the season. However, both of Aubrey's field goals came from 50-plus yards out, giving him five such field goals on the season to date. In Week 11, Dallas will face a bumbling Titans squad. Tennessee is allowing 26.6 points per contest, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.12: Brandon Aubrey made one field goal and six extra points last game for the Cowboys. Dallas destroyed Tennessee by a score of 51-30, though all the touchdowns left Aubrey with only a modest kicking performance. In fact, it was the first time in five outings that he failed to kick multiple field goals in a single game. In Week 12, Dallas will face division rival Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 23.7 points per tilt, which is 18th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in targets last game. Likely saw a staggering 12 balls thrown his way en route to seven catches for 66 yards in the win over Arizona. However, fellow tight end Theo Johnson stole a touchdown from him. Still, Likely's renewed usage with quarterback Jameis Winston under center was a pleasant surprise, as Likely only had five targets in the prior game versus Tennessee. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 5 versus Washington. The Commanders defense has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Likely exploded for 11 receptions and two touchdowns last game for the Giants. The 11 receptions set a career high, and Likely scored twice for the second time in five contests. Likely has a staggering 25 targets over the last two outings alone. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaiah Likely has remained extremely busy for the Giants, regardless of who lines up at quarterback.
