Likely has received double-digit targets in four of the last five games for the G-Men. Likely has scored three times in the last two contests, and five times on the season overall. Likely leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and touchdowns, and is second in receptions to Trey McBride. Likely should be primed for another big outing in Week 7 versus the Texans. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Isaiah Likely had a surprisingly poor game for the Giants his last time on the field. Likely managed just two catches for 12 yards in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. Likely had managed double-digit targets in each of the previous three games for the G-Men, so the lack of looks was eye-opening. Still, new quarterback J.J. McCarthy was working under center and targeted star wideout Malik Nabers with reckless abandon. Likely should see more work in Week 9 versus the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 235.4 passing yards per contest, which is 24th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.10: Isaiah Likely found the end zone again for the Giants last game. Likely snagged five passes for 53 yards and a touchdown in the 19-11 win over Philadelphia. Likely now has scored four touchdowns in his last four contests. He is a great bet to find the end zone again versus a suspect Washington pass defense. Washington has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns this season, which is tied for 25th in the league.  In addition, the Commanders are allowing 240 passing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.11: Isaiah Likely notched a career-high 127 yards receiving last game for the Giants. Likely reeled in nine passes, one of which went for a 66-yard touchdown, though the G-Men fell to Washington by a score of 24-21. Still, Likely has scored in back-to-back contests, and has five scores in his last five outings.  In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL. However, Jacksonville has surrendered just 10 passing scores this season, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Isaiah Likely had an unexpectedly quiet game for the Giants last week.  Despite the win, Likely managed just one grab for 35 yards. he had a season-low three targets for the contest.  Likely is having a breakout campaign for the G-Men overall, though, so expect a return to normalcy in Week 12 versus the Colts. Indy is allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Colts have also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jared Goff will look to build off a season-opener win as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Goff's performance and Detroit's overall in Week 1 weren't pretty, but he got the job done, finishing with 206 passing yards and two touchdowns. The game also showed that the Lions will continue to have a high-volume air attack, as the veteran ended with 39 pass attempts. Goff will now turn his focus to a Bills defense that ceded 274 passing yards and two touchdowns to C.J. Stroud in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Goff will look to keep his high production rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Goff benefited from playing from behind in Week 2 at Buffalo, racking up 327 passing yards and four touchdowns on a 68.4 percent completion rate. The veteran quarterback has now totaled 533 passing yards with a 6:0 TD:INT across his first two games, and Detroit's lacking defense has only helped his output so far. Goff will take on a Jets defense that's allowed a top-10 fantasy points per game (14.2) to quarterbacks in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Goff will continue to benefit from a high-powered offense as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Goff kept it rolling in Week 3, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. The veteran quarterback has completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards and eight touchdowns with no interceptions across three games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game (23.5) to QBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jared Goff will remain a high-volume option as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. No matter the outcome of each game so far, Goff has delivered consistent output, and Week 4 against the Panthers was no different. The veteran quarterback recorded season-high totals in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, completing 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in what was an eventual loss. He's now thrown for 250 or more yards in his last three games, and he's yet to commit a turnover this year. Goff will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jared Goff will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Goff recorded another monster performance heading into Detroit's bye week, and he's yet to throw an interception this season. The veteran quarterback has now completed 67 percent of passes for 1,485 yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions in five games. He'll face a Green Bay defense that allowed 258 passing yards and a 1:2 TD:INT ratio to Dak Prescott in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jared Goff will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Goff's story stayed the same in a Week 7 win over the Packers, completing 22 of 32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in three of six games, and he's also dished out two or more touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll have his biggest test of the season this week, though, as Minnesota has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to the quarterback position.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jared Goff will aim to return to dominance as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Goff finished Week 8 against a tough Minnesota defense with his worst fantasy performance of the season, completing 18 of 25 passes for 176 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. The veteran quarterback still has excellent figures this year with 1,964 passing yards 15 touchdowns and one pick across seven games. He'll face a Dolphins defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.10: Jared Goff will look to return to dominance as the Lions play the Patriots in Week 10. Goff was stuffed again in a narrow Week 9 win over the Dolphins, completing 17 of 25 passes for just 170 yards with zero touchdowns and an interception. The veteran quarterback has now thrown for a disappointing 346 yards and a 1:2 TD:INT in the last two weeks. He'll face a New England defense that ceded 372 passing yards and three touchdowns to Jordan Love in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.11: Jared Goff will aim to take some momentum into Week 11 as the Lions play the Buccaneers. Goff broke a two-game stretch of struggles in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, completing 65 percent of passes for 303 yards with a 3:2 TD:INT. The veteran has now dished out 18 touchdowns with 2,437 passing yards across nine games this campaign. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Jared Goff will look to keep Detroit rolling in Week 12 against the Bears. Goff put together another solid performance in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, slinging for 278 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran now sports a 20:4 TD:INT and has thrown for 2,716 yards across 10 games. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy quarterbacks so far this year and allowed 222 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception to Tyler Shough this past Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Goff is entering his 10th NFL season, including his sixth with the Lions. The 2016 No. 1 draft pick has been extremely successful through the air over the past three seasons (4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns in all three), which has helped him to fantasy finishes of seventh, sixth and ninth. Of course, there's some survivorship bias here, as Goff's per-game finishes during the span are 15th, seventh and 12th. The reason for the limited fantasy output is a lack of rushing, as Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and was held to 45 yards in 2025. Playing at his absolute ceiling as a passer and still no more than a fringe QB1, the 31-year-old is just a solid backup/occasional streaming option in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaac TeSlaa remains a touchdown-dependent option as the Lions take on the Bills in Week 2. TeSlaa was unable to convert on his one target in Week 1 against the Saints, which only made season hopes lower for him after a subpar training camp. He also remains the fifth option in the Detroit passing game behind Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta. Luckily, Buffalo gave up a whopping 40.0 PPR points to Houston wide receivers in Week 1, so this upcoming week could be TeSlaa's chance to return to relevance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. TeSlaa recorded his first catches of the season against the Bills in Week 2, reeling in two of five targets for 26 yards. While his final stat line was still modest, the second-year receiver's five targets are promising. With that being said, he still hasn't done enough to be considered more than a depth option, especially against a New York defense that's been tougher on wide receivers so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaac TeSlaa will look to replicate a solid performance as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. TeSlaa started the season quietly with just two catches for 26 yards across the first two games, but he reeled in all three targets for 66 yards against the Jets in Week 3. While this output isn't enough to warrant a start and is more translatable to a stash move, TeSlaa could be in store for more looks. The Panthers have also allowed a second-least 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaac TeSlaa could continue to have a big role as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. TeSlaa finished Week 4 against the Panthers with season-high targets, catches and yards, reeling in four of eight looks for four catches and 95 yards. After a slow start to the season, the second-year pass catcher has now posted a 7-161-0 receiving line in the last two games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to the wide receiver position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaac TeSlaa will aim to bounce back as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. After it appeared the second-year pass catcher was starting to carve out a role for himself again, TeSlaa recorded zero catches against the Cardinals before Detroit's bye. Hopefully the second game this year with zero catches was another anomaly, as there is plenty of love to spread with the Lions' high-volume offense. Green Bay has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. After a promising stretch from Weeks 2-5, TeSlaa has now recorded just one catch for 10 yards off four targets in his last two games. The young pass catcher will aim to get back to relevance against a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.10: Isaac TeSlaa will be a secondary option in Detroit's passing offense again in Week 10 against the Patriots. TeSlaa was quiet again in a gritty Week 9 win over Miami, reeling in one of two targets for just nine yards. After a solid stretch from Weeks 2 to 4, the second-year pass catcher has now recorded just two catches for 19 yards in his last four showings. Luckily, he'll face a New England defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Isaac TeSlaa remains a touchdown-dependent option heading into Week 11 as the Lions play the Buccaneers. TeSlaa found his first score of the season in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, but he was quiet otherwise. The second-year pass catcher has now recorded 13 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown across nine showings this season. He'll be hard to trust against a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.12: Isaac TeSlaa will look to take better advantage of his targets as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. TeSlaa was unable to record a catch in Week 11 against the Buccaneers, even off three targets. The second-year pass catcher has had a volatile season after finding the end zone six times in his rookie campaign. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: TeSlaa is a candidate for a Year 2 leap as the favorite for No. 3 WR duties in Detroit behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. TeSlaa barely played as a rookie (27 total targets), but he had a very specific role and, believe it or not, tied for 11th in the entire NFL with 11 end zone targets. That helped lead to six touchdowns, four of which came when his snaps increased during Detroit's final six games. The 2025 third-round pick has a big size edge on both St. Brown and Williams, so while consistent targets are a long shot, he's still likely to remain busy near the goal line. TeSlaa won't be more than a boom/bust situational target most weeks, but if one of the starters misses time, he'll be on the flex radar. Consider him with a late pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 battle with the Patriots. The rookie should remain on waiver wires after playing just three of Pittsburgh's 67 offensive snaps in their season-opening win. Bernard is below DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, and Pat Freiermuth on the food chain, and it would take an absence or two from his teammates for him to see an uptick in playing time.
outlooksByWeek.3: Germie Bernard and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional showdown. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, the rookie stepped into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Bernard caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in the 20-3 loss, seemingly earning the trust of Aaron Rodgers rather quickly. He led the team in yardage, was second in targets, and tied for second in receptions. Bernard faces Cincinnati's 9th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (25.0) to WRs and should be considered a roster stash until we see this type of performance consistently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Germie Bernard and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He caught his only target for 14 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. One week after leading the team in yardage while finishing second in targets, Bernard fell victim to a Steelers offense that prefers to spread the ball around, as Aaron Rodgers completed passes to nine different receivers in the win. Cleveland's defense is susceptible through the air, as they're tied for 29th in receiving TDs allowed (5) through three games, but Bernard is off the fantasy radar for now.
outlooksByWeek.5: Germie Bernard and the Steelers return home to square off against the Colts in Week 5. The rookie wideout caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Bernard should remain on fantasy benches while playing behind veterans DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, and Jaylen Warren, along with tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington. Indianapolis allows 35.0 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 20th, but his limited involvement on offense doesn't inspire much confidence.
outlooksByWeek.6: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Tampa Bay for an interconference clash in Week 6. He hauled in six of nine targets for 80 yards and had one carry for four yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 Week 5 victory. With Roman Wilson (finger) injured in the win and already ruled out for the meeting with the Buccaneers, Bernard has a real opportunity to fill that void and continue contributing in his debut season. The 2026 second-round pick notched career highs but is still searching for his first career touchdown, something he hopes to change against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Paris for an interconference clash against the Saints in Week 7. He caught 11 of 12 targets for 87 yards and the game-winning touchdown in Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime win in Week 6. The rookie erupted for career highs in every receiving category while notching his first-ever TD. Bernard tied DK Metcalf (11-93-0) for the team lead in receptions while finishing a close second in yardage and targets. He'll aim to stay hot against a New Orleans defense that ranks 18th by allowing 32.3 fantasy points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Germie Bernard and the Steelers welcome the division-rival Browns to town in Week 8. The rookie caught three of five targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Week 7 over the Saints in Paris. Bernard was relatively quiet after posting a 17-167-1 receiving line on 21 targets over his previous two outings. He'll look to bounce back versus a Cleveland defense tied for 19th in fantasy points allowed per game (32.4) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.10: In Week 10, Germie Bernard and the Steelers visit the Bengals in an AFC North showdown. He brought in all five of his targets for 30 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-6 victory in Week 8. The rookie paced the team in receptions, finished second in targets behind DK Metcalf (6), and was third in yardage in a game Aaron Rodgers completed just 13 passes for 172 yards. Bernard will try to get back on track against a Cincinnati defense allowing 31.1 fantasy points per game (15th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.11: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Philadelphia for a Week 11 interconference clash. He failed to bring in any of his three targets during Week 10's loss to Cincinnati but did gain 10 yards on his lone carry. Bernard was held without a catch for the first time since Week 1, when he played only three offensive snaps. Pittsburgh's offense struggled all night, gaining just 247 total yards, but the hope is that Bernard will bounce back versus an Eagles defense allowing 37.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Germie Bernard and the Steelers play host to the Broncos in a Week 12 clash on Black Friday. He caught six of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 defeat. Bernard led his team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and finished third in yardage after failing to record a catch in his last outing. The talented rookie will look to build upon that performance versus a stout Denver defense that ranks sixth in fantasy points allowed per game (28.1) to opposing WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bernard was selected by the Steelers in the second round of April's draft. Bernard is a solid, reliable receiver with good size who can align all over the formation (55% slot in 53 collegiate games). Despite playing at three schools in four years, Bernard's production increased each season, including a strong 64-862-7 receiving line (plus 18-101-2 rushing) in 2025. He dropped only four of 240 career targets. Bernard is likely to open his career third or fourth in line at receiver behind Michael Pittman Jr., DK Metcalf and perhaps Roman Wilson. That will create a tough path to consistent rookie-season usage and production, so he's only worth draft consideration in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange was one of four Jaguars to catch a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence in the season-opening win over the Browns, and the starting tight end should remain involved in the Week 2 game plan against the Broncos. The Broncos excelled at defending wide receivers last season but gave up the ninth-most receiving yards to TEs. Strange is a decent fantasy option in multi-TE formats or those with a tight end premium. However, with many mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, Strange is tough to trust as a starter in standard single-TE leagues. Strange has exceeded 61 receiving yards just once since the start of last season while scoring four TDs in 13 appearances over that span.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenton Strange remains a complementary piece in Jacksonville's passing game heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. He's locked in atop the Jaguars' TE depth chart, but Strange has just seven catches for 72 yards and a TD on 10 targets in three games-numbers elite options at his position often reach in one game. The Bengals have allowed 23 catches (third-most) and 299 yards (second-most) to TEs, so Strange has more fantasy appeal than usual in Week 4 and is a viable option in multi-TE or TE-premium formats. Even the favorable matchup isn't enough to propel him into the starting range in most one-TE leagues.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of those.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of them.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brenton Strange has picked up the pace after a slow start and is a viable Week 8 starter at TE for Jacksonville's home game against the Colts. He has caught 19 of 23 targets for 207 yards over the past three games after being limited to seven catches for 72 yards on 10 targets through Week 3, though Strange hasn't scored since the season opener. Strange has a nice opportunity to snap his five-game touchdown drought against the Colts, who have allowed five TDs to TEs, which is tied for fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brenton Strange leads the Jaguars with 28 catches this season and has averaged 65.5 receiving yards over the past four games after averaging a meager 24 yards per game through Week 3. Despite the recent uptick in production, he hasn't scored a TD since Week 1. Strange has a nice opportunity to end his touchdown drought in Week 9 against the Ravens, who have allowed six TDs to TEs, which is tied for fourth-most in the NFL. Given Strange's recent involvement and the favorable matchup, he's worth starting in Week 9.
outlooksByWeek.10: Brenton Strange is a viable fantasy option in Week 10 against the Titans, but he's far from a must-start. He leads the Jaguars with 30 catches through eight games but hasn't scored since the season opener and is averaging 45 yards per game, which ranks 10th among TEs. Tennessee has struggled to defend the pass in general, but the Titans have limited TEs to 43 yards per game, though they have also given up four TDs to the position through eight games.
outlooksByWeek.11: Brenton Strange remains a borderline fantasy starter at TE for Week 11 against the Giants. He scored his first TD since Week 1 in Jacksonville's Week 10 win over the Titans but had just nine receiving yards, dropping his season average to 41 yards per game. That's right in line with the 48 receiving yards per game that the Giants allow to TEs, as they are a better-than-average defense against the position. Rookies Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol have each recorded at least one catch in three consecutive games, but Strange remains the clear No. 1 TE for Jacksonville, handling a snap share north of 75%.
outlooksByWeek.12: Brenton Strange is a viable low-end starter at TE in Week 12 against the Titans, though Jacksonville's wideouts are more likely to find success versus Tennessee's leaky secondary. One of Strange's two TDs this season came in Week 10 at Tennessee, but he had a season-low nine receiving yards in that game. The Titans are holding TEs to 42 yards per game, though they have given up six TDs to the position. Strange ranks 14th at his position with 38 receiving yards per game.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.6: Zach Charbonnet continues to rehab from a torn ACL and isn't expected to play in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Charbonnet did have his 21-day practice window opened last week, and he got in a couple limited practice sessions, but the fact that the Seahawks are playing on Thursday night this week complicates his outlook for a return to action. As such, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani are slated to lead Seattle's RB corps again. Charbonnet does have a chance to make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.7: Zach Charbonnet (knee) and the Seahawks welcome the Chiefs to town for Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He's been on the physically unable to perform (PUP)/reserve list to begin 2026, but Seattle opened his three-week practice window back on Oct. 1. With that being said, Charbonnet will need to be activated by Thursday in order to avoid him being out for the rest of the season. He's expected to join the official roster after practicing in a limited fashion the last couple weeks. However, Charbonnet will likely be eased into the backfield rotation if he is indeed able to make his debut, so it would be wise to wait until after the meeting with Kansas City's defense that's tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a chance to return to Seattle's backfield in Week 8 against Chicago. Charbonnet has yet to play since tearing his ACL in January, but he was activated off the reserve/PUP list last week and logged a trio of full practices. Though he ultimately didn't play Sunday against Kansas City, another week of practice could be enough for Charbonnet to make his return Monday against the Bears. Should that happen, he'll face a Chicago defense that has given up five total touchdowns (three rushing, two receiving) to running backs through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Zach Charbonnet will look to build upon an uneventful season debut when the Seahawks host the Cardinals in Week 9. Charbonnet logged his first game action since January this past Monday against Chicago and finished with 23 yards on six carries along with six yards on three catches. He shared the backfield primarily with Jadarian Price (12 touches), and that arrangement may cap both players' weekly production moving forward. Arizona does present a decent matchup, as the Cardinals are tied for 20th in the NFL with 18.2 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.10: Zach Charbonnet seems to be emerging as Seattle's No. 1 running back heading into a Week 10 tilt against the Raiders. In his second game back from ACL surgery, Charbonnet led the Seahawks with 16 carries and 77 receiving yards against Arizona this past Sunday while adding one catch for nine yards. Rookie Jadarian Price still managed 13 touches, so Charbonnet doesn't seem likely to have the backfield all to himself. Both tailbacks could thrive against a Las Vegas defense that has allowed a league-worst 5.21 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.12: Zach Charbonnet appears to have seized the lead-RB role for Seattle heading into a Week 12 matchup against the 49ers. Charbonnet didn't debut until Week 8 against Chicago and had just nine touches in that game, but in his most recent appearance -- Week 10 versus Las Vegas -- he carried 20 times for 94 yards while logging a season-high 72% offensive snap share. Jadarian Price should continue to factor into the backfield mix as well, but there's a good chance that Charbonnet will be the leader of the team's backfield moving forward. He'll face a tough test against the 49ers, who have given up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (14.0) to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Charbonnet would've been entering his fourth NFL season as the clear lead back in Seattle, but a torn ACL during the team's playoff game against the 49ers has put his 2026 campaign in jeopardy. It's a tough break for the 2020 second-round NFL draft pick, who set career-high marks in touches (204) while ranking fifth among backs in rushing touchdowns (12) and carries inside the 5-yard line (16) last season. Charbonnet's minimal receiving role (career-low 24 targets) limited him to 11.3 fantasy points per game, however, and he has yet to deliver a top-20 fantasy campaign. Kenneth Walker III is gone, but first-round rookie Jadarian Price could very well cement himself a big offensive role by the time Charbonnet is healthy. The 25-year-old is worth only a late-round lottery ticket.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.3: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Antonio Williams finished third in targets for the Commanders last game. Williams caught just two balls on four looks, though, en route to only 15 yards receiving. Williams caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Antonio Williams had eight targets last game for Washington, which was second on the squad behind Stefon Diggs. Unfortunately, Williams could muster just three catches for 21 yards in the lackluster loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Williams, regardless of whether Terry McLaurin also suits up. McLaurin was sidelined with a hamstring issue. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Antonio Williams managed three catches last game for Washington. Even without the services of fellow wideout Stefon Diggs, Williams accumulated fewer than 35 yards receiving for the third-straight contest. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Antonio Williams should see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season, as No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Williams has double-digit catches in every game thus far during his rookie year, and should slot in just behind Stefon Diggs in terms of opportunities in the passing game moving forward. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.10: Antonio Williams tied for third on the Commanders in targets last game.  Unfortunately, despite seeing six targets, Williams managed only three catches for 25 yards in the 20-13 loss to the Rams. Williams is unlikely to break loose in Week 10 versus the Giants either. New York is allowing just 177.8 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.11: Antonio Williams found the end zone last game for Washington. The rookie snagged two passes for 42 yards and a touchdown in the 24-21 win over the G-Men. Williams has at least two catches in every game this season, and should continue to see steady work in the absence of Terry McLaurin. However, in Week 11, he will be facing a Bengals defense allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. In addition, Cincy has yielded just 11 passing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.12: Antonio Williams had a breakout performance last game for the Commanders. Williams snagged nine passes for 122 yards in the thrilling 22-20 win over the Bengals. This included several big catches down the stretch, including a 42-yarder from quarterback Jayden Daniels to put the Commanders in field goal range for the game-winning kick. Williams received a career-high 11 targets. In Week 12, Williams will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.9: Corey Kiner has had a minimal role in the Patriots' backfield entering a Week 9 matchup with the Packers. Kiner has rushed for 38 yards or more in three of the last four games, despite Rhamondre Stevenson leading the way in touches and TreVeyon Henderson factoring in when healthy. If Henderson were sidelined again in Week 9, Kiner may still not gather enough volume to be an option against a defense that's allowing 3.96 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.10: Corey Kiner could be in line for a significant role for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions, with both Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) uncertain to play. While Detroit is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing backs, volume remains king, and Kiner could serve as the No. 1 RB for Week 10 in Munich. Kiner figures to be a popular play in what could be a high-scoring game, despite Detroit allowing just 3.9 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.12: Corey Kiner brings double-digit touch potential into the Patriots' Week 12 game against the Chargers, as New England will likely run often with Tommy DeVito playing quarterback. The Chargers are allowing a modest 4.1 yards per carry but 10 touchdowns to running backs in 10 games, and six have topped 50 yards over the last five games. Kiner's lack of involvement in the passing game, paired with facing many eight-man fronts, tempers optimism, but opportunity should be available.
